Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Saṃyuttanikāyo

The Connected Discourses

Mahāvaggo

The Great Division

1. Maggasaṃyuttaṃ

1. The Connected Discourses on the Path

1. Avijjāvaggo

1. The Chapter on Ignorance

1. Avijjāsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Ignorance

1. Evaṃ [M 3.0001][V 3.0001][P 5.0001][T 5.0001] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

1. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Avijjā, bhikkhave, pubbaṅgamā akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā, anvadeva anudeva (sī. pī. ka.) ahirikaṃ anottappaṃ[V 3.0002]. Avijjāgatassa, bhikkhave, aviddasuno micchādiṭṭhi pahoti; micchādiṭṭhissa micchāsaṅkappo pahoti; micchāsaṅkappassa micchāvācā pahoti; micchāvācassa micchākammanto pahoti; micchākammantassa micchāājīvo pahoti; micchāājīvassa micchāvāyāmo pahoti; micchāvāyāmassa micchāsati pahoti; micchāsatissa micchāsamādhi pahoti.

“Bhikkhus, ignorance is the forerunner for the attainment of unwholesome states, followed by shamelessness and fearlessness of wrongdoing. For one who is endowed with ignorance, bhikkhus, for one without wisdom, wrong view arises. For one of wrong view, wrong intention arises. For one of wrong intention, wrong speech arises. For one of wrong speech, wrong action arises. For one of wrong action, wrong livelihood arises. For one of wrong livelihood, wrong effort arises. For one of wrong effort, wrong mindfulness arises. For one of wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration arises.

“Vijjā [M 3.0002] ca kho, bhikkhave, pubbaṅgamā kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā, anvadeva hirottappaṃ. Vijjāgatassa, bhikkhave[P 5.0002], viddasuno sammādiṭṭhi [T 5.0002] pahoti; sammādiṭṭhissa sammāsaṅkappo pahoti; sammāsaṅkappassa sammāvācā pahoti; sammāvācassa sammākammanto pahoti; sammākammantassa sammāājīvo pahoti; sammāājīvassa sammāvāyāmo pahoti; sammāvāyāmassa sammāsati pahoti; sammāsatissa sammāsamādhi pahotī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And, bhikkhus, knowledge is the forerunner for the attainment of wholesome states, followed by shame and fear of wrongdoing. For one who is endowed with knowledge, bhikkhus, for one with wisdom, right view arises. For one of right view, right intention arises. For one of right intention, right speech arises. For one of right speech, right action arises. For one of right action, right livelihood arises. For one of right livelihood, right effort arises. For one of right effort, right mindfulness arises. For one of right mindfulness, right concentration arises.”

2. Upaḍḍhasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Half

2. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakyesu viharati nagarakaṃ nāma nāgarakaṃ nāma (sī.), sakkaraṃ nāma (syā. ka.) sakyānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “upaḍḍhamidaṃ, bhante, brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā”ti.

2. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Sakkara, a market town of the Sakyans. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this is half of the holy life, that is, good friendship, good companionship, and good comradeship.”

“Mā hevaṃ, ānanda, mā hevaṃ, ānanda! Sakalamevidaṃ, ānanda, brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā. Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati.

“Do not say so, Ānanda! Do not say so, Ānanda! This is the entire holy life, Ānanda, that is, good friendship, good companionship, and good comradeship. For a bhikkhu, Ānanda, who has a good friend, a good companion, and a good comrade, it is to be expected that he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path and make much of the Noble Eightfold Path.

“Kathañcānanda, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idhānanda, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ; sammāsaṅkappaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ [T 5.0003] …pe… sammāvācaṃ bhāveti [V 3.0003] …pe… sammākammantaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāājīvaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāvāyāmaṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsatiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti.

“And how, Ānanda, does a bhikkhu who has a good friend, a good companion, and a good comrade develop the Noble Eightfold Path and make much of the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. He develops right intention… right speech… right action… right livelihood… right effort… right mindfulness… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who has a good friend, a good companion, and a good comrade develops the Noble Eightfold Path and makes much of the Noble Eightfold Path.

“Tadamināpetaṃ[M 3.0003][P 5.0003], ānanda, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā sakalamevidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā. Mamañhi, ānanda, kalyāṇamittaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti; jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti; maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti; sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti. Iminā kho etaṃ, ānanda, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā sakalamevidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“By this method also, Ānanda, it should be understood how this is the entire holy life, that is: good friendship, good companionship, and good comradeship. For, Ānanda, by relying on me as a good friend, beings subject to birth are freed from birth; beings subject to aging are freed from aging; beings subject to death are freed from death; beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. Indeed, Ānanda, it is by this method that it should be understood how this is the entire holy life, that is: good friendship, good companionship, and good comradeship.”

3. Sāriputtasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse to Sāriputta

3. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sakalamidaṃ, bhante, brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā”ti.

3. The setting is Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this is the entire holy life, that is: good friendship, good companionship, and good comradeship.”

“Sādhu [T 5.0004] sādhu, sāriputta! Sakalamidaṃ, sāriputta, brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā. Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ kalyāṇasahāyassa kalyāṇasampavaṅkassa – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ [V 3.0004] bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, sāriputta, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti?

“Good, good, Sāriputta! This is the entire holy life, Sāriputta, that is: good friendship, good companionship, and good comradeship. For a bhikkhu who has a good friend, a good companion, and a good comrade, Sāriputta, it is to be expected that he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path and make much of the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, Sāriputta, does a bhikkhu who has a good friend, a good companion, and a good comrade develop the Noble Eightfold Path and make much of the Noble Eightfold Path?

“Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ [P 5.0004] vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, sāriputta, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti.

Here, Sāriputta, a monk develops Right View that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminates in relinquishment... he develops Right Concentration that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminates in relinquishment. In this way, Sāriputta, a monk who has good friends, good companions, and is inclined towards good friends develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates it frequently.

“Tadamināpetaṃ, sāriputta, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā sakalamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā. Mamañhi, sāriputta, kalyāṇamittaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā [M 3.0004] parimuccanti; jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti; maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti; sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti. Iminā kho etaṃ, sāriputta, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ [T 5.0005] yathā sakalamidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā kalyāṇasahāyatā kalyāṇasampavaṅkatā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

By this method also, Sāriputta, it should be understood how this is the entirety of the holy life, that is: good friendship, good companionship, and inclination towards good friends. For, Sāriputta, by relying on me as a good friend, beings subject to birth are freed from birth; beings subject to aging are freed from aging; beings subject to death are freed from death; beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. By this method indeed, Sāriputta, it should be understood how this is the entirety of the holy life, that is: good friendship, good companionship, and inclination towards good friends.

4. Jāṇussoṇibrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Brahmin Jāṇussoṇi

4. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Addasā kho āyasmā ānando jāṇussoṇiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathena vaḷabhīrathena (sī.) sāvatthiyā niyyāyantaṃ. Setā sudaṃ assā yuttā honti setālaṅkārā, seto ratho, setaparivāro, setā rasmiyo, setā patodalaṭṭhi, setaṃ chattaṃ, setaṃ uṇhīsaṃ[V 3.0005], setāni vatthāni, setā upāhanā, setāya sudaṃ vālabījaniyā bījīyati. Tamenaṃ jano disvā evamāha – “brahmaṃ vata, bho, yānaṃ! Brahmayānarūpaṃ vata, bho”ti!!

4. At Sāvatthī. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Ānanda dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms. The Venerable Ānanda saw the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi leaving Sāvatthī in an all-white chariot drawn by mares. The yoked mares were white, with white ornaments; the chariot was white, with white coverings, white reins, a white goad, a white parasol, a white turban, white clothes, and white sandals. He was being fanned with a white tail-hair whisk. Seeing him, the people exclaimed, “Sirs, what a divine vehicle! Sirs, what an appearance of a divine vehicle!”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[P 5.0005]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

Then the Venerable Ānanda, having walked for alms in Sāvatthī and returned from his alms-round after the meal, approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:

“Idhāhaṃ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Addasaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, jāṇussoṇiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ sabbasetena vaḷavābhirathena sāvatthiyā niyyāyantaṃ. Setā sudaṃ assā yuttā honti setālaṅkārā, seto ratho, setaparivāro, setā rasmiyo, setā patodalaṭṭhi, setaṃ chattaṃ, setaṃ uṇhīsaṃ, setāni vatthāni, setā [T 5.0006] upāhanā, setāya sudaṃ vālabījaniyā bījīyati. Tamenaṃ jano disvā evamāha – ‘brahmaṃ vata, bho, yānaṃ! Brahmayānarūpaṃ vata, bho’ti!! Sakkā nu kho, bhante, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye brahmayānaṃ paññāpetu”nti?

“Here, venerable sir, in the morning, having dressed, I took my bowl and robe and entered Sāvatthī for alms. I saw, venerable sir, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi leaving Sāvatthī in an all-white chariot drawn by mares. The yoked mares were white, with white ornaments; the chariot was white, its coverings were white, the reins were white, the goad-stick was white, the parasol was white, the turban was white, the garments were white, and the sandals were white. He was being fanned with a white whisk. Seeing him, the people said this: ‘Oh, what a divine vehicle! Oh, what an appearance of a divine vehicle!’ Is it possible, venerable sir, to designate a Brahma-vehicle in this Dhamma and Discipline?”

“Sakkā[M 3.0005], ānandā”ti bhagavā avoca – “imasseva kho etaṃ, ānanda, ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa adhivacanaṃ – ‘brahmayānaṃ’ itipi, ‘dhammayānaṃ’ itipi, ‘anuttaro saṅgāmavijayo’ itipī”ti.

“It is possible, Ānanda,” the Blessed One said. “Ānanda, this is a designation for this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: ‘Brahma-vehicle,’ ‘Dhamma-vehicle,’ and ‘the unexcelled victory in battle.’”

“Sammādiṭṭhi, ānanda, bhāvitā bahulīkatā rāgavinayapariyosānā hoti, dosavinayapariyosānā hoti, mohavinayapariyosānā hoti. Sammāsaṅkappo, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno hoti, dosavinayapariyosāno hoti, mohavinayapariyosāno hoti. Sammāvācā, ānanda, bhāvitā bahulīkatā rāgavinayapariyosānā hoti, dosa…pe… mohavinayapariyosānā hoti. Sammākammanto, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno hoti, dosa… mohavinayapariyosāno hoti. Sammāājīvo, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno hoti, dosa… mohavinayapariyosāno hoti[V 3.0006]. Sammāvāyāmo, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno [T 5.0007] hoti, dosa… mohavinayapariyosāno hoti. Sammāsati, ānanda, bhāvitā bahulīkatā rāgavinayapariyosānā hoti, dosa… mohavinayapariyosānā hoti. Sammāsamādhi, ānanda, bhāvito bahulīkato rāgavinayapariyosāno [P 5.0006] hoti, dosa… mohavinayapariyosāno hoti.

“Right View, Ānanda, when developed and cultivated, culminates in the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, and the removal of delusion. Right Intention, Ānanda, when developed and cultivated, culminates in the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, and the removal of delusion. Right Speech, Ānanda, when developed and cultivated, culminates in the removal of lust... the removal of delusion. Right Action, Ānanda, when developed and cultivated, culminates in the removal of lust... the removal of delusion. Right Livelihood, Ānanda, when developed and cultivated, culminates in the removal of lust... the removal of delusion. Right Effort, Ānanda, when developed and cultivated, culminates in the removal of lust... the removal of delusion. Right Mindfulness, Ānanda, when developed and cultivated, culminates in the removal of lust... the removal of delusion. Right Concentration, Ānanda, when developed and cultivated, culminates in the removal of lust... the removal of delusion.

“Iminā kho etaṃ, ānanda, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā imassevetaṃ ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa adhivacanaṃ – ‘brahmayānaṃ’ itipi, ‘dhammayānaṃ’ itipi, ‘anuttaro saṅgāmavijayo’ itipī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

By this method, Ānanda, it should be understood how 'the Brahma-vehicle,' 'the Dhamma-vehicle,' and 'the unsurpassed victory in battle' are designations for this very Noble Eightfold Path.” The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, further said this:

“Yassa saddhā ca paññā ca, dhammā yuttā sadā dhuraṃ;

Hirī īsā mano yottaṃ, sati ārakkhasārathi.

“For whom faith and wisdom are the two qualities always yoked to the pole; conscience is the shaft, mind the harness, and mindfulness the protecting charioteer.

“Ratho sīlaparikkhāro, jhānakkho cakkavīriyo;

Upekkhā dhurasamādhi, anicchā parivāraṇaṃ.

The chariot is furnished with virtue, its axle is meditation, and its wheels are energy; equanimity is the balance of the yoke, and non-desire is its covering.

“Abyāpādo avihiṃsā, viveko yassa āvudhaṃ;

Titikkhā cammasannāho vammasannāho (sī.), yogakkhemāya vattati.

Non-ill will, harmlessness, and seclusion are its weapons; patience is its leather armor. It proceeds towards security from bondage.

“Etadattani [T 5.0008][M 3.0006] sambhūtaṃ, brahmayānaṃ anuttaraṃ;

Niyyanti dhīrā lokamhā, aññadatthu jayaṃ jaya”nti. catutthaṃ;

This unsurpassed Brahma-vehicle arises from within. Assuredly, the wise, having won the victory, go forth from the world.”

5. Kimatthiyasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Purpose

5. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ –

5. At Sāvatthī. Then a number of monks approached the Blessed One, and so on, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One:

“Idha no, bhante, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā amhe evaṃ pucchanti – ‘kimatthiyaṃ, āvuso, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhā mayaṃ, bhante, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ [V 3.0007] paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākaroma – ‘dukkhassa kho, āvuso, pariññatthaṃ bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti. Kacci mayaṃ, bhante, evaṃ puṭṭhā evaṃ byākaramānā vuttavādino ceva bhagavato homa, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhāma, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ [P 5.0007] byākaroma, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī”ti?

“Venerable sir, wanderers of other sects ask us: ‘For what purpose, friends, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?’ When asked thus, venerable sir, we answer those wanderers of other sects: ‘For the full understanding of suffering, friends, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’ Venerable sir, when we, being asked thus, answer in this way, do we state what was said by the Blessed One and not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is untrue? Do we explain the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no legitimate line of reasoning provides grounds for censure?”

“Taggha tumhe, bhikkhave, evaṃ puṭṭhā evaṃ byākaramānā vuttavādino ceva me hotha, na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhatha, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākarotha, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchati. Dukkhassa hi pariññatthaṃ mayi brahmacariyaṃ vussati. Sace vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘atthi panāvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa [T 5.0009] pariññāyā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘atthi kho, āvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa pariññāyā’”ti.

“Indeed, monks, when you are asked thus and answer in this way, you state what was said by me and do not misrepresent me with what is untrue. You explain the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no legitimate line of reasoning provides grounds for censure. For it is for the full understanding of suffering that the holy life is lived under me. If, monks, wanderers of other sects should ask you thus: ‘Is there then, friends, a path, is there a practice for the full understanding of this suffering?’—being asked thus, monks, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: ‘Indeed there is, friends, a path, there is a practice for the full understanding of this suffering.’”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, maggo, katamā paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa pariññāyāti? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo, ayaṃ paṭipadā etassa dukkhassa pariññāyāti. Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyāthā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the path, what is the practice for the full understanding of this suffering? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view… right concentration. This, monks, is the path, this is the practice for the full understanding of this suffering. Being asked thus, monks, you should answer those wanderers of other sects in this way.”

6. Paṭhamaaññatarabhikkhusuttaṃ

6. The First Discourse Concerning a Certain Monk

6. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 3.0007]. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘brahmacariyaṃ, brahmacariya’nti, bhante, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, bhante, brahmacariyaṃ, katamaṃ brahmacariyapariyosāna”nti?

6. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain monk approached the Blessed One, and so on. Having sat down to one side, that monk said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable Sir, it is said, “the holy life, the holy life.” What, Venerable Sir, is the holy life? And what is the culmination of the holy life?’”

“Ayameva kho, bhikkhu, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo brahmacariyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi[V 3.0008][P 5.0008]. Yo kho, bhikkhu, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – idaṃ brahmacariyapariyosāna”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Bhikkhu, this very Noble Eightfold Path is the holy life, that is: right view… right concentration. Bhikkhu, the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion—this is the culmination of the holy life.”

7. Dutiyaaññatarabhikkhusuttaṃ

7. The Second Discourse Concerning a Certain Monk

7. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ [T 5.0010] nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

7. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain monk approached the Blessed One, and so on. Having sat down to one side, that monk said this to the Blessed One:

“‘Rāgavinayo dosavinayo mohavinayo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kissa nu kho etaṃ, bhante, adhivacanaṃ – ‘rāgavinayo dosavinayo mohavinayo’”ti? “Nibbānadhātuyā kho etaṃ, bhikkhu, adhivacanaṃ – ‘rāgavinayo dosavinayo mohavinayo’ti. Āsavānaṃ khayo tena vuccatī”ti.

“‘Venerable Sir, it is said: “the dispelling of lust, the dispelling of hatred, the dispelling of delusion.” For what, Venerable Sir, is this a designation—“the dispelling of lust, the dispelling of hatred, the dispelling of delusion”?’ ‘Bhikkhu, this is a designation for the Nibbāna-element, that is, “the dispelling of lust, the dispelling of hatred, the dispelling of delusion.” The destruction of the taints is thereby meant.’”

Evaṃ vutte so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘amataṃ, amata’nti, bhante, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, bhante, amataṃ, katamo amatagāmimaggo”ti? “Yo kho, bhikkhu, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – idaṃ vuccati amataṃ. Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo amatagāmimaggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

When this was said, that monk said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘the Deathless, the Deathless.’ What, venerable sir, is the Deathless? What is the path leading to the Deathless?” “Monk, whatever is the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion—this is called the Deathless. This very Noble Eightfold Path is the path leading to the Deathless, that is: right view… right concentration.”

8. Vibhaṅgasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Analysis

8. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Ariyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ desessāmi vibhajissāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

8. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, I will teach you and analyze for you the Noble Eightfold Path. Listen to it and attend carefully; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“And what, monks, is the Noble Eightfold Path? It is this: right view… right concentration.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe [M 3.0008] ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ[V 3.0009], dukkhanirodhe [P 5.0009] ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi.

“And what, monks, is right view? Whatever, monks, is the knowledge of suffering, the knowledge of the origin of suffering, the knowledge of the cessation of suffering, the knowledge of the practice leading to the cessation of suffering—this, monks, is called right view.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo? Yo kho, bhikkhave, nekkhammasaṅkappo[T 5.0011], abyāpādasaṅkappo, avihiṃsāsaṅkappo – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo.

“And what, monks, is right thought? Whatever, monks, is the thought of renunciation, the thought of non-ill will, the thought of non-harming—this, monks, is called right thought.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammāvācā? Yā kho, bhikkhave, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāvācā.

“And what, monks, is right speech? Whatever, monks, is the abstinence from false speech, the abstinence from divisive speech, the abstinence from harsh speech, the abstinence from idle chatter—this, monks, is called right speech.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammākammanto? Yā kho, bhikkhave, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, abrahmacariyā veramaṇī – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammākammanto.

“And what, monks, is right action? Whatever, monks, is the abstinence from the destruction of life, the abstinence from taking what is not given, the abstinence from unchastity—this, monks, is called right action.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako micchāājīvaṃ pahāya sammāājīvena jīvitaṃ kappeti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāājīvo.

“And what, monks, is right livelihood? Here, monks, a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, maintains his life by right livelihood—this, monks, is called right livelihood.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāvāyāmo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati, uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti…pe… anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti…pe… uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṃ ārabhati cittaṃ paggaṇhāti padahati – ayaṃ [T 5.0012] vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāvāyāmo.

And what, monks, is right effort? Here, a monk generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; he endeavors, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. He generates desire for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states... he generates desire for the arising of unarisen wholesome states... he generates desire for the stability, non-disappearance, increase, expansion, and fulfillment through cultivation of arisen wholesome states; he endeavors, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives. This, monks, is called right effort.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammāsati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno [P 5.0010] satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati [V 3.0010] ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāsati.

And what, monks, is right mindfulness? Here, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... He dwells contemplating the mind in the mind... He dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. This, monks, is called right mindfulness.

“Katamo [M 3.0009] ca, bhikkhave, sammāsamādhi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno, sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti – ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāsamādhī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

And what, monks, is right concentration? Here, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and has rapture and happiness born of concentration. With the fading away of rapture, he dwells equanimously, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body; he enters and dwells in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: ‘He dwells happily, equanimous and mindful.’ With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. This, monks, is called right concentration.

9. Sūkasuttaṃ

9. The Sutta on the Spike

9. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0013]. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sālisūkaṃ vā yavasūkaṃ vā micchāpaṇihitaṃ hatthena vā pādena vā akkantaṃ hatthaṃ vā pādaṃ vā bhindissati bhecchati (ka.), lohitaṃ vā uppādessatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Micchāpaṇihitattā, bhikkhave, sūkassa. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, so vata bhikkhu micchāpaṇihitāya diṭṭhiyā micchāpaṇihitāya maggabhāvanāya avijjaṃ bhindissati, vijjaṃ uppādessati, nibbānaṃ sacchikarissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Micchāpaṇihitattā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā.

9. At Sāvatthī. Monks, just as it is impossible that a rice awn or a barley awn that is wrongly placed, when trodden upon by hand or by foot, would pierce the hand or the foot and draw blood. For what reason? Because, monks, the awn is wrongly placed. Even so, it is impossible that a monk with a wrongly directed view and a wrongly directed cultivation of the path would pierce ignorance, give rise to knowledge, and realize Nibbāna. For what reason? Because, monks, the view is wrongly directed.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sālisūkaṃ vā yavasūkaṃ vā sammāpaṇihitaṃ hatthena vā pādena vā akkantaṃ hatthaṃ vā pādaṃ vā bhindissati, lohitaṃ vā uppādessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Sammāpaṇihitattā, bhikkhave[P 5.0011], sūkassa. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, so vata bhikkhu sammāpaṇihitāya diṭṭhiyā sammāpaṇihitāya maggabhāvanāya avijjaṃ [V 3.0011] bhindissati, vijjaṃ uppādessati, nibbānaṃ sacchikarissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Sammāpaṇihitattā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā.

Monks, just as it is possible that a rice awn or a barley awn that is rightly placed, when trodden upon by hand or by foot, would pierce the hand or the foot and draw blood. For what reason? Because, monks, the awn is rightly placed. Even so, it is possible that a monk with a rightly directed view and a rightly directed cultivation of the path would pierce ignorance, give rise to knowledge, and realize Nibbāna. For what reason? Because, monks, the view is rightly directed.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammāpaṇihitāya diṭṭhiyā sammāpaṇihitāya maggabhāvanāya avijjaṃ bhindati, vijjaṃ uppādeti, nibbānaṃ sacchikarotīti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ [M 3.0010] vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ [T 5.0014] bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammāpaṇihitāya diṭṭhiyā sammāpaṇihitāya maggabhāvanāya avijjaṃ bhindati, vijjaṃ uppādeti, nibbānaṃ sacchikarotī”ti. Navamaṃ.

And how, monks, does a monk with a rightly directed view and a rightly directed cultivation of the path pierce ignorance, give rise to knowledge, and realize Nibbāna? Here, monks, a monk develops right view that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and matures in relinquishment… he develops right concentration that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and matures in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that a monk with a rightly directed view and a rightly directed cultivation of the path pierces ignorance, gives rise to knowledge, and realizes Nibbāna.

10. Nandiyasuttaṃ

10. The Sutta to Nandiya

10. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho nandiyo paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho nandiyo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kati nu kho, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā nibbānaṅgamā honti nibbānaparāyanā nibbānapariyosānā”ti?

10. At Sāvatthī. Then the wanderer Nandiya approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When he had concluded this courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated thus, the wanderer Nandiya said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Gotama, how many qualities, when developed and cultivated, lead to Nibbāna, have Nibbāna as their destination, and have Nibbāna as their final end?'

“Aṭṭhime kho, nandiya, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā nibbānaṅgamā honti nibbānaparāyanā nibbānapariyosānā. Katame aṭṭha? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ime kho, nandiya, aṭṭha dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā nibbānaṅgamā honti nibbānaparāyanā nibbānapariyosānā”ti. Evaṃ vutte nandiyo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ[V 3.0012], bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama [P 5.0012][T 5.0015] …pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Dasamaṃ.

“Nandiya, these eight qualities, when developed and cultivated, lead to Nibbāna, have Nibbāna as their destination, and have Nibbāna as their final end. What are the eight? They are as follows: right view... right concentration. These eight qualities, Nandiya, when developed and cultivated, lead to Nibbāna, have Nibbāna as their destination, and have Nibbāna as their final end.” When this was said, the wanderer Nandiya said to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable Gotama! Excellent, venerable Gotama! ... May the venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for as long as life lasts, from this day forward.” The tenth.

Avijjāvaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Ignorance.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that is:

Avijjañca upaḍḍhañca, sāriputto ca brāhmaṇo;

Kimatthiyo ca dve bhikkhū, vibhaṅgo sūkanandiyāti.

The Avijjā and Upaḍḍha, Sāriputta and the Brahmin; Kimatthiya and the two Bhikkhus, the Vibhaṅga, Sūka, and Nandiya.

2. Vihāravaggo

2. The Chapter on Abiding

1. Paṭhamavihārasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on Abiding

11. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0016]. “Icchāmahaṃ, bhikkhave, aḍḍhamāsaṃ paṭisalliyituṃ. Namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakenā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti [M 3.0011] kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā nāssudha koci bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamati, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakena.

11. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I wish to go into seclusion for half a month. I am not to be approached by anyone, except for the one who brings my almsfood.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied in assent to the Blessed One, and then no one approached the Blessed One, except for the one who brought his almsfood.

Atha kho bhagavā tassa aḍḍhamāsassa accayena paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito bhikkhū āmantesi – “yena svāhaṃ, bhikkhave, vihārena paṭhamābhisambuddho viharāmi, tassa padesena vihāsiṃ. So evaṃ pajānāmi – ‘micchādiṭṭhipaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; sammādiṭṭhipaccayāpi vedayitaṃ…pe… [V 3.0013] micchāsamādhipaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; sammāsamādhipaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; chandapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; vitakkapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; saññāpaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; chando ca avūpasanto hoti, vitakko ca avūpasanto hoti, saññā ca avūpasantā hoti, tappaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; chando [P 5.0013] ca vūpasanto hoti, vitakko ca vūpasanto hoti, saññā ca vūpasantā hoti, tappaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; appattassa pattiyā atthi āyāmaṃ vāyāmaṃ (sī. syā.), tasmimpi ṭhāne anuppatte tappaccayāpi vedayita’”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

Then, the Blessed One, after the passing of that half-month, having arisen from seclusion, addressed the bhikkhus: ‘Bhikkhus, I dwelt by a portion of that abiding by which I, having first become fully enlightened, dwell. I understood thus: “There is feeling conditioned by wrong view; there is feeling conditioned by right view… there is feeling conditioned by wrong concentration; there is feeling conditioned by right concentration; there is feeling conditioned by desire; there is feeling conditioned by thought; there is feeling conditioned by perception. When desire is unpacified, thought is unpacified, and perception is unpacified, there is feeling conditioned thereby. When desire is pacified, thought is pacified, and perception is pacified, there is feeling conditioned thereby. There is striving for the attainment of the unattained, and when that state has been attained, there is feeling conditioned thereby.”’ The first.

2. Dutiyavihārasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on Abiding

12. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Icchāmahaṃ, bhikkhave, temāsaṃ paṭisalliyituṃ. Namhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakenā”ti[T 5.0017]. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā nāssudha koci bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamati, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakena.

12. At Sāvatthī. ‘Bhikkhus, I wish to go into seclusion for three months. I am not to be approached by anyone, except for the one who brings my almsfood.’ ‘Yes, venerable sir,’ those bhikkhus replied in assent to the Blessed One, and then no one approached the Blessed One, except for the one who brought his almsfood.

Atha kho bhagavā tassa temāsassa accayena paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito bhikkhū āmantesi – “yena svāhaṃ, bhikkhave, vihārena paṭhamābhisambuddho viharāmi, tassa padesena vihāsiṃ. So evaṃ pajānāmi – ‘micchādiṭṭhipaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; micchādiṭṭhivūpasamapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; sammādiṭṭhipaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; sammādiṭṭhivūpasamapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ…pe… [V 3.0014] micchāsamādhipaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; micchāsamādhivūpasamapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ, sammāsamādhipaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; sammāsamādhivūpasamapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; chandapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; chandavūpasamapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; vitakkapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; vitakkavūpasamapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; saññāpaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; saññāvūpasamapaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; chando ca avūpasanto hoti, vitakko ca avūpasanto hoti, saññā ca avūpasantā hoti, tappaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; chando [P 5.0014] ca vūpasanto hoti[M 3.0012], vitakko ca vūpasanto hoti, saññā ca vūpasantā hoti, tappaccayāpi vedayitaṃ; appattassa pattiyā atthi āyāmaṃ vāyāmaṃ (sī. syā.), tasmimpi ṭhāne anuppatte tappaccayāpi vedayita’”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

Then, the Blessed One, after the passing of those three months, having arisen from seclusion, addressed the bhikkhus: ‘Bhikkhus, I dwelt by a portion of that abiding by which I, having first become fully enlightened, dwell. I understood thus: “There is feeling conditioned by wrong view; there is feeling conditioned by the stilling of wrong view; there is feeling conditioned by right view; there is feeling conditioned by the stilling of right view… there is feeling conditioned by wrong concentration; there is feeling conditioned by the stilling of wrong concentration; there is feeling conditioned by right concentration; there is feeling conditioned by the stilling of right concentration; there is feeling conditioned by desire; there is feeling conditioned by the stilling of desire; there is feeling conditioned by thought; there is feeling conditioned by the stilling of thought; there is feeling conditioned by perception; there is feeling conditioned by the stilling of perception. When desire is unpacified, thought is unpacified, and perception is unpacified, there is feeling conditioned thereby. When desire is pacified, thought is pacified, and perception is pacified, there is feeling conditioned thereby. There is striving for the attainment of the unattained, and when that state has been attained, there is feeling conditioned thereby.”’ The second.

3. Sekkhasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Trainee

13. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [T 5.0018] – “‘sekkho, sekkho’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sekkho hotī”ti?

13. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One... and having sat down to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, it is said, “a trainee, a trainee.” To what extent, venerable sir, is one a trainee?’

“Idha, bhikkhu, sekkhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato hoti…pe… sekkhena sammāsamādhinā samannāgato hoti. Ettāvatā kho, bhikkhu, sekkho hotī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

‘Here, bhikkhu, one is endowed with a trainee's right view... is endowed with a trainee's right concentration. To this extent, bhikkhu, one is a trainee.’ The third.

4. Paṭhamauppādasuttaṃ

4. The First Discourse on Origination

14. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Katame aṭṭha? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

14. At Sāvatthī. ‘Bhikkhus, these eight unarisen qualities, when developed and cultivated, arise only with the appearance of a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One. What are the eight? They are as follows: right view... right concentration. These eight unarisen qualities, Bhikkhus, when developed and cultivated, arise only with the appearance of a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One.’ The fourth.

5. Dutiyauppādasuttaṃ

5. The Second Discourse on Origination

15. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0015]. “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame aṭṭha? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi[P 5.0015]. Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

15. At Sāvatthī. ‘Bhikkhus, these eight unarisen qualities, when developed and cultivated, arise only in the Discipline of the Sugata. What are the eight? They are as follows: right view... right concentration. These eight unarisen qualities, Bhikkhus, when developed and cultivated, arise only in the Discipline of the Sugata.’ The fifth.

6. Paṭhamaparisuddhasuttaṃ

6. The First Discourse on Purity

16. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, dhammā parisuddhā pariyodātā anaṅgaṇā vigatūpakkilesā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Katame aṭṭha? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha dhammā parisuddhā pariyodātā [M 3.0013] anaṅgaṇā vigatūpakkilesā [T 5.0019] anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

16. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, these eight qualities—pure, radiant, stainless, and devoid of corruptions—not having arisen before, arise only with the manifestation of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One. What are the eight? They are: right view... right concentration. These eight qualities, Bhikkhus—pure, radiant, stainless, and devoid of corruptions—not having arisen before, arise only with the manifestation of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.' Sixth.

7. Dutiyaparisuddhasuttaṃ

7. The Second Discourse on Purity

17. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, dhammā parisuddhā pariyodātā anaṅgaṇā vigatūpakkilesā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame aṭṭha? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha dhammā parisuddhā pariyodātā anaṅgaṇā vigatūpakkilesā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

17. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, these eight qualities—pure, radiant, stainless, and devoid of corruptions—not having arisen before, arise only in the Discipline of the Sugata. What are the eight? They are: right view... right concentration. These eight qualities, Bhikkhus—pure, radiant, stainless, and devoid of corruptions—not having arisen before, arise only in the Discipline of the Sugata.' Seventh.

8. Paṭhamakukkuṭārāmasuttaṃ

8. The First Discourse at Kukkuṭārāma

18. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ca ānando āyasmā ca bhaddo pāṭaliputte viharanti kukkuṭārāme. Atha kho āyasmā bhaddo sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ [V 3.0016] kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā bhaddo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca –

18. Thus have I heard. At one time the Venerable Ānanda and the Venerable Bhadda were dwelling at Pāṭaliputta in the Kukkuṭārāma. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Bhadda arose from seclusion and approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Venerable Ānanda. After concluding a courteous and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Bhadda said this to the Venerable Ānanda:

“‘Abrahmacariyaṃ, abrahmacariya’nti, āvuso ānanda, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso, abrahmacariya”nti? “Sādhu [P 5.0016] sādhu, āvuso bhadda! Bhaddako kho te, āvuso bhadda, ummaṅgo, bhaddakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ, kalyāṇī paripucchā. Evañhi tvaṃ, āvuso bhadda, pucchasi – ‘abrahmacariyaṃ, abrahmacariyanti, āvuso ānanda, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso, abrahmacariya’”nti? “Evamāvuso”ti. “Ayameva kho[T 5.0020], āvuso, aṭṭhaṅgiko micchāmaggo abrahmacariyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāsamādhī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“‘The unholy life, the unholy life,’ friend Ānanda, is spoken of. What, friend, is the unholy life?” “Good, good, friend Bhadda! Excellent is your inquiry, friend Bhadda, excellent your discernment, and fine your question. For you ask thus: ‘The unholy life, the unholy life,’ friend Ānanda, is spoken of. What, friend, is the unholy life?’” “Yes, friend.” “This very eightfold wrong path, friend, is the unholy life; that is: wrong view… wrong concentration.” Eighth.

9. Dutiyakukkuṭārāmasuttaṃ

9. The Second Discourse at Kukkuṭārāma

19. Pāṭaliputtanidānaṃ. “‘Brahmacariyaṃ, brahmacariya’nti, āvuso ānanda, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso, brahmacariyaṃ, katamaṃ brahmacariyapariyosāna”nti? “Sādhu sādhu, āvuso bhadda! Bhaddako kho te, āvuso bhadda, ummaṅgo, bhaddakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ, kalyāṇī paripucchā. Evañhi tvaṃ, āvuso bhadda, pucchasi – ‘brahmacariyaṃ, brahmacariyanti, āvuso ānanda, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso[M 3.0014], brahmacariyaṃ, katamaṃ brahmacariyapariyosāna’”nti? “Evamāvuso”ti. “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo brahmacariyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Yo kho, āvuso, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – idaṃ brahmacariyapariyosāna”nti. Navamaṃ.

19. At Pāṭaliputta. “'The holy life, the holy life,' friend Ānanda, is spoken of. What, friend, is the holy life, and what is the culmination of the holy life?” “Good, good, friend Bhadda! Excellent is your inquiry, friend Bhadda, excellent your discernment, and fine your question. For you ask thus: ‘The holy life, the holy life,’ friend Ānanda, is spoken of. What, friend, is the holy life, and what is the culmination of the holy life?’” “Yes, friend.” “This very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, is the holy life; that is: right view... right concentration. The destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion—this, friend, is the culmination of the holy life.” Ninth.

10. Tatiyakukkuṭārāmasuttaṃ

10. The Third Discourse at Kukkuṭārāma

20. Pāṭaliputtanidānaṃ. “‘Brahmacariyaṃ, brahmacariya’nti, āvuso ānanda, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso, brahmacariyaṃ, katamo brahmacārī, katamaṃ brahmacariyapariyosāna”nti? “Sādhu [P 5.0017] sādhu, āvuso bhadda! Bhaddako kho te, āvuso bhadda, ummaṅgo, bhaddakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ, kalyāṇī paripucchā. Evañhi tvaṃ, āvuso bhadda, pucchasi – ‘brahmacariyaṃ, brahmacariyanti, āvuso [V 3.0017] ānanda, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho, āvuso, brahmacariyaṃ, katamo brahmacārī, katamaṃ brahmacariyapariyosāna’”nti? “Evamāvuso”ti. “Ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko [T 5.0021] maggo brahmacariyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Yo kho, āvuso, iminā ariyena aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena samannāgato – ayaṃ vuccati brahmacārī. Yo kho, āvuso, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – idaṃ brahmacariyapariyosāna”nti. Dasamaṃ.

20. At Pāṭaliputta. “'The holy life, the holy life,' friend Ānanda, is spoken of. What, friend, is the holy life, who is the practitioner of the holy life, and what is the culmination of the holy life?” “Good, good, friend Bhadda! Excellent is your inquiry, friend Bhadda, excellent your discernment, and fine your question. For you ask thus: ‘The holy life, the holy life,’ friend Ānanda, is spoken of. What, friend, is the holy life, who is the practitioner of the holy life, and what is the culmination of the holy life?’” “Yes, friend.” “This very Noble Eightfold Path, friend, is the holy life; that is: right view... right concentration. One who, friend, is endowed with this Noble Eightfold Path—this one is called a practitioner of the holy life. The destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion—this, friend, is the culmination of the holy life.” Tenth.

Tīṇi suttantāni ekanidānāni.Vihāravaggo dutiyo.

Three discourses with a single origin. The Chapter on Abidings, the Second.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for it is:

Dve vihārā ca sekkho ca, uppādā apare duve;

Parisuddhena dve vuttā, kukkuṭārāmena tayoti.

Two on Abiding and one on the Trainee, and two others on Arising; two are spoken of with ‘Purified,’ and three with ‘Kukkuṭārāma.’”

3. Micchattavaggo

3. The Chapter on Wrongness

1. Micchattasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Wrongness

21. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0022]. “Micchattañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, sammattañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca[P 5.0018], bhikkhave, micchattaṃ? Seyyathidaṃ – micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāsamādhi[M 3.0015]. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, micchattaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, sammattaṃ? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammatta”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

21. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you wrongness and rightness. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is wrongness? It is this: wrong view… wrong concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called wrongness. And what, bhikkhus, is rightness? It is this: right view… right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called rightness.' First.

2. Akusaladhammasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Unwholesome States

22. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Akusale ca kho, bhikkhave, dhamme desessāmi, kusale ca dhamme. Taṃ suṇātha. Katame ca, bhikkhave, akusalā dhammā? Seyyathidaṃ – micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāsamādhi. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, akusalā dhammā. Katame ca, bhikkhave, kusalā dhammā[V 3.0018]? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, kusalā dhammā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

22. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you unwholesome states and wholesome states. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, are unwholesome states? They are these: wrong view… wrong concentration. These, bhikkhus, are called unwholesome states. And what, bhikkhus, are wholesome states? They are these: right view… right concentration. These, bhikkhus, are called wholesome states.' Second.

3. Paṭhamapaṭipadāsuttaṃ

3. The First Discourse on Practice

23. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Micchāpaṭipadañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, sammāpaṭipadañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipadā? Seyyathidaṃ – micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipadā. Katamā [T 5.0023] ca, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipadā? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipadā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

23. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you wrong practice and right practice. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is wrong practice? It is this: wrong view… wrong concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called wrong practice. And what, bhikkhus, is right practice? It is this: right view… right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called right practice.” The third.

4. Dutiyapaṭipadāsuttaṃ

4. The Second Discourse on Practice

24. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Gihino vāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pabbajitassa vā micchāpaṭipadaṃ na vaṇṇemi. Gihi vā, bhikkhave, pabbajito vā micchāpaṭipanno micchāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu [P 5.0019] nārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ”.

24. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I do not praise wrong practice, whether of a householder or of one who has gone forth. A householder or one who has gone forth, bhikkhus, who practices wrongly, on account of wrong practice, does not accomplish the wholesome Dhamma, the Noble Path.”

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipadā? Seyyathidaṃ – micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipadā. Gihino vāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pabbajitassa vā micchāpaṭipadaṃ na vaṇṇemi. Gihi vā, bhikkhave, pabbajito vā micchāpaṭipanno micchāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu nārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is wrong practice? It is this: wrong view… wrong concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called wrong practice. Bhikkhus, I do not praise wrong practice, whether of a householder or of one who has gone forth. A householder or one who has gone forth, bhikkhus, who practices wrongly, on account of wrong practice, does not accomplish the wholesome Dhamma, the Noble Path.”

“Gihino vāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pabbajitassa vā sammāpaṭipadaṃ vaṇṇemi. Gihi vā, bhikkhave, pabbajito vā sammāpaṭipanno sammāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusalaṃ. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipadā? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipadā. Gihino vāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pabbajitassa vā sammāpaṭipadaṃ vaṇṇemi. Gihi vā, bhikkhave[M 3.0016], pabbajito vā sammāpaṭipanno sammāpaṭipattādhikaraṇahetu ārādhako hoti ñāyaṃ dhammaṃ kusala”nti. Catutthaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I praise right practice, whether of a householder or of one who has gone forth. A householder or one who has gone forth, bhikkhus, who practices rightly, on account of right practice, accomplishes the wholesome Dhamma, the Noble Path. And what, bhikkhus, is right practice? It is this: right view… right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called right practice. Bhikkhus, I praise right practice, whether of a householder or of one who has gone forth. A householder or one who has gone forth, bhikkhus, who practices rightly, on account of right practice, accomplishes the wholesome Dhamma, the Noble Path.” The fourth.

5. Paṭhamaasappurisasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on the Unworthy Person

25. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0019]. “Asappurisañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, sappurisañca[T 5.0024]. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, asappuriso? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvāco, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asappuriso”.

25. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unworthy person and the worthy person. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is an unworthy person? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person has wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, and wrong concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called an unworthy person.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sappuriso? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvāco, sammākammanto[P 5.0020], sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sappuriso”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is a worthy person? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person has right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called a worthy person.” The fifth.

6. Dutiyaasappurisasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on the Unworthy Person

26. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Asappurisañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, asappurisena asappurisatarañca. Sappurisañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi sappurisena sappurisatarañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, asappuriso? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchādiṭṭhiko hoti…pe… micchāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asappuriso”.

26. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unworthy person and the one who is more unworthy than the unworthy person. And I will teach you the worthy person and the one who is more worthy than the worthy person. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the unworthy person? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person has wrong view… wrong concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called the unworthy person.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, asappurisena asappurisataro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchādiṭṭhiko hoti…pe… micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇī, micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asappurisena asappurisataro.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the one who is more unworthy than the unworthy person? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person has wrong view… wrong concentration, wrong knowledge, and wrong liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the one who is more unworthy than the unworthy person.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sappuriso? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammādiṭṭhiko [T 5.0025] hoti…pe… sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sappuriso.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the worthy person? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person has right view… right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called the worthy person.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sappurisena sappurisataro? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammādiṭṭhiko hoti…pe… sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇī, sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sappurisena sappurisataro”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the one who is more worthy than the worthy person? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person has right view… right concentration, right knowledge, and right liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the one who is more worthy than the worthy person.” The sixth.

7. Kumbhasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Pot

27. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 3.0017][V 3.0020]. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kumbho anādhāro suppavattiyo hoti, sādhāro duppavattiyo hoti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, cittaṃ anādhāraṃ suppavattiyaṃ hoti, sādhāraṃ duppavattiyaṃ hoti. Ko [P 5.0021] ca, bhikkhave, cittassa ādhāro? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ cittassa ādhāro. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kumbho anādhāro suppavattiyo hoti, sādhāro duppavattiyo hoti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, cittaṃ anādhāraṃ suppavattiyaṃ hoti, sādhāraṃ duppavattiyaṃ hotī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

27. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, just as a pot without a support is easy to turn over, while one with a support is difficult to turn over; even so, bhikkhus, the mind without a support is easy to turn over, while the mind with a support is difficult to turn over. And what, bhikkhus, is the support for the mind? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view… right concentration. This is the support for the mind. Just as a pot without a support is easy to turn over, while one with a support is difficult to turn over; even so, bhikkhus, the mind without a support is easy to turn over, while the mind with a support is difficult to turn over.” The seventh.

8. Samādhisuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Concentration

28. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Ariyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, sammāsamādhiṃ desessāmi saupanisaṃ saparikkhāraṃ. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, ariyo sammāsamādhi saupaniso saparikkhāro? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsati sammāsamādhi (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.). Yā [T 5.0026] kho, bhikkhave, imehi sattahaṅgehi cittassa ekaggatā saparikkhāratā saparikkhatā (sī. pī.) – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyo sammāsamādhi saupaniso itipi saparikkhāro itipī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

28. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the noble right concentration that is with its requisites and with its accessories. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the noble right concentration that is with its requisites and with its accessories? It is this: right view… right mindfulness. Whatever one-pointedness of mind is equipped with these seven factors—this, bhikkhus, is called the noble right concentration that is with its requisites and also with its accessories.” The eighth.

9. Vedanāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Feeling

29. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Tisso imā, bhikkhave, vedanā. Katamā tisso? Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso vedanā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi[P 5.0022]. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Navamaṃ.

29. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these three feelings. What three? Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These, bhikkhus, are the three feelings. For the full understanding of these three feelings, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? It is this: right view… right concentration. For the full understanding of these three feelings, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.”

10. Uttiyasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse to Uttiya

30. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0021]. Atha kho āyasmā uttiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā uttiyo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha mayhaṃ, bhante, rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko [M 3.0018] udapādi – ‘pañca kāmaguṇā vuttā bhagavatā. Katame nu kho pañca kāmaguṇā vuttā bhagavatā’”ti? “Sādhu sādhu, uttiya! Pañcime kho, uttiya, kāmaguṇā vuttā mayā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā… jivhāviññeyyā rasā… kāyaviññeyyā [T 5.0027] phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, uttiya, pañca kāmaguṇā vuttā mayā. Imesaṃ kho, uttiya, pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ pahānāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Imesaṃ kho, uttiya, pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ pahānāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

30. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Uttiya approached the Blessed One… and said to him while seated to one side: “Venerable sir, while I was alone in seclusion, this thought arose in my mind: ‘The Blessed One has spoken of the five strands of sensual pleasure. What are the five strands of sensual pleasure spoken of by the Blessed One?’” “Good, good, Uttiya! These five strands of sensual pleasure have been spoken of by me. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, charming, of a lovely nature, connected with sensual pleasure, and arousing passion; sounds cognizable by the ear… odors cognizable by the nose… flavors cognizable by the tongue… tangibles cognizable by the body that are desirable, agreeable, charming, of a lovely nature, connected with sensual pleasure, and arousing passion. These, Uttiya, are the five strands of sensual pleasure spoken of by me. For the abandoning of these five strands of sensual pleasure, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? It is right view… right concentration. For the abandoning of these five strands of sensual pleasure, this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.”

Micchattavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on Wrongness, the Third.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Micchattaṃ akusalaṃ dhammaṃ, duve paṭipadāpi ca;

Asappurisena dve kumbho, samādhi vedanuttiyenāti.

Wrongness, Unwholesome States, and two on Practice; two with an Unworthy Person, the Pot, Concentration, Feeling, and Uttiya.

4. Paṭipattivaggo

4. 4. The Chapter on Practice

1. Paṭhamapaṭipattisuttaṃ

1. 1. The First Discourse on Practice

31. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0028][P 5.0023]. “Micchāpaṭipattiñca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, sammāpaṭipattiñca[V 3.0022]. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipatti? Seyyathidaṃ – micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipatti. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipatti? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipattī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

31. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you wrong practice and right practice. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is wrong practice? It is: wrong view… wrong concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called wrong practice. And what, bhikkhus, is right practice? It is: right view… right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called right practice.”

2. Dutiyapaṭipattisuttaṃ

2. 2. The Second Discourse on Practice

32. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Micchāpaṭipannañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, sammāpaṭipannañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, micchāpaṭipanno? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco micchādiṭṭhiko hoti…pe… micchāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave[M 3.0019], micchāpaṭipanno. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipanno? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco sammādiṭṭhiko hoti…pe… sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammāpaṭipanno”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

32. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the one who practices wrongly and the one who practices rightly. Listen to that. And who, bhikkhus, is the one who practices wrongly? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person has wrong view… wrong concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called the one who practices wrongly. And who, bhikkhus, is the one who practices rightly? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person has right view… right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called the one who practices rightly.”

3. Viraddhasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on What is Neglected

33. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo viraddho, viraddho tesaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī. Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo āraddho, āraddho tesaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī. Katamo [P 5.0024][T 5.0029] ca, bhikkhave, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo viraddho, viraddho tesaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī. Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo āraddho, āraddho tesaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

33. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, for whomever the Noble Eightfold Path is neglected, for them the Noble Eightfold Path that rightly leads to the destruction of suffering is neglected. For whomever, bhikkhus, the Noble Eightfold Path is undertaken, for them the Noble Eightfold Path that rightly leads to the destruction of suffering is undertaken. And what, bhikkhus, is the Noble Eightfold Path? It is this: right view… right concentration. For whomever, bhikkhus, this Noble Eightfold Path is neglected, for them the Noble Eightfold Path that rightly leads to the destruction of suffering is neglected. For whomever, bhikkhus, this Noble Eightfold Path is undertaken, for them the Noble Eightfold Path that rightly leads to the destruction of suffering is undertaken.”

4. Pāraṅgamasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Going to the Far Shore

34. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya [V 3.0023] saṃvattanti. Katame aṭṭha? Seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ime kho, bhikkhave, aṭṭha dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattantī”ti.

34. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, these eight things, when developed and cultivated, conduce to going from the near shore to the far shore. What eight? It is this: right view… right concentration. These eight things, bhikkhus, when developed and cultivated, conduce to going from the near shore to the far shore.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, then said further:

“Appakā te manussesu, ye janā pāragāmino;

Athāyaṃ itarā pajā, tīramevānudhāvati.

“Few are they among humans, the people who go to the far shore; but this other populace just runs along this shore.”

“Ye ca kho sammadakkhāte, dhamme dhammānuvattino;

Te janā pāramessanti, maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ.

“Indeed, those who live in accordance with the well-expounded Dhamma—those people will cross over the realm of Death, so difficult to cross, and reach the further shore.”

“Kaṇhaṃ dhammaṃ vippahāya, sukkaṃ bhāvetha paṇḍito;

Okā anokamāgamma, viveke yattha dūramaṃ.

“The wise person, having abandoned dark states, should cultivate bright states. Having gone from the home to the homeless state, into that seclusion where it is difficult to find delight.”

“Tatrābhiratimiccheyya, hitvā kāme akiñcano;

Pariyodapeyya attānaṃ, cittaklesehi paṇḍito.

“Therein, one should desire great delight. The wise person, having abandoned sensual pleasures and being without impediments, should thoroughly cleanse themselves from the defilements of the mind.”

“Yesaṃ [M 3.0020][T 5.0030] sambodhiyaṅgesu, sammā cittaṃ subhāvitaṃ;

Ādānapaṭinissagge, anupādāya ye ratā;

Khīṇāsavā jutimanto, te loke parinibbutā”ti. catutthaṃ;

“Those for whom the mind is well-developed in the factors of enlightenment, who delight in the relinquishing of grasping, being without clinging—they whose taints are destroyed, who are radiant, they are fully extinguished in this world.”

5. Paṭhamasāmaññasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on the State of a Recluse

35. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[P 5.0025]. “Sāmaññañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, sāmaññaphalāni ca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, sāmaññaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sāmaññaṃ. Katamāni ca, bhikkhave, sāmaññaphalāni? Sotāpattiphalaṃ, sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, anāgāmiphalaṃ, arahattaphalaṃ – imāni vuccanti, bhikkhave, sāmaññaphalānī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

35. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you recluseship and the fruits of recluseship. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is recluseship? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view... right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called recluseship. And what, bhikkhus, are the fruits of recluseship? The fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arahantship. These, bhikkhus, are called the fruits of recluseship.' The Fifth.

6. Dutiyasāmaññasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Recluseship

36. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0024]. “Sāmaññañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, sāmaññatthañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca kho, bhikkhave, sāmaññaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sāmaññaṃ. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sāmaññattho? Yo kho, bhikkhave, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sāmaññattho”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

36. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you recluseship and the goal of recluseship. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is recluseship? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view... right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called recluseship. And what, bhikkhus, is the goal of recluseship? It is the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion. This, bhikkhus, is called the goal of recluseship.' The Sixth.

7. Paṭhamabrahmaññasuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse on Brahminhood

37. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Brahmaññañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, brahmaññaphalāni ca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca kho, bhikkhave, brahmaññaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, brahmaññaṃ. Katamāni ca, bhikkhave, brahmaññaphalāni[T 5.0031]? Sotāpattiphalaṃ[P 5.0026], sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, anāgāmiphalaṃ, arahattaphalaṃ – imāni vuccanti, bhikkhave, brahmaññaphalānī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

37. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you brahminhood and the fruits of brahminhood. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is brahminhood? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view... right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called brahminhood. And what, bhikkhus, are the fruits of brahminhood? The fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arahantship. These, bhikkhus, are called the fruits of brahminhood.' The Seventh.

8. Dutiyabrahmaññasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse on Brahminhood

38. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Brahmaññañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, brahmaññatthañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, brahmaññaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, brahmaññaṃ. Katamo [M 3.0021] ca, bhikkhave, brahmaññattho? Yo kho, bhikkhave, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, brahmaññattho”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

38. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you brahminhood and the goal of brahminhood. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is brahminhood? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view... right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called brahminhood. And what, bhikkhus, is the goal of brahminhood? It is the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion. This, bhikkhus, is called the goal of brahminhood.' The Eighth.

9. Paṭhamabrahmacariyasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on the Holy Life

39. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Brahmacariyañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, brahmacariyaphalāni ca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ [V 3.0025] – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṃ. Katamāni [T 5.0032] ca, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaphalāni? Sotāpattiphalaṃ, sakadāgāmiphalaṃ, anāgāmiphalaṃ, arahattaphalaṃ – imāni vuccanti, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaphalānī”ti. Navamaṃ.

39. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you the holy life and the fruits of the holy life. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the holy life? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view... right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called the holy life. And what, bhikkhus, are the fruits of the holy life? The fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arahantship. These, bhikkhus, are called the fruits of the holy life.' The Ninth.

10. Dutiyabrahmacariyasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on the Holy Life

40. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Brahmacariyañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi, brahmacariyatthañca. Taṃ suṇātha. Katamañca, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṃ. Katamo [P 5.0027] ca, bhikkhave, brahmacariyattho? Yo kho, bhikkhave, rāgakkhayo dosakkhayo mohakkhayo – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, brahmacariyattho”ti. Dasamaṃ.

40. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, I will teach you the holy life and the goal of the holy life. Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the holy life? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view... right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called the holy life. And what, bhikkhus, is the goal of the holy life? It is the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion. This, bhikkhus, is called the goal of the holy life.' The Tenth.

Paṭipattivaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter on Practice.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Paṭipatti paṭipanno ca, viraddhañca pāraṃgamā;

Sāmaññena ca dve vuttā, brahmaññā apare duve;

Brahmacariyena dve vuttā, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

Practice and the practitioner, the one who has strayed and the one gone beyond; two are taught concerning recluseship, and another two concerning brahminhood; two are taught concerning the holy life—for this reason, it is called a chapter.

5. Aññatitthiyapeyyālavaggo

5. The Chapter of the Repetition Series on Adherents of Other Sects

1. Rāgavirāgasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Dispassion for Lust

41. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0033]. “Sace vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kimatthiyaṃ, āvuso, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti, evaṃ [M 3.0022] puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘rāgavirāgatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti. Sace pana vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā [V 3.0026] evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘atthi panāvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā rāgavirāgāyā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘atthi kho, āvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā rāgavirāgāyā’ti. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, maggo, katamā ca paṭipadā rāgavirāgāya[P 5.0028]? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo, ayaṃ paṭipadā rāgavirāgāyāti. Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyāthā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

41. At Sāvatthī. 'Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects should ask you thus: “For what purpose, friends, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?”—being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: “It is for the purpose of dispassion for lust, friends, that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.” If those wanderers of other sects should ask you thus: “But is there a path, friends, is there a practice for dispassion for lust?”—being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: “There is a path, friends, there is a practice for dispassion for lust.” And what, bhikkhus, is the path, and what is the practice for dispassion for lust? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view... right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is the path, this is the practice for dispassion for lust. Being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus.' The First.

2-7. Saṃyojanappahānādisuttachakkaṃ

2–7. The Six Discourses on the Abandoning of Fetters, and so forth

42-47. “Sace vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kimatthiyaṃ, āvuso, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ [T 5.0034] paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘saṃyojanappahānatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti…pe… ‘anusayasamugghātanatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti…pe… ‘addhānapariññatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti…pe… ‘āsavānaṃ khayatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti…pe… ‘vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti…pe… ‘ñāṇadassanatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti…pe…. Sattamaṃ.
