42–47. “Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects were to ask you: ‘For what purpose, friends, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?’—being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: ‘For the abandonment of fetters, friends, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’… ‘For the uprooting of latent tendencies, friends, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’… ‘For the full understanding of the long course, friends, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’… ‘For the destruction of the taints, friends, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’… ‘For the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation, friends, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’… ‘For knowledge and vision, friends, the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’… The seventh.

8. Anupādāparinibbānasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Final Nibbāna Without Clinging

48. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Sace [P 5.0029] vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kimatthiyaṃ, āvuso, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘anupādāparinibbānatthaṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī’ti. Sace pana vo, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘atthi panāvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā anupādāparinibbānāyā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ [T 5.0035] paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha [M 3.0023] – ‘atthi kho, āvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā anupādāparinibbānāyā’ti[V 3.0027]. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, maggo, katamā ca paṭipadā anupādāparinibbānāya? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, maggo, ayaṃ paṭipadā anupādāparinibbānāyāti. Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyāthā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

48. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects were to ask you: ‘For what purpose, friends, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?’—being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: ‘It is for the purpose of final Nibbāna without clinging, friends, that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.’ If, bhikkhus, those wanderers of other sects were to ask you: ‘But is there, friends, a path, is there a practice for final Nibbāna without clinging?’—being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: ‘There is, friends, a path, there is a practice for final Nibbāna without clinging.’ And what, bhikkhus, is that path, what is that practice for final Nibbāna without clinging? It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view… right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is the path, this is the practice for final Nibbāna without clinging.’ Being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers of other sects in this way.” The eighth.

Aññatitthiyapeyyālavaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter: The Repetition Series on Other Sectarians.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Virāgasaṃyojanaṃ anusayaṃ, addhānaṃ āsavā khayā;

Vijjāvimuttiñāṇañca, anupādāya aṭṭhamī.

Dispassion, Fetter, Latent Tendency, The Long Course, Destruction of Taints; Knowledge-and-Liberation and Knowledge-and-Vision, and Without Clinging is the eighth.

6. Sūriyapeyyālavaggo

6. The Sixth Chapter: The Repetition Series on the Sun

1. Kalyāṇamittasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Good Friend

49. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0036]. “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – aruṇuggaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave[P 5.0030], bhikkhuno ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā. Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… [V 3.0028] sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

49. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, just as the dawn is the forerunner, the precursor, of the sunrise, so too, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, good friendship is the forerunner, the precursor, for the arising of the Noble Eightfold Path. For a bhikkhu with a good friend, bhikkhus, it is to be expected that he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path, that he will cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu with a good friend develop the Noble Eightfold Path, cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu with a good friend develops the Noble Eightfold Path, cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.” The first.

2-6. Sīlasampadādisuttapañcakaṃ

2-6. Five Discourses beginning with the Accomplishment of Virtue.

50-54. “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – aruṇuggaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya [M 3.0024] etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – sīlasampadā. Sīlasampannassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ… yadidaṃ [T 5.0037] – chandasampadā… yadidaṃ – attasampadā… yadidaṃ – diṭṭhisampadā… yadidaṃ – appamādasampadā…. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

50-54. “Bhikkhus, just as the dawn is the forerunner and precursor of the sunrise, so too, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, the accomplishment of virtue is the forerunner and precursor for the arising of the Noble Eightfold Path. For a bhikkhu accomplished in virtue, bhikkhus, it is to be expected that he will develop and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path. The same is said for the accomplishment of aspiration, the accomplishment of self, the accomplishment of view, and the accomplishment of heedfulness.” The sixth.

7. Yonisomanasikārasampadāsuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Accomplishment of Wise Attention

55. “Sūriyassa[P 5.0031], bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – aruṇuggaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimmittaṃ, yadidaṃ – yonisomanasikārasampadā. Yonisomanasikārasampannassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

55. “Bhikkhus, for the rising sun, this is the forerunner and precursor, namely, the dawn. So too, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, for the arising of the Noble Eightfold Path, this is the forerunner and precursor, namely, the accomplishment of wise attention. For a bhikkhu who is accomplished in wise attention, bhikkhus, this is to be expected: he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path, he will cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu accomplished in wise attention develop the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and which culminates in relinquishment… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and which culminates in relinquishment. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu accomplished in wise attention develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.” The seventh.

1. Kalyāṇamittasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Good Friend

56. “Sūriyassa[V 3.0029], bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – aruṇuggaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ[T 5.0038], yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā. 56. “Bhikkhus, just as the dawn is the forerunner and precursor of the rising sun, so too, for a bhikkhu, this is the forerunner and precursor for the arising of the Noble Eightfold Path, that is, good friendship. For a bhikkhu who has a good friend, bhikkhus, it is to be expected that he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path and practice it frequently. Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which has the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, and the removal of delusion as its culmination… he develops right concentration, which has the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, and the removal of delusion as its culmination. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu who has a good friend develops the Noble Eightfold Path and practices it frequently.” First.

The Sun Series Chapter, the Sixth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this:

Kalyāṇamittaṃ sīlañca, chando ca attasampadā;

Diṭṭhi ca appamādo ca, yoniso bhavati sattamaṃ.

Good friendship, virtue, and aspiration; personal accomplishment, view, and heedfulness, with wise attention as the seventh.

2-6. Sīlasampadādisuttapañcakaṃ

2-6. Five Discourses beginning with the Accomplishment of Virtue

71-75. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Ekadhammo, bhikkhave, bahūpakāro ariyassa aṭṭhaṅgikassa maggassa uppādāya. Katamo ekadhammo? Yadidaṃ – sīlasampadā…pe… yadidaṃ – chandasampadā…pe… yadidaṃ – attasampadā…pe… yadidaṃ – diṭṭhisampadā…pe… yadidaṃ [P 5.0035] – appamādasampadā…pe…. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

71-75. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, one thing is of great assistance for the arising of the Noble Eightfold Path. What is that one thing? It is the accomplishment in virtue… it is the accomplishment in wholesome desire… it is the accomplishment in mind… it is the accomplishment in view… it is the accomplishment in heedfulness….” Sixth.

7. Yonisomanasikārasampadāsuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Accomplishment in Wise Attention

76. “Yadidaṃ – yonisomanasikārasampadā. Yonisomanasikārasampannassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

76. “It is the accomplishment in wise attention. For a bhikkhu accomplished in wise attention, bhikkhus, it is to be expected that he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path, that he will cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu accomplished in wise attention develop the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops Right View… he develops Right Concentration which has the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, and the removal of delusion as its culmination. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu accomplished in wise attention develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.” Seventh.

Ekadhammapeyyālavaggo sattamo.

The Repetition Series on a Single Thing, the Seventh Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Kalyāṇamittaṃ [T 5.0043] sīlañca, chando ca attasampadā;

Diṭṭhi ca appamādo ca, yoniso bhavati sattamaṃ.

Good friendship, virtue, and wholesome desire, accomplishment in mind; view and heedfulness, and wise attention is the seventh.

77. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0044][V 3.0033][M 3.0028]. “Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi, yena anuppanno vā ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo uppajjati, uppanno vā ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati, yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, kalyāṇamittatā. Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha[P 5.0036], bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

77. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I do not see any other single thing on account of which the unarisen Noble Eightfold Path arises and the arisen Noble Eightfold Path goes to the fulfillment of its development, as this: good friendship. For a bhikkhu with good friends, bhikkhus, it is to be expected that he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path, that he will cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu with good friends develop the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops Right View based on seclusion… he develops Right Concentration based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu with good friends develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.” First.

1. Gaṅgāpeyyālavaggo

1. The Chapter of the Repetition Series on the Ganges

1. Paṭhamapācīnaninnasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on Leaning to the East

91. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0048]. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Kathañca, bhikkhave[V 3.0036], bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

91. At Sāvatthī. “Just as, bhikkhus, the Ganges river leans eastward, slopes eastward, and inclines eastward; so too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates it leans towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and inclines towards Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu who develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates it lean towards Nibbāna, slope towards Nibbāna, and incline towards Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, culminating in relinquishment… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu who develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates it leans towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and inclines towards Nibbāna.” First.

2-5. Dutiyādipācīnaninnasuttacatukkaṃ

2-5. The Group of Four Discourses on Leaning Eastward, Beginning with the Second

92-95. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yamunā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… seyyathāpi[P 5.0039], bhikkhave, aciravatī nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sarabhū nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… seyyathāpi[T 5.0049], bhikkhave, mahī nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe…. Pañcamaṃ.

“Just as, bhikkhus, the Yamunā river leans eastward, slopes eastward, and inclines eastward; so too, bhikkhus… and so on… Just as, bhikkhus, the Aciravatī river leans eastward, slopes eastward, and inclines eastward; so too, bhikkhus… and so on… Just as, bhikkhus, the Sarabhū river leans eastward, slopes eastward, and inclines eastward; so too, bhikkhus… and so on… Just as, bhikkhus, the Mahī river leans eastward, slopes eastward, and inclines eastward; so too, bhikkhus… and so on…” Fifth.

6. The Sixth Discourse on Leaning Eastward

96. “Seyyathāpi[M 3.0031], bhikkhave, yā kācimā mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, sabbā tā pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ [T 5.0050] aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. 96. “Bhikkhus, just as all these great rivers—namely, the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—incline towards the east, slope towards the east, and tend towards the east; even so, a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path incline towards Nibbāna, slope towards Nibbāna, and tend towards Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna.” Sixth.

Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ [V 3.0038] maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

98–102. “Just as, bhikkhus, the Yamunā river inclines towards the ocean, slopes towards the ocean, and tends towards the ocean; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu… Just as, bhikkhus, the Aciravatī river inclines towards the ocean, slopes towards the ocean, and tends towards the ocean; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu… Just as, bhikkhus, the Sarabhū river inclines towards the ocean, slopes towards the ocean, and tends towards the ocean; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu… Just as, bhikkhus, the Mahī river inclines towards the ocean, slopes towards the ocean, and tends towards the ocean; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu… Just as, bhikkhus, whatever great rivers there are, namely, the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—all of them incline towards the ocean, slope towards the ocean, and tend towards the ocean; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu developing and cultivating the Noble Eightfold Path inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu developing and cultivating the Noble Eightfold Path incline towards Nibbāna, slope towards Nibbāna, and tend towards Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu developing and cultivating the Noble Eightfold Path inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna.” Sixth.

Gaṅgāpeyyālavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Ganges Repetition Series Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Cha pācīnato ninnā, cha ninnā ca samuddato;

Ete dve cha dvādasa honti, vaggo tena pavuccatīti;

Gaṅgāpeyyālī pācīnaninnavācanamaggī, vivekanissitaṃ dvādasakī paṭhamakī.

Six inclining eastwards, and six inclining towards the ocean; these two sixes become twelve, therefore the chapter is so called. The Ganges Repetition Series is the sequence of recitation on inclining eastwards; the first twelvefold section is based on seclusion.

The Third Twelvefold Section on Immersion in the Deathless.

1. Paṭhamapācīnaninnasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on Leaning Eastward

127. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo [T 5.0058] nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

127. “Just as, bhikkhus, the River Gaṅgā inclines to the east, slopes to the east, and tends to the east; even so, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu developing and cultivating the Noble Eightfold Path inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu developing and cultivating the Noble Eightfold Path incline towards Nibbāna, slope towards Nibbāna, and tend towards Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view that inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna… he develops right concentration that inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu developing and cultivating the Noble Eightfold Path inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna.” First.

2-6. Dutiyādipācīnaninnasuttapañcakaṃ

2-6. The Pentad of Discourses Beginning with the Second, on Leaning Eastward.

128-132. “Seyyathāpi[V 3.0047], bhikkhave, yamunā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, aciravatī nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sarabhū nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahī nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā [M 3.0037] pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yā kācimā mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, sabbā tā pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo [T 5.0059] nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

128-132. 'Just as, bhikkhus, the river Yamunā slopes to the east, slants to the east, and tends to the east; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu... Just as, bhikkhus, the river Aciravatī slopes to the east, slants to the east, and tends to the east; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu... Just as, bhikkhus, the river Sarabhū slopes to the east, slants to the east, and tends to the east; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu... Just as, bhikkhus, the river Mahī slopes to the east, slants to the east, and tends to the east; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu... Just as, bhikkhus, whatever great rivers there are, namely, the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī, all of them slope to the east, slant to the east, and tend to the east; in the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and making it much-practiced, slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and making it much-practiced, slope towards Nibbāna, slant towards Nibbāna, and tend towards Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops Right View that slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna... he develops Right Concentration that slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and making it much-practiced, slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna.' Sixth.

1. Paṭhamasamuddaninnasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on Sloping to the Ocean

133. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī samuddaninnā samuddapoṇā samuddapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

133. “Just as, bhikkhus, the river Ganges slopes towards the ocean, slants towards the ocean, and tends towards the ocean; even so, a bhikkhu, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and making it much-practiced, slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and making it much-practiced, slope towards Nibbāna, slant towards Nibbāna, and tend towards Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops Right View that slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna... he develops Right Concentration that slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and making it much-practiced, slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna.” First.

2-6. Dutiyādisamuddaninnasuttapañcakaṃ

2-6. The Five Suttas Beginning with the Second on Inclining to the Ocean

134-138. “Seyyathāpi[V 3.0048], bhikkhave, yamunā nadī samuddaninnā samuddapoṇā samuddapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… seyyathāpi[T 5.0060], bhikkhave, aciravatī nadī samuddaninnā samuddapoṇā samuddapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sarabhū nadī samuddaninnā samuddapoṇā samuddapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahī nadī samuddaninnā [M 3.0038] samuddapoṇā samuddapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu…pe… seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yā kācimā mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī sarabhū, mahī, sabbā tā samuddaninnā samuddapoṇā samuddapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

134-138. 'Just as, bhikkhus, the river Yamunā slopes towards the ocean, slants towards the ocean, and tends towards the ocean; even so, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu... Just as, bhikkhus, the river Aciravatī slopes towards the ocean, slants towards the ocean, and tends towards the ocean; even so, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu... Just as, bhikkhus, the river Sarabhū slopes towards the ocean, slants towards the ocean, and tends towards the ocean; even so, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu... Just as, bhikkhus, the river Mahī slopes towards the ocean, slants towards the ocean, and tends towards the ocean; even so, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu... Just as, bhikkhus, whatever great rivers there are, such as these—the Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—all of them slope towards the ocean, slant towards the ocean, and tend towards the ocean; even so, a bhikkhu, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and making it much-practiced, slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and making it much-practiced, slope towards Nibbāna, slant towards Nibbāna, and tend towards Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops Right View that slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna... he develops Right Concentration that slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, by developing the Noble Eightfold Path and making it much-practiced, slopes towards Nibbāna, slants towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna.' Sixth.

(Gaṅgāpeyyālī).

(The Gaṅgā Repetition Series is concluded.)

Dutiyagaṅgāpeyyālavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on the Gaṅgā Repetition Series is the second.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this:

Cha [T 5.0061] pācīnato ninnā, cha ninnā ca samuddato;

Ete dve cha dvādasa honti, vaggo tena pavuccatīti;

Nibbānaninno dvādasakī, catutthakī chaṭṭhā navakī.

Six slope towards the east, and six slope towards the ocean; these two sets of six become twelve, and therefore it is called a chapter. The twelve are about sloping towards Nibbāna; the fourth, the sixth, and the ninth.

5. Appamādapeyyālavaggo

5. 5. The Chapter on the Repetition Series on Heedfulness

1. Tathāgatasuttaṃ

1. 1. The Discourse on the Tathāgata

139. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0062][V 3.0049]. “Yāvatā, bhikkhave, sattā apadā vā dvipadā dipadā (sī.) vā catuppadā vā bahuppadā bahupadā (?) vā rūpino vā arūpino vā saññino vā asaññino [P 5.0042] vā nevasaññīnāsaññino vā, tathāgato tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā; appamādo tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aggamakkhāyati. Appamattassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ [M 3.0039] bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti.

139. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, insofar as there are any beings—whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed; whether with form or formless; whether percipient, non-percipient, or neither percipient nor non-percipient—the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is declared the foremost among them. In the same way, bhikkhus, whatever wholesome qualities there are, all of them are rooted in heedfulness and converge upon heedfulness; heedfulness is declared the foremost among those qualities. For a heedful bhikkhu, bhikkhus, this is to be expected: he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path, he will cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, bhikkhus, does a heedful bhikkhu develop and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops Right View, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment… he develops Right Concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a heedful bhikkhu develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path."

“Yāvatā, bhikkhave, sattā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuppadā vā bahuppadā vā rūpino vā arūpino vā saññino vā asaññino vā nevasaññīnāsaññino vā, tathāgato [T 5.0063] tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā; appamādo tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aggamakkhāyati. Appamattassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ [V 3.0050] maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañca[T 5.0064], bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti.

“Bhikkhus, insofar as there are any beings—whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed; whether with form or formless; whether percipient, non-percipient, or neither percipient nor non-percipient—the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is declared the foremost among them. Just so, bhikkhus, whatever wholesome qualities there are, all of them have heedfulness as their root and converge on heedfulness; heedfulness is declared the foremost among those qualities. For a heedful bhikkhu, bhikkhus, this is to be expected: he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path, he will cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, bhikkhus, does a heedful bhikkhu develop and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops Right View, which has the removal of lust as its consummation, the removal of hatred as its consummation, and the removal of delusion as its consummation… he develops Right Concentration, which has the removal of lust as its consummation, the removal of hatred as its consummation, and the removal of delusion as its consummation. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a heedful bhikkhu develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.”

“Yāvatā, bhikkhave, sattā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuppadā vā bahuppadā vā rūpino vā arūpino vā saññino vā asaññino vā nevasaññīnāsaññino vā, tathāgato tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā; appamādo tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aggamakkhāyati. Appamattassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha[P 5.0043], bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti amatogadhaṃ amataparāyanaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti amatogadhaṃ amataparāyanaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu [M 3.0040] appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti.

“Bhikkhus, insofar as there are any beings—whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed; whether with form or formless; whether percipient, non-percipient, or neither percipient nor non-percipient—the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is declared the foremost among them. So too, bhikkhus, whatever wholesome states there are, they are all rooted in heedfulness, converge upon heedfulness; and of those states, heedfulness is declared the foremost. For a heedful bhikkhu, bhikkhus, this is to be expected: he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path, he will cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, bhikkhus, does a heedful bhikkhu develop the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops Right View, which is immersed in the Deathless, has the Deathless as its final resort, the Deathless as its culmination… he develops Right Concentration, which is immersed in the Deathless, has the Deathless as its final resort, the Deathless as its culmination. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a heedful bhikkhu develops the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.”

“Yāvatā[V 3.0051], bhikkhave, sattā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuppadā vā bahuppadā vā rūpino vā arūpino vā saññino vā asaññino vā nevasaññīnāsaññino vā, tathāgato tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā; appamādo tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aggamakkhāyati. Appamattassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, insofar as there are any beings—whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed; whether with form or formless; whether percipient, non-percipient, or neither percipient nor non-percipient—the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, is declared the foremost among them. In the very same way, bhikkhus, whatever wholesome states there are, all of them are rooted in heedfulness and converge on heedfulness; and heedfulness is declared the foremost among them. Bhikkhus, it is to be expected of a heedful bhikkhu that he will develop the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, bhikkhus, does a heedful bhikkhu develop and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops Right View that is inclined towards Nibbāna, sloping towards Nibbāna, leading towards Nibbāna... he develops Right Concentration that is inclined towards Nibbāna, sloping towards Nibbāna, leading towards Nibbāna. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a heedful bhikkhu develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path.” First.

2. Padasuttaṃ

2. Discourse on the Footprint

140. “Seyyathāpi[T 5.0065], bhikkhave, yāni kānici jaṅgalānaṃ pāṇānaṃ padajātāni, sabbāni tāni hatthipade samodhānaṃ gacchanti; hatthipadaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – mahantattena; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā; appamādo tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aggamakkhāyati. Appamattassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

140. “Monks, just as all the footprints of creatures that walk on the ground are encompassed by the elephant’s footprint, and the elephant’s footprint is declared the chief among them because of its great size; even so, monks, whatever wholesome states there are, all are rooted in heedfulness, have heedfulness as their convergence; heedfulness is declared the chief of those states. It is to be expected, monks, that a monk who is heedful will develop the Noble Eightfold Path and practise it extensively. And how, monks, does a heedful monk develop and practise extensively the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops Right View, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, maturing in relinquishment… he develops Right Concentration, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, maturing in relinquishment. In this way, monks, a heedful monk develops and practises extensively the Noble Eightfold Path.” Second.

3-7. Kūṭādisuttapañcakaṃ

3-7. The Group of Five Discourses Beginning with Kūṭa

141. “Seyyathāpi[V 3.0052], bhikkhave, kūṭāgārassa yā kāci gopānasiyo sabbā tā kūṭaṅgamā kūṭaninnā kūṭasamosaraṇā; kūṭaṃ tāsaṃ aggamakkhāyati[M 3.0041]; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… tatiyaṃ.

141. “Just as, monks, whatever rafters there are in a peaked house, all of them go to the peak, incline to the peak, converge at the peak; the peak is declared to be their chief; even so, monks… Third.”

142. “Seyyathāpi[P 5.0044], bhikkhave, ye keci mūlagandhā, kāḷānusāriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… catutthaṃ.

142. “Just as, monks, among whatever root fragrances there are, black aloe is declared to be the chief; even so, monks… Fourth.”

143. “Seyyathāpi[T 5.0066], bhikkhave, ye keci sāragandhā, lohitacandanaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… [V 3.0053] pañcamaṃ.

143. “Just as, monks, among whatever heartwood fragrances there are, red sandalwood is declared the chief; even so, monks… Fifth.”

144. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci pupphagandhā, vassikaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… chaṭṭhaṃ.

144. “Just as, monks, among whatever flower fragrances there are, jasmine is declared to be the chief; even so, monks… Sixth.”

145. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci kuṭṭarājāno, sabbe te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā bhavanti, rājā tesaṃ cakkavatti aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… sattamaṃ.

145. “Just as, monks, whatever petty kings there are, all are followers of the wheel-turning monarch, and the wheel-turning monarch is declared the chief among them; even so, monks… Seventh.”

8-10. Candimādisuttatatiyakaṃ

8-10. The Group of Three Discourses Beginning with the Moon

146. “Seyyathāpi[V 3.0054], bhikkhave, yā kāci tārakarūpānaṃ pabhā, sabbā tā candimappabhāya candimāpabhāya (syā. ka.) kalaṃ nāgghanti soḷasiṃ, candappabhā tāsaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… aṭṭhamaṃ.

146. “Just as, monks, whatever radiance there is of the host of stars, all of that is not worth a sixteenth part of the moon’s radiance; the moon’s radiance is declared the chief among them; even so, monks… Eighth.”

147. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve ādicco nabhaṃ abbhussakkamāno sabbaṃ ākāsagataṃ tamagataṃ abhivihacca bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evameva kho, bhikkhave…pe… navamaṃ.

147. “Just as, monks, in the autumn season, when the sky is clear and cloudless, the sun, ascending into the sky, having dispelled all the mass of darkness in space, shines, blazes, and radiates; even so, monks… Ninth.”

148. “Seyyathāpi[P 5.0045], bhikkhave, yāni kānici tantāvutānaṃ vatthānaṃ, kāsikavatthaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā; appamādo tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aggamakkhāyati. Appamattassetaṃ, bhikkhave[V 3.0055], bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvessati ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarissati. Kathañca[T 5.0067], bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

148. “Just as, monks, among whatever cloths woven on a loom there are, Kāsi cloth is declared the chief; even so, monks, whatever wholesome states there are, all are rooted in heedfulness, have heedfulness as their convergence; heedfulness is declared the chief of those states. It is to be expected, monks, that a heedful monk will develop the Noble Eightfold Path and practise it extensively. And how, monks, does a heedful monk develop and practise extensively the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops Right View, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, maturing in relinquishment… he develops Right Concentration, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, maturing in relinquishment. In this way, monks, a heedful monk develops and practises extensively the Noble Eightfold Path.” The tenth.

(Yadapi tathāgataṃ, tadapi vitthāretabbaṃ).

(Whatever is stated thus should also be elaborated.)

Appamādapeyyālavaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter: The Repetition Series on Heedfulness.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that is:

Tathāgataṃ [M 3.0042] padaṃ kūṭaṃ, mūlaṃ sāro ca vassikaṃ;

Rājā candimasūriyā ca, vatthena dasamaṃ padaṃ.

The Tathāgata, Pada, Kūṭa, Mūla, Sāra, and Vassika; Rāja, Candima and Suriya, and with Vattha as the tenth discourse.

6. Balakaraṇīyavaggo

6. The Chapter on Exertion

1. Balasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Exertion

149. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0068]. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci balakaraṇīyā kammantā karīyanti, sabbe te pathaviṃ nissāya pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya [P 5.0046] evamete balakaraṇīyā kammantā karīyanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti.

149. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, just as whatever tasks requiring exertion are performed, they are all performed in reliance on the earth, established on the earth; even so, monks, a monk, in reliance on virtue, established in virtue, develops the Noble Eightfold Path and practises it extensively. And how, monks, does a monk, in reliance on virtue, established in virtue, develop the Noble Eightfold Path and practise it extensively? Here, monks, a monk develops Right View based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, maturing in relinquishment… In this way, monks, a monk, in reliance on virtue, established in virtue, develops the Noble Eightfold Path and practises it extensively.”

(Paragaṅgāpeyyālīvaṇṇiyato paripuṇṇasuttanti vitthāramaggī).

(The complete sutta should be elaborated in detail according to the Far Shore Ganges Repetition Series.)

“Seyyathāpi[V 3.0056], bhikkhave, ye keci balakaraṇīyā kammantā karīyanti, sabbe te pathaviṃ nissāya pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya evamete balakaraṇīyā kammantā karīyanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti. Kathañca[T 5.0069], bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti.

Just as, monks, whatever tasks requiring exertion are performed, they are all performed in dependence on the earth, established on the earth; in the very same way, monks, a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, develops and cultivates assiduously the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, monks, does a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, develop and cultivate assiduously the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops right view that has the removal of lust as its culmination, the removal of hatred as its culmination, and the removal of delusion as its culmination... he develops right concentration that has the removal of lust as its culmination, the removal of hatred as its culmination, and the removal of delusion as its culmination. It is in this way, monks, that a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, develops and cultivates assiduously the Noble Eightfold Path.

“Seyyathāpi[M 3.0043], bhikkhave, ye keci balakaraṇīyā kammantā karīyanti, sabbe te pathaviṃ nissāya pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya evamete balakaraṇīyā kammantā karīyanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti amatogadhaṃ amataparāyanaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti amatogadhaṃ amataparāyanaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti.

Just as, monks, whatever tasks requiring exertion are performed, they are all performed in dependence on the earth, established on the earth; in the very same way, monks, a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, develops and cultivates assiduously the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, monks, does a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, develop and cultivate assiduously the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops right view that is immersed in the Deathless, has the Deathless as its final resort, and culminates in the Deathless... he develops right concentration that is immersed in the Deathless, has the Deathless as its final resort, and culminates in the Deathless. It is in this way, monks, that a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, develops and cultivates assiduously the Noble Eightfold Path.

“Seyyathāpi[V 3.0057], bhikkhave, ye keci balakaraṇīyā kammantā [T 5.0070] karīyanti, sabbe te pathaviṃ nissāya pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya evamete balakaraṇīyā kammantā karīyanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

Just as, monks, whatever tasks requiring exertion are performed, they are all performed in dependence on the earth, established on the earth; in the very same way, monks, a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, develops and cultivates assiduously the Noble Eightfold Path. And how, monks, does a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, develop and cultivate assiduously the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops right view that slopes towards Nibbāna, inclines towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna... he develops right concentration that slopes towards Nibbāna, inclines towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. It is in this way, monks, that a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, develops and cultivates assiduously the Noble Eightfold Path. The first.

2. Bījasuttaṃ

2. The Sutta on the Seed

150. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye kecime bījagāmabhūtagāmā vuḍḍhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjanti, sabbe te pathaviṃ nissāya pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya evamete bījagāmabhūtagāmā vuḍḍhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto vuḍḍhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ pāpuṇāti dhammesu. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto vuḍḍhiṃ [M 3.0044] virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ pāpuṇāti dhammesu? Idha, bhikkhave[T 5.0071], bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ [P 5.0047] vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto vuḍḍhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ pāpuṇāti dhammesū”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

150. Just as, monks, whatever kinds of seeds and plants attain growth, increase, and abundance, they all do so in dependence on the earth, established on the earth, and in this way attain growth, increase, and abundance; in the very same way, monks, a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, while developing the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivating it assiduously, attains growth, increase, and abundance in wholesome qualities. And how, monks, does a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, while developing the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivating it assiduously, attain growth, increase, and abundance in wholesome qualities? Here, monks, a monk develops right view based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and maturing in relinquishment... he develops right concentration based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and maturing in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that a monk, in dependence on virtue, established in virtue, while developing the Noble Eightfold Path and cultivating it assiduously, attains growth, increase, and abundance in wholesome qualities. The second.

3. Nāgasuttaṃ

3. The Sutta on the Nāga

151. “Seyyathāpi[V 3.0058], bhikkhave, himavantaṃ pabbatarājaṃ nissāya nāgā kāyaṃ vaḍḍhenti, balaṃ gāhenti; te tattha kāyaṃ vaḍḍhetvā balaṃ gāhetvā kusobbhe otaranti, kusobbhe kussubbhe (sī. syā.), kusubbhe (pī. ka.) otaritvā mahāsobbhe otaranti, mahāsobbhe otaritvā kunnadiyo otaranti, kunnadiyo otaritvā mahānadiyo otaranti, mahānadiyo otaritvā mahāsamuddaṃ mahāsamuddasāgaraṃ (sabbattha) saṃ. ni. 2.23 otaranti, te tattha mahantattaṃ vepullattaṃ āpajjanti kāyena; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto mahantattaṃ vepullattaṃ pāpuṇāti dhammesu. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto mahantattaṃ vepullattaṃ pāpuṇāti dhammesu? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ [T 5.0072] nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto mahantattaṃ vepullattaṃ pāpuṇāti dhammesū”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

151. Bhikkhus, just as nāgas, relying on Himavanta, the king of mountains, develop their bodies and gain strength; having developed their bodies and gained strength there, they descend into small lakes; having descended into small lakes, they descend into great lakes; having descended into great lakes, they descend into small rivers; having descended into small rivers, they descend into great rivers; having descended into great rivers, they descend into the great ocean, and there they attain greatness and expansiveness in body. Even so, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, relying on virtue and established in virtue, developing the noble eightfold path and cultivating it frequently, attains greatness and expansiveness in wholesome qualities. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu, relying on virtue and established in virtue, developing the noble eightfold path and cultivating it frequently, attain greatness and expansiveness in wholesome qualities? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu, relying on virtue and established in virtue, developing the noble eightfold path and cultivating it frequently, attains greatness and expansiveness in wholesome qualities.

4. Rukkhasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Tree

152. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rukkho pācīnaninno pācīnapoṇo pācīnapabbhāro. So mūlacchinno mūlacchinde kate (syā.) katamena papateyyā”ti? “Yena[P 5.0048], bhante, ninno yena poṇo yena pabbhāro”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno [M 3.0045] hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Catutthaṃ.

152. “Bhikkhus, suppose there were a tree leaning eastward, sloping eastward, inclining eastward. If it were cut at the root, in which direction would it fall?” “Venerable sir, it would fall in the direction it leans, slopes, and inclines.” “Just so, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops the Noble Eightfold Path, who cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path, inclines toward Nibbāna, slopes toward Nibbāna, and tends toward Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu who develops the Noble Eightfold Path, who cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path, incline toward Nibbāna, slope toward Nibbāna, and tend toward Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu who develops the Noble Eightfold Path, who cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path, inclines toward Nibbāna, slopes toward Nibbāna, and tends toward Nibbāna.”

5. Kumbhasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Pot

153. “Seyyathāpi[V 3.0059], bhikkhave, kumbho nikkujjo vamateva udakaṃ, no paccāvamati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto vamateva [T 5.0073] pāpake akusale dhamme, no paccāvamati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto vamateva pāpake akusale dhamme, no paccāvamati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto vamateva pāpake akusale dhamme, no paccāvamatī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

153. “Bhikkhus, just as a pot turned upside down vomits out water and does not take it back in, so too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path vomits out evil, unwholesome qualities and does not take them back in. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu develop and cultivate the Noble Eightfold Path so that he vomits out evil, unwholesome qualities and does not take them back in? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment. Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path vomits out evil, unwholesome qualities and does not take them back in.”

6. Sūkasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Spike

154. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sālisūkaṃ vā yavasūkaṃ vā sammāpaṇihitaṃ hatthena vā pādena vā akkantaṃ hatthaṃ vā pādaṃ vā bhindissati lohitaṃ vā uppādessatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Sammāpaṇihitattā, bhikkhave, sūkassa. Evameva [P 5.0049] kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammāpaṇihitāya diṭṭhiyā sammāpaṇihitāya maggabhāvanāya avijjaṃ bhindissati, vijjaṃ uppādessati, nibbānaṃ sacchikarissatīti – ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Sammāpaṇihitattā, bhikkhave, diṭṭhiyā. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammāpaṇihitāya diṭṭhiyā sammāpaṇihitāya maggabhāvanāya avijjaṃ bhindati, vijjaṃ uppādeti, nibbānaṃ sacchikaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… [T 5.0074] sammāsamādhiṃ [M 3.0046] bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammāpaṇihitāya diṭṭhiyā sammāpaṇihitāya maggabhāvanāya avijjaṃ bhindati, vijjaṃ uppādeti, nibbānaṃ sacchikarotī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

154. “Bhikkhus, just as a spike of rice or a spike of barley, if rightly placed, when trodden upon by hand or foot, would pierce the hand or foot and cause blood to arise—this is possible. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, of the rightly placed nature of the spike. In the very same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu with a rightly directed view and a rightly directed development of the path will shatter ignorance, cause knowledge to arise, and realize Nibbāna—this is possible. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, of the rightly directed view. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu with a rightly directed view and a rightly directed development of the path shatter ignorance, cause knowledge to arise, and realize Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, on dispassion, on cessation, and results in relinquishment. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu with a rightly directed view and a rightly directed development of the path shatters ignorance, causes knowledge to arise, and realizes Nibbāna.”

7. Ākāsasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Space

155. “Seyyathāpi[V 3.0060], bhikkhave, ākāse vividhā vātā vāyanti – puratthimāpi vātā vāyanti, pacchimāpi vātā vāyanti, uttarāpi vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇāpi vātā vāyanti, sarajāpi vātā vāyanti, arajāpi vātā vāyanti, sītāpi vātā vāyanti, uṇhāpi vātā vāyanti, parittāpi vātā vāyanti, adhimattāpi vātā vāyanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayato ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroto cattāropi satipaṭṭhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi sammappadhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi iddhipādā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, pañcapi indriyāni bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, pañcapi balāni bhāvanāparipūriṃ gacchanti, sattapi bojjhaṅgā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayato ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroto cattāropi satipaṭṭhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi sammappadhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi iddhipādā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, pañcapi indriyāni bhāvanāpāripūriṃ [T 5.0075] gacchanti, pañcapi balāni bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, sattapi bojjhaṅgā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ [P 5.0050] bhāvayato ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroto cattāropi satipaṭṭhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi sammappadhānā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, cattāropi iddhipādā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, pañcapi indriyāni bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, pañcapi balāni bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, sattapi bojjhaṅgā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchantī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

155. “Monks, just as various winds blow in the sky—easterly winds blow, westerly winds blow, northerly winds blow, southerly winds blow, dusty winds blow, dustless winds blow, cold winds blow, hot winds blow, gentle winds blow, and strong winds blow—even so, monks, for a monk who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path, the four establishments of mindfulness go to the fulfillment of their development, the four right strivings go to the fulfillment of their development, the four bases of spiritual power go to the fulfillment of their development, the five faculties go to the fulfillment of their development, the five powers go to the fulfillment of their development, and the seven factors of enlightenment go to the fulfillment of their development. And how, monks, for a monk who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path, do the four establishments of mindfulness go to the fulfillment of their development... and the seven factors of enlightenment go to the fulfillment of their development? Here, monks, a monk develops right view... he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that for a monk who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path, the four establishments of mindfulness go to the fulfillment of their development, the four right strivings go to the fulfillment of their development, the four bases of spiritual power go to the fulfillment of their development, the five faculties go to the fulfillment of their development, the five powers go to the fulfillment of their development, and the seven factors of enlightenment go to the fulfillment of their development.”

8. Paṭhamameghasuttaṃ

8. The First Discourse on the Cloud

156. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gimhānaṃ pacchime māse ūhataṃ rajojallaṃ, tamenaṃ mahāakālamegho ṭhānaso antaradhāpeti vūpasameti; evameva [M 3.0047] kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme ṭhānaso antaradhāpeti vūpasameti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento [V 3.0061] ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme ṭhānaso antaradhāpeti vūpasameti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ [T 5.0076] nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme ṭhānaso antaradhāpeti vūpasametī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

156. “Monks, just as in the last month of the hot season, stirred-up dust and dirt is instantly dispelled and pacified by a great unseasonal cloud; even so, monks, a monk who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path instantly dispels and pacifies whatever evil, unwholesome states have arisen. And how, monks, does a monk who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path instantly dispel and pacify whatever evil, unwholesome states have arisen? Here, monks, a monk develops right view… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that a monk who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path instantly dispels and pacifies whatever evil, unwholesome states have arisen.” The eighth.

9. Dutiyameghasuttaṃ

9. The Second Discourse on the Cloud

157. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, uppannaṃ mahāmeghaṃ, tamenaṃ mahāvāto antarāyeva antaradhāpeti vūpasameti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme antarāyeva antaradhāpeti vūpasameti. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme antarāyeva antaradhāpeti vūpasameti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ [P 5.0051] vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme antarāyeva antaradhāpeti vūpasametī”ti. Navamaṃ.

157. “Monks, just as a great cloud that has arisen is dispersed and calmed by a great wind right then and there; even so, monks, a monk who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path dispels and calms arisen evil, unwholesome states right then and there. And how, monks, does a monk who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path dispel and calm arisen evil, unwholesome states right then and there? Here, monks, a monk develops right view… he develops right concentration that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that a monk who develops and cultivates the Noble Eightfold Path dispels and calms arisen evil, unwholesome states right then and there.” The ninth.

10. Nāvāsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Ship

158. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sāmuddikāya nāvāya vettabandhanabandhāya cha māsāni udake pariyādāya pariyātāya (ka.), pariyāhatāya (?) hemantikena thalaṃ ukkhittāya vātātapaparetāni bandhanāni tāni pāvussakena meghena abhippavuṭṭhāni [T 5.0077] appakasireneva paṭippassambhanti, pūtikāni bhavanti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayato ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroto appakasireneva saṃyojanāni paṭippassambhanti, pūtikāni bhavanti[M 3.0048]. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayato ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroto appakasireneva saṃyojanāni paṭippassambhanti, pūtikāni bhavanti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ [V 3.0062] bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvayato ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroto appakasireneva saṃyojanāni paṭippassambhanti, pūtikāni bhavantī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

158. “Monks, just as for a sea-going vessel bound with cane fastenings, having plied the waters for six months and then been hauled up on dry land during the winter season, its fastenings, afflicted by wind and sun, when drenched by a heavy rain cloud, are easily allayed and become rotten; in this very same way, monks, for a monk who develops and makes much of the Noble Eightfold Path, the fetters are easily allayed and become rotten. And how, monks, for a monk who develops and makes much of the Noble Eightfold Path, are the fetters easily allayed and become rotten? Here, monks, a monk develops right view… and so on… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment… and so on… It is in this way, monks, that for a monk who develops and makes much of the Noble Eightfold Path, the fetters are easily allayed and become rotten.” The tenth.

11. Āgantukasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on the Visitor

159. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, āgantukāgāraṃ. Tattha puratthimāyapi disāya āgantvā vāsaṃ kappenti, pacchimāyapi disāya āgantvā vāsaṃ kappenti, uttarāyapi disāya āgantvā vāsaṃ kappenti, dakkhiṇāyapi disāya āgantvā vāsaṃ kappenti, khattiyāpi āgantvā vāsaṃ kappenti, brāhmaṇāpi [P 5.0052] āgantvā vāsaṃ kappenti, vessāpi āgantvā vāsaṃ kappenti, suddāpi āgantvā vāsaṃ kappenti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto ye dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā, te dhamme abhiññā parijānāti[T 5.0078], ye dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā, te dhamme abhiññā pajahati, ye dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā, te dhamme abhiññā sacchikaroti, ye dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā, te dhamme abhiññā bhāveti.

159. “Monks, it is just like a guesthouse. People come and take up residence there from the eastern direction, from the western direction, from the northern direction, and from the southern direction; nobles come and take up residence, brahmins come and take up residence, merchants come and take up residence, and commoners come and take up residence. In this very same way, monks, when a monk develops and makes much of the Noble Eightfold Path, he fully understands with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be fully understood, he abandons with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be abandoned, he realizes with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be realized, and he develops with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be developed.

“Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā? Pañcupādānakkhandhātissa vacanīyaṃ. Katame pañca? Seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho…pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā. Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā? Avijjā ca bhavataṇhā ca – ime, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā. Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā? Vijjā ca vimutti ca – ime, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā. Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā? Samatho ca vipassanā ca – ime, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto, ye dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā te dhamme abhiññā parijānāti…pe… ye [M 3.0049] dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā, te dhamme abhiññā bhāveti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ [V 3.0063] nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu [T 5.0079] ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto ye dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā, te dhamme abhiññā parijānāti, ye dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā, te dhamme abhiññā pajahati, ye dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā, te dhamme [P 5.0053] abhiññā sacchikaroti, ye dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā, te dhamme abhiññā bhāvetī”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

“And what, monks, are the phenomena to be fully understood with higher knowledge? It should be said: the five aggregates of clinging. What five? That is to say: the aggregate of clinging to form… and so on… the aggregate of clinging to consciousness. These, monks, are the phenomena to be fully understood by higher knowledge. And what, monks, are the phenomena to be abandoned by higher knowledge? Ignorance and craving for existence—these, monks, are the phenomena to be abandoned by higher knowledge. And what, monks, are the phenomena to be realized by higher knowledge? True knowledge and liberation—these, monks, are the phenomena to be realized by higher knowledge. And what, monks, are the phenomena to be developed by higher knowledge? Serenity and insight—these, monks, are the phenomena to be developed by higher knowledge. And how, monks, does a monk, when developing and making much of the Noble Eightfold Path, fully understand with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be fully understood… and so on… develop with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be developed? Here, monks, a monk develops right view… and so on… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment… and so on… In this way, monks, a monk, when developing and making much of the Noble Eightfold Path, fully understands with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be fully understood, abandons with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be abandoned, realizes with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be realized, and develops with higher knowledge those phenomena that are to be developed.” The eleventh.

12. Nadīsuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on the River

160. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā. Atha mahājanakāyo āgaccheyya kuddāla-piṭakaṃ ādāya – ‘mayaṃ imaṃ gaṅgaṃ nadiṃ pacchāninnaṃ karissāma pacchāpoṇaṃ pacchāpabbhāra’nti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nu so mahājanakāyo gaṅgaṃ nadiṃ pacchāninnaṃ kareyya pacchāpoṇaṃ pacchāpabbhāra”nti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Taṃ kissa hetu”? “Gaṅgā, bhante, nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā. Sā na sukarā pacchāninnaṃ kātuṃ pacchāpoṇaṃ pacchāpabbhāraṃ. Yāvadeva pana so mahājanakāyo kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāventaṃ ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarontaṃ rājāno vā rājamahāmattā vā mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā ñātisālohitā vā bhogehi abhihaṭṭhuṃ pavāreyyuṃ – ‘ehambho purisa, kiṃ te ime kāsāvā anudahanti, kiṃ muṇḍo kapālamanusaṃcarasi! Ehi, hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjassu, puññāni ca karohī’ti. So [T 5.0080] vata, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāvento ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaronto sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yañhi taṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ dīgharattaṃ vivekaninnaṃ vivekapoṇaṃ vivekapabbhāraṃ taṃ vata hīnāyāvattissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkaroti? Idha[P 5.0054], bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… [V 3.0064] sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu [M 3.0050] ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bhāveti, ariyaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ maggaṃ bahulīkarotī”ti. (Yadapi balakaraṇīyaṃ, tadapi vitthāretabbaṃ.) Dvādasamaṃ.

160. “Suppose, monks, the Ganges river slopes, inclines, and tends to the east. Then a great crowd of people were to come, taking spades and baskets, thinking: ‘We will make this Ganges river slope, incline, and tend to the west.’ What do you think, monks, could that great crowd of people make the Ganges river slope, incline, and tend to the west?” “No, venerable sir.” “For what reason?” “Because, venerable sir, the Ganges river slopes, inclines, and tends to the east. It is not easy to make it slope, incline, and tend to the west. That great crowd of people would only partake of weariness and vexation.” “In the very same way, monks, when a monk is developing and frequently practicing the Noble Eightfold Path, even if kings or royal ministers, friends or colleagues, relatives or kinsmen should entice him with wealth, saying: ‘Come, good man, why do these saffron robes scorch you? Why do you wander about with a shaven head and a bowl? Come, return to the lower life, enjoy wealth, and do meritorious deeds!’—it is not possible, monks, that a monk who is developing and frequently practicing the Noble Eightfold Path would renounce the training and return to the lower life. For what reason? Because that mind has for a long time been sloping, inclining, and tending to seclusion; it is not possible for it to return to the lower life. And how, monks, does a monk develop and frequently practice the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops right view, which is based on seclusion… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment… It is in this way, monks, that a monk develops and frequently practices the Noble Eightfold Path.” (Whatever was expanded in the Balakaraṇīya Sutta should also be expanded here.) The twelfth.

Balakaraṇīyavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Balakaraṇīya Chapter, the Sixth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Balaṃ bījañca nāgo ca, rukkho kumbhena sūkiyā;

Ākāsena ca dve meghā, nāvā āgantukā nadīti.

Strength, Seed, and Elephant, the Tree, the Pot, the Awn; the Sky, and the two Clouds, the Boat, the Visitor, and the River.

7. Esanāvaggo
