7. The Chapter on Searches

1. Esanāsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Searches

161. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0081]. “Tisso imā, bhikkhave, esanā. Katamā tisso? Kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso esanā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ abhiññāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ abhiññāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti.

161. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, there are these three searches. Which three? The search for sensual pleasures, the search for existence, and the search for a practice based on wrong view. These, monks, are the three searches. For the direct knowledge of these three searches, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops right view, which is based on seclusion… he develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. For the direct knowledge of these three searches, this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.”

“Tisso imā kho, bhikkhave, esanā. Katamā tisso? Kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso esanā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ abhiññāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… [V 3.0065] sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ abhiññāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti.

“Monks, there are these three searches. What three? The search for sensual pleasure, the search for existence, and the search for a practice based on wrong view. These, monks, are the three searches. For the direct knowledge of these three searches, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops right view… he develops right concentration culminating in the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, and the removal of delusion. For the direct knowledge of these three searches, this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.”

“Tisso [T 5.0082] imā kho, bhikkhave, esanā. Katamā tisso? Kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso esanā. Imāsaṃ kho[M 3.0051], bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ abhiññāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti amatogadhaṃ amataparāyanaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ abhiññāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti.

“Monks, there are these three searches. What three? The search for sensual pleasures, the search for existence, and the search for a practice based on wrong view. These, monks, are the three searches. For the direct knowledge of these three searches, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops right view… he develops right concentration that enters into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and has the Deathless as its final end. For the direct knowledge of these three searches, this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.”

“Tisso imā kho, bhikkhave, esanā. Katamā tisso? Kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso esanā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ abhiññāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… [V 3.0066] sammāsamādhiṃ [P 5.0055] bhāveti nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ abhiññāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti.

“Monks, there are these three searches. What three? The search for sensual pleasures, the search for existence, and the search for a practice based on wrong view. These, monks, are the three searches. For the direct knowledge of these three searches, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, monks, a monk develops right view… he develops right concentration that slopes towards Nibbāna, inclines towards Nibbāna, and tends towards Nibbāna. For the direct knowledge of these three searches, this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.”

“Tisso imā, bhikkhave, esanā. Katamā tisso? Kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso [T 5.0083] esanā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ pariññāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. (Yadapi abhiññā, tadapi pariññāya vitthāretabbaṃ.)

“Monks, there are these three searches. What three? The search for sensual pleasures, the search for existence, and the search for a practice based on wrong view. These, monks, are the three searches. For the full understanding of these three searches… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. (This should be expanded for ‘full understanding’ in the same way as for ‘direct knowledge’.)”

“Tisso imā, bhikkhave, esanā. Katamā tisso? Kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso esanā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ parikkhayāya…pe… [V 3.0067] ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. (Yadapi abhiññā, tadapi parikkhayāya vitthāretabbaṃ.)

Bhikkhus, there are these three searches. What three? The search for sensual pleasures, the search for existence, and the search for a holy life. These, bhikkhus, are the three searches. For the utter destruction of these three searches… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

“Tisso imā, bhikkhave, esanā. Katamā tisso? Kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso esanā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ pahānāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ esanānaṃ pahānāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo [T 5.0084] bhāvetabbo”ti. (Yadapi abhiññā, tadapi pahānāya vitthāretabbaṃ.) Paṭhamaṃ.

Bhikkhus, there are these three searches. What three? The search for sensual pleasures, the search for existence, and the search for a holy life. These, bhikkhus, are the three searches. For the abandoning of these three searches, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view… he develops right concentration which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and ripens in relinquishment. For the abandoning of these three searches, this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

2. Vidhāsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Conceit

162. “Tisso [M 3.0052][P 5.0056] imā, bhikkhave, vidhā. Katamā tisso? ‘Seyyohamasmī’ti vidhā, ‘sadisohamasmī’ti vidhā, ‘hīnohamasmī’ti vidhā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso vidhā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ vidhānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… [V 3.0068] sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave tissannaṃ vidhānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. (Yathā esanā, evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ). Dutiyaṃ.

162. Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of conceit. What three? The conceit ‘I am superior,’ the conceit ‘I am equal,’ and the conceit ‘I am inferior.’ These, bhikkhus, are the three kinds of conceit. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three kinds of conceit, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view… he develops right concentration which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and ripens in relinquishment. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three kinds of conceit, this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

3. Āsavasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Taints

163. “Tayome, bhikkhave, āsavā. Katame tayo? Kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, avijjāsavo – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo āsavā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇannaṃ āsavānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

163. Bhikkhus, there are these three taints. What three? The taint of sensuality, the taint of existence, and the taint of ignorance. These, bhikkhus, are the three taints. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three taints… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

4. Bhavasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Existence

164. “Tayome, bhikkhave, bhavā. Katame tayo? Kāmabhavo[T 5.0085], rūpabhavo, arūpabhavo – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo bhavā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇannaṃ bhavānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… [V 3.0069] ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

164. Bhikkhus, there are these three states of existence. What three? The sensual state of existence, the form state of existence, and the formless state of existence. These, bhikkhus, are the three states of existence. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three states of existence… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

5. Dukkhatāsuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Suffering

165. “Tisso imā, bhikkhave, dukkhatā. Katamā tisso? Dukkhadukkhatā, saṅkhāradukkhatā, vipariṇāmadukkhatā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso dukkhatā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ dukkhatānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

165. Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of suffering. What three? Suffering due to pain, suffering due to formations, and suffering due to change. These, bhikkhus, are the three kinds of suffering. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three kinds of suffering… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

6. Khilasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Mental Obstructions

166. “Tayome[V 3.0070][P 5.0057], bhikkhave, khilā. Katame tayo? Rāgo khilo, doso khilo, moho khilo – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo khilā. Imesaṃ [M 3.0053] kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇannaṃ khilānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

166. Bhikkhus, there are these three mental obstructions. What three? Lust is a mental obstruction, hatred is a mental obstruction, and delusion is a mental obstruction. These, bhikkhus, are the three mental obstructions. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three mental obstructions… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

7. Malasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Stains

167. “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, malāni. Katamāni tīṇi? Rāgo malaṃ, doso malaṃ, moho malaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi malāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇannaṃ malānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya [T 5.0086] parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… [V 3.0071] ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

167. Bhikkhus, there are these three stains. What three? Lust is a stain, hatred is a stain, and delusion is a stain. These, bhikkhus, are the three stains. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three stains… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

8. Nīghasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Afflictions

168. “Tayome, bhikkhave, nīghā. Katame tayo? Rāgo nīgho, doso nīgho, moho nīgho – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo nīghā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇannaṃ nīghānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

168. Bhikkhus, there are these three afflictions. What three? Lust is an affliction, hatred is an affliction, and delusion is an affliction. These, bhikkhus, are the three afflictions. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three afflictions… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

9. Vedanāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Feelings

169. “Tisso imā, bhikkhave, vedanā. Katamā tisso? Sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso vedanā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… [V 3.0072] ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Navamaṃ.

169. Bhikkhus, there are these three feelings. What three? Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These, bhikkhus, are the three feelings. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three feelings… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

10. Taṇhāsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Craving

170. “Tisso [P 5.0058] imā, bhikkhave, taṇhā. Katamā tisso? Kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā – imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso taṇhā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ taṇhānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha, bhikkhave[T 5.0087], bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ taṇhānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

170. Bhikkhus, there are these three cravings. What three? Craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence. These, bhikkhus, are the three cravings. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three cravings, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and ripens in relinquishment… he develops right concentration which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and ripens in relinquishment. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandoning of these three cravings… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be developed.

11. Tasināsuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on Thirst

171. “Tisso [M 3.0054] imā, bhikkhave, tasinā. Katamā tisso? Kāmatasinā, bhavatasinā, vibhavatasinā. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ tasinānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… [V 3.0073] rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ…pe… amatogadhaṃ amataparāyanaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ…pe… [V 3.0074] nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ. Imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ tasinānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

171. Monks, there are these three thirsts. Which three? Thirst for sensual pleasures, thirst for existence, and thirst for non-existence. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these three thirsts... ending in the removal of passion, ending in the removal of aversion, ending in the removal of delusion... plunging into the Deathless, having the Deathless as its final destination, ending in the Deathless... inclining towards Nibbāna, tending towards Nibbāna, slanting towards Nibbāna. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these three thirsts... this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated. The eleventh.

Esanāvaggo sattamo.

The Chapter on Questing is the seventh.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Esanā vidhā āsavo, bhavo ca dukkhatā khilā;

Malaṃ nīgho ca vedanā, dve taṇhā tasināya cāti.

The Esanā Sutta, the Vidhā Sutta, the Āsava Sutta, and the Bhava Sutta; the Dukkhatā Sutta, the Khila Sutta, the Mala Sutta, and the Nīgha Sutta; the Vedanā Sutta, and the two suttas, Taṇhā and Tasinā.

8. Oghavaggo

8. The Chapter on Floods

1. Oghasuttaṃ

1. The Floods Discourse

172. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0088][V 3.0075]. “Cattārome[P 5.0059], bhikkhave, oghā. Katame cattāro? Kāmogho, bhavogho, diṭṭhogho, avijjogho – ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro oghā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ oghānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. (Yathā esanā, evaṃ sabbaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ.) Paṭhamaṃ.

172. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, there are these four floods. Which four? The flood of sensuality, the flood of existence, the flood of views, and the flood of ignorance. These, monks, are the four floods. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these four floods… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” (As the Esanā Sutta was elaborated, so should this all be elaborated.) The first.

2. Yogasuttaṃ

2. The Yokes Discourse

173. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, yogā. Katame cattāro? Kāmayogo, bhavayogo, diṭṭhiyogo avijjāyogo – ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro yogā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ yogānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… [V 3.0076] ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

173. “Monks, there are these four yokes. Which four? The yoke of sensuality, the yoke of existence, the yoke of views, and the yoke of ignorance. These, monks, are the four yokes. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these four yokes… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” The second.

3. Upādānasuttaṃ

3. The Clinging Discourse

174. “Cattārimāni[M 3.0055], bhikkhave, upādānāni. Katamāni cattāri? Kāmupādānaṃ, diṭṭhupādānaṃ, sīlabbatupādānaṃ, attavādupādānaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri upādānāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ upādānānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

174. “Monks, there are these four kinds of clinging. What four? Clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to precepts and vows, and clinging to the doctrine of self. These, monks, are the four kinds of clinging. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these four kinds of clinging… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” The third.

4. Ganthasuttaṃ

4. The Bonds Discourse

175. “Cattārome[T 5.0089], bhikkhave, ganthā. Katame cattāro? Abhijjhā kāyagantho, byāpādo kāyagantho, sīlabbataparāmāso kāyagantho, idaṃsaccābhiniveso kāyagantho – ime [P 5.0060] kho, bhikkhave, cattāro ganthā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ ganthānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

175. “Monks, there are these four bonds. What four? The bodily bond of covetousness, the bodily bond of ill will, the bodily bond of grasping at precepts and vows, and the bodily bond of dogmatic insistence that ‘this alone is truth.’ These, monks, are the four bonds. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these four bonds… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” The fourth.

5. Anusayasuttaṃ

5. The Latent Tendencies Discourse

176. “Sattime, bhikkhave, anusayā. Katame satta? Kāmarāgānusayo, paṭighānusayo, diṭṭhānusayo[V 3.0077], vicikicchānusayo, mānānusayo, bhavarāgānusayo, avijjānusayo – ime kho, bhikkhave, sattānusayā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sattannaṃ anusayānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

176. “Monks, there are these seven latent tendencies. What seven? The latent tendency to sensual lust, the latent tendency to aversion, the latent tendency to views, the latent tendency to doubt, the latent tendency to conceit, the latent tendency to lust for existence, and the latent tendency to ignorance. These, monks, are the seven latent tendencies. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these seven latent tendencies... this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” The fifth.

6. Kāmaguṇasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Cords of Sensual Pleasure

177. “Pañcime, bhikkhave, kāmaguṇā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā…pe… ghānaviññeyyā gandhā…pe… jivhāviññeyyā rasā…pe… kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā – ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca kāmaguṇā. Imesaṃ [T 5.0090] kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

177. “Monks, there are these five cords of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable, of a pleasing nature, connected with sensual pleasure, and enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear... Odors cognizable by the nose... Flavors cognizable by the tongue... Tangibles cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, of a pleasing nature, connected with sensual pleasure, and enticing. These, monks, are the five cords of sensual pleasure. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these five cords of sensual pleasure... this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” The sixth.

7. Nīvaraṇasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Hindrances

178. “Pañcimāni[M 3.0056], bhikkhave, nīvaraṇāni. Katamāni pañca? Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ, thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ, uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ, vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

178. “Monks, there are these five hindrances. What five? The hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, and the hindrance of doubt. These, monks, are the five hindrances. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these five hindrances... this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” The seventh.

8. Upādānakkhandhasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Aggregates of Clinging

179. “Pañcime, bhikkhave, upādānakkhandhā. Katame pañca? Seyyathidaṃ – rūpupādānakkhandho[V 3.0078], vedanupādānakkhandho[P 5.0061], saññupādānakkhandho, saṅkhārupādānakkhandho, viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañcupādānakkhandhā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ upādānakkhandhānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

179. “Monks, there are these five aggregates subject to clinging. What five? They are: the form aggregate subject to clinging, the feeling aggregate subject to clinging, the perception aggregate subject to clinging, the mental formations aggregate subject to clinging, and the consciousness aggregate subject to clinging. These, monks, are the five aggregates subject to clinging. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these five aggregates subject to clinging… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” The eighth.

9. Orambhāgiyasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Lower Fetters

180. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, orambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Katamāni pañca? Sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso, kāmacchando, byāpādo – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcorambhāgiyāni [T 5.0091] saṃyojanāni. Imesaṃ kho bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya…pe… ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Navamaṃ.

180. “Monks, there are these five lower fetters. What five? They are: self-identity view, doubt, grasping at precepts and vows, sensual desire, and ill will. These, monks, are the five lower fetters. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandonment of these five lower fetters… this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” The ninth.

10. Uddhambhāgiyasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Higher Fetters

181. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, uddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Katamāni pañca? Rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya [M 3.0057] parikkhayāya pahānāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti.

181. “Bhikkhus, there are these five higher fetters. What five? Lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance. These, bhikkhus, are the five higher fetters. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandonment of these five higher fetters, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated. And what is the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu cultivates right view based on seclusion… he cultivates right concentration based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and ripening in relinquishment. For the direct knowledge, for the full understanding, for the utter destruction, and for the abandonment of these five higher fetters, this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.”

“Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, uddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Katamāni pañca? Rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Imesaṃ [T 5.0092] kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ [P 5.0062] saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo. Katamo ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko [V 3.0079] maggo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiṃ bhāveti…pe… sammāsamādhiṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ… amatogadhaṃ amataparāyanaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ… nibbānaninnaṃ nibbānapoṇaṃ nibbānapabbhāraṃ. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya ayaṃ ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvetabbo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, there are these five higher fetters. What five? Lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance. These, bhikkhus, are the five higher fetters. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, destruction, and abandonment of these five higher fetters, the Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated. What is the Noble Eightfold Path? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu cultivates right view... right concentration, which has as its culmination the removal of lust, has as its culmination the removal of hatred, has as its culmination the removal of delusion... plunging into the Deathless, having the Deathless as its destination, having the Deathless as its culmination... inclining toward Nibbāna, sloping toward Nibbāna, leading toward Nibbāna. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, destruction, and abandonment of these five higher fetters, this Noble Eightfold Path is to be cultivated.” The tenth.

Oghavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Chapter on Floods, the Eighth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Ogho yogo upādānaṃ, ganthaṃ anusayena ca;

Kāmaguṇā nīvaraṇaṃ, khandhā oruddhambhāgiyāti.

The Flood, the Yoke, Clinging, the Bond, and the Latent Tendency; The Strands of Sensuality, the Hindrances, the Aggregates, the Lower and Higher Fetters.

Vagguddānaṃ –

The Chapter Summary:

Avijjāvaggo paṭhamo, dutiyaṃ vihāraṃ vuccati;

Micchattaṃ tatiyo vaggo, catutthaṃ paṭipanneneva.

The Chapter on Ignorance is the first; the second is called Abiding. The third is the Chapter on Wrongness; the fourth, on One Who Has Entered the Path.

Titthiyaṃ [V 3.0080] pañcamo vaggo, chaṭṭho sūriyena ca;

Bahukate sattamo vaggo, uppādo aṭṭhamena ca.

The fifth is the Chapter on Sectarians, and the sixth is on the Sun; the seventh is the Chapter on Much Done, and the eighth is on Arising.

Divasavaggo navamo, dasamo appamādena ca;

Ekādasabalavaggo, dvādasa esanā pāḷiyaṃ;

Oghavaggo bhavati terasāti.

The ninth is the Chapter on the Day, and the tenth is on Heedfulness; the eleventh is the Chapter on Strength, the twelfth in the text is on Seeking; the Chapter on Floods is the thirteenth.

Maggasaṃyuttaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Path is concluded.

2. Bojjhaṅgasaṃyuttaṃ

2. The Connected Discourses on the Factors of Enlightenment

1. Pabbatavaggo

1. The Chapter on the Mountain

1. Himavantasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Himavanta

182. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0081][M 3.0058][P 5.0063]. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, himavantaṃ [T 5.0093] pabbatarājānaṃ nissāya nāgā kāyaṃ vaḍḍhenti, balaṃ gāhenti; te tattha kāyaṃ vaḍḍhetvā balaṃ gāhetvā kusobbhe otaranti, kusobbhe otaritvā mahāsobbhe otaranti, mahāsobbhe otaritvā kunnadiyo otaranti, kunnadiyo otaritvā mahānadiyo otaranti, mahānadiyo otaritvā mahāsamuddasāgaraṃ otaranti; te tattha mahantattaṃ vepullattaṃ āpajjanti kāyena; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto mahantattaṃ vepullattaṃ pāpuṇāti dhammesu. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto mahantattaṃ vepullattaṃ pāpuṇāti dhammesūti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ; dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ [P 5.0064] bhāveti…pe… vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ [T 5.0094] bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto mahantattaṃ vepullattaṃ pāpuṇāti dhammesū”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, just as nāgas, relying on Himavanta, the king of mountains, make their bodies grow and gain strength; and having made their bodies grow and gained strength there, they descend into small pools; having descended into small pools, they descend into great pools; having descended into great pools, they descend into small rivers; having descended into small rivers, they descend into great rivers; having descended into great rivers, they descend into the great ocean; there they attain greatness and expansiveness in body. Even so, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, relying on virtue and established in virtue, by developing the seven factors of enlightenment and making much of them, attains greatness and expansiveness in wholesome states. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu, relying on virtue and established in virtue, by developing the seven factors of enlightenment and making much of them, attain greatness and expansiveness in wholesome states? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminates in relinquishment. He develops the enlightenment factor of the investigation of phenomena... he develops the enlightenment factor of energy... he develops the enlightenment factor of rapture... he develops the enlightenment factor of tranquility... he develops the enlightenment factor of concentration... he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminates in relinquishment. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu, relying on virtue and established in virtue, by developing the seven factors of enlightenment and making much of them, attains greatness and expansiveness in wholesome states.” The first.

2. Kāyasuttaṃ

2. 2. The Discourse on the Body

183. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0082]. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ kāyo āhāraṭṭhitiko, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati, anāhāro no tiṭṭhati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhanti.

1. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, just as this body is sustained by nutriment, persists in dependence on nutriment, and does not persist without nutriment; even so, bhikkhus, the five hindrances are sustained by nutriment, persist in dependence on nutriment, and do not persist without nutriment.”

“Ko [M 3.0059] ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā kāmacchandassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā kāmacchandassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, subhanimittaṃ. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā kāmacchandassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā kāmacchandassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

1. “And what, bhikkhus, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen sensual desire, or for the increase and expansion of arisen sensual desire? There is, bhikkhus, the sign of the beautiful. Therein, the frequent practice of unwise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen sensual desire, or for the increase and expansion of arisen sensual desire.”

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā byāpādassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā byāpādassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, paṭighanimittaṃ. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā byāpādassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā byāpādassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

182. “And what, bhikkhus, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen ill will, or for the increase and expansion of arisen ill will? There is, bhikkhus, the sign of aversion. Therein, the frequent practice of unwise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen ill will, or for the increase and expansion of arisen ill will.”

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā thinamiddhassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā thinamiddhassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi[T 5.0095], bhikkhave, arati tandi vijambhitā bhattasammado cetaso ca līnattaṃ. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro [P 5.0065] – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā thinamiddhassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā thinamiddhassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen sloth and torpor, or for the increase and expansion of arisen sloth and torpor? There are, monks, discontent, laziness, stretching, drowsiness from food, and sluggishness of mind. Therein, frequent unwise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen sloth and torpor, or for the increase and expansion of arisen sloth and torpor.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, cetaso avūpasamo. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen restlessness and remorse, or for the increase and expansion of arisen restlessness and remorse? There is, monks, a lack of tranquility in the mind. Therein, frequent unwise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen restlessness and remorse, or for the increase and expansion of arisen restlessness and remorse.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannāya vā vicikicchāya uppādāya, uppannāya vā vicikicchāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, vicikicchāṭṭhānīyā dhammā. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro [V 3.0083] – ayamāhāro anuppannāya vā vicikicchāya uppādāya, uppannāya vā vicikicchāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen doubt, or for the increase and expansion of arisen doubt? There are, monks, things that are a basis for doubt. Therein, frequent unwise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen doubt, or for the increase and expansion of arisen doubt.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ kāyo āhāraṭṭhitiko, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati, anāhāro no tiṭṭhati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ime pañca nīvaraṇā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhanti.

Just as, monks, this body is sustained by nutriment, persists in dependence on nutriment, and does not persist without nutriment; even so, monks, these five hindrances are sustained by nutriment, persist in dependence on nutriment, and do not persist without nutriment.

“Seyyathāpi[M 3.0060], bhikkhave, ayaṃ kāyo āhāraṭṭhitiko, āhāraṃ paṭicca [T 5.0096] tiṭṭhati, anāhāro no tiṭṭhati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhanti.

Just as, monks, this body is sustained by nutriment, persists in dependence on nutriment, and does not persist without nutriment; even so, monks, these seven factors of enlightenment are sustained by nutriment, persist in dependence on nutriment, and do not persist without nutriment.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, satisambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyā dhammā. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness? There are, monks, things that are a basis for the enlightenment factor of mindfulness. Therein, frequent wise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness.

“Ko [P 5.0066] ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, kusalākusalā dhammā, sāvajjānavajjā dhammā, hīnapaṇītā dhammā, kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena? There are, monks, phenomena that are wholesome and unwholesome, blameworthy and blameless, inferior and superior, counterparts to the dark and the bright. Therein, frequent wise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, ārambhadhātu ārabbhadhātu (syā. ka.) nikkamadhātu parakkamadhātu. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa [T 5.0097] vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of energy, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of energy? There are, monks, the element of initiative, the element of exertion, and the element of striving. Therein, frequent wise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of energy, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of energy.

“Ko [V 3.0084] ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, pītisambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyā dhammā. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of rapture, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of rapture? There are, monks, things that are a basis for the enlightenment factor of rapture. Therein, frequent wise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of rapture, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of rapture.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave[M 3.0061], kāyapassaddhi, cittapassaddhi. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of tranquility, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of tranquility? There are, monks, tranquility of body and tranquility of mind. Therein, frequent wise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of tranquility, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of tranquility.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, samathanimittaṃ samādhinimittaṃ (syā.) abyagganimittaṃ. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of concentration, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of concentration? There are, monks, the sign of serenity and the sign of non-distraction. Therein, frequent wise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of concentration, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of concentration.

“Ko [T 5.0098][P 5.0067] ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyā dhammā. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity? There are, monks, things that are a basis for the enlightenment factor of equanimity. Therein, frequent wise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ayaṃ kāyo āhāraṭṭhitiko, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhati, anāhāro no tiṭṭhati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ime satta bojjhaṅgā āhāraṭṭhitikā, āhāraṃ paṭicca tiṭṭhanti, anāhārā no tiṭṭhantī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

Just as, bhikkhus, this body is sustained by nutriment, subsists in dependence on nutriment, and does not subsist without nutriment; even so, bhikkhus, these seven enlightenment factors are sustained by nutriment, subsist in dependence on nutriment, and do not subsist without nutriment.

3. Sīlasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Virtue

184. “Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sīlasampannā samādhisampannā ñāṇasampannā vimuttisampannā [V 3.0085] vimuttiñāṇadassanasampannā, dassanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahukāraṃ bahūpakāraṃ (syā.) vadāmi; savanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahukāraṃ vadāmi; upasaṅkamanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahukāraṃ vadāmi; payirupāsanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahukāraṃ vadāmi; anussatimpāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahukāraṃ vadāmi; anupabbajjampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bahukāraṃ vadāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathārūpānaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammaṃ sutvā dvayena vūpakāsena vūpakaṭṭho dvayena vūpakaṭṭho (sī. syā.) viharati – kāyavūpakāsena ca cittavūpakāsena ca. So tathā vūpakaṭṭho viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ anussarati anuvitakketi.

184. Bhikkhus, as to those bhikkhus who are accomplished in virtue, accomplished in concentration, accomplished in wisdom, accomplished in liberation, and accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation—I say, bhikkhus, that the sight of such bhikkhus is of great benefit; I say, bhikkhus, that hearing of such bhikkhus is of great benefit; I say, bhikkhus, that approaching such bhikkhus is of great benefit; I say, bhikkhus, that attending upon such bhikkhus is of great benefit; I say, bhikkhus, that recollecting such bhikkhus is of great benefit; I say, bhikkhus, that going forth in imitation of such bhikkhus is of great benefit. For what reason? Bhikkhus, having heard the Dhamma from such bhikkhus, one dwells withdrawn by a twofold withdrawal: withdrawal of body and withdrawal of mind. Dwelling thus withdrawn, one recollects that Dhamma and repeatedly reflects on it.

“Yasmiṃ [T 5.0099][M 3.0062] samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathā vūpakaṭṭho viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ anussarati anuvitakketi, satisambojjhaṅgo [P 5.0068] tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti; satisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti; satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. So tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati.

On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells thus withdrawn, recollecting that Dhamma and repeatedly reflecting on it, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of mindfulness is aroused in the bhikkhu; on that occasion the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness; and on that occasion the enlightenment factor of mindfulness comes to fulfillment in its development. Dwelling thus mindful, he investigates, examines, and scrutinizes that Dhamma with wisdom.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti; dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti; dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Tassa taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato pavicarato parivīmaṃsamāpajjato āraddhaṃ hoti vīriyaṃ asallīnaṃ.

On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells thus mindful and investigates, examines, and scrutinizes that Dhamma with wisdom, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena is aroused in the bhikkhu; on that occasion the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena; and on that occasion the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena comes to fulfillment in its development. As he investigates, examines, and scrutinizes that Dhamma with wisdom, his unsluggish energy is aroused.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato pavicarato parivīmaṃsamāpajjato āraddhaṃ hoti vīriyaṃ asallīnaṃ, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti; vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti; vīriyasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Āraddhavīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā.

On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who investigates, examines, and scrutinizes that Dhamma with wisdom, his unsluggish energy is aroused, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of energy is aroused in the bhikkhu; on that occasion the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of energy; and on that occasion the enlightenment factor of energy comes to fulfillment in its development. For one whose energy is aroused, unworldly joy arises.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno āraddhavīriyassa uppajjati pīti [T 5.0100] nirāmisā, pītisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti; pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti; pītisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Pītimanassa kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati.

On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu whose energy is aroused, unworldly joy arises, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of joy is aroused in the bhikkhu; on that occasion the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of joy; and on that occasion the enlightenment factor of joy comes to fulfillment in its development. For one whose mind is joyful, the body becomes tranquil and the mind becomes tranquil.

“Yasmiṃ [V 3.0086] samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pītimanassa kāyopi passambhati cittampi passambhati, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti; passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti; passaddhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ [P 5.0069] gacchati. Passaddhakāyassa sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati.

On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu with a joyful mind, the body becomes tranquil and the mind becomes tranquil, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of tranquility is aroused in the bhikkhu. On that occasion, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of tranquility; on that occasion, the enlightenment factor of tranquility comes to fulfillment in its development. For one whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno passaddhakāyassa sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati, samādhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti[M 3.0063]; samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti; samādhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. So tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti.

On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, the mind of a bhikkhu—whose body is tranquil and who is happy—becomes concentrated, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of concentration is aroused in the bhikkhu. On that occasion, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of concentration; on that occasion, the enlightenment factor of concentration comes to fulfillment in its development. He well regards with equanimity the mind thus concentrated.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti; upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti; upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

On whatever occasion, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu well regards with equanimity the mind thus concentrated, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of equanimity is aroused in the bhikkhu. On that occasion, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity; on that occasion, the enlightenment factor of equanimity comes to fulfillment in its development.

“Evaṃ bhāvitesu kho, bhikkhave, sattasu sambojjhaṅgesu evaṃ bahulīkatesu satta phalā sattānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā. Katame satta phalā [T 5.0101] sattānisaṃsā? Diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti. No ce diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti, atha maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti. No ce diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti, atha pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti. No ce diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti, atha pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti. No ce diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce pañcannaṃ [P 5.0070] orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti, no ce pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, atha pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti. No ce diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti, no ce pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ [V 3.0087] saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, no ce pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, atha [T 5.0102] pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti. No ce diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti[M 3.0064], no ce pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, no ce pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, no ce pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, atha pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā uddhaṃsoto hoti akaniṭṭhagāmī. Evaṃ bhāvitesu kho, bhikkhave, sattasu bojjhaṅgesu evaṃ bahulīkatesu ime satta phalā sattānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

Bhikkhus, when the seven factors of enlightenment are thus developed and frequently cultivated, seven fruits and seven benefits are to be expected. What are the seven fruits and seven benefits? One attains final knowledge at the very outset in this present life. If one does not attain final knowledge at the very outset in this present life, then one attains final knowledge at the time of death. If one does not attain final knowledge at the very outset in this present life, and does not attain final knowledge at the time of death, then with the destruction of the five lower fetters, one becomes an antarāparinibbāyī (one who attains Parinibbāna in the interval). If one does not attain final knowledge at the very outset in this present life, does not attain final knowledge at the time of death, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become an antarāparinibbāyī, then with the destruction of the five lower fetters, one becomes an upahaccaparinibbāyī (one who attains Parinibbāna after passing the midpoint of the lifespan). If one does not attain final knowledge at the very outset in this present life, does not attain final knowledge at the time of death, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become an antarāparinibbāyī, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become an upahaccaparinibbāyī, then with the destruction of the five lower fetters, one becomes an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī (one who attains Parinibbāna without exertion). If one does not attain final knowledge at the very outset in this present life, does not attain final knowledge at the time of death, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become an antarāparinibbāyī, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become an upahaccaparinibbāyī, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, then with the destruction of the five lower fetters, one becomes a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī (one who attains Parinibbāna with exertion). If one does not attain final knowledge at the very outset in this present life, does not attain final knowledge at the time of death, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become an antarāparinibbāyī, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become an upahaccaparinibbāyī, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, and with the destruction of the five lower fetters, does not become a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, then with the destruction of the five lower fetters, one is bound upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm. Bhikkhus, when the seven factors of enlightenment are thus developed and frequently cultivated, these seven fruits and seven benefits are to be expected.” The Third Sutta.

4. Vatthasuttaṃ

4. The Vattha Sutta

185. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso, bhikkhavo”ti! “Āvuso”ti [P 5.0071] kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

185. At one time the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. There the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus: "Friends, bhikkhus!" "Friend," those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta then said this:

“Sattime, āvuso, bojjhaṅgā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, pītisambojjhaṅgo, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, samādhisambojjhaṅgo, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ime kho, āvuso, satta bojjhaṅgā. Imesaṃ khvāhaṃ, āvuso, sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ yena yena bojjhaṅgena [T 5.0103] ākaṅkhāmi pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tena tena bojjhaṅgena pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharāmi; yena yena bojjhaṅgena ākaṅkhāmi majjhanhikaṃ samayaṃ viharituṃ, tena tena bojjhaṅgena majjhanhikaṃ samayaṃ viharāmi; yena yena bojjhaṅgena ākaṅkhāmi sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tena tena bojjhaṅgena sāyanhasamayaṃ viharāmi. Satisambojjhaṅgo iti ce me, āvuso, hoti, ‘appamāṇo’ti me hoti, ‘susamāraddho’ti me hoti, tiṭṭhantañca naṃ ‘tiṭṭhatī’ti pajānāmi. Sacepi me cavati, ‘idappaccayā me cavatī’ti pajānāmi…pe… [V 3.0088] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo iti ce me, āvuso, hoti, ‘appamāṇo’ti me hoti, ‘susamāraddho’ti me hoti, tiṭṭhantañca naṃ ‘tiṭṭhatī’ti pajānāmi. Sacepi me cavati, ‘idappaccayā me cavatī’ti pajānāmi.

“Friends, there are these seven enlightenment factors. Which seven? The mindfulness enlightenment factor, the investigation of phenomena enlightenment factor, the energy enlightenment factor, the rapture enlightenment factor, the tranquility enlightenment factor, the concentration enlightenment factor, and the equanimity enlightenment factor—these, friends, are the seven enlightenment factors. Among these seven enlightenment factors, friends, whichever enlightenment factor I wish to dwell in during the forenoon, I dwell in that enlightenment factor during the forenoon; whichever enlightenment factor I wish to dwell in during the midday, I dwell in that enlightenment factor during the midday; whichever enlightenment factor I wish to dwell in during the evening, I dwell in that enlightenment factor during the evening. If, friends, the mindfulness enlightenment factor is present in me, it is immeasurable for me, it is well-aroused for me. And when it is persisting, I know, ‘It is persisting.’ And if it passes away from me, I know, ‘It passes away from me because of this condition.’ … If, friends, the equanimity enlightenment factor is present in me, it is immeasurable for me, it is well-aroused for me. And when it is persisting, I know, ‘It is persisting.’ And if it passes away from me, I know, ‘It passes away from me because of this condition.’”

“Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rañño vā rājamahāmattassa vā nānārattānaṃ dussānaṃ dussakaraṇḍako pūro assa. So yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya [M 3.0065] pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ pubbaṇhasamayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya majjhanhikaṃ samayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ majjhanhikaṃ samayaṃ pārupeyya; yaññadeva dussayugaṃ ākaṅkheyya sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupituṃ, taṃ tadeva dussayugaṃ sāyanhasamayaṃ pārupeyya. Evameva [P 5.0072] khvāhaṃ, āvuso, imesaṃ sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ yena yena bojjhaṅgena ākaṅkhāmi pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tena tena bojjhaṅgena pubbaṇhasamayaṃ viharāmi; [T 5.0104] yena yena bojjhaṅgena ākaṅkhāmi majjhanhikaṃ samayaṃ viharituṃ, tena tena bojjhaṅgena majjhanhikaṃ samayaṃ viharāmi; yena yena bojjhaṅgena ākaṅkhāmi sāyanhasamayaṃ viharituṃ, tena tena bojjhaṅgena sāyanhasamayaṃ viharāmi. Satisambojjhaṅgo iti ce me, āvuso, hoti, ‘appamāṇo’ti me hoti, ‘susamāraddho’ti me hoti, tiṭṭhantañca naṃ ‘tiṭṭhatī’ti pajānāmi. Sacepi me cavati, ‘idappaccayā me cavatī’ti pajānāmi…pe… [V 3.0089] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo iti ce me, āvuso, hoti, ‘appamāṇo’ti me hoti, ‘susamāraddho’ti me hoti, tiṭṭhantañca naṃ ‘tiṭṭhatī’ti pajānāmi. Sacepi me cavati, ‘idappaccayā me cavatī’ti pajānāmī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

Just as, friends, a king or a royal minister might have a chest full of garments of various colors. Whatever pair of garments he wished to put on in the morning, that very pair he would put on in the morning; whatever pair of garments he wished to put on at midday, that very pair he would put on at midday; whatever pair of garments he wished to put on in the evening, that very pair he would put on in the evening. In the same way, friends, with these seven factors of enlightenment, whichever factor of enlightenment I wish to dwell with in the morning, I dwell with that very factor of enlightenment in the morning; whichever factor of enlightenment I wish to dwell with at midday, I dwell with that very factor of enlightenment at midday; whichever factor of enlightenment I wish to dwell with in the evening, I dwell with that very factor of enlightenment in the evening. Friends, if the mindfulness factor of enlightenment arises in me, it is for me 'immeasurable,' it is for me 'well-aroused.' When it is persisting, I know: 'It is persisting.' And if it ceases, I know: 'It ceases because of this condition.' … Friends, if the equanimity factor of enlightenment arises in me, it is for me 'immeasurable,' it is for me 'well-aroused.' When it is persisting, I know: 'It is persisting.' And if it ceases, I know: 'It ceases because of this condition.'

5. Bhikkhusuttaṃ

5. The Bhikkhu Sutta

186. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘bojjhaṅgā, bojjhaṅgā’ti, bhante, vuccanti. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, ‘bojjhaṅgā’ti vuccantī”ti? “Bodhāya saṃvattantīti kho, bhikkhu, tasmā ‘bojjhaṅgā’ti vuccanti. Idha, bhikkhu, satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Tassime satta bojjhaṅge bhāvayato kāmāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati[T 5.0105], bhavāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati, avijjāsavāpi cittaṃ vimuccati. Vimuttasmiṃ vimuttamiti ñāṇaṃ hoti. ‘Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti. Bodhāya saṃvattantīti, bhikkhu, tasmā ‘bojjhaṅgā’ti vuccantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

186. At Sāvatthī. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One… and sitting to one side, he said to the Blessed One: “‘Factors of enlightenment, factors of enlightenment,’ it is said, venerable sir. To what extent, venerable sir, are they called ‘factors of enlightenment’?” “Because they conduce to enlightenment, bhikkhu, they are therefore called ‘factors of enlightenment.’ Here, bhikkhu, one develops the mindfulness factor of enlightenment, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminates in relinquishment… one develops the equanimity factor of enlightenment, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminates in relinquishment. For one who develops these seven factors of enlightenment, the mind is liberated from the taint of sensual pleasure, the mind is liberated from the taint of existence, and the mind is liberated from the taint of ignorance. When liberated, the knowledge arises: ‘I am liberated.’ One understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’ Because they conduce to enlightenment, bhikkhu, they are therefore called ‘factors of enlightenment.’”

6. Kuṇḍaliyasuttaṃ

6. The Kuṇḍaliya Sutta

187. Ekaṃ [V 3.0090][M 3.0066][P 5.0073] samayaṃ bhagavā sākete viharati añjanavane migadāye. Atha kho kuṇḍaliyo paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho kuṇḍaliyo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ahamasmi, bho gotama, ārāmanissayī ārāmanisādī (sī.), ārāmaniyādī (syā.) parisāvacaro. Tassa mayhaṃ, bho gotama, pacchābhattaṃ bhuttapātarāsassa ayamācāro ayamāhāro (syā. ka.) hoti – ārāmena ārāmaṃ uyyānena uyyānaṃ anucaṅkamāmi anuvicarāmi. So tattha passāmi eke samaṇabrāhmaṇe itivādappamokkhānisaṃsañceva kathaṃ kathente upārambhānisaṃsañca – ‘bhavaṃ pana gotamo kimānisaṃso viharatī’”ti? “Vijjāvimuttiphalānisaṃso kho, kuṇḍaliya, tathāgato viharatī”ti.

187. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāketa in the Añjana Grove, the deer sanctuary. Then the wanderer Kuṇḍaliya approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their pleasant and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the wanderer Kuṇḍaliya said to the Blessed One: 'I, Master Gotama, am one who resides in parks and frequents assemblies. For me, Master Gotama, after the meal, having finished my morning meal, this is my custom: I wander and roam from park to park, from garden to garden. There I see some ascetics and brahmins engaged in talk that has the advantage of being free from refutation and the advantage of censure. But with what advantage does Master Gotama dwell?' 'The Tathāgata, Kuṇḍaliya, dwells with the fruit of knowledge and liberation as his advantage.'

“Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī”ti? “Satta kho, kuṇḍaliya, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī”ti. “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrentī”ti? “Cattāro kho, kuṇḍaliya, satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrentī”ti[T 5.0106]. “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā, bahulīkatā cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrentī”ti? “Tīṇi kho, kuṇḍaliya, sucaritāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrentī”ti. “Katame pana, bho gotama, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā tīṇi sucaritāni paripūrentī”ti? “Indriyasaṃvaro [P 5.0074] kho, kuṇḍaliya, bhāvito bahulīkato tīṇi sucaritāni paripūretī”ti.

“But, Master Gotama, what things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill knowledge and liberation?” “Kuṇḍaliya, the seven factors of enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, fulfill knowledge and liberation.” “And what things, Master Gotama, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment?” “Kuṇḍaliya, the four foundations of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment.” “And what things, Master Gotama, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness?” “Kuṇḍaliya, the three kinds of good conduct, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness.” “And what things, Master Gotama, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the three kinds of good conduct?” “Kuṇḍaliya, restraint of the sense faculties, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the three kinds of good conduct.”

“Kathaṃ bhāvito ca, kuṇḍaliya, indriyasaṃvaro kathaṃ bahulīkato tīṇi sucaritāni paripūretīti? Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā manāpaṃ nābhijjhati nābhihaṃsati, na rāgaṃ janeti. Tassa ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṃ cittaṃ ajjhattaṃ susaṇṭhitaṃ suvimuttaṃ. Cakkhunā kho paneva rūpaṃ disvā amanāpaṃ na maṅku hoti appatiṭṭhitacitto adīnamānaso abyāpannacetaso. Tassa ṭhito ca kāyo hoti ṭhitaṃ cittaṃ ajjhattaṃ susaṇṭhitaṃ suvimuttaṃ.

“And how, Kuṇḍaliya, is restraint of the sense faculties developed and cultivated so that it fulfills the three kinds of good conduct? Here, Kuṇḍaliya, a bhikkhu, having seen a pleasing form with the eye, does not covet it, is not elated by it, and does not generate lust. His mental body is established, and his mind is established internally, well-settled, and well-liberated. And having seen an unpleasing form with the eye, he is not sullen, his mind is not unsettled, he is not dejected, and his mind is without ill will. His mental body is established, and his mind is established internally, well-settled, and well-liberated.

“Puna [M 3.0067] caparaṃ, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… [V 3.0091] ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya manāpaṃ nābhijjhati nābhihaṃsati, na rāgaṃ janeti. Tassa ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṃ cittaṃ ajjhattaṃ susaṇṭhitaṃ suvimuttaṃ. Manasā kho paneva dhammaṃ viññāya amanāpaṃ na maṅku hoti appatiṭṭhitacitto adīnamānaso abyāpannacetaso. Tassa ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṃ cittaṃ ajjhattaṃ susaṇṭhitaṃ suvimuttaṃ.

Furthermore, Kuṇḍaliya, a monk, having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled an odor with the nose… having tasted a flavor with the tongue… having felt a tangible object with the body… having cognized a pleasing mental object with the mind, does not covet it, nor does he exult in it, nor does he generate lust. His mental body is established, and his mind is established internally, well-settled, and well-liberated. Furthermore, having cognized an unpleasing mental object with the mind, he is not dismayed, his mind is not unsettled, he is not of dejected mind, nor of a hateful mind. His mental body is established, and his mind is established internally, well-settled, and well-liberated.

“Yato kho, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā manāpāmanāpesu rūpesu [T 5.0107] ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṃ cittaṃ ajjhattaṃ susaṇṭhitaṃ suvimuttaṃ. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā…pe… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā…pe… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā…pe… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā…pe… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya manāpāmanāpesu dhammesu ṭhito ca kāyo hoti, ṭhitaṃ cittaṃ ajjhattaṃ susaṇṭhitaṃ suvimuttaṃ[P 5.0075]. Evaṃ bhāvito kho, kuṇḍaliya, indriyasaṃvaro evaṃ bahulīkato tīṇi sucaritāni paripūreti.

When, Kuṇḍaliya, a monk, having seen a form with the eye, has his mental body established and his mind established internally, well-settled, and well-liberated with regard to pleasing and unpleasing forms; and having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled an odor with the nose… having tasted a flavor with the tongue… having felt a tangible object with the body… having cognized a mental object with the mind, has his mental body established and his mind established internally, well-settled, and well-liberated with regard to pleasing and unpleasing mental objects; in this way, Kuṇḍaliya, restraint of the faculties, when thus developed and frequently practiced, fulfills the three kinds of good conduct.

“Kathaṃ bhāvitāni ca, kuṇḍaliya, tīṇi sucaritāni kathaṃ bahulīkatāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti? Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu kāyaduccaritaṃ pahāya kāyasucaritaṃ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṃ [V 3.0092] pahāya vacīsucaritaṃ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṃ pahāya manosucaritaṃ bhāveti. Evaṃ bhāvitāni kho, kuṇḍaliya, tīṇi sucaritāni evaṃ bahulīkatāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti.

And how, Kuṇḍaliya, are the three good conducts developed and frequently practiced so that they fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness? Here, Kuṇḍaliya, a monk abandons bodily misconduct and develops bodily good conduct; he abandons verbal misconduct and develops verbal good conduct; he abandons mental misconduct and develops mental good conduct. Thus, Kuṇḍaliya, when so developed and so frequently practiced, the three good conducts fulfill the four foundations of mindfulness.

“Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, kuṇḍaliya, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā kathaṃ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti? Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, kuṇḍaliya, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā evaṃ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti.

And how, Kuṇḍaliya, are the four foundations of mindfulness developed and frequently practiced so that they fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment? Here, Kuṇḍaliya, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world; he dwells contemplating feelings in feelings… he dwells contemplating mind in mind… he dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. Thus, Kuṇḍaliya, when so developed and so frequently practiced, the four foundations of mindfulness fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment.

“Kathaṃ [T 5.0108] bhāvitā ca, kuṇḍaliya, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti? Idha, kuṇḍaliya, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ [M 3.0068] bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, kuṇḍaliya, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī”ti.

And how, Kuṇḍaliya, are the seven factors of enlightenment developed and frequently practiced so that they fulfill knowledge and liberation? Here, Kuṇḍaliya, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. Thus, Kuṇḍaliya, when so developed and so frequently practiced, the seven factors of enlightenment fulfill knowledge and liberation.

Evaṃ vutte kuṇḍaliyo paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama! Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya, cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evameva bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

When this was said, the wanderer Kuṇḍaliya said to the Blessed One: "Excellent, Master Gotama, excellent! Just as, Master Gotama, one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms; in the same way, the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama. I go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of monks. May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts."

7. Kūṭāgārasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Gabled House

188. “Seyyathāpi[V 3.0093], bhikkhave, kūṭāgārassa yā kāci gopānasiyo, sabbā tā kūṭaninnā kūṭapoṇā kūṭapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro.

188. Just as, monks, whatever rafters there are in a gabled house, all of them incline towards the peak, slope towards the peak, and converge at the peak; in the same way, monks, a monk who develops and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and converges upon Nibbāna.

“Kathañca[P 5.0076], bhikkhave, bhikkhu satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro[T 5.0109]? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satta bojjhaṅge bhāvento satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Sattamaṃ.

And how, monks, does a monk, by developing and cultivating the seven factors of enlightenment, incline towards Nibbāna, slope towards Nibbāna, and converge upon Nibbāna? Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that a monk, by developing and cultivating the seven factors of enlightenment, inclines towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and converges upon Nibbāna.

8. Upavānasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Upavāna

189. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ca upavāno āyasmā ca sāriputto kosambiyaṃ viharanti ghositārāme. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā upavāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā upavānena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ upavānaṃ etadavoca –

189. At one time, the Venerable Upavāna and the Venerable Sāriputta were dwelling at Kosambī, in Ghosita’s Monastery. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta arose from seclusion and approached the Venerable Upavāna. Having approached, he exchanged joyful greetings with the Venerable Upavāna. Having concluded the courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Venerable Upavāna:

“Jāneyya [M 3.0069] nu kho, āvuso upavāna, bhikkhu ‘paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā evaṃ susamāraddhā me satta bojjhaṅgā phāsuvihārāya saṃvattantī’”ti? “Jāneyya kho, āvuso sāriputta[V 3.0094], bhikkhu ‘paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā evaṃ susamāraddhā me satta bojjhaṅgā phāsuvihārāya saṃvattantī’”ti.

“Friend Upavāna, could a monk know for himself: ‘Thus, through wise attention, my seven factors of enlightenment, being well undertaken, conduce to a comfortable dwelling’?” “Friend Sāriputta, a monk could indeed know for himself: ‘Thus, through wise attention, my seven factors of enlightenment, being well undertaken, conduce to a comfortable dwelling.’”

“Satisambojjhaṅgaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu ārabbhamāno pajānāti ‘cittañca me suvimuttaṃ, thinamiddhañca me susamūhataṃ, uddhaccakukkuccañca me suppaṭivinītaṃ, āraddhañca me vīriyaṃ, aṭṭhiṃkatvā manasi karomi, no [T 5.0110] ca līna’nti…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ āvuso, bhikkhu ārabbhamāno pajānāti ‘cittañca [P 5.0077] me suvimuttaṃ, thinamiddhañca me susamūhataṃ, uddhaccakukkuccañca me suppaṭivinītaṃ, āraddhañca me vīriyaṃ, aṭṭhiṃkatvā manasi karomi, no ca līna’nti. Evaṃ kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhu jāneyya ‘paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā evaṃ susamāraddhā me satta bojjhaṅgā phāsuvihārāya saṃvattantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Friend, when a bhikkhu is practicing the mindfulness enlightenment factor, he knows: ‘My mind is well liberated, sloth and torpor are thoroughly uprooted by me, restlessness and remorse are well subdued by me, and my energy is aroused. I attend, paying heed, and it is not sluggish.’ ... Friend, when a bhikkhu is practicing the equanimity enlightenment factor, he knows: ‘My mind is well liberated, sloth and torpor are thoroughly uprooted by me, restlessness and remorse are well subdued by me, and my energy is aroused. I attend, paying heed, and it is not sluggish.’ Thus, friend Sāriputta, a bhikkhu would know for himself: ‘Through wise attention, my seven factors of enlightenment, being well practiced in this way, lead to a comfortable dwelling.’”

9. Paṭhamauppannasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on the Arisen

190. “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… [V 3.0095] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti. Navamaṃ.

190. “Bhikkhus, these seven factors of enlightenment, being developed and cultivated, arise where they have not arisen before, but not apart from the manifestation of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One. Which seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness... the enlightenment factor of equanimity.
