These, bhikkhus, are the seven factors of enlightenment that, being developed and cultivated, arise where they have not arisen before, but not apart from the manifestation of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.”

10. Dutiyauppannasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on the Arisen

191. “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

191. “Bhikkhus, these seven factors of enlightenment, being developed and cultivated, arise where they have not arisen before, but not apart from the discipline of the Sugata. Which seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness... the enlightenment factor of equanimity. These, bhikkhus, are the seven factors of enlightenment that, being developed and cultivated, arise where they have not arisen before, but not apart from the discipline of the Sugata.”

Pabbatavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on the Mountain.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse thereof:

Himavantaṃ [T 5.0111] kāyaṃ sīlaṃ, vatthaṃ bhikkhu ca kuṇḍali;

Kūṭañca upavānañca, uppannā apare duveti.

Himavanta, Kāya, and Sīla, Vattha, a Bhikkhu, and Kuṇḍaliya; Kūṭa and Upavāna, and two further discourses on the Arisen.

2. Gilānavaggo

2. The Chapter on the Sick

1. Pāṇasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Living Beings

192. “Seyyathāpi[M 3.0070][P 5.0078][T 5.0112], bhikkhave, ye keci pāṇā cattāro iriyāpathe kappenti – kālena gamanaṃ, kālena ṭhānaṃ, kālena nisajjaṃ, kālena seyyaṃ, sabbe te pathaviṃ nissāya pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhāya evamete cattāro iriyāpathe kappenti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti.

192. “Just as, bhikkhus, whatever living beings there are assume the four postures—walking at the appropriate time, standing at the appropriate time, sitting at the appropriate time, and lying down at the appropriate time—all of them, relying on the earth, established on the earth, thus assume these four postures; in this very same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, relying on virtue, established in virtue, develops the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment.”

“Kathañca[V 3.0096], bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu, relying on virtue and established in virtue, develop and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the mindfulness factor of enlightenment, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment… he develops the equanimity factor of enlightenment, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. This is how, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, relying on virtue and established in virtue, develops and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment.”

2. Paṭhamasūriyūpamasuttaṃ

2. The First Discourse on the Simile of the Sun

193. “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – aruṇuggaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā. Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati.

193. “Bhikkhus, for the rising of the sun, this is the forerunner, this is the precursor: the dawn. In the same way, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, for the arising of the seven factors of enlightenment, this is the forerunner, this is the precursor: good friendship. For a bhikkhu who has good friends, bhikkhus, it is to be expected that he will develop the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment.”

“Kathañca[T 5.0113], bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu [P 5.0079] kalyāṇamitto satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu with good friends develop and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the mindfulness factor of enlightenment, which is based on seclusion… he develops the equanimity factor of enlightenment, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. This is how, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu with good friends develops and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment.”

3. Dutiyasūriyūpamasuttaṃ

3. The Second Discourse on the Simile of the Sun

194. “Sūriyassa[M 3.0071], bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – aruṇuggaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ [V 3.0097] pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – yonisomanasikāro. Yonisomanasikārasampannassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati.

194. “Bhikkhus, for the rising of the sun, this is the forerunner, this is the precursor: the dawn. In the same way, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, for the arising of the seven factors of enlightenment, this is the forerunner, this is the precursor: wise attention. For a bhikkhu endowed with wise attention, bhikkhus, it is to be expected that he will develop the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu endowed with wise attention develop and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the mindfulness factor of enlightenment, which is based on seclusion… he develops the equanimity factor of enlightenment, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. This is how, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with wise attention develops and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment.”

4. Paṭhamagilānasuttaṃ

4. The First Discourse on Sickness

195. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahākassapo pippaliguhāyaṃ vipphaliguhāyaṃ (sī.) viharati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha [T 5.0114] kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahākassapo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ mahākassapaṃ etadavoca –

195. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Now at that time the Venerable Mahākassapa was dwelling in the Pipphali Cave, afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and approached the Venerable Mahākassapa. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Mahākassapa:

“Kacci te, kassapa, khamanīyaṃ kacci yāpanīyaṃ? Kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti? “Na [P 5.0080] me, bhante, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.

“Kassapa, are you enduring? Are you getting by? Are your painful feelings receding and not increasing? Is their receding evident, and not their increase?” “Venerable sir, I am not enduring; I am not getting by. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not receding; their increase is evident, not their receding.”

“Sattime, kassapa, bojjhaṅgā mayā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo kho, kassapa, mayā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati…pe… [V 3.0098] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo kho, kassapa, mayā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya [M 3.0072] nibbānāya saṃvattati. Ime kho, kassapa, satta bojjhaṅgā mayā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattantī”ti. “Taggha, bhagavā, bojjhaṅgā; taggha, sugata, bojjhaṅgā”ti.

“Kassapa, these seven factors of enlightenment have been well proclaimed by me. When developed and cultivated, they conduce to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness, Kassapa, has been well proclaimed by me. When developed and cultivated, it conduces to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna… The enlightenment factor of equanimity, Kassapa, has been well proclaimed by me. When developed and cultivated, it conduces to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. These, Kassapa, are the seven factors of enlightenment that have been well proclaimed by me. When developed and cultivated, they conduce to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.” “Truly, O Blessed One, they are factors of enlightenment! Truly, O Sugata, they are factors of enlightenment!”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā mahākassapo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandi. Vuṭṭhahi cāyasmā mahākassapo tamhā ābādhā. Tathāpahīno cāyasmato mahākassapassa so ābādho ahosīti. Catutthaṃ.

The Blessed One said this. Pleased, the Venerable Mahākassapa delighted in the Blessed One’s speech. And the Venerable Mahākassapa arose from that illness. And that illness of the Venerable Mahākassapa was thus abandoned. The Fourth.

5. Dutiyagilānasuttaṃ

5. The Second Discourse on the Sick

196. Ekaṃ [T 5.0115] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā mahāmoggallāno gijjhakūṭe pabbate viharati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ etadavoca –

196. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Now at that time the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was dwelling on the Vulture Peak Mountain, afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. Then in the evening, the Blessed One arose from seclusion and approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna:

“Kacci te, moggallāna, khamanīyaṃ kacci yāpanīyaṃ? Kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti? “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.

“Moggallāna, are you enduring? Are you getting by? Are your painful feelings receding and not increasing? Is their receding apparent, and not their increasing?” “Venerable sir, I am not enduring; I am not getting by. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not receding; their increasing is apparent, not their receding.”

“Sattime, moggallāna, bojjhaṅgā mayā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo kho, moggallāna, mayā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati…pe… [V 3.0099] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo kho, moggallāna, mayā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Ime kho, moggallāna, satta bojjhaṅgā mayā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattantī”ti. “Taggha[T 5.0116], bhagavā, bojjhaṅgā; taggha, sugata, bojjhaṅgā”ti.

“Moggallāna, these seven factors of enlightenment have been well proclaimed by me. When developed and cultivated, they conduce to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness, Moggallāna, has been well proclaimed by me; when developed and cultivated, it conduces to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna… The enlightenment factor of equanimity, Moggallāna, has been well proclaimed by me; when developed and cultivated, it conduces to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. These, Moggallāna, are the seven factors of enlightenment that have been well proclaimed by me; when developed and cultivated, they conduce to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.” “Truly, O Blessed One, they are factors of enlightenment! Truly, O Sugata, they are factors of enlightenment!”

Idamavoca [M 3.0073] bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandi. Vuṭṭhahi cāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tamhā ābādhā. Tathāpahīno cāyasmato mahāmoggallānassa so ābādho ahosīti. Pañcamaṃ.

The Blessed One said this. Pleased, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna delighted in the Blessed One’s speech. And the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna arose from that illness. Thus that illness of the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was abandoned. The Fifth.

6. Tatiyagilānasuttaṃ

6. The Third Discourse on Sickness

197. Ekaṃ [P 5.0081] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho āyasmā mahācundo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ mahācundaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “paṭibhantu taṃ, cunda, bojjhaṅgā”ti.

197. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place. Now at that time the Blessed One was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. Then the Venerable Mahācunda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. To the Venerable Mahācunda, as he was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this: “Cunda, may the factors of enlightenment occur to you.”

“Sattime, bhante, bojjhaṅgā bhagavatā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo kho, bhante, bhagavatā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati…pe… [V 3.0100] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo kho, bhante, bhagavatā sammadakkhāto bhāvito bahulīkato abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Ime kho, bhante, satta bojjhaṅgā bhagavatā sammadakkhātā bhāvitā bahulīkatā abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattantī”ti. “Taggha[T 5.0117], cunda, bojjhaṅgā; taggha, cunda, bojjhaṅgā”ti.

“Venerable Sir, these seven factors of enlightenment have been well proclaimed by the Blessed One. When developed and cultivated, they conduce to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness, Venerable Sir, has been well proclaimed by the Blessed One. When developed and cultivated, it conduces to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna… The enlightenment factor of equanimity, Venerable Sir, has been well proclaimed by the Blessed One. When developed and cultivated, it conduces to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. These, Venerable Sir, are the seven factors of enlightenment that have been well proclaimed by the Blessed One. When developed and cultivated, they conduce to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.” “Truly, Cunda, they are factors of enlightenment! Truly, Cunda, they are factors of enlightenment!”

Idamavocāyasmā cundo. Samanuñño satthā ahosi. Vuṭṭhahi ca bhagavā tamhā ābādhā. Tathāpahīno ca bhagavato so ābādho ahosīti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

The Venerable Cunda said this. The Teacher approved. And the Blessed One arose from that illness. And that illness of the Blessed One was thus abandoned. The Sixth.

7. Pāraṅgamasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Going to the Far Shore

198. “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattanti. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā apārā pāraṃ gamanāya saṃvattantī”ti.

198. “Bhikkhus, these seven factors for enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, conduce to going from the near shore to the far shore. What are the seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… the enlightenment factor of equanimity. These, bhikkhus, are the seven factors for enlightenment that, when developed and cultivated, conduce to going from the near shore to the far shore.”

“Appakā [M 3.0074][P 5.0082] te manussesu, ye janā pāragāmino;

Athāyaṃ itarā pajā, tīramevānudhāvati.

“Few are those among humans, the people who go to the far shore; but this other generation runs along this very shore.”

“Ye ca kho sammadakkhāte, dhamme dhammānuvattino;

Te janā pāramessanti, maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ.

“But those people who, in the well-expounded Dhamma, practice in accordance with the Dhamma, they will go to the far shore, beyond the domain of Death, so hard to cross.”

“Kaṇhaṃ dhammaṃ vippahāya, sukkaṃ bhāvetha paṇḍito;

Okā anokamāgamma, viveke yattha dūramaṃ.

“The wise person should abandon the dark state and develop the bright. Having gone from a home to the homeless state, into seclusion where it is hard to delight,”

“Tatrābhiratimiccheyya[V 3.0101], hitvā kāme akiñcano;

Pariyodapeyya attānaṃ, cittaklesehi paṇḍito.

“There one should wish for delight. Having abandoned sensual pleasures, possessing nothing, the wise person should cleanse themself from the defilements of the mind.”

“Yesaṃ sambodhiyaṅgesu, sammā cittaṃ subhāvitaṃ;

Ādānappaṭinissagge, anupādāya ye ratā;

Khīṇāsavā jutimanto, te loke parinibbutā”ti. sattamaṃ;

“Those whose minds are well-developed in the factors for enlightenment, who, without clinging, delight in the relinquishing of grasping; they, with taints destroyed, radiant, are fully extinguished in the world.” The Seventh.

8. Viraddhasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Neglected

199. “Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā viraddhā, viraddho tesaṃ [T 5.0118] ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī. Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā āraddhā, āraddho tesaṃ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ime satta bojjhaṅgā viraddhā, viraddho tesaṃ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī. Yesaṃ kesañci, bhikkhave, ime satta bojjhaṅgā āraddhā, āraddho tesaṃ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

199. “Bhikkhus, for whomever the seven factors for enlightenment are missed, for them the noble path leading rightly to the destruction of suffering is missed. For whomever, bhikkhus, the seven factors for enlightenment are undertaken, for them the noble path leading rightly to the destruction of suffering is undertaken. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness... the enlightenment factor of equanimity. For whomever, bhikkhus, these seven factors for enlightenment are missed, for them the noble path leading rightly to the destruction of suffering is missed. For whomever, bhikkhus, these seven factors for enlightenment are undertaken, for them the noble path leading rightly to the destruction of suffering is undertaken.” The Eighth.

9. Ariyasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Noble

200. “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ariyā niyyānikā nīyanti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ariyā niyyānikā nīyanti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā”ti. Navamaṃ.

200. “Bhikkhus, these seven factors for enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, are noble and emancipating; they lead the one who practices them to the right destruction of suffering. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness... the enlightenment factor of equanimity. Indeed, bhikkhus, these seven factors for enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, are noble and emancipating; they lead the one who practices them to the right destruction of suffering.” The Ninth.

10. Nibbidāsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Disenchantment

201. “Sattime[M 3.0075], bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā [V 3.0102] ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattantī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

201. “Bhikkhus, these seven factors for enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, conduce to utter disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to calming, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness... the enlightenment factor of equanimity. Indeed, bhikkhus, these seven factors for enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, conduce to utter disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to calming, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.” The Tenth.

Gilānavaggo [P 5.0083] dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on the Sick.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of it:

Pāṇā [T 5.0119] sūriyūpamā dve, gilānā apare tayo;

Pāraṅgāmī viraddho ca, ariyo nibbidāya cāti.

The Pāṇa Sutta, two on the Simile of the Sun, another three on the Sick; the Pāraṅgāmī, the Viraddha, the Ariya, and the Nibbidā.

3. Udāyivaggo

3. The Chapter on Udāyi

1. Bodhāyasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse for Awakening

202. Atha [T 5.0120] kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

202. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One... having sat down at one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:

“‘Bojjhaṅgā, bojjhaṅgā’ti, bhante, vuccanti. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, ‘bojjhaṅgā’ti vuccantī”ti? “‘Bodhāya saṃvattantī’ti kho, bhikkhu, tasmā bojjhaṅgāti vuccanti. Idha, bhikkhu, satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. ‘Bodhāya saṃvattantī’ti kho, bhikkhu, tasmā ‘bojjhaṅgā’ti vuccantī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“‘Factors for enlightenment, factors for enlightenment,’ venerable sir, it is said. To what extent, venerable sir, are they called ‘factors for enlightenment’?” “Bhikkhu, they conduce to enlightenment, therefore they are called ‘factors for enlightenment.’ Here, bhikkhu, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion… and so on… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. Bhikkhu, they conduce to enlightenment, therefore they are called ‘factors for enlightenment.’” The First.

2. Bojjhaṅgadesanāsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Teaching of the Factors for Enlightenment

203. “Satta [V 3.0103] vo, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅge desessāmi; taṃ suṇātha. Katame ca, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

203. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the seven factors for enlightenment; listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, are the seven factors for enlightenment? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… and so on… the enlightenment factor of equanimity. These, bhikkhus, are the seven factors for enlightenment.” The Second.

3. Ṭhāniyasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on What is Foundational

204. “Kāmarāgaṭṭhāniyānaṃ[M 3.0076][P 5.0084], kāmarāgaṭṭhānīyānaṃ (sī.) bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppanno ceva kāmacchando uppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati. Byāpādaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppanno ceva byāpādo uppajjati, uppanno ca byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya [T 5.0121] vepullāya saṃvattati. Thinamiddhaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca thinamiddhaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāyaṃ saṃvattati. Uddhaccakukkuccaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati. Vicikicchāṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppannā ceva vicikicchā uppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati.

204. “Bhikkhus, by frequently attending to things that are a foundation for sensual passion, unarisen sensual desire arises, and arisen sensual desire increases and expands. By frequently attending to things that are a foundation for ill will, unarisen ill will arises, and arisen ill will increases and expands. By frequently attending to things that are a foundation for sloth and torpor, unarisen sloth and torpor arise, and arisen sloth and torpor increase and expand. By frequently attending to things that are a foundation for restlessness and remorse, unarisen restlessness and remorse arise, and arisen restlessness and remorse increase and expand. By frequently attending to things that are a foundation for doubt, unarisen doubt arises, and arisen doubt increases and expands.”

“Satisambojjhaṅgaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati…pe… [V 3.0104] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṭṭhāniyānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ manasikārabahulīkārā anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, by frequently attending to things that are a foundation for the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness arises, and the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness is brought to fulfillment by development... and so on... Bhikkhus, by frequently attending to things that are a foundation for the enlightenment factor of equanimity, the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity arises, and the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity is brought to fulfillment by development.” The Third.

4. Ayonisomanasikārasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Unwise Attention

205. “Ayoniso, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando uppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati; anuppanno [P 5.0085] ceva byāpādo uppajjati, uppanno ca byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati; anuppannañceva [T 5.0122] thinamiddhaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca thinamiddhaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati; anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati; anuppannā ceva vicikicchā uppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati; anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo nuppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo nirujjhati…pe… anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo nuppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo nirujjhati.

205. “Bhikkhus, for one who attends unwisely, unarisen sensual desire arises, and arisen sensual desire conduces to growth and expansion; unarisen ill will arises, and arisen ill will conduces to growth and expansion; unarisen sloth and torpor arise, and arisen sloth and torpor conduce to growth and expansion; unarisen restlessness and remorse arise, and arisen restlessness and remorse conduce to growth and expansion; unarisen doubt arises, and arisen doubt conduces to growth and expansion; the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness does not arise, and the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness ceases… and so on… the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity does not arise, and the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity ceases.

Yoniso [M 3.0077] ca kho, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando nuppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando pahīyati; anuppanno ceva byāpādo nuppajjati, uppanno ca byāpādo pahīyati; anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṃ nuppajjati, uppannañca thinamiddhaṃ pahīyati; anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṃ [V 3.0105] nuppajjati, uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahīyati; anuppannā ceva vicikicchā nuppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā pahīyati.

But, Bhikkhus, for one who attends wisely, unarisen sensual desire does not arise, and arisen sensual desire is abandoned; unarisen ill will does not arise, and arisen ill will is abandoned; unarisen sloth and torpor do not arise, and arisen sloth and torpor are abandoned; unarisen restlessness and remorse do not arise, and arisen restlessness and remorse are abandoned; unarisen doubt does not arise, and arisen doubt is abandoned.

“Anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati…pe… anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“The unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness arises, and the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness goes to the fulfillment of development... and so on... the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity arises, and the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity goes to the fulfillment of development.” The Fourth.

5. Aparihāniyasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Non-Decline

206. “Satta [T 5.0123] vo, bhikkhave, aparihāniye dhamme desessāmi; taṃ suṇātha. Katame [P 5.0086] ca, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniyā dhammā? Yadidaṃ – satta bojjhaṅgā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ime kho, bhikkhave, satta aparihāniyā dhammā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

206. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you seven principles that lead to non-decline; listen to that. And what, Bhikkhus, are the seven principles that lead to non-decline? They are these: the seven factors of enlightenment. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness... and so on... the enlightenment factor of equanimity. These, Bhikkhus, are the seven principles that lead to non-decline.” The Fifth.

6. Taṇhakkhayasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Destruction of Craving

207. “Yo, bhikkhave, maggo yā paṭipadā taṇhakkhayāya saṃvattati, taṃ maggaṃ taṃ paṭipadaṃ bhāvetha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, maggo katamā ca paṭipadā taṇhakkhayāya saṃvattati? Yadidaṃ – satta bojjhaṅgā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”ti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā udāyī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kathaṃ bhāvitā nu kho, bhante, satta bojjhaṅgā, kathaṃ bahulīkatā taṇhakkhayāya saṃvattantī”ti?

207. “Bhikkhus, you should develop the path and the practice that lead to the destruction of craving. And what, Bhikkhus, is the path, and what is the practice that leads to the destruction of craving? It is these: the seven factors of enlightenment. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness... and so on... the enlightenment factor of equanimity.” When this was said, the Venerable Udāyī said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, how is it that the seven factors of enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, lead to the destruction of craving?”

“Idha[V 3.0106], udāyi, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ abyāpajjaṃ abyāpajjhaṃ (sī. syā. pī.). Tassa satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvayato vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ abyāpajjaṃ taṇhā pahīyati. Taṇhāya pahānā kammaṃ pahīyati. Kammassa pahānā dukkhaṃ pahīyati…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ [M 3.0078] nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ abyāpajjaṃ. Tassa upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvayato vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ abyāpajjaṃ taṇhā pahīyati [P 5.0087] taṇhāya pahānā kammaṃ pahīyati[V 3.0107]. Kammassa pahānā dukkhaṃ pahīyati. Iti kho, udāyi, taṇhakkhayā kammakkhayo, kammakkhayā dukkhakkhayo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Here, Udāyī, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment, and is vast, sublime, immeasurable, and free from affliction. For him who develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment, and is vast, sublime, immeasurable, and free from affliction, craving is abandoned. Due to the abandonment of craving, kamma is abandoned. Due to the abandonment of kamma, suffering is abandoned... and so on... he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment, and is vast, sublime, immeasurable, and free from affliction. For him who develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity that is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment, and is vast, sublime, immeasurable, and free from affliction, craving is abandoned. Due to the abandonment of craving, kamma is abandoned. Due to the abandonment of kamma, suffering is abandoned. Thus indeed, Udāyī, from the destruction of craving comes the destruction of kamma; from the destruction of kamma comes the destruction of suffering.” Sixth.

7. Taṇhānirodhasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Cessation of Craving

208. “Yo[T 5.0124], bhikkhave, maggo yā paṭipadā taṇhānirodhāya saṃvattati, taṃ maggaṃ taṃ paṭipadaṃ bhāvetha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, maggo katamā ca paṭipadā taṇhānirodhāya saṃvattati? Yadidaṃ – satta bojjhaṅgā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo. Kathaṃ bhāvitā, ca bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṃ bahulīkatā taṇhānirodhāya saṃvattanti?

208. “Bhikkhus, you should develop the path and the practice that lead to the cessation of craving. And what, Bhikkhus, is the path, what is the practice that leads to the cessation of craving? It is these: the seven factors of enlightenment. What are the seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… and so on... the enlightenment factor of equanimity. And how, Bhikkhus, are the seven factors of enlightenment developed and cultivated so that they lead to the cessation of craving?”

“Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṃ bahulīkatā taṇhānirodhāya saṃvattantī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Here, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminates in relinquishment… and so on... he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminates in relinquishment. Thus developed, Bhikkhus, thus cultivated, the seven factors of enlightenment lead to the cessation of craving.” Seventh.

8. Nibbedhabhāgiyasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse Pertaining to Penetration

209. “Nibbedhabhāgiyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, maggaṃ desessāmi; taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, nibbedhabhāgiyo maggo? Yadidaṃ – satta bojjhaṅgā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo”ti. Evaṃ vutte āyasmā udāyī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kathaṃ bhāvitā nu kho, bhante, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṃ bahulīkatā nibbedhāya saṃvattantī”ti?

209. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the path pertaining to penetration; listen to it. And what, Bhikkhus, is the path pertaining to penetration? It is these: the seven factors of enlightenment. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… and so on… the enlightenment factor of equanimity.” When this was said, the Venerable Udāyī said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, how is it that the seven factors of enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, conduce to penetration?”

“Idha, udāyi, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ [P 5.0088] abyāpajjaṃ. So satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvitena cittena anibbiddhapubbaṃ appadālitapubbaṃ lobhakkhandhaṃ nibbijjhati padāleti[V 3.0108]; anibbiddhapubbaṃ appadālitapubbaṃ [T 5.0125] dosakkhandhaṃ nibbijjhati padāleti; anibbiddhapubbaṃ appadālitapubbaṃ mohakkhandhaṃ nibbijjhati padāleti…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ [M 3.0079] vossaggapariṇāmiṃ vipulaṃ mahaggataṃ appamāṇaṃ abyāpajjaṃ. So upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāvitena cittena anibbiddhapubbaṃ appadālitapubbaṃ lobhakkhandhaṃ nibbijjhati padāleti; anibbiddhapubbaṃ appadālitapubbaṃ dosakkhandhaṃ nibbijjhati padāleti; anibbiddhapubbaṃ appadālitapubbaṃ mohakkhandhaṃ nibbijjhati padāleti. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, udāyi, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṃ bahulīkatā nibbedhāya saṃvattantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Here, Udāyī, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment, and is vast, exalted, immeasurable, and free from affliction. With a mind developed in the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, he penetrates and shatters the mass of greed that was not previously penetrated or shattered; he penetrates and shatters the mass of hatred that was not previously penetrated or shattered; he penetrates and shatters the mass of delusion that was not previously penetrated or shattered… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment, and is vast, exalted, immeasurable, and free from affliction. With a mind developed in the enlightenment factor of equanimity, he penetrates and shatters the mass of greed that was not previously penetrated or shattered; he penetrates and shatters the mass of hatred that was not previously penetrated or shattered; he penetrates and shatters the mass of delusion that was not previously penetrated or shattered. Thus developed, Udāyī, and thus frequently practiced, the seven factors of enlightenment conduce to penetration.” The Eighth.

9. Ekadhammasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on One Thing

210. “Nāhaṃ[V 3.0109], bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi, yo evaṃ bhāvito bahulīkato saṃyojanīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya saṃvattati, yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo. Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṃ bahulīkatā saṃyojanīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya saṃvattanti?

210. “Monks, I do not see even one other thing that, when thus developed and frequently practiced, leads to the abandoning of the phenomena that are the objects of the fetters, as are these seven factors of enlightenment. What are the seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness... the enlightenment factor of equanimity. And how, monks, are the seven factors of enlightenment developed and frequently practiced so that they lead to the abandoning of the phenomena that are the objects of the fetters?”

“Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṃ bahulīkatā saṃyojanīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya saṃvattanti.

“Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion... he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. Thus, monks, when these seven factors of enlightenment are developed in this way and frequently practiced in this way, they lead to the abandoning of the phenomena that are the objects of the fetters.”

“Katame [T 5.0126][P 5.0089] ca, bhikkhave, saṃyojanīyā dhammā? Cakkhu, bhikkhave, saṃyojanīyo dhammo. Etthete uppajjanti saṃyojanavinibandhā ajjhosānā…pe… jivhā saṃyojanīyā dhammā. Etthete uppajjanti saṃyojanavinibandhā ajjhosānā…pe… mano saṃyojanīyo dhammo. Etthete uppajjanti saṃyojanavinibandhā ajjhosānā. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, saṃyojanīyā dhammā”ti. Navamaṃ.

“And what, monks, are the phenomena that are the objects of the fetters? The eye, monks, is a phenomenon that is an object of the fetters. Herein arise those bonds of the fetters and attachments... The tongue is a phenomenon that is an object of the fetters. Herein arise those bonds of the fetters and attachments... The mind is a phenomenon that is an object of the fetters. Herein arise those bonds of the fetters and attachments. These, monks, are called the phenomena that are the objects of the fetters.” The Ninth.

10. Udāyisuttaṃ

10. The Discourse with Udāyī

211. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sumbhesu viharati setakaṃ nāma sumbhānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho āyasmā udāyī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā udāyī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

211. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sumbhas, at a market town of the Sumbhas named Setaka. Then the Venerable Udāyī approached the Blessed One… and having sat down to one side, the Venerable Udāyī said this to the Blessed One:

“Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Yāva bahukatañca me, bhante, bhagavati pemañca gāravo [V 3.0110] ca hirī ca ottappañca. Ahañhi, bhante, pubbe agārikabhūto samāno [M 3.0080] abahukato ahosiṃ dhammena dhamme (?) abahukato saṅghena. So khvāhaṃ bhagavati pemañca gāravañca hiriñca ottappañca sampassamāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito. Tassa me bhagavā dhammaṃ desesi – ‘iti rūpaṃ, iti rūpassa samudayo, iti rūpassa atthaṅgamo; iti vedanā…pe… iti saññā… iti saṅkhārā… iti viññāṇaṃ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti.

“It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is amazing, venerable sir! How very beneficial to me, venerable sir, have been this affection, respect, moral shame, and moral dread towards the Blessed One! For formerly, venerable sir, when I was a householder, I did not have high esteem for the Dhamma, and I did not have high esteem for the Saṅgha. But I, clearly perceiving this affection, respect, moral shame, and moral dread for the Blessed One, went forth from the household life into homelessness. To me, the Blessed One taught the Dhamma: ‘Such is form, such is the origin of form, such is the cessation of form; such is feeling… such is perception… such are formations… such is consciousness, such is the origin of consciousness, such is the cessation of consciousness.’”

“So khvāhaṃ, bhante, suññāgāragato imesaṃ pañcupādānakkhandhānaṃ [T 5.0127] ukkujjāvakujjaṃ samparivattento ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti [P 5.0090] yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ. Dhammo ca me, bhante, abhisamito, maggo ca me paṭiladdho; yo me bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṃ tathattāya upanessati yathāhaṃ – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānissāmi.

“Then, venerable sir, having gone to a secluded place, while repeatedly reflecting on the arising and passing away of these five aggregates subject to clinging, I directly knew as it really is: ‘This is suffering’; I directly knew as it really is: ‘This is the origin of suffering’; I directly knew as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering’; I directly knew as it really is: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ The Dhamma has been realized by me, venerable sir, and the path has been attained by me; which, having been developed and frequently practiced by me, will lead me, dwelling thus, to that state whereby I will know: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”

“Satisambojjhaṅgo me, bhante, paṭiladdho, yo me bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṃ tathattāya upanessati yathāhaṃ – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānissāmi…pe… [V 3.0111] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo me, bhante, paṭiladdho, yo me bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṃ tathattāya upanessati yathāhaṃ – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānissāmi. Ayaṃ kho me, bhante, maggo paṭiladdho, yo me bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṃ tathattāya upanessati yathāhaṃ – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānissāmī”ti.

“Venerable sir, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness has been attained by me; which, having been developed and cultivated by me, will lead me, while dwelling in such and such a way, to that state wherein I shall know: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’ ... The enlightenment factor of equanimity has been attained by me, venerable sir; which, having been developed and cultivated by me, will lead me, while dwelling in such and such a way, to that state wherein I shall know: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’ This, indeed, is the path that has been attained by me, venerable sir; which, having been developed and cultivated by me, will lead me, while dwelling in such and such a way, to that state wherein I shall know: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”

“Sādhu sādhu, udāyi! Eso hi te, udāyi, maggo paṭiladdho, yo te bhāvito bahulīkato tathā tathā viharantaṃ tathattāya upanessati yathā tvaṃ – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ [T 5.0128] karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānissasī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Good, good, Udāyī! This, indeed, is the path that has been attained by you, Udāyī; which, having been developed and frequently practiced by you, will lead you, while dwelling in such and such a way, to that very state wherein you shall know: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no other for this state of being.’” The Tenth.

Udāyivaggo tatiyo.

The Udāyī Chapter, the Third.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this:

Bodhāya [M 3.0081] desanā ṭhānā, ayoniso cāparihānī;

Khayo nirodho nibbedho, ekadhammo udāyināti.

Bodhāya, Desanā, and Ṭhāna; Ayoniso and Aparihāni; Khaya, Nirodha, and Nibbedha; Ekadhamma, and Udāyī.

4. Nīvaraṇavaggo

4. The Chapter on the Hindrances

1. Paṭhamakusalasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on the Wholesome

212. “Ye [T 5.0129][P 5.0091] keci, bhikkhave, dhammā kusalā kusalabhāgiyā kusalapakkhikā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā; appamādo tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aggamakkhāyati. Appamattassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati.

212. “Bhikkhus, whatever dhammas are wholesome, partake of the wholesome, or are on the side of the wholesome, they all have heedfulness as their root and converge on heedfulness; heedfulness is declared the foremost among them. For a heedful bhikkhu, bhikkhus, this is to be expected: he will develop the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivate them frequently.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti[V 3.0112]? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appamatto satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a heedful bhikkhu develop the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivate them frequently? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness based on seclusion… and so on… the enlightenment factor of equanimity based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a heedful bhikkhu develops the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivates them frequently.” First.

2. Dutiyakusalasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on the Wholesome

213. “Ye keci, bhikkhave, dhammā kusalā kusalabhāgiyā kusalapakkhikā, sabbe te yonisomanasikāramūlakā yonisomanasikārasamosaraṇā; yonisomanasikāro tesaṃ dhammānaṃ aggamakkhāyati. Yonisomanasikārasampannassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati.

213. “Bhikkhus, whatever dhammas are wholesome, partake of the wholesome, or are on the side of the wholesome, they all have wise attention as their root and converge on wise attention; wise attention is declared the foremost among them. For a bhikkhu endowed with wise attention, bhikkhus, this is to be expected: he will develop the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivate them frequently.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno satta bojjhaṅge [T 5.0130] bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave[M 3.0082], bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu endowed with wise attention develop the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivate them frequently? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness based on seclusion… and so on… the enlightenment factor of equanimity based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu endowed with wise attention develops the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivates them frequently.” Second.

3. Upakkilesasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Corruptions

214. “Pañcime[P 5.0092], bhikkhave, jātarūpassa upakkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhaṃ jātarūpaṃ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṃ, na ca pabhassaraṃ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā upeti kammāya. Katame pañca? Ayo, bhikkhave, jātarūpassa upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhaṃ jātarūpaṃ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṃ, na ca pabhassaraṃ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā upeti kammāya. Lohaṃ, bhikkhave, jātarūpassa upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhaṃ jātarūpaṃ…pe… tipu, bhikkhave, jātarūpassa upakkileso…pe… [V 3.0113] sīsaṃ, bhikkhave, jātarūpassa upakkileso…pe… sajjhu, bhikkhave, jātarūpassa upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhaṃ jātarūpaṃ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṃ, na ca pabhassaraṃ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā upeti kammāya. Ime [T 5.0131] kho, bhikkhave, pañca jātarūpassa upakkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhaṃ jātarūpaṃ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṃ, na ca pabhassaraṃ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā upeti kammāya.

214. “Bhikkhus, there are these five corruptions of gold, by which gold, being corrupted, is neither soft nor workable, nor radiant; it is brittle and does not properly lend itself to being worked. What five? Iron, bhikkhus, is a corruption of gold, by which gold, being corrupted, is neither soft nor workable, nor radiant; it is brittle and does not properly lend itself to being worked. Copper, bhikkhus, is a corruption of gold… and so on… Tin, bhikkhus, is a corruption of gold… Lead, bhikkhus, is a corruption of gold… Silver, bhikkhus, is a corruption of gold, by which gold, being corrupted, is neither soft nor workable, nor radiant; it is brittle and does not properly lend itself to being worked. These, bhikkhus, are the five corruptions of gold, by which gold, being corrupted, is neither soft nor workable, nor radiant; it is brittle and does not properly lend itself to being worked.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, pañcime cittassa upakkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhaṃ cittaṃ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṃ, na ca pabhassaraṃ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā samādhiyati āsavānaṃ khayāya. Katame pañca? Kāmacchando, bhikkhave, cittassa upakkileso, yena upakkilesena upakkiliṭṭhaṃ cittaṃ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṃ, na ca pabhassaraṃ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā samādhiyati āsavānaṃ khayāya…pe… ime [P 5.0093] kho, bhikkhave, pañca cittassa upekkilesā, yehi upakkilesehi upakkiliṭṭhaṃ cittaṃ na ceva mudu hoti na ca kammaniyaṃ, na ca pabhassaraṃ pabhaṅgu ca, na ca sammā samādhiyati āsavānaṃ khayāyā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Just so, bhikkhus, these are the five defilements of the mind, by which a defiled mind is neither soft nor workable, nor luminous; it is brittle and is not rightly concentrated for the destruction of the taints. What five? Sensual desire, bhikkhus, is a defilement of the mind, by which a defiled mind is neither soft nor workable, nor luminous; it is brittle and is not rightly concentrated for the destruction of the taints… and so on… These, bhikkhus, are the five defilements of the mind, by which a defiled mind is neither soft nor workable, nor luminous; it is brittle and is not rightly concentrated for the destruction of the taints.” Third.

4. Anupakkilesasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Non-Defilement

215. “Sattime[V 3.0114], bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti[T 5.0132]. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo [M 3.0083] cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattati…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattantī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

215. “Bhikkhus, these seven factors of enlightenment are non-obstructing, non-hindering, not defilements of the mind; when developed and cultivated, they conduce to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness, bhikkhus, is non-obstructing, non-hindering, not a defilement of the mind; when developed and cultivated, it conduces to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation… and so on… The enlightenment factor of equanimity, bhikkhus, is non-obstructing, non-hindering, not a defilement of the mind; when developed and cultivated, it conduces to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation. These, bhikkhus, are the seven factors of enlightenment that are non-obstructing, non-hindering, not defilements of the mind; when developed and cultivated, they conduce to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation.” Fourth.

5. Ayonisomanasikārasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Unwise Attention

216. “Ayoniso, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva kāmacchando uppajjati, uppanno ca kāmacchando bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati; anuppanno ceva byāpādo uppajjati, uppanno ca byāpādo bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati; anuppannañceva thinamiddhaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca thinamiddhaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati; anuppannañceva uddhaccakukkuccaṃ uppajjati, uppannañca uddhaccakukkuccaṃ bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattati; anuppannā [P 5.0094] ceva vicikicchā uppajjati, uppannā ca vicikicchā [T 5.0133] bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya saṃvattatī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

216. “Bhikkhus, for one who attends unwisely, unarisen sensual desire arises, and arisen sensual desire conduces to its great increase and expansion; unarisen ill will arises, and arisen ill will conduces to its great increase and expansion; unarisen sloth and torpor arises, and arisen sloth and torpor conduces to its great increase and expansion; unarisen restlessness and remorse arises, and arisen restlessness and remorse conduces to its great increase and expansion; unarisen doubt arises, and arisen doubt conduces to its great increase and expansion.” The fifth.

6. Yonisomanasikārasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Wise Attention

217. “Yoniso [V 3.0115] ca kho, bhikkhave, manasikaroto anuppanno ceva satisambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca satisambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati…pe… anuppanno ceva upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo uppajjati, uppanno ca upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchatī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

217. “Indeed, Bhikkhus, for one who attends wisely, the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness arises, and the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness goes to the completion of its development… the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity arises, and the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity goes to the completion of its development.” The sixth.

7. Buddhisuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Growth

218. “Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā buddhiyā aparihānāya saṃvattanti. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo. Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā buddhiyā aparihānāya saṃvattantī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

218. “Bhikkhus, these seven factors of enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, conduce to growth and non-decline. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… the enlightenment factor of equanimity. These, Bhikkhus, are the seven factors of enlightenment that, when developed and cultivated, conduce to growth and non-decline.” The seventh.

8. Āvaraṇanīvaraṇasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Obstructions and Hindrances

219. “Pañcime, bhikkhave, āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso upakkilesā paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā. Katame pañca? Kāmacchando, bhikkhave, āvaraṇo nīvaraṇo [M 3.0084] cetaso upakkileso paññāya dubbalīkaraṇo. Byāpādo, bhikkhave, āvaraṇo nīvaraṇo cetaso upakkileso paññāya dubbalīkaraṇo. Thinamiddhaṃ, bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ cetaso upakkilesaṃ paññāya dubbalīkaraṇaṃ. Uddhaccakukkuccaṃ[P 5.0095], bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ cetaso upakkilesaṃ paññāya dubbalīkaraṇaṃ. Vicikicchā, bhikkhave, āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso upakkilesā [V 3.0116] paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso upakkilesā paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā.

219. “Bhikkhus, these five are obstructors, hindrances, defilements of the mind, and weakeners of wisdom. What five? Sensual desire, Bhikkhus, is an obstructor, a hindrance, a defilement of the mind, and a weakener of wisdom. Ill will, Bhikkhus, is an obstructor, a hindrance, a defilement of the mind, and a weakener of wisdom. Sloth and torpor, Bhikkhus, is an obstructor, a hindrance, a defilement of the mind, and a weakener of wisdom. Restlessness and remorse, Bhikkhus, is an obstructor, a hindrance, a defilement of the mind, and a weakener of wisdom. Doubt, Bhikkhus, is an obstructor, a hindrance, a defilement of the mind, and a weakener of wisdom. These, indeed, Bhikkhus, are the five obstructors, hindrances, defilements of the mind, and weakeners of wisdom.

“Sattime[T 5.0134], bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattati…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anupakkileso bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anupakkilesā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattantīti.

“Bhikkhus, these seven factors of enlightenment are non-obstructors, non-hindrances, and non-defilements of the mind; when developed and cultivated, they conduce to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation. What seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness, Bhikkhus, is a non-obstructor, a non-hindrance, and a non-defilement of the mind; when developed and cultivated, it conduces to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation… The enlightenment factor of equanimity, Bhikkhus, is a non-obstructor, a non-hindrance, and a non-defilement of the mind; when developed and cultivated, it conduces to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation. These, indeed, Bhikkhus, are the seven factors of enlightenment that are non-obstructors, non-hindrances, and non-defilements of the mind; when developed and cultivated, they conduce to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation.”

“Yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbaṃ cetaso samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti, imassa pañca nīvaraṇā tasmiṃ samaye na honti. Satta bojjhaṅgā tasmiṃ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

“Bhikkhus, at a time when a noble disciple listens to the Dhamma—taking it to heart, applying his mind, focusing his entire mind, and lending an attentive ear—at that time the five hindrances are not present in him. At that time, the seven factors of enlightenment reach the fulfillment of their development.”

“Katame pañca nīvaraṇā tasmiṃ samaye na honti? Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ tasmiṃ samaye na hoti, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ tasmiṃ samaye na hoti, thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ tasmiṃ samaye na hoti, uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ tasmiṃ samaye na hoti, vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ tasmiṃ samaye na hoti. Imassa pañca nīvaraṇā tasmiṃ samaye na honti.

“Which five hindrances are not present at that time? The hindrance of sensual desire is not present at that time; the hindrance of ill will is not present at that time; the hindrance of sloth and torpor is not present at that time; the hindrance of restlessness and remorse is not present at that time; the hindrance of doubt is not present at that time. For this one, these five hindrances are not present at that time.”

“Katame satta bojjhaṅgā tasmiṃ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti[T 5.0135]? Satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati…pe… [V 3.0117] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Ime satta bojjhaṅgā tasmiṃ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti. Yasmiṃ[P 5.0096], bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako aṭṭhiṃ katvā manasi katvā sabbaṃ cetaso samannāharitvā ohitasoto [M 3.0085] dhammaṃ suṇāti, imassa pañca nīvaraṇā tasmiṃ samaye na honti. Ime satta bojjhaṅgā tasmiṃ samaye bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Which seven factors of enlightenment reach the culmination of development at that time? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness reaches the culmination of development at that time… the enlightenment factor of equanimity reaches the culmination of development at that time. These seven factors of enlightenment reach the culmination of development at that time. Bhikkhus, at a time when a noble disciple, having made it a matter of importance, having attended to it, having brought it all together in his mind, listens to the Dhamma with an attentive ear, for this one the five hindrances are not present at that time. These seven factors of enlightenment reach the culmination of development at that time.” The eighth.

9. Rukkhasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Tree

220. “Santi, bhikkhave, mahārukkhā aṇubījā mahākāyā rukkhānaṃ ajjhāruhā, yehi rukkhā ajjhārūḷhā obhaggavibhaggā vipatitā senti. Katame ca te, bhikkhave, mahārukkhā aṇubījā mahākāyā rukkhānaṃ ajjhāruhā, yehi rukkhā ajjhārūḷhā obhaggavibhaggā vipatitā senti senti. seyyathidaṃ (katthaci)? Assattho, nigrodho, pilakkho, udumbaro, kacchako, kapitthano – ime kho te, bhikkhave, mahārukkhā aṇubījā mahākāyā rukkhānaṃ ajjhāruhā, yehi rukkhā ajjhārūḷhā obhaggavibhaggā vipatitā senti. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco kulaputto yādisake kāme ohāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito hoti, so tādisakehi kāmehi tato vā pāpiṭṭhatarehi obhaggavibhaggo vipatito seti.

220. “Bhikkhus, there are great trees with small seeds and massive bodies that grow over other trees, by which the trees that are grown over lie broken, shattered, and fallen. And what, Bhikkhus, are those great trees with small seeds and massive bodies that grow over other trees, by which the trees that are grown over lie broken, shattered, and fallen? The assattha, the nigrodha, the pilakkha, the udumbara, the kacchako, and the kapitthano. These, Bhikkhus, are the great trees with small seeds and massive bodies that grow over other trees, by which the trees that are grown over lie broken, shattered, and fallen. In the very same way, Bhikkhus, here some clansman, having abandoned sensual pleasures of a certain kind, goes forth from the household life into homelessness. He lies broken, shattered, and fallen on account of such sensual pleasures, or by even worse ones.”

“Pañcime, bhikkhave, āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso ajjhāruhā paññāya [T 5.0136] dubbalīkaraṇā. Katame pañca? Kāmacchando, bhikkhave, āvaraṇo nīvaraṇo cetaso ajjhāruho paññāya dubbalīkaraṇo. Byāpādo, bhikkhave, āvaraṇo nīvaraṇo cetaso ajjhāruho paññāya dubbalīkaraṇo. Thinamiddhaṃ, bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ cetaso ajjhāruhaṃ paññāya dubbalīkaraṇaṃ. Uddhaccakukkuccaṃ, bhikkhave, āvaraṇaṃ nīvaraṇaṃ cetaso ajjhāruhaṃ paññāya dubbalīkaraṇaṃ. Vicikicchā, bhikkhave, āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso ajjhāruhā paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā. Ime kho, bhikkhave[P 5.0097], pañca āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā cetaso ajjhāruhā paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā.

Bhikkhus, these five are obstructions, hindrances, that overwhelm the mind and weaken wisdom. What five? Bhikkhus, sensual desire is an obstruction, a hindrance, that overwhelms the mind and weakens wisdom. Ill will is an obstruction, a hindrance, that overwhelms the mind and weakens wisdom. Sloth and torpor is an obstruction, a hindrance, that overwhelms the mind and weakens wisdom. Restlessness and remorse is an obstruction, a hindrance, that overwhelms the mind and weakens wisdom. Doubt is an obstruction, a hindrance, that overwhelms the mind and weakens wisdom. These, indeed, bhikkhus, are the five obstructions, hindrances, that overwhelm the mind and weaken wisdom.

“Sattime[V 3.0118], bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anajjhāruhā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo anīvaraṇo cetaso anajjhāruho bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattati…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, anāvaraṇo [M 3.0086] anīvaraṇo cetaso anajjhāruho bhāvito bahulīkato vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā anāvaraṇā anīvaraṇā cetaso anajjhāruhā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattantī”ti. Navamaṃ.

Bhikkhus, these seven factors for awakening are non-obstructing, non-hindering, and do not overwhelm the mind; when developed and frequently practiced, they conduce to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation. What seven? Bhikkhus, the factor for awakening of mindfulness is non-obstructing, non-hindering, and does not overwhelm the mind; when developed and frequently practiced, it conduces to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation. … Bhikkhus, the factor for awakening of equanimity is non-obstructing, non-hindering, and does not overwhelm the mind; when developed and frequently practiced, it conduces to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation. These, indeed, bhikkhus, are the seven factors for awakening that are non-obstructing, non-hindering, and do not overwhelm the mind; when developed and frequently practiced, they conduce to the realization of the fruit of knowledge and liberation.” The ninth.

10. Nīvaraṇasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Hindrances

221. “Pañcime, bhikkhave, nīvaraṇā andhakaraṇā acakkhukaraṇā aññāṇakaraṇā paññānirodhikā vighātapakkhiyā anibbānasaṃvattanikā. Katame pañca? Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ, bhikkhave, andhakaraṇaṃ acakkhukaraṇaṃ aññāṇakaraṇaṃ paññānirodhikaṃ vighātapakkhiyaṃ anibbānasaṃvattanikaṃ[T 5.0137]. Byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ, bhikkhave…pe… thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ, bhikkhave… uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ, bhikkhave… vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ, bhikkhave, andhakaraṇaṃ acakkhukaraṇaṃ aññāṇakaraṇaṃ paññānirodhikaṃ vighātapakkhiyaṃ anibbānasaṃvattanikaṃ. Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇā andhakaraṇā acakkhukaraṇā aññāṇakaraṇā paññānirodhikā vighātapakkhiyā anibbānasaṃvattanikā.

221. Bhikkhus, these five hindrances are blinding, non-vision-producing, ignorance-producing, destructive to wisdom, siding with distress, and not conducive to Nibbāna. What five? The hindrance of sensual desire, bhikkhus, is blinding, non-vision-producing, ignorance-producing, destructive to wisdom, siding with distress, and not conducive to Nibbāna. The hindrance of ill will, bhikkhus… the hindrance of sloth and torpor… the hindrance of restlessness and remorse… the hindrance of doubt, bhikkhus, is blinding, non-vision-producing, ignorance-producing, destructive to wisdom, siding with distress, and not conducive to Nibbāna. These, indeed, bhikkhus, are the five hindrances that are blinding, non-vision-producing, ignorance-producing, destructive to wisdom, siding with distress, and not conducive to Nibbāna.

“Sattime, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅgā cakkhukaraṇā ñāṇakaraṇā paññābuddhiyā avighātapakkhiyā nibbānasaṃvattanikā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, cakkhukaraṇo ñāṇakaraṇo paññābuddhiyo avighātapakkhiyo nibbānasaṃvattaniko…pe… [V 3.0119] upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo, bhikkhave, cakkhukaraṇo ñāṇakaraṇo paññābuddhiyo avighātapakkhiyo nibbānasaṃvattaniko. Ime kho, bhikkhave[P 5.0098], satta bojjhaṅgā cakkhukaraṇā ñāṇakaraṇā paññābuddhiyā avighātapakkhiyā nibbānasaṃvattanikā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

Bhikkhus, these seven factors for awakening are vision-producing, knowledge-producing, causing wisdom to grow, siding with non-distress, and conducive to Nibbāna. What seven? The factor for awakening of mindfulness, bhikkhus, is vision-producing, knowledge-producing, causing wisdom to grow, siding with non-distress, and conducive to Nibbāna… The factor for awakening of equanimity, bhikkhus, is vision-producing, knowledge-producing, causing wisdom to grow, siding with non-distress, and conducive to Nibbāna. These, indeed, bhikkhus, are the seven factors for awakening that are vision-producing, knowledge-producing, causing wisdom to grow, siding with non-distress, and conducive to Nibbāna.” The tenth.

Nīvaraṇavaggo catuttho.

The fourth chapter, on the Hindrances.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Dve kusalā kilesā ca, dve yoniso ca buddhi ca;

Āvaraṇā nīvaraṇā rukkhaṃ, nīvaraṇañca te dasāti.

Two on the Wholesome, and Defilements; two on Proper Application, and Wisdom; Obstruction, Hindrance, the Tree, and Hindrance—these are the ten.

5. Cakkavattivaggo

5. The Chapter on the Wheel-Turning Monarch

1. Vidhāsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Conceits

222. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0138][M 3.0087]. “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā tisso vidhā pajahiṃsu, sabbe te sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā tisso vidhā pajahissanti, sabbe te sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā tisso vidhā pajahanti, sabbe te sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Katamesaṃ sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ? Satisambojjhaṅgassa…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā tisso vidhā pajahiṃsu…pe… pajahissanti…pe… pajahanti, sabbe te imesaṃyeva sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

222. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past abandoned the three kinds of conceit, all of them did so because of having developed and cultivated the seven factors for awakening. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will abandon the three kinds of conceit, all of them will do so because of having developed and cultivated the seven factors for awakening. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the present abandon the three kinds of conceit, all of them do so because of having developed and cultivated the seven factors for awakening. Because of having developed and cultivated which seven factors for awakening? The factor for awakening of mindfulness… the factor for awakening of equanimity. Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past abandoned the three kinds of conceit… will abandon… abandon, all of them did so because of having developed and cultivated these same seven factors for awakening.” The first.

2. Cakkavattisuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Wheel-Turning Monarch

223. “Rañño[V 3.0120][P 5.0099], bhikkhave, cakkavattissa pātubhāvā sattannaṃ ratanānaṃ pātubhāvo hoti. Katamesaṃ sattannaṃ? Cakkaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, hatthiratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, assaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, maṇiratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, itthiratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, gahapatiratanassa pātubhāvo hoti, pariṇāyakaratanassa pātubhāvo hoti[T 5.0139]. Rañño, bhikkhave, cakkavattissa pātubhāvā imesaṃ sattannaṃ ratanānaṃ pātubhāvo hoti.

223. “Bhikkhus, with the appearance of a wheel-turning monarch, there is the appearance of seven treasures. What seven? There is the appearance of the wheel treasure, the elephant treasure, the horse treasure, the jewel treasure, the woman treasure, the householder treasure, and the counselor treasure. Bhikkhus, with the appearance of a wheel-turning monarch, there is the appearance of these seven treasures.

“Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgaratanānaṃ pātubhāvo hoti. Katamesaṃ sattannaṃ? Satisambojjhaṅgassa ratanassa pātubhāvo hoti…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa ratanassa pātubhāvo hoti. Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa imesaṃ sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgaratanānaṃ pātubhāvo hotī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, with the appearance of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, there is the appearance of the seven treasures of the factors for awakening. What seven? There is the appearance of the treasure of the factor for awakening of mindfulness… there is the appearance of the treasure of the factor for awakening of equanimity. Bhikkhus, with the appearance of the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, there is the appearance of these seven treasures of the factors for awakening.” The second.

3. Mārasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Māra

224. “Mārasenappamaddanaṃ [M 3.0088] vo, bhikkhave, maggaṃ desessāmi; taṃ suṇātha. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, mārasenappamaddano maggo? Yadidaṃ – satta bojjhaṅgā. Katame satta? Satisambojjhaṅgo…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo – ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, mārasenappamaddano maggo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

224. “Monks, I will teach you the path that crushes Māra’s army. Listen to it. And what, monks, is the path that crushes Māra’s army? It is these seven factors of enlightenment. Which seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… the enlightenment factor of equanimity. This, monks, is the path that crushes Māra’s army.” Third.

4. Duppaññasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Unwise

225. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘duppañño eḷamūgo, duppañño eḷamūgo’ti[V 3.0121], bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, ‘duppañño eḷamūgo’ti vuccatī”ti? “Sattannaṃ kho, bhikkhu, bojjhaṅgānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā ‘duppañño eḷamūgo’ti vuccati. Katamesaṃ [P 5.0100] sattannaṃ? Satisambojjhaṅgassa…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhu[T 5.0140], sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā ‘duppañño eḷamūgo’ti vuccatī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

225. Then a certain monk approached the Blessed One… and sitting to one side, said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said: ‘Unwise and slow-witted, unwise and slow-witted.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is one called ‘unwise and slow-witted’?” “Monk, one is called ‘unwise and slow-witted’ because of not developing and not cultivating the seven factors of enlightenment. Which seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… the enlightenment factor of equanimity. It is because of not developing and not cultivating these seven factors of enlightenment that one is called ‘unwise and slow-witted.’” Fourth.

5. Paññavantasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Wise

226. “‘Paññavā aneḷamūgo, paññavā aneḷamūgo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, ‘paññavā aneḷamūgo’ti vuccatī”ti? “Sattannaṃ kho, bhikkhu, bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ‘paññavā aneḷamūgo’ti vuccati. Katamesaṃ sattannaṃ? Satisambojjhaṅgassa…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhu, sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ‘paññavā aneḷamūgo’ti vuccatī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

226. “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘Wise and not slow-witted, wise and not slow-witted.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is one called ‘wise and not slow-witted’?” “Monk, one is called ‘wise and not slow-witted’ because of developing and cultivating the seven factors of enlightenment. Which seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… the enlightenment factor of equanimity. It is because of developing and cultivating these seven factors of enlightenment that one is called ‘wise and not slow-witted.’” Fifth.

6. Daliddasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Impoverished

227. “‘Daliddo, daliddo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, ‘daliddo’ti vuccatī”ti? “Sattannaṃ kho, bhikkhu, bojjhaṅgānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā ‘daliddo’ti vuccati. Katamesaṃ sattannaṃ? Satisambojjhaṅgassa…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhu, sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā ‘daliddo’ti vuccatī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

227. “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘impoverished, impoverished.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is one called ‘impoverished’?” “Monk, one is called ‘impoverished’ because of not developing and not cultivating the seven factors of enlightenment. Which seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… the enlightenment factor of equanimity. It is because of not developing and not cultivating these seven factors of enlightenment, monk, that one is called ‘impoverished.’” Sixth.

7. Adaliddasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on One Who is Not Impoverished

228. “‘Adaliddo[M 3.0089], adaliddo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, ‘adaliddo’ti vuccatī”ti? “Sattannaṃ kho, bhikkhu, bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ‘adaliddo’ti vuccati. Katamesaṃ sattannaṃ? Satisambojjhaṅgassa [T 5.0141] …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa – imesaṃ [V 3.0122] kho, bhikkhu, sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ‘adaliddo’ti vuccatī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

228. “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘not impoverished, not impoverished.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is one called ‘not impoverished’?” “Monk, one is called ‘not impoverished’ because of developing and cultivating the seven factors of enlightenment. Which seven? The enlightenment factor of mindfulness… the enlightenment factor of equanimity. It is because of developing and cultivating these seven factors of enlightenment, monk, that one is called ‘not impoverished.’” Seventh.

8. Ādiccasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Sun

229. “Ādiccassa[P 5.0101], bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – aruṇuggaṃ. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ uppādāya etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – kalyāṇamittatā. Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

229. “Monks, for the rising of the sun, this is the forerunner, this is the precursor, that is, the dawn. In the very same way, monks, for the arising of the seven factors of enlightenment, this is the forerunner, this is the precursor, that is, good friendship. For a monk who has a good friend, monks, it is to be expected that he will develop the seven factors of enlightenment and that he will cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment. And how, monks, does a monk who has a good friend develop the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment?
