Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and ripens in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that a monk who has a good friend develops the seven factors of enlightenment and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment.” Eighth.

9. Ajjhattikaṅgasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Internal Factor

230. “Ajjhattikaṃ, bhikkhave, aṅganti karitvā nāññaṃ ekaṅgampi samanupassāmi sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ uppādāya, yathayidaṃ – bhikkhave, yonisomanasikāro. Yonisomanasikārasampannassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno satta bojjhaṅge [T 5.0142] bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti [V 3.0123] vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yonisomanasikārasampanno satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti. Navamaṃ.

230. “Monks, having considered internal factors, I do not see any other single factor for the arising of the seven factors of enlightenment, such as this: appropriate attention. Monks, for a monk who is endowed with appropriate attention, it is to be expected that he will develop and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment. And how, monks, does a monk endowed with appropriate attention develop and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment? Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that a monk endowed with appropriate attention develops and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment.” Ninth.

10. Bāhiraṅgasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the External Factor

231. “Bāhiraṃ[M 3.0090][P 5.0102], bhikkhave, aṅganti karitvā nāññaṃ ekaṅgampi samanupassāmi sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ uppādāya, yathayidaṃ – bhikkhave, kalyāṇamittatā. Kalyāṇamittassetaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – satta bojjhaṅge bhāvessati, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarissati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkaroti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto satta bojjhaṅge bhāveti, satta bojjhaṅge bahulīkarotī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

231. “Monks, having considered external factors, I do not see any other single factor for the arising of the seven factors of enlightenment, such as this: good friendship. Monks, for a monk who has good friends, it is to be expected that he will develop and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment. And how, monks, does a monk with good friends develop and cultivate the seven factors of enlightenment? Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that a monk with good friends develops and cultivates the seven factors of enlightenment.” Tenth.

Cakkavattivaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter on the Wheel-Turning Monarch.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this is:

Vidhā cakkavatti māro, duppañño paññavena ca;

Daliddo adaliddo ca, ādiccaṅgena te dasāti.

Vidhā, Cakkavatti, Māra, the Unwise and the Wise; the Indigent and the Not-Indigent, the Sun, and two on the Factor—these are the ten.

6. Sākacchavaggo

6. 6. The Chapter on Discussion

1. Āhārasuttaṃ

1. 1. The Discourse on Nutriment

232. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0143]. “Pañcannañca, bhikkhave, nīvaraṇānaṃ sattannañca bojjhaṅgānaṃ āhārañca anāhārañca desessāmi; taṃ suṇātha. Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā kāmacchandassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā kāmacchandassa bhiyyobhāvāya [P 5.0103] vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave[V 3.0124], subhanimittaṃ. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā kāmacchandassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā kāmacchandassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

232. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, I will teach the nutriment and non-nutriment for the five hindrances and the seven factors of enlightenment. Listen to that. And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen sensual desire, and for the increase and expansion of arisen sensual desire? There is, monks, the sign of the beautiful. In regard to that, frequent improper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen sensual desire, and for the increase and expansion of arisen sensual desire.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā byāpādassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā byāpādassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, paṭighanimittaṃ[M 3.0091]. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā byāpādassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā byāpādassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen ill will, and for the increase and expansion of arisen ill will? There is, monks, the sign of aversion. In regard to that, frequent improper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen ill will, and for the increase and expansion of arisen ill will.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā thinamiddhassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā thinamiddhassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, arati tandi vijambhitā bhattasammado cetaso ca līnattaṃ. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā thinamiddhassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā thinamiddhassa bhiyyobhāvāya [T 5.0144] vepullāya.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen sloth and torpor, and for the increase and expansion of arisen sloth and torpor? There are, monks, discontent, languor, yawning, drowsiness after a meal, and sluggishness of mind. In regard to these, frequent improper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen sloth and torpor, and for the increase and expansion of arisen sloth and torpor.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, cetaso avūpasamo. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen restlessness and remorse, and for the increase and expansion of arisen restlessness and remorse? There is, monks, an unquieted state of mind. In regard to that, frequent improper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen restlessness and remorse, and for the increase and expansion of arisen restlessness and remorse.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannāya vā vicikicchāya uppādāya, uppannāya vā vicikicchāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, vicikicchāṭṭhānīyā dhammā. Tattha ayonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannāya vā vicikicchāya uppādāya, uppannāya vā vicikicchāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen doubt, and for the increase and expansion of arisen doubt? There are, monks, things that are a basis for doubt. In regard to them, frequent improper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of unarisen doubt, and for the increase and expansion of arisen doubt.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, satisambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyā [P 5.0104] dhammā. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness? There are, monks, things that are a basis for the enlightenment factor of mindfulness. In regard to them, frequent proper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness.

“Ko [V 3.0125] ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya [T 5.0145] pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, kusalākusalā dhammā sāvajjānavajjā dhammā hīnapaṇītā dhammā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of investigation of states, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of investigation of states? There are, monks, wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, and states with dark and bright counterparts. In regard to them, frequent proper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of investigation of states, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of investigation of states.

“Ko [M 3.0092] ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, ārambhadhātu nikkamadhātu parakkamadhātu. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of energy, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of energy? There are, monks, the element of initiative, the element of exertion, and the element of striving. In regard to them, frequent proper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of energy, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of energy.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, pītisambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyā dhammā. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of rapture, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of rapture? There are, monks, things that are a basis for the enlightenment factor of rapture. In regard to them, frequent proper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of rapture, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of rapture.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, kāyappassaddhi cittappassaddhi[T 5.0146]. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of tranquility, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of tranquility? There are, monks, tranquility of body and tranquility of mind. In regard to them, frequent proper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of tranquility, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of tranquility.

“Ko [P 5.0105] ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, samathanimittaṃ abyagganimittaṃ. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

“And what, monks, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of concentration, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of concentration? There are, monks, the sign of calm and the sign of non-distraction. In regard to them, frequent proper attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of concentration, and for the development and fulfillment of the arisen enlightenment factor of concentration.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, āhāro anuppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyā [V 3.0126] dhammā. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamāhāro anuppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity? There are, Bhikkhus, states that are a basis for the enlightenment factor of equanimity. Therein, the frequent practice of wise attention—this is the nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā kāmacchandassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā kāmacchandassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, asubhanimittaṃ[M 3.0093]. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā kāmacchandassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā kāmacchandassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen sensual desire, or for the increase and abundance of arisen sensual desire? There is, Bhikkhus, the sign of the foul. Therein, the frequent practice of wise attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen sensual desire, or for the increase and abundance of arisen sensual desire.

“Ko [T 5.0147] ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā byāpādassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā byāpādassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, mettācetovimutti. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā byāpādassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā byāpādassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen ill will, or for the increase and abundance of arisen ill will? There is, Bhikkhus, the liberation of mind through loving-kindness. Therein, the frequent practice of wise attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen ill will, or for the increase and abundance of arisen ill will.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā thinamiddhassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā thinamiddhassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, ārambhadhātu nikkamadhātu parakkamadhātu. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā thinamiddhassa uppādāya[P 5.0106], uppannassa vā thinamiddhassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen sloth and torpor, or for the increase and abundance of arisen sloth and torpor? There are, Bhikkhus, the element of initiative, the element of setting forth, and the element of striving. Therein, the frequent practice of wise attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen sloth and torpor, or for the increase and abundance of arisen sloth and torpor.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, cetaso vūpasamo. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā uddhaccakukkuccassa bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen restlessness and remorse, or for the increase and abundance of arisen restlessness and remorse? There is, Bhikkhus, the calming of the mind. Therein, the frequent practice of wise attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen restlessness and remorse, or for the increase and abundance of arisen restlessness and remorse.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannāya vā vicikicchāya uppādāya, uppannāya vā vicikicchāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya? Atthi, bhikkhave, kusalākusalā dhammā sāvajjānavajjā dhammā hīnapaṇītā dhammā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā. Tattha yonisomanasikārabahulīkāro [T 5.0148][V 3.0127] – ayamanāhāro anuppannāya vā vicikicchāya uppādāya, uppannāya vā vicikicchāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen doubt, or for the increase and abundance of arisen doubt? There are, Bhikkhus, wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, and states that are dark and bright with their counterparts. Therein, the frequent practice of wise attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of unarisen doubt, or for the increase and abundance of arisen doubt.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, satisambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyā dhammā. Tattha amanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā satisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness? There are, Bhikkhus, states that are a basis for the enlightenment factor of mindfulness. Therein, the frequent practice of non-attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of mindfulness.

“Ko [M 3.0094] ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, kusalākusalā dhammā sāvajjānavajjā dhammā hīnapaṇītā dhammā kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgā dhammā. Tattha amanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena? There are, Bhikkhus, wholesome and unwholesome states, blameworthy and blameless states, inferior and superior states, and states that are dark and bright with their counterparts. Therein, the frequent practice of non-attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa [P 5.0107] bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, ārambhadhātu nikkamadhātu parakkamadhātu. Tattha amanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa [T 5.0149] bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of energy, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of energy? There are, Bhikkhus, the element of initiative, the element of setting forth, and the element of striving. Therein, the frequent practice of non-attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of energy, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of energy.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, pītisambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyā dhammā. Tattha amanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of rapture, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of rapture? There are, Bhikkhus, states that are a basis for the enlightenment factor of rapture. Therein, the frequent practice of non-attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of rapture, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of rapture.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, kāyappassaddhi cittappassaddhi. Tattha amanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, Bhikkhus, is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of tranquility, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of tranquility? There are, Bhikkhus, tranquility of body and tranquility of mind. Therein, the frequent practice of non-attention—this is the non-nutriment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of tranquility, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of tranquility.

“Ko [V 3.0128] ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, samathanimittaṃ abyagganimittaṃ. Tattha amanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya, uppannassa vā samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā.

And what, bhikkhus, is the non-nourishment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of concentration, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of concentration? There is, bhikkhus, the sign of serenity and the sign of non-distraction. Therein, the frequent practice of non-attention—this is the non-nourishment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of concentration, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of concentration.

“Ko ca, bhikkhave, anāhāro anuppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa [T 5.0150] uppādāya, uppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā? Atthi, bhikkhave, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyā dhammā. Tattha amanasikārabahulīkāro – ayamanāhāro anuppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa uppādāya[M 3.0095], uppannassa vā upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya pāripūriyā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is the non-nourishment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity? There are, bhikkhus, states that are the basis for the enlightenment factor of equanimity. Therein, the frequent practice of non-attention—this is the non-nourishment for the arising of the unarisen enlightenment factor of equanimity, or for the fulfillment through development of the arisen enlightenment factor of equanimity. The First.

2. Pariyāyasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Exposition

233. Atha [P 5.0108] kho sambahulā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pavisiṃsu. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “atippago kho tāva sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya carituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyāmā”ti.

233. Then, a number of bhikkhus, having dressed in the morning and taking their bowls and robes, entered Sāvatthī for alms. Then, this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: “It is still too early to go for alms in Sāvatthī. What if we were to approach the park of the wanderers of other sects?”

Atha kho te bhikkhū yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṃ –

Then, those bhikkhus approached the park of the wanderers of other sects. Having approached, they exchanged courteous greetings with those wanderers of other sects. Having concluded their cordial and memorable talk, they sat down to one side. The wanderers of other sects then said this to those bhikkhus who were seated to one side:

“Samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo sāvakānaṃ evaṃ dhammaṃ deseti – ‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvethā’ti. Mayampi kho, āvuso, sāvakānaṃ evaṃ dhammaṃ desema – ‘etha tumhe, āvuso, pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvethā’ti. Idha no, āvuso, ko viseso, ko [T 5.0151] adhippayāso, kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ samaṇassa vā [V 3.0129] gotamassa amhākaṃ vā, yadidaṃ – dhammadesanāya vā dhammadesanaṃ, anusāsaniyā vā anusāsani”nti?

“Friends, the ascetic Gotama teaches his disciples the Dhamma thus: ‘Come, bhikkhus, having abandoned the five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—develop the seven factors of enlightenment as they really are.’ We too, friends, teach our disciples the Dhamma thus: ‘Come, friends, having abandoned the five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—develop the seven factors of enlightenment as they really are.’ Here, friends, what is the distinction, what is the special quality, what is the difference between the ascetic Gotama and us, that is, between his teaching of the Dhamma and ours, or between his instruction and ours?”

Atha kho te bhikkhū tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ bhāsitaṃ neva abhinandiṃsu nappaṭikkosiṃsu; anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃsu – “bhagavato santike etassa bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānissāmā”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ [P 5.0109] nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ –

Then those bhikkhus neither approved of nor rejected the statement of those wanderers of other sects. Without approving or rejecting it, they rose from their seats and departed, thinking: “We shall learn the meaning of this statement in the Blessed One’s presence.” Then, having gone for alms in Sāvatthī and returned from their alms-round after the meal, those bhikkhus approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:

“Idha [M 3.0096] mayaṃ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pavisimha. Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘atippago kho tāva sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya carituṃ, yaṃnūna mayaṃ yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyāmā’ti. Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkamimha; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṃ sammodimha. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdimha. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho amhe, bhante, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṃ –

“Venerable sir, here, in the morning, having dressed and taken our bowls and robes, we entered Sāvatthī for alms. Then, venerable sir, this thought occurred to us: ‘It is still too early to wander for alms in Sāvatthī. What if we were to go to the park of the wanderers of other sects?’ Then, venerable sir, we went to the park of the wanderers of other sects. Having approached, we exchanged greetings with those wanderers of other sects. After concluding our cordial and memorable conversation, we sat down to one side. While we were seated to one side, venerable sir, those wanderers of other sects said this to us:”

“Samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo sāvakānaṃ evaṃ dhammaṃ deseti ‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya [T 5.0152] dubbalīkaraṇe satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvethā’ti. Mayampi kho, āvuso, sāvakānaṃ evaṃ dhammaṃ desema – ‘etha tumhe, āvuso, pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvethā’ti. Idha no, āvuso, ko viseso, ko adhippayāso, kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ samaṇassa vā gotamassa amhākaṃ vā, yadidaṃ – dhammadesanāya vā dhammadesanaṃ, anusāsaniyā vā anusāsani”nti?

“‘Friends, the ascetic Gotama teaches his disciples the Dhamma thus: “Come, bhikkhus, having abandoned the five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—develop the seven factors of enlightenment as they really are.” We too, friends, teach our disciples the Dhamma thus: “Come, friends, having abandoned the five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—develop the seven factors of enlightenment as they really are.” Here, friends, what is the distinction, what is the special quality, what is the difference between the ascetic Gotama and us, that is, between his teaching of the Dhamma and ours, or between his instruction and ours?’”

“Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ bhāsitaṃ neva abhinandimha nappaṭikkosimha, anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamimha – ‘bhagavato santike etassa bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānissāmā’”ti.

“Then, venerable sir, we neither approved of nor rejected the statement of those wanderers of other sects. Without approving or rejecting it, we rose from our seats and departed, thinking: ‘We shall learn the meaning of this statement in the presence of the Blessed One.’”

“Evaṃvādino[V 3.0130], bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘atthi panāvuso, pariyāyo, yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma pañca nīvaraṇā dasa honti, satta bojjhaṅgā catuddasā’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā na ceva sampāyissanti, uttariñca vighātaṃ āpajjissanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yathā taṃ, bhikkhave, avisayasmiṃ. “Nāhaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yo imesaṃ pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena cittaṃ ārādheyya, aññatra tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā ito vā pana sutvā”.

“Bhikkhus, when wanderers of other sects speak thus, they should be addressed thus: ‘Friends, is there a way by which the five hindrances become ten, and the seven factors of enlightenment become fourteen?’ When asked thus, bhikkhus, those wanderers of other sects will be unable to explain and will moreover encounter vexation. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, it is not within their domain. Bhikkhus, I do not see anyone in the world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, who could satisfy the mind with an explanation of these questions, apart from the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata or one who has heard it from them.”

“Katamo [T 5.0153][M 3.0097][P 5.0110] ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo, yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma pañca nīvaraṇā dasa honti? Yadapi, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ kāmacchando tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ, yadapi bahiddhā kāmacchando tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ. ‘Kāmacchandanīvaraṇa’nti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti. Yadapi, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ byāpādo tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ, yadapi bahiddhā byāpādo tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ. ‘Byāpādanīvaraṇa’nti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti. Yadapi, bhikkhave, thinaṃ tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ, yadapi middhaṃ tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ. ‘Thinamiddhanīvaraṇa’nti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti. Yadapi, bhikkhave, uddhaccaṃ tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ, yadapi kukkuccaṃ tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ. ‘Uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇa’nti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti. Yadapi, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ dhammesu vicikicchā tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ, yadapi bahiddhā dhammesu vicikicchā tadapi nīvaraṇaṃ. ‘Vicikicchānīvaraṇa’nti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo, yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma pañca nīvaraṇā dasa honti.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the way by which the five hindrances become ten? Whatever sensual desire is internal, that is a hindrance; whatever sensual desire is external, that is a hindrance. Thus, it comes to be designated as the ‘sensual desire hindrance.’ In this way, it becomes twofold. Whatever ill will is internal, that is a hindrance; whatever ill will is external, that is a hindrance. Thus, it comes to be designated as the ‘ill will hindrance.’ In this way, it becomes twofold. Whatever sloth is, that is a hindrance; whatever torpor is, that is a hindrance. Thus, it comes to be designated as the ‘sloth and torpor hindrance.’ In this way, it becomes twofold. Whatever restlessness is, that is a hindrance; whatever remorse is, that is a hindrance. Thus, it comes to be designated as the ‘restlessness and remorse hindrance.’ In this way, it becomes twofold. Whatever doubt regarding phenomena is internal, that is a hindrance; whatever doubt regarding phenomena is external, that is a hindrance. Thus, it comes to be designated as the ‘doubt hindrance.’ In this way, it becomes twofold. This, bhikkhus, is the way by which the five hindrances become ten.”

“Katamo [T 5.0154] ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo, yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma satta bojjhaṅgā catuddasa honti? Yadapi, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ dhammesu sati tadapi satisambojjhaṅgo, yadapi bahiddhā dhammesu sati tadapi satisambojjhaṅgo. ‘Satisambojjhaṅgo’ti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the way by which the seven factors of enlightenment become fourteen? Whatever mindfulness regarding phenomena is internal, that is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness; whatever mindfulness regarding phenomena is external, that is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness. Thus, it comes to be designated as the ‘enlightenment factor of mindfulness.’ In this way, it becomes twofold.

“Yadapi[P 5.0111], bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ dhammesu paññāya pavicinati pavicināti (ka.) pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati [V 3.0131] tadapi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo, yadapi bahiddhā dhammesu paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati tadapi dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo. ‘Dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo’ti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever one investigates, examines, and arrives at the scrutiny of internal phenomena with wisdom, that is the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena. Whatever one investigates, examines, and arrives at the scrutiny of external phenomena with wisdom, that also is the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena. Thus, it comes to be designated as 'the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena.' In this way, it becomes twofold.

“Yadapi, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ vīriyaṃ tadapi vīriyasambojjhaṅgo, yadapi cetasikaṃ vīriyaṃ tadapi vīriyasambojjhaṅgo. ‘Vīriyasambojjhaṅgo’ti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever bodily energy there is, that is the enlightenment factor of energy. Whatever mental energy there is, that also is the enlightenment factor of energy. Thus, it comes to be designated as 'the enlightenment factor of energy.' In this way, it becomes twofold.

“Yadapi[M 3.0098], bhikkhave, savitakkasavicārā pīti tadapi pītisambojjhaṅgo, yadapi avitakkaavicārā pīti tadapi pītisambojjhaṅgo. ‘Pītisambojjhaṅgo’ti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever rapture there is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, that is the enlightenment factor of rapture. Whatever rapture there is without initial application and sustained application, that also is the enlightenment factor of rapture. Thus, it comes to be designated as 'the enlightenment factor of rapture.' In this way, it becomes twofold.

“Yadapi, bhikkhave, kāyappassaddhi tadapi passaddhisambojjhaṅgo, yadapi cittappassaddhi tadapi passaddhisambojjhaṅgo. ‘Passaddhisambojjhaṅgo’ti [T 5.0155] iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever tranquility of body there is, that is the enlightenment factor of tranquility. Whatever tranquility of mind there is, that also is the enlightenment factor of tranquility. Thus, it comes to be designated as 'the enlightenment factor of tranquility.' In this way, it becomes twofold.

“Yadapi, bhikkhave, savitakko savicāro samādhi tadapi samādhisambojjhaṅgo, yadapi avitakkaavicāro samādhi tadapi samādhisambojjhaṅgo. ‘Samādhisambojjhaṅgo’ti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti.

“Bhikkhus, whatever concentration there is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, that is the enlightenment factor of concentration. Whatever concentration there is without initial application and sustained application, that also is the enlightenment factor of concentration. Thus, it comes to be designated as 'the enlightenment factor of concentration.' In this way, it becomes twofold.

“Yadapi, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ dhammesu upekkhā tadapi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo, yadapi bahiddhā dhammesu upekkhā tadapi upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo. ‘Upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo’ti iti hidaṃ uddesaṃ gacchati. Tadamināpetaṃ pariyāyena dvayaṃ hoti. Ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo, yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma satta bojjhaṅgā catuddasā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, whatever equanimity there is towards internal phenomena, that is the enlightenment factor of equanimity. Whatever equanimity there is towards external phenomena, that also is the enlightenment factor of equanimity. Thus, it comes to be designated as 'the enlightenment factor of equanimity.' In this way, it becomes twofold. This, bhikkhus, is the way by which the seven factors of enlightenment become fourteen.”

3. Aggisuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Fire

234. Atha [P 5.0112] kho sambahulā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiyaṃ [V 3.0132] piṇḍāya pavisiṃsu[V 3.0133]. (Pariyāyasuttasadisaṃ).

234. Then, a number of bhikkhus, having dressed in the morning, took their bowls and robes and entered Sāvatthī for alms. (Similar to the Pariyāya Sutta.)

“Evaṃvādino, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘yasmiṃ, āvuso, samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, katamesaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bojjhaṅgānaṃ akālo bhāvanāya, katamesaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bojjhaṅgānaṃ kālo bhāvanāya? Yasmiṃ panāvuso, samaye uddhataṃ cittaṃ hoti, katamesaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bojjhaṅgānaṃ akālo bhāvanāya, katamesaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bojjhaṅgānaṃ kālo bhāvanāyā’ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhā[T 5.0156], bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā na ceva sampāyissanti, uttariñca vighātaṃ āpajjissanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yathā taṃ, bhikkhave, avisayasmiṃ.

“Bhikkhus, wanderers of other sects who speak thus should be addressed in this way: ‘Friends, at a time when the mind is sluggish, for which factors of awakening is it the wrong time for cultivation, and for which is it the right time for cultivation? And, friends, at a time when the mind is agitated, for which factors of awakening is it the wrong time for cultivation, and for which is it the right time for cultivation?’ When asked thus, bhikkhus, the wanderers of other sects will not be able to answer satisfactorily, and furthermore, they will come to vexation. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, it is not their domain.”

“Nāhaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya yo imesaṃ pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena [M 3.0099] cittaṃ ārādheyya, aññatra tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā ito vā pana sutvā.

“Bhikkhus, I do not see anyone in this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, who could satisfy the mind with an explanation of these questions, except for the Tathāgata, or a disciple of the Tathāgata, or one who has heard it from this dispensation.”

“Yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, akālo tasmiṃ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Līnaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ taṃ etehi dhammehi dussamuṭṭhāpayaṃ hoti.

“Bhikkhus, at a time when the mind is sluggish, it is the wrong time for the cultivation of the tranquility factor of awakening, the wrong time for the cultivation of the concentration factor of awakening, and the wrong time for the cultivation of the equanimity factor of awakening. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, a sluggish mind is difficult to arouse by means of these states.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso parittaṃ aggiṃ ujjāletukāmo assa. So tattha allāni [V 3.0134] ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca gomayāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya[P 5.0113], udakavātañca dadeyya, paṃsukena ca okireyya; bhabbo nu kho so puriso parittaṃ aggiṃ ujjālitu”nti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Suppose, bhikkhus, a man wished to make a small fire blaze. If he were to put wet grass, wet cow-dung, and wet firewood into it, apply a damp wind to it, and scatter dust over it, would that man be able to make the small fire blaze?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṃ samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, akālo tasmiṃ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Līnaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ taṃ etehi dhammehi dussamuṭṭhāpayaṃ hoti.

“Just so, bhikkhus, at a time when the mind is sluggish, it is the wrong time for the cultivation of the tranquility factor of awakening, the wrong time for the cultivation of the concentration factor of awakening, and the wrong time for the cultivation of the equanimity factor of awakening. For what reason? Bhikkhus, a sluggish mind is difficult to arouse by means of these states.”

“Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, kālo tasmiṃ [T 5.0157] samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Līnaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ taṃ etehi dhammehi susamuṭṭhāpayaṃ hoti.

“And, bhikkhus, at a time when the mind is sluggish, it is the right time for the cultivation of the investigation-of-phenomena factor of awakening, the right time for the cultivation of the energy factor of awakening, and the right time for the cultivation of the rapture factor of awakening. For what reason? Bhikkhus, a sluggish mind is easy to arouse by means of these states.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso parittaṃ aggiṃ ujjāletukāmo assa. So tattha sukkhāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni gomayāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya, mukhavātañca dadeyya, na ca paṃsukena okireyya; bhabbo nu kho so puriso parittaṃ aggiṃ ujjālitu”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”.

“Suppose, bhikkhus, a man wished to make a small fire blaze. If he were to put dry grass, dry cow-dung, and dry firewood into it, blow on it with his mouth, and not scatter dust over it, would that man be able to make the small fire blaze?” “Yes, venerable sir.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṃ samaye līnaṃ cittaṃ hoti, kālo tasmiṃ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Līnaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ taṃ etehi dhammehi susamuṭṭhāpayaṃ hoti.

“Just so, bhikkhus, at a time when the mind is sluggish, it is the right time for the cultivation of the investigation-of-phenomena factor of awakening, the right time for the cultivation of the energy factor of awakening, and the right time for the cultivation of the rapture factor of awakening. For what reason? Bhikkhus, a sluggish mind is easy to arouse by means of these states.”

“Yasmiṃ[M 3.0100], bhikkhave, samaye uddhattaṃ cittaṃ hoti, akālo tasmiṃ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa [P 5.0114] bhāvanāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Uddhataṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ taṃ etehi dhammehi duvūpasamayaṃ hoti.

“Bhikkhus, at a time when the mind is agitated, it is the wrong time for the cultivation of the investigation-of-phenomena factor of awakening, the wrong time for the cultivation of the energy factor of awakening, and the wrong time for the cultivation of the rapture factor of awakening. For what reason? Bhikkhus, an agitated mind is difficult to calm by means of these states.”

“Seyyathāpi[V 3.0135], bhikkhave, puriso mahantaṃ aggikkhandhaṃ nibbāpetukāmo assa. So tattha sukkhāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni ca gomayāni pakkhipeyya, sukkhāni ca kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya, mukhavātañca dadeyya, na ca paṃsukena okireyya; bhabbo nu kho so puriso [T 5.0158] mahantaṃ aggikkhandhaṃ nibbāpetu”nti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Suppose, bhikkhus, a man wished to extinguish a great mass of fire. If he were to put dry grass, dry cow-dung, and dry firewood into it, blow on it with his mouth, and not scatter dust over it, would that man be able to extinguish the great mass of fire?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṃ samaye uddhataṃ cittaṃ hoti, akālo tasmiṃ samaye dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo vīriyasambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, akālo pītisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Uddhataṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ taṃ etehi dhammehi duvūpasamayaṃ hoti.

“Just so, bhikkhus, at a time when the mind is agitated, it is the wrong time for the cultivation of the investigation-of-phenomena factor of awakening, the wrong time for the cultivation of the energy factor of awakening, and the wrong time for the cultivation of the rapture factor of awakening. For what reason? Bhikkhus, an agitated mind is difficult to calm by means of these states.”

“Yasmiñca kho, bhikkhave, samaye uddhataṃ cittaṃ hoti, kālo tasmiṃ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Uddhataṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ taṃ etehi dhammehi suvūpasamayaṃ hoti.

“And, bhikkhus, at a time when the mind is agitated, it is the right time for the cultivation of the tranquility factor of awakening, the right time for the cultivation of the concentration factor of awakening, and the right time for the cultivation of the equanimity factor of awakening. For what reason? Bhikkhus, an agitated mind is easy to calm by means of these states.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso mahantaṃ aggikkhandhaṃ nibbāpetukāmo assa. So tattha allāni ceva tiṇāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca gomayāni pakkhipeyya, allāni ca kaṭṭhāni pakkhipeyya, udakavātañca dadeyya, paṃsukena ca okireyya; bhabbo nu kho so puriso mahantaṃ aggikkhandhaṃ nibbāpetu”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”.

“Suppose, bhikkhus, a man wished to extinguish a great mass of fire. If he were to put wet grass, wet cow-dung, and wet firewood into it, apply a damp wind to it, and scatter dust over it, would that man be able to extinguish the great mass of fire?” “Yes, venerable sir.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yasmiṃ samaye uddhataṃ cittaṃ [P 5.0115] hoti, kālo tasmiṃ samaye passaddhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo samādhisambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya, kālo upekkhāsambojjhaṅgassa bhāvanāya. Taṃ kissa hetu? Uddhataṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ taṃ etehi dhammehi suvūpasamayaṃ hoti. Satiñca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sabbatthikaṃ vadāmī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

Even so, bhikkhus, when the mind is agitated, that is the time for the cultivation of the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the time for the cultivation of the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the time for the cultivation of the enlightenment factor of equanimity. For what reason? Bhikkhus, an agitated mind is well calmed by these dhammas. And I declare, bhikkhus, that mindfulness is desirable in all circumstances. Third.

4. Mettāsahagatasuttaṃ

4. Mettāsahagatasutta: The Discourse Accompanied by Loving-Kindness

235. Ekaṃ [T 5.0159][M 3.0101] samayaṃ bhagavā koliyesu viharati haliddavasanaṃ nāma koliyānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya haliddavasanaṃ piṇḍāya pavisiṃsu[V 3.0136]. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “atippago kho tāva haliddavasane piṇḍāya carituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyāmā”ti.

235. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Koliyans, at Haliddavasana, a town of the Koliyans. Then a number of monks, having dressed in the morning and taken their bowls and robes, entered Haliddavasana for alms. Then this thought occurred to those monks: “It is still too early to go for alms in Haliddavasana. It would be good if we were to approach the park of the wanderers of other sects.”

Atha kho te bhikkhū yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṃ –

Then those monks approached the park of the wanderers of other sects. Having approached, they exchanged greetings with those wanderers of other sects. After concluding their courteous and memorable talk, they sat down to one side. When they were seated to one side, the wanderers of other sects said this to those monks:

“Samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo sāvakānaṃ evaṃ dhammaṃ deseti – ‘etha tumhe, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā [P 5.0116] vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharatha. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya [T 5.0160] sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ karuṇāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharatha. Muditāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ muditāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharatha. Upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharathā’”ti.

“Friends, the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma to his disciples thus: ‘Come, monks, having abandoned the five hindrances, which are defilements of the mind and cause the weakening of wisdom, dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness; likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus, above, below, and across, everywhere, for all as for oneself, dwell pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness—vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will. Dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by compassion; likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus, above, below, and across, everywhere, for all as for oneself, dwell pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by compassion—vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will. Dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy; likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus, above, below, and across, everywhere, for all as for oneself, dwell pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy—vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will. Dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by equanimity; likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus, above, below, and across, everywhere, for all as for oneself, dwell pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will.’”

“Mayampi [M 3.0102] kho, āvuso, sāvakānaṃ evaṃ dhammaṃ desema – ‘etha tumhe, āvuso, pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha…pe… karuṇāsahagatena cetasā… muditāsahagatena cetasā… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā [V 3.0137] ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharathā’ti. Idha no, āvuso, ko viseso, ko adhippayāso, kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ samaṇassa vā gotamassa amhākaṃ vā, yadidaṃ – dhammadesanāya [P 5.0117] vā [T 5.0161] dhammadesanaṃ, anusāsaniyā vā anusāsani”nti?

“Friends, we too teach the Dhamma to our disciples thus: ‘Come, friends, having abandoned the five hindrances, which are defilements of the mind and cause the weakening of wisdom, dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness… with a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by sympathetic joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity, dwell pervading one direction; likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus, above, below, and across, everywhere, for all as for oneself, dwell pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, and without ill will.’ Herein, friends, what is the distinction, what is the superiority, what is the difference between the ascetic Gotama and us, regarding the teaching of the Dhamma or the instruction?”

Atha kho te bhikkhū tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ bhāsitaṃ neva abhinandiṃsu nappaṭikkosiṃsu. Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamiṃsu – “bhagavato santike etassa bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānissāmā”ti. Atha kho te bhikkhū haliddavasane piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ –

Then those monks neither approved of nor rejected the statement of those wanderers of other sects. Without approving of or rejecting it, they rose from their seats and departed, thinking: “We shall know the meaning of this statement in the presence of the Blessed One.” Then, having wandered for alms in Haliddavasana and returned from their alms-round, after their meal, those monks approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said this to the Blessed One:

“Idha mayaṃ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya haliddavasane piṇḍāya pavisimha. Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘atippago kho tāva haliddavasane piṇḍāya carituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyāmā’”ti.

“Venerable sir, this morning, having dressed and taken our bowls and robes, we entered Haliddavasana for alms. Then, venerable sir, this thought occurred to us: ‘It is still too early to wander for alms in Haliddavasana. What if we were to go to the park of the wanderers of other sects?’”

“Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkamimha, upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṃ sammodimha. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdimha. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho amhe, bhante, te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṃ –

“Then, venerable sir, we approached the park of the wanderers of other sects. Having approached, we exchanged greetings with those wanderers of other sects. After concluding our courteous and memorable talk, we sat down to one side. When we were seated to one side, venerable sir, those wanderers of other sects said this to us:”

“Samaṇo, āvuso, gotamo sāvakānaṃ evaṃ dhammaṃ deseti – ‘etha [T 5.0162] tumhe, bhikkhave, pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā [M 3.0103] viharatha…pe… karuṇāsahagatena cetasā [V 3.0138]… muditāsahagatena cetasā… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena [P 5.0118] appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharathā’”ti.

‘Friends, the ascetic Gotama teaches the Dhamma to his disciples thus: “Come, monks, having abandoned the five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness… with a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by appreciative joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity, dwell pervading one direction. Likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all as for oneself, dwell pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, without ill will.”’

“Mayampi kho, āvuso, sāvakānaṃ evaṃ dhammaṃ desema – ‘etha tumhe, āvuso, pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha…pe… karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha, tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ; iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā [T 5.0163] viharathā’ti. Idha no, āvuso, ko viseso, ko adhippayāso, kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ samaṇassa vā gotamassa amhākaṃ vā, yadidaṃ, dhammadesanāya vā dhammadesanaṃ, anusāsaniyā vā anusāsani”nti?

‘Friends, we too teach the Dhamma to our disciples thus: “Come, friends, having abandoned the five hindrances—defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom—dwell pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness… with a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by appreciative joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity, dwell pervading one direction. Likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all as for oneself, dwell pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—vast, exalted, immeasurable, without enmity, without ill will.” Here, friends, what is the distinction, what is the special quality, what is the difference between the ascetic Gotama and us, that is, between his teaching of the Dhamma and ours, or his instruction and ours?’

Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ bhāsitaṃ neva abhinandimha nappaṭikkosimha, anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkamimha – ‘bhagavato santike etassa bhāsitassa atthaṃ ājānissāmā’ti.

Then, venerable sir, we neither delighted in nor scorned the statement of those wanderers of other sects. Without delighting in or scorning it, we rose from our seats and departed, thinking: ‘We shall learn the meaning of this statement in the presence of the Blessed One.’

“Evaṃvādino, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘kathaṃ bhāvitā panāvuso, mettācetovimutti, kiṃgatikā hoti, kiṃparamā, kiṃphalā, kiṃpariyosānā? Kathaṃ bhāvitā panāvuso, karuṇācetovimutti, kiṃgatikā hoti, kiṃparamā, kiṃphalā, kiṃpariyosānā? Kathaṃ bhāvitā panāvuso, muditācetovimutti, kiṃgatikā hoti, kiṃparamā, kiṃphalā, kiṃpariyosānā? Kathaṃ bhāvitā panāvuso, upekkhācetovimutti, kiṃgatikā hoti, kiṃparamā, kiṃphalā, kiṃpariyosānā’”ti? Evaṃ puṭṭhā, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā [V 3.0139] paribbājakā na ceva sampāyissanti, uttariñca vighātaṃ āpajjissanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Yathā taṃ, bhikkhave, avisayasmiṃ. “Nāhaṃ taṃ, bhikkhave, passāmi sadevake [M 3.0104] loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yo imesaṃ pañhānaṃ veyyākaraṇena cittaṃ ārādheyya, aññatra tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena [T 5.0164] vā ito vā pana sutvā”.

“Monks, when wanderers of other sects speak thus, they should be addressed as follows: ‘How, friends, is the liberation of mind by loving-kindness cultivated? What is its destination, what its supreme state, what its fruit, what its culmination? How, friends, is the liberation of mind by compassion cultivated? What is its destination, what its supreme state, what its fruit, what its culmination? How, friends, is the liberation of mind by appreciative joy cultivated? What is its destination, what its supreme state, what its fruit, what its culmination? How, friends, is the liberation of mind by equanimity cultivated? What is its destination, what its supreme state, what its fruit, what its culmination?’ When asked thus, monks, those wanderers of other sects will not be able to answer and will, moreover, fall into vexation. For what reason? Because, monks, it is beyond their domain. Monks, I do not see anyone in this world with its devas, its Māra, and its Brahmās, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans, who could satisfy the mind with an explanation of these questions, except for the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata, or one who has heard it from this source.”

“Kathaṃ [P 5.0119] bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, mettācetovimutti, kiṃgatikā hoti, kiṃparamā, kiṃphalā, kiṃpariyosānā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mettāsahagataṃ satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… mettāsahagataṃ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. So sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati ‘paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati ‘paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūlañca paṭikūlañca tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṃ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako ca tattha viharati sato sampajāno, subhaṃ vā kho pana vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharati. Subhaparamāhaṃ, bhikkhave, mettācetovimuttiṃ vadāmi, idhapaññassa bhikkhuno uttarivimuttiṃ appaṭivijjhato.

“And how, monks, is the liberation of mind by loving-kindness cultivated? What is its destination, what its supreme state, what its fruit, what its culmination? Here, monks, a monk develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor accompanied by loving-kindness... develops the equanimity enlightenment factor accompanied by loving-kindness, which is based on seclusion, dispassion, cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. If he wishes: ‘May I dwell perceiving repulsiveness in what is not repulsive,’ he dwells perceiving repulsiveness there. If he wishes: ‘May I dwell perceiving non-repulsiveness in what is repulsive,’ he dwells perceiving non-repulsiveness there. If he wishes: ‘May I dwell perceiving repulsiveness in both what is not repulsive and what is repulsive,’ he dwells perceiving repulsiveness there. If he wishes: ‘May I dwell perceiving non-repulsiveness in both what is repulsive and what is not repulsive,’ he dwells perceiving non-repulsiveness there. If he wishes: ‘Having avoided both what is not repulsive and what is repulsive, may I dwell equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending,’ he dwells there equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending. Or else, having attained the beautiful liberation, he dwells there. Monks, I say that the liberation of mind by loving-kindness has the beautiful as its supreme state—for a monk with mundane wisdom who has not penetrated to a further liberation.”

“Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, karuṇācetovimutti, kiṃgatikā hoti, kiṃparamā, kiṃphalā, kiṃpariyosānā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu karuṇāsahagataṃ satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… [V 3.0140] karuṇāsahagataṃ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ[T 5.0165]. So sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati…pe… sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūlañca paṭikūlañca tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṃ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako tattha viharati sato sampajāno. Sabbaso vā pana rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ākāsānañcāyatanaparamāhaṃ[P 5.0120], bhikkhave, karuṇācetovimuttiṃ [M 3.0105] vadāmi, idhapaññassa bhikkhuno uttarivimuttiṃ appaṭivijjhato.

And how, monks, is the liberation of mind through compassion developed? What is its destination, what its supreme state, what its fruit, what its culmination? Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness accompanied by compassion... develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity accompanied by compassion, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. If he wishes: ‘May I dwell perceiving repulsiveness in what is not repulsive,’ he dwells perceiving repulsiveness there... If he wishes: ‘Having avoided both what is not repulsive and what is repulsive, may I dwell equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending,’ he dwells equanimous there, mindful and clearly comprehending. Or else, with the complete transcending of perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and with non-attention to perceptions of diversity, perceiving ‘space is infinite,’ he enters and dwells in the dimension of infinite space. Monks, I declare that the liberation of mind through compassion has the dimension of infinite space as its supreme state—for a monk wise in this world who has not penetrated a further liberation.

“Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, muditācetovimutti, kiṃgatikā hoti, kiṃparamā, kiṃphalā, kiṃpariyosānā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu muditāsahagataṃ satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti…pe… muditāsahagataṃ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. So sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati [V 3.0141] …pe… sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūlañca paṭikūlañca tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṃ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako tattha viharati sato sampajāno. Sabbaso vā pana ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Viññāṇañcāyatanaparamāhaṃ, bhikkhave, muditācetovimuttiṃ vadāmi, idhapaññassa bhikkhuno uttarivimuttiṃ appaṭivijjhato.

And how, monks, is the liberation of mind through sympathetic joy developed? What is its destination, what its supreme state, what its fruit, what its culmination? Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness accompanied by sympathetic joy... develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity accompanied by sympathetic joy, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. If he wishes: ‘May I dwell perceiving repulsiveness in what is not repulsive,’ he dwells perceiving repulsiveness there... If he wishes: ‘Having avoided both what is not repulsive and what is repulsive, may I dwell equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending,’ he dwells equanimous there, mindful and clearly comprehending. Or else, by entirely transcending the dimension of infinite space, perceiving ‘consciousness is infinite,’ he enters and dwells in the dimension of infinite consciousness. Monks, I declare that the liberation of mind through sympathetic joy has the dimension of infinite consciousness as its supreme state—for a monk wise in this world who has not penetrated a further liberation.

“Kathaṃ [T 5.0166] bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, upekkhācetovimutti, kiṃgatikā hoti, kiṃparamā, kiṃphalā, kiṃpariyosānā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu upekkhāsahagataṃ satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… upekkhāsahagataṃ upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. So sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati ‘paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati ‘paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati ‘appaṭikūlañca paṭikūlañca tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṃ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako tattha viharati sato sampajāno. Sabbaso [P 5.0121] vā pana viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ākiñcaññāyatanaparamāhaṃ, bhikkhave, upekkhācetovimuttiṃ vadāmi, idhapaññassa bhikkhuno uttarivimuttiṃ appaṭivijjhato”ti. Catutthaṃ.

And how, monks, is the liberation of mind through equanimity developed? What is its destination, what is its supreme state, what is its fruit, and what is its culmination? Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness accompanied by equanimity, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity accompanied by equanimity, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and culminating in relinquishment. If he wishes, ‘May I dwell perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ he dwells there perceiving the repulsive. If he wishes, ‘May I dwell perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ he dwells there perceiving the unrepulsive. If he wishes, ‘May I dwell perceiving the repulsive in both the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ he dwells there perceiving the repulsive. If he wishes, ‘May I dwell perceiving the unrepulsive in both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ he dwells there perceiving the unrepulsive. If he wishes, ‘Having avoided both the unrepulsive and the repulsive, may I dwell equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending,’ he dwells there equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending. Or else, having completely transcended the dimension of infinite consciousness, perceiving ‘there is nothing,’ he enters and dwells in the dimension of nothingness. Monks, I declare that the liberation of mind through equanimity has the dimension of nothingness as its supreme state for a monk wise in this world who has not penetrated a further liberation.

5. Saṅgāravasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse with Saṅgārava

236. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0142][M 3.0106]. Atha kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

236. The setting is Sāvatthī. Then the brahmin Saṅgārava approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. When this courteous and memorable talk was concluded, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Saṅgārava said this to the Blessed One:

“Ko [T 5.0167] nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo yenekadā dīgharattaṃ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā? Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo yenekadā dīgharattaṃ asajjhāyakatāpi mantā paṭibhanti, pageva sajjhāyakatā”ti?

“What, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the reason, why at one time even mantras long recited do not come to mind, let alone those not recited? And what, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the reason, why at another time even mantras not recited for a long time do come to mind, let alone those recited?”

“Yasmiṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, samaye kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati, ubhayatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṃ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

“Brahmin, at a time when one dwells with a mind beset and overcome by sensual lust, and one does not understand as it really is the escape from arisen sensual lust, at that time one neither knows nor sees as it really is one's own welfare, nor the welfare of others, nor the welfare of both. Even mantras long recited do not come to mind, let alone those not recited.

“Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto saṃsaṭṭho lākhāya vā haliddiyā vā nīliyā vā mañjiṭṭhāya vā. Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṃ na jāneyya na passeyya. Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṃ samaye kāmarāgapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati kāmarāgaparetena, uppannassa ca kāmarāgassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṃ [P 5.0122] samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi…pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṃ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

Just as, Brahmin, there might be a bowl of water mixed with lac-dye, or turmeric, or indigo, or madder. Therein, a man with good eyesight, examining his own facial reflection, would not know or see it as it really is. In the very same way, Brahmin, at a time when one dwells with a mind beset by sensual lust, overcome by sensual lust, and one does not know as it really is the escape from arisen sensual lust, at that time one neither knows nor sees as it really is one's own welfare, nor the welfare of others, nor the welfare of both. Even mantras long recited do not come to mind, let alone those not recited.

“Puna [T 5.0168] caparaṃ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṃ samaye byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati byāpādaparetena, uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi…pe… [V 3.0143] ubhayatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṃ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

Furthermore, Brahmin, when one dwells with a mind beset by ill will, overwhelmed by ill will, and does not know as it really is the escape from arisen ill will, at that time one neither knows nor sees as it really is one's own welfare, nor the welfare of others, nor the welfare of both. Even mantras long recited do not come to mind, let alone those not recited.

“Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto agginā santatto pakkuthito pakkudhito (ka.), ukkaṭṭhito (sī.), ukkuṭṭhito (syā.) usmudakajāto [M 3.0107] ussadakajāto (sī.), usmādakajāto (syā.). Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṃ na jāneyya na passeyya. Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṃ samaye byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati byāpādaparetena, uppannassa ca byāpādassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi tasmiṃ samaye…pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṃ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

Just as, Brahmin, a bowl of water heated by fire, boiling and steaming—a person with good eyesight, examining their own facial reflection, would not know or see it as it really is. In the same way, Brahmin, when one dwells with a mind beset by ill will, overwhelmed by ill will, and does not know as it really is the escape from arisen ill will, at that time one neither knows nor sees as it really is one's own welfare, nor the welfare of others, nor the welfare of both. Even mantras long recited do not come to mind, let alone those not recited.

“Puna caparaṃ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṃ samaye thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati thinamiddhaparetena, uppannassa ca thinamiddhassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi…pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṃ samaye [T 5.0169] yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṃ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

Furthermore, Brahmin, when one dwells with a mind beset by sloth and torpor, overwhelmed by sloth and torpor, and does not know as it really is the escape from arisen sloth and torpor, at that time one neither knows nor sees as it really is one's own welfare, nor the welfare of others, nor the welfare of both. Even mantras long recited do not come to mind, let alone those not recited.

“Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto sevālapaṇakapariyonaddho. Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno [P 5.0123] yathābhūtaṃ na jāneyya na passeyya. Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṃ samaye thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati thinamiddhaparetena, uppannassa ca thinamiddhassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi…pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṃ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

Just as, Brahmin, a bowl of water is covered with moss and water plants—a person with good eyesight, examining their own facial reflection, would not know or see it as it really is. In the same way, Brahmin, when one dwells with a mind beset by sloth and torpor, overwhelmed by sloth and torpor, and does not know as it really is the escape from arisen sloth and torpor, at that time one neither knows nor sees as it really is one's own welfare, nor the welfare of others, nor the welfare of both. Even mantras long recited do not come to mind, let alone those not recited.

“Puna caparaṃ, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṃ samaye uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati uddhaccakukkuccaparetena, uppannassa ca uddhaccakukkuccassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi…pe… [V 3.0144] ubhayatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṃ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

Furthermore, Brahmin, when one dwells with a mind beset by restlessness and remorse, overwhelmed by restlessness and remorse, and does not know as it really is the escape from arisen restlessness and remorse, at that time one neither knows nor sees as it really is one's own welfare, nor the welfare of others, nor the welfare of both. Even mantras long recited do not come to mind, let alone those not recited.

“Seyyathāpi, brāhmaṇa, udapatto vāterito calito bhanto ūmijāto. Tattha cakkhumā puriso sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno yathābhūtaṃ [T 5.0170][M 3.0108] na jāneyya na passeyya. Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yasmiṃ samaye uddhaccakukkuccapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā viharati uddhaccakukkuccaparetena, uppannassa ca uddhaccakukkuccassa nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, attatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati, paratthampi…pe… ubhayatthampi tasmiṃ samaye yathābhūtaṃ na jānāti na passati; dīgharattaṃ sajjhāyakatāpi mantā nappaṭibhanti, pageva asajjhāyakatā.

Just as, Brahmin, a bowl of water stirred by the wind, agitated, disturbed, and rippling—a person with good eyesight, examining their own facial reflection, would not know or see it as it really is. In the same way, Brahmin, when one dwells with a mind beset by restlessness and remorse, overwhelmed by restlessness and remorse, and does not know as it really is the escape from arisen restlessness and remorse, at that time one neither knows nor sees as it really is one's own welfare, nor the welfare of others, nor the welfare of both. Even mantras long recited do not come to mind, let alone those not recited.
