Then the Blessed One, having risen from his sickness, not long after recovering from his illness, came out from his dwelling and sat down on a prepared seat in the shade behind the dwelling. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “I have seen, venerable sir, the Blessed One's comfort; I have seen, venerable sir, the Blessed One's endurance; I have seen, venerable sir, the Blessed One's sustenance. But, venerable sir, because of the Blessed One’s illness, my body has become as if stiff, the directions are not clear to me, and the teachings do not occur to me. Yet, venerable sir, I had this small measure of comfort: ‘The Blessed One will not attain final Nibbāna so long as he has not made some statement concerning the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.’”

“Kiṃ pana dāni, ānanda, bhikkhusaṅgho mayi paccāsīsati paccāsiṃsati (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)? Desito, ānanda, mayā dhammo anantaraṃ abāhiraṃ karitvā. Natthānanda, tathāgatassa dhammesu ācariyamuṭṭhi. Yassa nūna, ānanda, evamassa – ‘ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmī’ti vā, ‘mamuddesiko bhikkhusaṅgho’ti vā, so nūna, ānanda, bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha kiñcideva udāhareyya. Tathāgatassa kho, ānanda, na evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmī’ti vā[T 5.0205], ‘mamuddesiko bhikkhusaṅgho’ti vā. Sa kiṃ so nūna (sī. pī.), ānanda, tathāgato bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ārabbha kiñcideva udāharissati! Etarahi kho panāhaṃ, ānanda, jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako addhagato vayoanuppatto. Āsītiko me vayo vattati. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, jajjarasakaṭaṃ jarasakaṭaṃ (sabbattha) veḷamissakena vegamissakena (sī.), veḷumissakena (syā. kaṃ.), vedhamissakena (pī. ka.), vekhamissakena (ka.) yāpeti; evameva kho, ānanda, vedhamissakena maññe tathāgatassa kāyo yāpeti.

“But now, Ānanda, what does the Saṅgha of bhikkhus expect of me? I have taught the Dhamma, Ānanda, without making an inner or an outer. There is no ‘teacher’s fist,’ Ānanda, in the Tathāgata with regard to the teachings. For one who might think, Ānanda, ‘I will lead the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,’ or ‘The Saṅgha of bhikkhus is directed towards me,’ that person should make some statement concerning the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. But it does not occur to the Tathāgata, Ānanda, ‘I will lead the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,’ or ‘The Saṅgha of bhikkhus is directed towards me.’ So why, Ānanda, would the Tathāgata make any statement concerning the Saṅgha of bhikkhus? Now, Ānanda, I am old, aged, elderly, I have reached a great age, and my life is coming to an end. I am eighty years old. Just as, Ānanda, a worn-out cart is kept going with the help of straps, even so, Ānanda, I think the Tathāgata’s body is kept going with the help of repairs.

“Yasmiṃ[V 3.0231][P 5.0154], ānanda, samaye tathāgato sabbanimittānaṃ amanasikārā ekaccānaṃ vedanānaṃ nirodhā animittaṃ cetosamādhiṃ upasampajja viharati, phāsutaro phāsutaraṃ (sabbattha), ānanda, tasmiṃ samaye tathāgatassa kāyo hoti tathāgatassa hoti (bahūsu). Tasmātihānanda, attadīpā viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā.

“Ānanda, at whatever time the Tathāgata, by not attending to all signs and through the cessation of certain feelings, attains and abides in the signless concentration of mind, at that time, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s body is more comfortable. Therefore, Ānanda, dwell as islands unto yourselves, as refuges unto yourselves, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as your island, with the Dhamma as your refuge, with no other refuge.”

“Kathañcānanda, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo? Idhānanda, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno [M 3.0134] satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo. Ye hi keci, ānanda, etarahi vā mamaccaye vā attadīpā viharissanti attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā[T 5.0206]; tamatagge mete, ānanda, bhikkhū bhavissanti ye keci sikkhākāmā”ti. Navamaṃ.

“And how, Ānanda, does a bhikkhu dwell as an island unto himself, as a refuge unto himself, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings… mind in mind… phenomena in phenomena—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. It is in this way, Ānanda, that a bhikkhu dwells as an island unto himself, as a refuge unto himself, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge. Ānanda, whoever, either now or after I have passed away, shall dwell as islands unto themselves, as refuges unto themselves, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as their island, with the Dhamma as their refuge, with no other refuge—those bhikkhus of mine who are desirous of training will be in the supreme position.” Ninth.

10. Bhikkhunupassayasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse at the Bhikkhunīs' Residence

376. Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhuniyo yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho tā bhikkhuniyo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ –

376. Then the Venerable Ānanda, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and went to a certain bhikkhunīs' residence. Having gone there, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then a number of bhikkhunīs approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, they paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those bhikkhunīs said this to the Venerable Ānanda:

“Idha, bhante ānanda, sambahulā bhikkhuniyo catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittā supaṭṭhitacittā (sī. pī. ka.) viharantiyo uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ sañjānantī”ti sampajānantīti (ka.). “Evametaṃ[P 5.0155], bhaginiyo, evametaṃ, bhaginiyo! Yo hi koci, bhaginiyo, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacitto viharati, tassetaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ‘uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ sañjānissatī’”ti.

“Venerable Ānanda, in this Dispensation, many nuns, dwelling with well-established minds in the four foundations of mindfulness, clearly know a noble distinction beyond the previous one.” “This is so, sisters, this is so! Sisters, for any monk or nun who dwells with a well-established mind in the four foundations of mindfulness, this is to be expected: ‘They will clearly know a noble distinction beyond the previous one.’”

Atha [V 3.0232] kho āyasmā ānando tā bhikkhuniyo dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmā ānando sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

Then the Venerable Ānanda, having instructed, encouraged, aroused, and gladdened those nuns with a Dhamma talk, rose from his seat and departed. Then the Venerable Ānanda, having wandered for alms in Sāvatthī and returned from his alms-round after the meal, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:

“Idhāhaṃ, bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena aññataro bhikkhunupassayo [T 5.0207] tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṃ. Atha kho, bhante, sambahulā bhikkhuniyo yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ [M 3.0135] nisinnā kho, bhante, tā bhikkhuniyo maṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘idha, bhante ānanda, sambahulā bhikkhuniyo catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittā viharantiyo uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ sañjānantī’ti. Evaṃ vuttāhaṃ, bhante, tā bhikkhuniyo etadavocaṃ – ‘evametaṃ, bhaginiyo, evametaṃ, bhaginiyo! Yo hi koci, bhaginiyo, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacitto viharati, tassetaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ sañjānissatī’”ti.

“Venerable Sir, this morning, having dressed and taken my bowl and robes, I approached a certain nunnery. Having approached, I sat down on the prepared seat. Then, Venerable Sir, many nuns approached me. Having approached, they paid homage to me and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Venerable Sir, those nuns said this to me: ‘Venerable Ānanda, in this Dispensation, many nuns, dwelling with well-established minds in the four foundations of mindfulness, clearly know a noble distinction beyond the previous one.’ When this was said, Venerable Sir, I said this to those nuns: ‘This is so, sisters, this is so! Sisters, for any monk or nun who dwells with a well-established mind in the four foundations of mindfulness, this is to be expected: they will clearly know a noble distinction beyond the previous one.’”

“Evametaṃ, ānanda, evametaṃ, ānanda! Yo hi koci, ānanda, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacitto viharati, tassetaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – ‘uḷāraṃ pubbenāparaṃ visesaṃ sañjānissati’” sañjānissatīti (bahūsu).

“It is so, Ānanda, it is so, Ānanda! For any monk or nun, Ānanda, who dwells with a well-established mind in the four foundations of mindfulness, this is to be expected: ‘They will clearly know a noble distinction beyond the previous one.’”

“Katamesu catūsu? Idhānanda, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Tassa [P 5.0156] kāye kāyānupassino viharato kāyārammaṇo vā uppajjati kāyasmiṃ pariḷāho, cetaso vā līnattaṃ, bahiddhā vā cittaṃ vikkhipati. Tenānanda tenahānanda (sī.), bhikkhunā kismiñcideva pasādanīye nimitte cittaṃ paṇidahitabbaṃ. Tassa kismiñcideva pasādanīye nimitte cittaṃ paṇidahato [T 5.0208] pāmojjaṃ jāyati. Pamuditassa pīti jāyati. Pītimanassa kāyo passambhati. Passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vedayati vediyati (sī.). Sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yassa khvāhaṃ atthāya cittaṃ paṇidahiṃ, so me attho [V 3.0233] abhinipphanno. Handa, dāni paṭisaṃharāmī’ti. So paṭisaṃharati ceva na ca vitakketi na ca vicāreti. ‘Avitakkomhi avicāro, ajjhattaṃ satimā sukhamasmī’ti pajānāti”.

“In which four? Here, Ānanda, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. While he is dwelling contemplating the body in the body, an object connected with the body may arise, or a feverishness in the body, or mental sluggishness, or his mind may be scattered outwardly. Then, Ānanda, that monk should direct his mind to some pleasing sign. When he directs his mind to some pleasing sign, joy arises. For one who is joyful, rapture arises. For one whose mind is rapturous, the body becomes tranquil. With a tranquil body, one experiences happiness. The mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated. He reflects thus: ‘The purpose for which I directed my mind has been accomplished. Now, I shall withdraw.’ So he withdraws, and neither thinks nor examines. He understands: ‘I am without thought, without examination; inwardly mindful, I am happy.’”

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, bhikkhu vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Tassa dhammesu dhammānupassino viharato dhammārammaṇo vā uppajjati kāyasmiṃ pariḷāho, cetaso vā līnattaṃ, bahiddhā vā cittaṃ vikkhipati. Tenānanda, bhikkhunā kismiñcideva pasādanīye nimitte cittaṃ paṇidahitabbaṃ. Tassa kismiñcideva pasādanīye nimitte cittaṃ paṇidahato pāmojjaṃ jāyati[M 3.0136]. Pamuditassa pīti jāyati. Pītimanassa kāyo passambhati. Passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vedayati. Sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yassa khvāhaṃ atthāya cittaṃ paṇidahiṃ, so me attho abhinipphanno. Handa, dāni paṭisaṃharāmī’ti. So paṭisaṃharati ceva na ca vitakketi na ca vicāreti. ‘Avitakkomhi avicāro, ajjhattaṃ satimā sukhamasmī’ti pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, paṇidhāya bhāvanā hoti.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, a monk dwells contemplating feelings in feelings… the mind in the mind… phenomena in phenomena—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. While he is dwelling contemplating phenomena in phenomena, a mental object may arise, or a feverishness in the body, or sluggishness of mind, or his mind may be scattered outwardly. Then, Ānanda, that monk should direct his mind to some pleasing sign. When he directs his mind to some pleasing sign, joy arises. For one who is joyful, rapture arises. For one whose mind is rapturous, the body becomes tranquil. With a tranquil body, one experiences happiness. The mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated. He reflects thus: ‘The purpose for which I directed my mind has been accomplished. Now, I shall withdraw.’ So he withdraws, and neither thinks nor examines. He understands: ‘I am without thought, without examination, inwardly mindful, and happy.’ Thus, Ānanda, is development by directing the mind.”

“Kathañcānanda[T 5.0209], appaṇidhāya bhāvanā hoti? Bahiddhā[P 5.0157], ānanda, bhikkhu cittaṃ appaṇidhāya ‘appaṇihitaṃ me bahiddhā citta’nti pajānāti. Atha pacchāpure ‘asaṃkhittaṃ vimuttaṃ appaṇihita’nti pajānāti. Atha ca pana ‘kāye kāyānupassī viharāmi ātāpī sampajāno satimā sukhamasmī’ti pajānāti. Bahiddhā, ānanda, bhikkhu cittaṃ appaṇidhāya ‘appaṇihitaṃ me bahiddhā citta’nti pajānāti. Atha pacchāpure ‘asaṃkhittaṃ vimuttaṃ appaṇihita’nti pajānāti. Atha ca pana ‘vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharāmi ātāpī sampajāno satimā sukhamasmī’ti pajānāti. Bahiddhā, ānanda, bhikkhu cittaṃ appaṇidhāya ‘appaṇihitaṃ me bahiddhā citta’nti pajānāti. Atha pacchāpure ‘asaṃkhittaṃ vimuttaṃ appaṇihita’nti pajānāti. Atha ca pana ‘citte cittānupassī viharāmi ātāpī sampajāno satimā sukhamasmī’ti pajānāti. Bahiddhā, ānanda, bhikkhu cittaṃ appaṇidhāya ‘appaṇihitaṃ me bahiddhā citta’nti pajānāti. Atha pacchāpure ‘asaṃkhittaṃ vimuttaṃ appaṇihita’nti pajānāti. Atha ca pana ‘dhammesu dhammānupassī viharāmi ātāpī sampajāno satimā sukhamasmī’ti pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, appaṇidhāya bhāvanā hoti.

“And how, Ānanda, is there development without directing? A bhikkhu, Ānanda, not directing his mind externally, understands: ‘My mind is not directed externally.’ Then, afterwards and before, he understands: ‘It is uncontracted, liberated, and undirected.’ And further, he understands: ‘I dwell contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, and I am at ease.’ A bhikkhu, Ānanda, not directing his mind externally, understands: ‘My mind is not directed externally.’ Then, afterwards and before, he understands: ‘It is uncontracted, liberated, and undirected.’ And further, he understands: ‘I dwell contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, and I am at ease.’ A bhikkhu, Ānanda, not directing his mind externally, understands: ‘My mind is not directed externally.’ Then, afterwards and before, he understands: ‘It is uncontracted, liberated, and undirected.’ And further, he understands: ‘I dwell contemplating the mind in the mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, and I am at ease.’ A bhikkhu, Ānanda, not directing his mind externally, understands: ‘My mind is not directed externally.’ Then, afterwards and before, he understands: ‘It is uncontracted, liberated, and undirected.’ And further, he understands: ‘I dwell contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, and I am at ease.’ Thus, Ānanda, there is development without directing.”

“Iti [V 3.0234] kho, ānanda, desitā mayā paṇidhāya bhāvanā, desitā appaṇidhāya bhāvanā. Yaṃ, ānanda, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hitesinā [T 5.0210] anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya, kataṃ vo taṃ mayā. Etāni, ānanda, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni! Jhāyathānanda, mā pamādattha; mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha! Ayaṃ vo amhākaṃ anusāsanī”ti.

“Thus, Ānanda, development with directing has been taught by me, and development without directing has been taught by me. Ānanda, whatever should be done by a teacher for his disciples—one who seeks their welfare and is compassionate—out of compassion, that has been done for you by me. Here, Ānanda, are these roots of trees; here are these empty huts. Meditate, Ānanda, do not be heedless; do not be remorseful afterwards. This is our instruction to you.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti. Dasamaṃ.

The Blessed One said this. Satisfied, the Venerable Ānanda delighted in the Blessed One's words. The Tenth.

Ambapālivaggo paṭhamo.

The First Ambapāli Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Ambapāli [M 3.0137][P 5.0158] sato bhikkhu, sālā kusalarāsi ca;

Sakuṇagdhi makkaṭo sūdo, gilāno bhikkhunupassayoti.

Ambapāli, Sato, Bhikkhu, Sāḷa, and Kusalarāsi; Sakuṇagghi, Makkaṭa, Sūda, Gilāna, and Bhikkhunupassaya.

2. Nālandavaggo

2. The Nālandā Chapter

1. Mahāpurisasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Great Man

377. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0211]. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘mahāpuriso, mahāpuriso’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, mahāpuriso hotī”ti? “Vimuttacittattā khvāhaṃ, sāriputta, ‘mahāpuriso’ti vadāmi. Avimuttacittattā ‘no mahāpuriso’ti vadāmi”.

377. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated thus, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the Blessed One: “‘Great man, great man,’ it is said, venerable sir. To what extent, venerable sir, is one a great man?” “Because of a liberated mind, Sāriputta, I say one is a ‘great man.’ Because of an unliberated mind, I say one is ‘not a great man.’”

“Kathañca, sāriputta, vimuttacitto hoti? Idha, sāriputta, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Tassa kāye kāyānupassino viharato cittaṃ virajjati, vimuccati anupādāya āsavehi. Vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… [V 3.0235] dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Tassa dhammesu dhammānupassino viharato cittaṃ virajjati, vimuccati anupādāya āsavehi. Evaṃ kho, sāriputta, vimuttacitto hoti. Vimuttacittattā khvāhaṃ, sāriputta, ‘mahāpuriso’ti vadāmi. Avimuttacittattā ‘no mahāpuriso’ti vadāmī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And how, Sāriputta, is one liberated in mind? Here, Sāriputta, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. For one who dwells contemplating the body in the body, his mind becomes dispassionate and is liberated from the taints through non-clinging. In regard to feelings… in regard to the mind… he dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. For one who dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, his mind becomes dispassionate and is liberated from the taints through non-clinging. It is in this way, Sāriputta, that one is liberated in mind. It is because of a liberated mind, Sāriputta, that I say one is a ‘great man.’ Because of an unliberated mind, I say one is ‘not a great man.’”

2. Nālandasuttaṃ

2. The Nālandā Discourse

378. Ekaṃ [P 5.0159] samayaṃ bhagavā nālandāyaṃ viharati pāvārikambavane. Atha [T 5.0212] kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati! Na cāhu, na [M 3.0138] ca bhavissati, na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro, yadidaṃ – sambodhiya”nti. “Uḷārā kho tyāyaṃ, sāriputta, āsabhī vācā bhāsitā, ekaṃso gahito, sīhanādo nadito – ‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati! Na cāhu, na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro, yadidaṃ – sambodhiya’”nti.

378. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Nālandā in Pāvārika’s mango grove. Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down to one side. Seated thus, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I have such faith in the Blessed One that there has not been, nor will there be, nor is there now any other ascetic or brahmin more greatly accomplished in higher knowledge than the Blessed One with regard to enlightenment.” “Sāriputta, this grand and bold statement has been spoken by you, a categorical assertion has been made, a lion’s roar has been roared: ‘Venerable sir, I have such faith in the Blessed One that there has not been, nor will there be, nor is there now any other ascetic or brahmin more greatly accomplished in higher knowledge than the Blessed One with regard to enlightenment.’”

“Kiṃ nu te, sāriputta, ye te ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto cetasā ceto paricca viditā – ‘evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ iti vā, ‘evaṃdhammā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ iti vā, ‘evaṃpaññā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ iti vā, ‘evaṃvihārino te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ iti vā, ‘evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ’ iti vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”!

“What now, Sāriputta, as to those who were in the past, the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones—were all those Blessed Ones known to you, having encompassed their minds with your mind, thus: ‘Such was the virtue of those Blessed Ones,’ or ‘Such were the qualities of those Blessed Ones,’ or ‘Such was the wisdom of those Blessed Ones,’ or ‘Such was the abiding of those Blessed Ones,’ or ‘Such was the liberation of those Blessed Ones’?” “It is not so, venerable sir.”

“Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ye te bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto cetasā ceto paricca viditā – ‘evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto bhavissanti’ iti vā, ‘evaṃdhammā te bhagavanto bhavissanti’ iti vā, ‘evaṃpaññā te bhagavanto bhavissanti’ iti vā, ‘evaṃvihārino te bhagavanto bhavissanti’ iti [T 5.0213] vā, ‘evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto bhavissanti’ iti vā”ti? “No [P 5.0160] hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What then, Sāriputta, as to those who will be in the future, the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones—are all those Blessed Ones known to you, having encompassed their minds with your mind, thus: ‘Such will be the virtue of those Blessed Ones,’ or ‘Such will be the Dhamma of those Blessed Ones,’ or ‘Such will be the wisdom of those Blessed Ones,’ or ‘Such will be the abiding of those Blessed Ones,’ or ‘Such will be the liberation of those Blessed Ones’?” “It is not so, venerable sir.”

“Kiṃ [V 3.0236] pana tyāhaṃ kiṃ pana te (sī.), sāriputta, etarahi, arahaṃ sammāsambuddho cetasā ceto paricca vidito – ‘evaṃsīlo bhagavā’ iti vā, ‘evaṃdhammo bhagavā’ iti vā, ‘evaṃpañño bhagavā’ iti vā, ‘evaṃvihārī bhagavā’ iti vā, ‘evaṃvimutto bhagavā’ iti vā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“What then, Sāriputta? Am I, at this present time, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, known to you, having encompassed my mind with your mind, thus: ‘The Blessed One is of such virtue,’ or ‘The Blessed One is of such Dhamma,’ or ‘The Blessed One is of such wisdom,’ or ‘The Blessed One is of such an abiding,’ or ‘The Blessed One is of such liberation’?” “That is not so, venerable sir.”

“Ettha ca te, sāriputta, atītānāgatapaccuppannesu arahantesu sammāsambuddhesu cetopariyañāṇaṃ cetopariyāyañāṇaṃ (bahūsu) natthi. Atha kiñcarahi tyāyaṃ, sāriputta, uḷārā āsabhī vācā bhāsitā, ekaṃso gahito, sīhanādo nadito – ‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati! Na cāhu, na ca bhavissati, na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā’ bhiyyobhiññataro, yadidaṃ – sambodhiya”nti?

“Since, Sāriputta, you have no knowledge that encompasses the minds of the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past, future, and present, for what reason then have you spoken this grand and bold speech, made this categorical assertion, and roared this lion’s roar: ‘Venerable sir, I have such faith in the Blessed One that there has not been, nor will there be, nor is there now any other ascetic or brahmin more greatly accomplished in higher knowledge than the Blessed One, that is to say, with regard to enlightenment’?”

“Na [M 3.0139] kho me na kho me taṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.), bhante, atītānāgatapaccuppannesu arahantesu sammāsambuddhesu cetopariyañāṇaṃ atthi, api ca me dhammanvayo vidito. Seyyathāpi, bhante, rañño paccantimaṃ nagaraṃ daḷhuddhāpaṃ daḷhuddāpaṃ (sī. pī. ka.), daḷhaddhāpaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) daḷhapākāratoraṇaṃ ekadvāraṃ. Tatrassa dovāriko paṇḍito byatto medhāvī aññātānaṃ nivāretā ñātānaṃ pavesetā. So tassa nagarassa samantā anupariyāyapathaṃ anukkamamāno na passeyya pākārasandhiṃ [T 5.0214] vā pākāravivaraṃ vā, antamaso biḷāranikkhamanamattampi. Tassa evamassa – ‘ye kho keci oḷārikā pāṇā imaṃ nagaraṃ pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā, sabbe te imināva dvārena pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā’ti. Evameva kho me, bhante, dhammanvayo vidito – ‘yepi te, bhante, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya, cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe, catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittā, satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā, anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhiṃsu. Yepi te, bhante, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya, cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe, catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittā, satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ [P 5.0161] bhāvetvā, anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhissanti. Bhagavāpi, bhante, etarahi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya, cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe, catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacitto, satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā, anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’”ti.

“Venerable sir, I do not have knowledge that encompasses the minds of the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past, future, and present. However, the way of the Dhamma is known to me. Just as, venerable sir, a king's frontier city might have strong foundations, strong walls and gate-towers, and a single gate. There would be a gatekeeper there—wise, skilled, and intelligent—who prevents entry to the unknown and admits the known. As he patrols the path all around that city, he would not see a joint in the wall or a gap in the wall, not even one large enough for a cat to slip through. It would occur to him: ‘Whatever gross beings enter or leave this city, all do so only by this gate.’ In this very way, venerable sir, the way of the Dhamma is known to me: ‘Those Blessed Ones, venerable sir, who were Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the past—all those Blessed Ones, having abandoned the five hindrances, the defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom, with their minds well-established in the four establishments of mindfulness, and having developed the seven factors of enlightenment as they truly are, fully awakened to the unexcelled perfect enlightenment. Those Blessed Ones, venerable sir, who will be Arahants, Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the future—all those Blessed Ones, having abandoned the five hindrances, the defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom, with their minds well-established in the four establishments of mindfulness, and having developed the seven factors of enlightenment as they truly are, will fully awaken to the unexcelled perfect enlightenment. And the Blessed One, venerable sir, who is at present the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having abandoned the five hindrances, the defilements of the mind that weaken wisdom, with his mind well-established in the four establishments of mindfulness, and having developed the seven factors of enlightenment as they truly are, is fully awakened to the unexcelled perfect enlightenment.’”

“Sādhu [V 3.0237] sādhu, sāriputta! Tasmātiha tvaṃ, sāriputta, imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ abhikkhaṇaṃ bhāseyyāsi bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ. Yesampi hi, sāriputta, moghapurisānaṃ bhavissati tathāgate kaṅkhā [T 5.0215] vā vimati vā, tesampimaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ sutvā yā tathāgate kaṅkhā vā vimati vā sā pahīyissatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Good, good, Sāriputta! Therefore, Sāriputta, you should frequently speak this exposition of the Dhamma to the monks, nuns, male lay followers, and female lay followers. For, Sāriputta, even those foolish persons who may have doubt or uncertainty about the Tathāgata, upon hearing this exposition of the Dhamma, that doubt or uncertainty of theirs about the Tathāgata will be abandoned.”

3. Cundasuttaṃ

3. The Cunda Sutta

379. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto magadhesu [M 3.0140] viharati nālakagāmake ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Cundo ca samaṇuddeso āyasmato sāriputtassa upaṭṭhāko hoti.

379. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. At that time the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling among the Magadhans at the small village of Nālaka, afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. And the novice Cunda was the attendant of the Venerable Sāriputta.

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto teneva ābādhena parinibbāyi. Atha kho cundo samaṇuddeso āyasmato sāriputtassa pattacīvaramādāya yena sāvatthi jetavanaṃ anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāmo yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho cundo samaṇuddeso [P 5.0162] āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “āyasmā, bhante, sāriputto parinibbuto. Idamassa pattacīvara”nti.

Then the Venerable Sāriputta attained final Nibbāna on account of that very illness. Then the novice Cunda, taking the bowl and robes of the Venerable Sāriputta, went to Sāvatthī, to Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park, to where the Venerable Ānanda was, and approached him. Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the novice Cunda said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “Venerable sir, the Venerable Sāriputta has attained final Nibbāna. This is his bowl and robes.”

“Atthi kho idaṃ, āvuso cunda, kathāpābhataṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Āyāmāvuso cunda, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocessāmā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho cundo samaṇuddeso āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi.

“Friend Cunda, this news is indeed a reason for seeing the Blessed One. Come, friend Cunda, let us approach the Blessed One; having approached, we will report this matter to the Blessed One.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the novice Cunda replied in assent to the Venerable Ānanda.

Atha kho āyasmā ca ānando cundo ca samaṇuddeso yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ [T 5.0216] etadavoca – “ayaṃ, bhante, cundo samaṇuddeso evamāha – ‘āyasmā, bhante, sāriputto parinibbuto; idamassa pattacīvara’nti. Api ca me, bhante, madhurakajāto viya kāyo, disāpi me na pakkhāyanti, dhammāpi maṃ nappaṭibhanti ‘āyasmā sāriputto parinibbuto’ti sutvā”.

Then the Venerable Ānanda and the novice Cunda approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this novice Cunda says thus: ‘Venerable sir, the Venerable Sāriputta has attained Parinibbāna; this is his bowl and robe.’ Indeed, venerable sir, upon hearing that the Venerable Sāriputta has attained Parinibbāna, my body is as if drugged, the directions are not clear to me, and the teachings do not occur to me.”

“Kiṃ [V 3.0238] nu kho te, ānanda, sāriputto sīlakkhandhaṃ vā ādāya parinibbuto, samādhikkhandhaṃ vā ādāya parinibbuto, paññākkhandhaṃ vā ādāya parinibbuto, vimuttikkhandhaṃ vā ādāya parinibbuto, vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhaṃ vā ādāya parinibbuto”ti? “Na ca kho me, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto sīlakkhandhaṃ vā ādāya parinibbuto, samādhikkhandhaṃ vā…pe… paññākkhandhaṃ vā… vimuttikkhandhaṃ vā… vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhaṃ vā ādāya parinibbuto. Api ca me, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto ovādako ahosi otiṇṇo viññāpako sandassako samādapako samuttejako sampahaṃsako, akilāsu dhammadesanāya, anuggāhako sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Taṃ mayaṃ āyasmato sāriputtassa dhammojaṃ dhammabhogaṃ dhammānuggahaṃ anussarāmā”ti.

“What, Ānanda? Has Sāriputta attained Parinibbāna by taking with him the aggregate of virtue? Or the aggregate of concentration? Or the aggregate of wisdom? Or the aggregate of liberation? Or the aggregate of the knowledge of reviewing?” “No, venerable sir, the Venerable Sāriputta has not attained Parinibbāna by taking with him the aggregate of virtue, nor the aggregate of concentration… nor the aggregate of wisdom… nor the aggregate of liberation… nor the aggregate of the knowledge of reviewing. Moreover, venerable sir, the Venerable Sāriputta was an instructor, one who made the teachings clear and penetrable, one who pointed things out, one who encouraged, one who stimulated, and one who gladdens. He was tireless in teaching the Dhamma and a supporter of his companions in the holy life. We recall that Venerable Sāriputta’s Dhamma-sustenance, Dhamma-enjoyment, and support through the Dhamma.”

“Nanu [M 3.0141] taṃ, ānanda, mayā paṭikacceva paṭigacceva (sī. pī.) akkhātaṃ – ‘sabbehi piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo[P 5.0163]. Taṃ kutettha, ānanda, labbhā! Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Seyyathāpi, ānanda, mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato yo [T 5.0217] mahantataro khandho so palujjeyya; evameva kho ānanda, mahato bhikkhusaṅghassa tiṭṭhato sāravato sāriputto parinibbuto. Taṃ kutettha, ānanda, labbhā! Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjī’ti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Tasmātihānanda, attadīpā viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā.

“Ānanda, was it not declared by me from the very beginning that with all things that are dear and agreeable there is separation, severance, and becoming other? How, Ānanda, could it be obtained here that what is born, come to be, conditioned, and of a nature to perish, should not perish? That circumstance does not exist. Just as, Ānanda, from a great tree, standing and possessing heartwood, the largest branch should break; even so, Ānanda, from the great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, standing and possessing heartwood, Sāriputta has attained Parinibbāna. How, Ānanda, could it be obtained here that what is born, come to be, conditioned, and of a nature to perish, should not perish? That circumstance does not exist. Therefore, Ānanda, dwell with yourselves as an island, with yourselves as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge.”

“Kathañcānanda, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo? Idhānanda, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo. Ye hi keci, ānanda, etarahi vā mamaccaye vā attadīpā viharissanti attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā; tamatagge mete, ānanda, bhikkhū bhavissanti ye keci sikkhākāmā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“And how, Ānanda, does a bhikkhu dwell with himself as an island, with himself as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings… mind in mind… phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. It is in this way, Ānanda, that a bhikkhu dwells with himself as an island, with himself as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge. Ānanda, any bhikkhus who, either now or after my passing, shall dwell with themselves as an island, with themselves as a refuge, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as their island, the Dhamma as their refuge, with no other refuge—those bhikkhus of mine who are desirous of training will be in the highest state.” The third.

4. Ukkacelasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse at Ukkacelā

380. Ekaṃ [V 3.0239] samayaṃ bhagavā vajjīsu viharati ukkacelāyaṃ gaṅgāya nadiyā tīre mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ aciraparinibbutesu sāriputtamoggallānesu. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto ajjhokāse [T 5.0218] nisinno hoti.

380. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Vajjis at Ukkacelā on the bank of the river Ganges with a great Saṅgha of bhikkhus, not long after Sāriputta and Moggallāna had attained Parinibbāna. Now at that time, the Blessed One was sitting in the open, surrounded by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

Atha kho bhagavā tuṇhībhūtaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anuviloketvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “api [P 5.0164] myāyaṃ, bhikkhave, parisā suññā viya khāyati parinibbutesu sāriputtamoggallānesu. Asuññā me, bhikkhave, parisā hoti[M 3.0142], anapekkhā tassaṃ disāyaṃ hoti, yassaṃ disāyaṃ sāriputtamoggallānā viharanti. Ye hi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etapparamaṃyeva sāvakayugaṃ etaparamaṃyeva (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) ahosi – seyyathāpi mayhaṃ sāriputtamoggallānā. Yepi te, bhikkhave, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tesampi bhagavantānaṃ etapparamaṃyeva sāvakayugaṃ bhavissati – seyyathāpi mayhaṃ sāriputtamoggallānā. Acchariyaṃ, bhikkhave, sāvakānaṃ! Abbhutaṃ, bhikkhave, sāvakānaṃ! Satthu ca nāma sāsanakarā bhavissanti ovādappaṭikarā, catunnañca parisānaṃ piyā bhavissanti manāpā garubhāvanīyā ca! Acchariyaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa, abbhutaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa! Evarūpepi nāma sāvakayuge parinibbute natthi tathāgatassa soko vā paridevo vā! Taṃ kutettha, bhikkhave, labbhā! Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato ye mahantatarā khandhā te palujjeyyuṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, mahato [T 5.0219] bhikkhusaṅghassa tiṭṭhato sāravato sāriputtamoggallānā parinibbutā. Taṃ kutettha, bhikkhave, labbhā! Yaṃ taṃ jātaṃ bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ palokadhammaṃ, taṃ vata mā palujjīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, attadīpā viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā.

Then the Blessed One, surveying the silent assembly of bhikkhus, addressed them: 'Bhikkhus, this assembly of mine appears as if empty now that Sāriputta and Moggallāna have attained Parinibbāna. My assembly is not empty, bhikkhus; I have no concern for that direction in which Sāriputta and Moggallāna dwell. For, bhikkhus, those who were the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the past—they too had such a supreme pair of disciples as I have in Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Those who will be the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones in the future—they too will have such a supreme pair of disciples as I have in Sāriputta and Moggallāna. It is wonderful, bhikkhus, concerning the disciples! It is marvelous, bhikkhus, concerning the disciples! They will be followers of the Teacher's instruction and responders to advice, and will be dear, agreeable, respected, and esteemed by the four assemblies. It is wonderful, bhikkhus, concerning the Tathāgata! It is marvelous, bhikkhus, concerning the Tathāgata! Even when such a pair of disciples has attained Parinibbāna, there is no sorrow or lamentation in the Tathāgata. Bhikkhus, how could it be obtained here? That what is born, has come into being, is conditioned, and is of a nature to perish, should not perish—such a condition does not exist. Just as, bhikkhus, the largest branches of a great, standing tree possessed of heartwood might break off; even so, bhikkhus, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have attained Parinibbāna from the great, standing Bhikkhu Saṅgha possessed of essence. Bhikkhus, how could it be obtained here? That what is born, has come into being, is conditioned, and is of a nature to perish, should not perish—such a condition does not exist. Therefore, bhikkhus, dwell as islands unto yourselves, as a refuge unto yourselves, with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as an island, with the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge.'

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī [V 3.0240] viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo. Ye [P 5.0165] hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi vā mamaccaye vā attadīpā viharissanti attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā; tamatagge mete, bhikkhave, bhikkhū bhavissanti ye keci sikkhākāmā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu dwell having himself as an island, having himself as a refuge, with no other refuge; having the Dhamma as an island, having the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings… mind in mind… phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu dwells having himself as an island, having himself as a refuge, with no other refuge; having the Dhamma as an island, having the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge. Those bhikkhus, whether now or after my passing, who shall dwell having themselves as an island, having themselves as a refuge, with no other refuge; having the Dhamma as an island, having the Dhamma as a refuge, with no other refuge—they will be at the very top among my bhikkhus, those who are desirous of training.”

5. Bāhiyasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse to Bāhiya

381. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 3.0143]. Atha kho āyasmā bāhiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā bāhiyo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ [T 5.0220] sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Tasmātiha tvaṃ, bāhiya, ādimeva visodhehi kusalesu dhammesu. Ko cādi kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ? Sīlañca suvisuddhaṃ, diṭṭhi ca ujukā. Yato ca kho te, bāhiya, sīlañca suvisuddhaṃ bhavissati, diṭṭhi ca ujukā, tato tvaṃ, bāhiya, sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bhāveyyāsi”.

381. The setting is Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Bāhiya approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at a suitable place. Seated at a suitable place, the Venerable Bāhiya said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that I, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, might dwell alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and with a resolute mind.” “Therefore, Bāhiya, you should first purify the very beginning in regard to wholesome qualities. And what is the beginning of wholesome qualities? Virtue that is thoroughly purified and a view that is straight. When, Bāhiya, your virtue is thoroughly purified and your view is straight, then, Bāhiya, relying on virtue, established in virtue, you should develop the four establishments of mindfulness.”

“Katame cattāro? Idha, tvaṃ, bāhiya, kāye kāyānupassī viharāhi ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharāhi ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Yato kho tvaṃ, bāhiya, sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṃ bhāvessasi, tato tuyhaṃ, bāhiya, yā ratti vā divaso vā āgamissati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihānī”ti.

“Which four? Here, Bāhiya, you should dwell contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. You should dwell contemplating feelings in feelings… mind in mind… phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. When, Bāhiya, relying on virtue, established in virtue, you develop these four foundations of mindfulness in this way, then, Bāhiya, whatever night or day comes to you, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.”

Atha [P 5.0166] kho āyasmā bāhiyo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmā bāhiyo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva [V 3.0241] agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi[T 5.0221]. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā bāhiyo arahataṃ ahosīti. Pañcamaṃ.

Then the Venerable Bāhiya, having rejoiced in and approved of the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed. Then, dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the Venerable Bāhiya, not long after, in this very life, by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge, entered upon and dwelled in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. He directly knew: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being.” And the Venerable Bāhiya became one of the arahants. The Fifth.

6. Uttiyasuttaṃ

6. The Uttiya Sutta

382. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā uttiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā uttiyo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yamahaṃ bhagavato [M 3.0144] dhammaṃ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyya”nti. “Tasmātiha tvaṃ, uttiya, ādimeva visodhehi kusalesu dhammesu. Ko cādi kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ? Sīlañca suvisuddhaṃ, diṭṭhi ca ujukā. Yato ca kho te, uttiya, sīlañca suvisuddhaṃ bhavissati, diṭṭhi ca ujukā, tato tvaṃ, uttiya, sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bhāveyyāsi”.

382. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Uttiya approached the Blessed One… As he was sitting to one side, the Venerable Uttiya said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute.” “Therefore, Uttiya, you should first purify the beginning of wholesome qualities. And what is the beginning of wholesome qualities? Virtue that is thoroughly purified and view that is straight. When, Uttiya, your virtue is thoroughly purified and your view is straight, then, Uttiya, relying on virtue, established in virtue, you should develop the four establishments of mindfulness.”

“Katame cattāro? Idha tvaṃ, uttiya, kāye kāyānupassī viharāhi ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharāhi ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Yato kho tvaṃ, uttiya, sīlaṃ nissāya sīle patiṭṭhāya ime cattāro satipaṭṭhāne evaṃ bhāvessasi, tato tvaṃ, uttiya, gamissasi maccudheyyassa pāra”nti.

“Which four? Here, Uttiya, you should dwell contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. You should dwell contemplating feelings in feelings… mind in mind… phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. When, Uttiya, relying on virtue, established in virtue, you develop these four establishments of mindfulness in this way, then, Uttiya, you will go to the far shore of the realm of death.”

Atha kho āyasmā uttiyo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā [T 5.0222] uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmā uttiyo eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva – yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ – brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi. Aññataro ca panāyasmā uttiyo arahataṃ ahosīti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

Then the Venerable Uttiya, having rejoiced in and approved of the Blessed One’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed. Then, dwelling alone, secluded, diligent, ardent, and resolute, the Venerable Uttiya, not long after, by realizing it for himself with direct knowledge, entered and dwelled in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. He directly knew: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.” And the Venerable Uttiya became one of the arahants. The Sixth.

7. Ariyasuttaṃ

7. The Noble Discourse

383. “Cattārome[V 3.0242], bhikkhave, satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ariyā niyyānikā niyyanti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ime [P 5.0167] kho, bhikkhave, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ariyā niyyānikā niyyanti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

383. “Bhikkhus, these four establishments of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, are noble and lead out; they lead the one who practices them to the complete destruction of suffering. What are the four? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world; he dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in mind... phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. These, bhikkhus, are the four establishments of mindfulness that, when developed and cultivated, are noble and lead out, and lead the one who practices them to the complete destruction of suffering.” The Seventh.

8. Brahmasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Brahmā

384. Ekaṃ [M 3.0145] samayaṃ bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe paṭhamābhisambuddho. Atha kho bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “ekāyano ayaṃ maggo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṃ [T 5.0223] atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”.

384. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā, on the bank of the river Nerañjarā, at the foot of the Ajapāla Banyan Tree, having just become fully awakened. Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind: ‘This is the sole path for the purification of beings, for the overcoming of sorrow and lamentation, for the disappearance of suffering and displeasure, for the attainment of the noble path, for the realization of Nibbāna, namely, the four establishments of mindfulness.’

“Katame cattāro? Kāye vā bhikkhu kāyānupassī vihareyya ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu vā bhikkhu…pe… citte vā bhikkhu…pe… dhammesu vā bhikkhu dhammānupassī vihareyya ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ekāyano ayaṃ maggo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”ti.

“What are the four? A monk should dwell contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world; he should dwell contemplating feelings in feelings… the mind in the mind… phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. This is the sole path for the purification of beings, for the overcoming of sorrow and lamentation, for the disappearance of suffering and displeasure, for the attainment of the noble path, for the realization of Nibbāna, namely, the four establishments of mindfulness.”

Atha kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā [V 3.0243] puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi. Atha kho brahmā sahampati ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ, sugata! Ekāyano ayaṃ, bhante, maggo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”[P 5.0168].

Then Brahmā Sahampati, having known with his mind the reflection in the Blessed One's mind, just as a strong man might stretch out his bent arm or bend his stretched-out arm, disappeared from the Brahmā-world and reappeared in front of the Blessed One. Then Brahmā Sahampati, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, extended his joined hands in reverential salutation towards the Blessed One and said to him: ‘So it is, Blessed One! So it is, Sugata! This, venerable sir, is the sole path for the purification of beings, for the complete overcoming of sorrow and lamentation, for the cessation of suffering and displeasure, for the attainment of the noble path, for the realization of Nibbāna—that is, the four establishments of mindfulness.’

“Katame cattāro? Kāye vā, bhante, bhikkhu kāyānupassī vihareyya ātāpī sampajāno satimā[T 5.0224], vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu vā, bhante, bhikkhu…pe… citte vā, bhante, bhikkhu…pe… dhammesu vā, bhante, bhikkhu dhammānupassī vihareyya ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ekāyano ayaṃ, bhante, maggo sattānaṃ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṃ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamāya [M 3.0146] ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya, yadidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”ti.

“Which four? Here, venerable sir, a monk should dwell contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world; he should dwell contemplating feelings in feelings… the mind in the mind… phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. This, venerable sir, is the sole path for the purification of beings, for the complete overcoming of sorrow and lamentation, for the cessation of suffering and displeasure, for the attainment of the noble path, for the realization of Nibbāna—that is, the four establishments of mindfulness.”

Idamavoca brahmā sahampati. Idaṃ vatvā athāparaṃ etadavoca –

Brahmā Sahampati said this. Having said this, he further said this:

“Ekāyanaṃ jātikhayantadassī, maggaṃ pajānāti hitānukampī;

Etena maggena tariṃsu pubbe, tarissanti ye ca taranti ogha”nti. aṭṭhamaṃ;

“The one who sees the end of birth, compassionate for the welfare of beings, knows the one direct path. By this path they crossed the flood in the past, by this path they will cross, and by this path they are crossing.” Eighth.

9. Sedakasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse at Sedaka

385. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sumbhesu viharati sedakaṃ nāma sumbhānaṃ nigamo. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, caṇḍālavaṃsiko caṇḍālavaṃsaṃ ussāpetvā medakathālikaṃ antevāsiṃ āmantesi – ‘ehi tvaṃ, samma medakathālike, caṇḍālavaṃsaṃ abhiruhitvā mama uparikhandhe tiṭṭhāhī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, ācariyā’ti kho, bhikkhave, medakathālikā antevāsī caṇḍālavaṃsikassa paṭissutvā caṇḍālavaṃsaṃ abhiruhitvā ācariyassa uparikhandhe aṭṭhāsi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, caṇḍālavaṃsiko medakathālikaṃ antevāsiṃ etadavoca – ‘tvaṃ, samma [V 3.0244] medakathālike, mamaṃ rakkha, ahaṃ taṃ rakkhissāmi. Evaṃ mayaṃ aññamaññaṃ [P 5.0169] guttā aññamaññaṃ rakkhitā [T 5.0225] sippāni ceva dassessāma, lābhañca lābhe ca (sī.) lacchāma, sotthinā ca caṇḍālavaṃsā orohissāmā’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, medakathālikā antevāsī caṇḍālavaṃsikaṃ etadavoca – ‘na kho panetaṃ, ācariya, evaṃ bhavissati. Tvaṃ, ācariya, attānaṃ rakkha, ahaṃ attānaṃ rakkhissāmi. Evaṃ mayaṃ attaguttā attarakkhitā sippāni ceva dassessāma, lābhañca lacchāma, sotthinā ca caṇḍālavaṃsā orohissāmā’”ti. “So tattha ñāyo”ti bhagavā etadavoca, “yathā medakathālikā antevāsī ācariyaṃ avoca. Attānaṃ, bhikkhave, rakkhissāmīti satipaṭṭhānaṃ sevitabbaṃ; paraṃ rakkhissāmīti satipaṭṭhānaṃ sevitabbaṃ. Attānaṃ, bhikkhave, rakkhanto paraṃ rakkhati, paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhati”.

385. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sumbhas, at a market town of the Sumbhas named Sedaka. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Once upon a time, bhikkhus, a bamboo acrobat, having set up his bamboo pole, addressed his apprentice Medakathālika: ‘Come, my dear Medakathālika, climb the bamboo pole and stand on my shoulders.’ ‘Yes, teacher,’ replied Medakathālika, the apprentice, and having assented to the bamboo acrobat, he climbed the bamboo pole and stood on the teacher’s shoulders. Then, bhikkhus, the bamboo acrobat said to his apprentice Medakathālika: ‘You, my dear Medakathālika, protect me, and I will protect you. Thus, with one guarding the other, with one protecting the other, we will display our skills, gain a profit, and descend safely from the bamboo pole.’ When this was said, Medakathālika the apprentice replied to the bamboo acrobat: ‘That is not how it will be, teacher. You, teacher, protect yourself, and I will protect myself. Thus, self-guarded and self-protected, we will display our skills, gain a profit, and descend safely from the bamboo pole.’” “That is the correct way,” the Blessed One said, “just as Medakathālika the apprentice spoke to his teacher. ‘I will protect myself,’ bhikkhus—thus should the establishment of mindfulness be cultivated. ‘I will protect others,’ bhikkhus—thus should the establishment of mindfulness be cultivated. By protecting oneself, bhikkhus, one protects others; by protecting others, one protects oneself.”

“Kathañca[M 3.0147], bhikkhave, attānaṃ rakkhanto paraṃ rakkhati? Āsevanāya, bhāvanāya, bahulīkammena – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, attānaṃ rakkhanto paraṃ rakkhati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhati? Khantiyā, avihiṃsāya, mettacittatāya, anudayatāya – evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhati. Attānaṃ, bhikkhave, rakkhissāmīti satipaṭṭhānaṃ sevitabbaṃ; paraṃ rakkhissāmīti satipaṭṭhānaṃ sevitabbaṃ. Attānaṃ, bhikkhave, rakkhanto paraṃ rakkhati, paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhatī”ti. Navamaṃ.

“And how, bhikkhus, does one protect others by protecting oneself? By cultivation, by development, and by repeated practice—it is in this way, bhikkhus, that by protecting oneself, one protects others. And how, bhikkhus, does one protect oneself by protecting others? By patience, by non-harming, by a mind of loving-kindness, and by compassion—it is in this way, bhikkhus, that by protecting others, one protects oneself. ‘I will protect myself,’ bhikkhus—thus the establishment of mindfulness should be cultivated. ‘I will protect others,’ bhikkhus—thus the establishment of mindfulness should be cultivated. By protecting oneself, bhikkhus, one protects others; by protecting others, one protects oneself.” Ninth.

10. Janapadakalyāṇīsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Beauty of the Land

386. Evaṃ [T 5.0226] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sumbhesu viharati sedakaṃ nāma sumbhānaṃ nigamo. Tatra [P 5.0170] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

386. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sumbhas at Sedaka, a market town of the Sumbhas. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus, saying, “Bhikkhus.” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ‘janapadakalyāṇī, janapadakalyāṇī’ti kho, bhikkhave, mahājanakāyo sannipateyya. ‘Sā kho panassa janapadakalyāṇī paramapāsāvinī nacce, paramapāsāvinī gīte. Janapadakalyāṇī naccati gāyatī’ti kho, bhikkhave, bhiyyosomattāya mahājanakāyo [V 3.0245] sannipateyya. Atha puriso āgaccheyya jīvitukāmo amaritukāmo sukhakāmo dukkhappaṭikūlo. Tamenaṃ evaṃ vadeyya – ‘ayaṃ te, ambho purisa, samatittiko telapatto antarena ca mahāsamajjaṃ antarena ca janapadakalyāṇiyā pariharitabbo. Puriso ca te ukkhittāsiko piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhissati. Yattheva naṃ thokampi chaḍḍessati tattheva te siro pātessatī’ti. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, api nu so puriso amuṃ telapattaṃ amanasikaritvā bahiddhā pamādaṃ āhareyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

“Suppose, bhikkhus, a great crowd were to gather, crying, ‘The beauty of the land! The beauty of the land!’ And that beauty of the land were a supreme performer in dance and song. An even larger crowd would gather, crying, ‘The beauty of the land is dancing and singing!’ Then a man would come along, desiring to live and not to die, desiring happiness and averse to suffering. They would say to him: ‘Here, good man, is a bowl filled to the brim with oil. You must carry it between the great assembly and the beauty of the land. A man with a drawn sword will follow right behind you, and wherever you spill even a little, right there he will cut off your head.’ What do you think, bhikkhus? Would that man, failing to attend to that bowl of oil, give in to external heedlessness?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.”

“Upamā kho myāyaṃ, bhikkhave, katā atthassa viññāpanāya. Ayaṃ cevettha attho – samatittiko telapattoti kho, bhikkhave, kāyagatāya etaṃ satiyā adhivacanaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘kāyagatā sati no bhāvitā [T 5.0227] bhavissati bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā [M 3.0148] anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā’ti. Evañhi kho, bhikkhave, sikkhitabba”nti. Dasamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I have given this simile to make the meaning clear. And this is the meaning: ‘A bowl of oil filled to the brim,’ bhikkhus, is a designation for mindfulness directed to the body. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will develop mindfulness directed to the body, make it a regular practice, make it our vehicle, make it our foundation, establish it, consolidate it, and properly undertake it.’ This, bhikkhus, is how you should train yourselves.” Tenth.

Nālandavaggo dutiyo.

The Nālandā Chapter, the Second.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of its contents:

Mahāpuriso [P 5.0171] nālandaṃ, cundo celañca bāhiyo;

Uttiyo ariyo brahmā, sedakaṃ janapadena cāti.

The Great Man, Nālandā, Cunda, Cela, and Bāhiya; Uttiya, the Noble One, Brahmā, Sedaka, and with the Land.

3. Sīlaṭṭhitivaggo

3. The Chapter on the Foundation of Virtue

1. Sīlasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Virtue

387. Evaṃ [T 5.0228] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ca ānando āyasmā ca bhaddo pāṭaliputte viharanti kukkuṭārāme. Atha kho āyasmā bhaddo sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā bhaddo [V 3.0246] āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “yānimāni, āvuso ānanda, kusalāni sīlāni vuttāni bhagavatā, imāni kusalāni sīlāni kimatthiyāni vuttāni bhagavatā”ti?

387. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Venerable Ānanda and the Venerable Bhadda were dwelling at Pāṭaliputta in the Kukkuṭārāma. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Bhadda arose from his seclusion and approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Ānanda. After concluding this courteous and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Bhadda said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “Friend Ānanda, regarding these wholesome virtues spoken of by the Blessed One—for what purpose were these wholesome virtues spoken of by the Blessed One?”

“Sādhu sādhu, āvuso bhadda! Bhaddako kho te, āvuso bhadda, ummaṅgo ummaggo (sī. syā. kaṃ.), bhaddakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ, kalyāṇī paripucchā. Evañhi tvaṃ, āvuso bhadda, pucchasi – ‘yānimāni āvuso ānanda, kusalāni sīlāni vuttāni bhagavatā, imāni kusalāni sīlāni kimatthiyāni vuttāni bhagavatā’”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. “Yānimāni, āvuso bhadda, kusalāni sīlāni vuttāni bhagavatā, imāni kusalāni sīlāni yāvadeva catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvanāya vuttāni bhagavatā”.

“Good, good, friend Bhadda! Good indeed is your ingenuity, friend Bhadda, good your intelligence, and excellent your questioning. For you ask thus: ‘Friend Ānanda, these wholesome virtues spoken of by the Blessed One—for what purpose were these wholesome virtues spoken of by the Blessed One?’” “Yes, friend.” “Friend Bhadda, these wholesome virtues spoken of by the Blessed One were spoken for the very purpose of developing the four foundations of mindfulness.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ[T 5.0229]; vedanāsu…pe… [M 3.0149] citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Yānimāni[P 5.0172], āvuso bhadda, kusalāni sīlāni vuttāni bhagavatā, imāni kusalāni sīlāni yāvadeva imesaṃ catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvanāya vuttāni bhagavatā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Which four? Here, friend, a monk dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating feelings… mind… phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. Friend Bhadda, whatever wholesome virtues have been spoken of by the Blessed One, these wholesome virtues have been spoken of by the Blessed One just for the development of these four foundations of mindfulness.” This is the first.

2. Ciraṭṭhitisuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Long-Lasting Stability

388. Taṃyeva nidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā bhaddo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, āvuso ānanda, hetu, ko paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hoti? Ko panāvuso ānanda, hetu, ko paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti?

388. The same introduction. Seated to one side, the Venerable Bhadda said to the Venerable Ānanda: “What, friend Ānanda, is the cause, what is the reason why, when the Tathāgata has attained final Nibbāna, the true Dhamma does not endure long? And what, friend Ānanda, is the cause, what is the reason why, when the Tathāgata has attained final Nibbāna, the true Dhamma endures long?”

“Sādhu sādhu, āvuso bhadda! Bhaddako kho te, āvuso bhadda, ummaṅgo, bhaddakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ, kalyāṇī paripucchā. Evañhi tvaṃ, āvuso bhadda, pucchasi – ‘ko nu kho, āvuso ānanda, hetu, ko paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hoti? Ko panāvuso ānanda, hetu, ko paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko [V 3.0247] hotī’”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. “Catunnaṃ kho, āvuso, satipaṭṭhānānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hoti. Catunnañca kho, āvuso, satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hoti”.

“Good, good, friend Bhadda! Good indeed is your ingenuity, friend Bhadda, good your intelligence, and excellent your questioning. For you ask thus: ‘What, friend Ānanda, is the cause, what is the reason why, when the Tathāgata has attained final Nibbāna, the true Dhamma does not endure long? And what, friend Ānanda, is the cause, what is the reason why, when the Tathāgata has attained final Nibbāna, the true Dhamma endures long?’” “Yes, friend.” “It is, friend, because of the non-development and non-cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness that, when the Tathāgata has attained final Nibbāna, the true Dhamma does not endure long. And it is because of the development and cultivation of the four foundations of mindfulness that, when the Tathāgata has attained final Nibbāna, the true Dhamma endures long.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idhāvuso[T 5.0230], bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Imesaṃ kho, āvuso, catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hoti. Imesañca kho, āvuso, catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Which four? Here, friend, a monk dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world; feelings as feelings… mind as mind… phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. It is, friend, because of the non-development and non-cultivation of these four foundations of mindfulness that, when the Tathāgata has attained final Nibbāna, the true Dhamma does not endure long. And it is, friend, because of the development and cultivation of these four foundations of mindfulness that, when the Tathāgata has attained final Nibbāna, the true Dhamma endures long.” The second.

3. Parihānasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Decline

389. Ekaṃ [M 3.0150] samayaṃ āyasmā ca ānando āyasmā ca bhaddo pāṭaliputte [P 5.0173] viharanti kukkuṭārāme. Atha kho āyasmā bhaddo sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā bhaddo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, āvuso ānanda, hetu, ko paccayo yena saddhammaparihānaṃ hoti? Ko nu kho, āvuso ānanda, hetu, ko paccayo yena saddhammaaparihānaṃ hotī”ti?

389. On one occasion Venerable Ānanda and Venerable Bhadda were dwelling at Pāṭaliputta in the Cock's Monastery. Then, in the evening, Venerable Bhadda arose from seclusion and approached Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with Venerable Ānanda, and when they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Venerable Bhadda said to Venerable Ānanda: “What, friend Ānanda, is the cause, what is the reason whereby there is decline of the true Dhamma? And what, friend Ānanda, is the cause, what is the reason whereby there is no decline of the true Dhamma?”

“Sādhu sādhu, āvuso bhadda! Bhaddako kho te, āvuso bhadda, ummaṅgo, bhaddakaṃ paṭibhānaṃ, kalyāṇī paripucchā. Evañhi tvaṃ, āvuso bhadda, pucchasi – ‘ko nu kho, āvuso ānanda, hetu, ko paccayo yena saddhammaparihānaṃ [T 5.0231] hoti? Ko panāvuso ānanda, hetu, ko paccayo yena saddhammaaparihānaṃ hotī’”ti? “Evamāvuso”ti. “Catunnaṃ kho, āvuso[V 3.0248], satipaṭṭhānānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā saddhammaparihānaṃ hoti. Catunnañca kho, āvuso, satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā saddhammaaparihānaṃ hoti”.

“Good, good, friend Bhadda! Good indeed is your ingenuity, friend Bhadda, good your intelligence, and excellent your questioning. For you ask thus: ‘What, friend Ānanda, is the cause, what is the reason by which there is decline of the true Dhamma? And what, friend Ānanda, is the cause, what is the reason by which there is no decline of the true Dhamma?’” “Yes, friend.” “It is, friend, because the four foundations of mindfulness have not been developed and not been cultivated that there is decline of the true Dhamma. And it is, friend, because the four foundations of mindfulness have been developed and cultivated that there is no decline of the true Dhamma.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Imesaṃ kho, āvuso, catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā saddhammaparihānaṃ hoti. Imesañca kho, āvuso, catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā saddhammaaparihānaṃ hotī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Which four? Here, friend, a monk dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating feelings as feelings… mind as mind… phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. It is, friend, because these four foundations of mindfulness have not been developed and not been cultivated that the true Dhamma declines. And it is, friend, because these four foundations of mindfulness have been developed and cultivated that the true Dhamma does not decline.” The third.

4. Suddhasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Purity

390. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, satipaṭṭhānā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu [P 5.0174] …pe… citte [M 3.0151] …pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

390. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four foundations of mindfulness. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating feelings as feelings… mind as mind… phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. These, bhikkhus, are the four foundations of mindfulness.”

5. Aññatarabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

5. A Certain Brahmin

391. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena [T 5.0232] bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hoti? Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu, ko paccayo yena tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti?

391. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's Park. Then a certain brahmin approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having exchanged courteous and amiable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that brahmin said to the Blessed One: “What, Venerable Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition by which, when the Tathāgata has attained Parinibbāna, the true Dhamma does not last long? And what, Venerable Gotama, is the cause, what is the condition by which, when the Tathāgata has attained Parinibbāna, the true Dhamma lasts long?”

“Catunnaṃ [V 3.0249] kho, brāhmaṇa, satipaṭṭhānānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hoti. Catunnañca kho, brāhmaṇa, satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hoti.

“Brahmin, it is because the four foundations of mindfulness have not been developed and not been frequently practiced that the true Dhamma does not endure long after the Tathāgata's Parinibbāna. But, Brahmin, it is because the four foundations of mindfulness have been developed and frequently practiced that the true Dhamma endures long after the Tathāgata's Parinibbāna.

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idha, brāhmaṇa, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Imesaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ abhāvitattā abahulīkatattā tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo na ciraṭṭhitiko hoti. Imesañca kho, brāhmaṇa, catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā tathāgate parinibbute saddhammo ciraṭṭhitiko hotī”ti.

“Which four? Here, brahmin, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating feelings as feelings… mind as mind… phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world. It is, brahmin, because these four foundations of mindfulness have not been developed and not been frequently practiced that the true Dhamma does not long endure after the Tathāgata's Parinibbāna. But it is, brahmin, because these four foundations of mindfulness have been developed and frequently practiced that the true Dhamma long endures after the Tathāgata's Parinibbāna.”

Evaṃ vutte so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ[T 5.0233], bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

When this was said, that brahmin said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Venerable Gotama!… From this day forth, may the Venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”

6. Padesasuttaṃ

6. A Portion

392. Ekaṃ [M 3.0152] samayaṃ āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno āyasmā ca anuruddho sākete viharanti kaṇḍakīvane kaṇṭakīvane (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). Atha kho āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca mahāmoggallāno sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitā yenāyasmā aniruddho tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā anuruddhena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ [P 5.0175] sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – “‘sekho, sekho’ti sekkho sekkhoti (syā. kaṃ.), āvuso anuruddha, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, sekho hotī”ti? “Catunnaṃ kho, āvuso, satipaṭṭhānānaṃ padesaṃ bhāvitattā sekho hoti”.

392. On one occasion, the Venerable Sāriputta, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, and the Venerable Anuruddha were dwelling at Sāketa in the Kaṇḍakī Grove. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, having arisen from seclusion, approached the Venerable Anuruddha. Having approached, they exchanged cordial greetings with the Venerable Anuruddha. After concluding their courteous and friendly talk, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Venerable Anuruddha: “Friend Anuruddha, it is said, ‘a trainee, a trainee.’ To what extent, friend, is one a trainee?” “Friend, one is a trainee because of having developed a portion of the four foundations of mindfulness.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ?
