Here, Bhikkhus, a noble disciple is mindful, endowed with supreme maturity of mindfulness, one who remembers and recollects again and again what was done and said long ago. He dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... he dwells contemplating mind in mind... he dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. This, Bhikkhus, is called the faculty of mindfulness.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, samādhindriyaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako vossaggārammaṇaṃ karitvā labhati samādhiṃ, labhati cittassa ekaggataṃ. So vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti [T 5.0263] yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, samādhindriyaṃ.

“And what, Bhikkhus, is the faculty of concentration? Here, Bhikkhus, a noble disciple, making relinquishment his object, attains concentration, attains one-pointedness of mind. He, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without applied and sustained thought, and has rapture and happiness born of concentration. With the fading away of rapture, he dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body; he enters and dwells in the third jhāna, of which the noble ones declare: 'Equanimous and mindful, he dwells happily.' With the abandoning of happiness and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and displeasure, he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is neither painful nor pleasant and has the purification of mindfulness through equanimity. This, Bhikkhus, is called the faculty of concentration.”

“Katamañca[P 5.0199], bhikkhave, paññindriyaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya, sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā. So ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ [M 3.0175] pajānāti – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, paññindriyaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyānī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“And what, Bhikkhus, is the faculty of wisdom? Here, Bhikkhus, a noble disciple is wise, endowed with wisdom that comprehends arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and rightly leads to the destruction of suffering. He knows as it really is: 'This is suffering.' He knows as it really is: 'This is the origin of suffering.' He knows as it really is: 'This is the cessation of suffering.' He knows as it really is: 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.' This, Bhikkhus, is called the faculty of wisdom. These, indeed, Bhikkhus, are the five faculties.” The tenth.

Suddhikavaggo paṭhamo.

The Suddhika Chapter, the first.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Suddhikañceva [V 3.0275] dve sotā, arahantā apare duve;

Samaṇabrāhmaṇā daṭṭhabbaṃ, vibhaṅgā apare duveti.

The Suddhika Sutta, two on the Stream-enterer, another two on the Arahant; two on Ascetics and Brahmins, the Daṭṭhabba Sutta, and another two on Analysis.

2. Mudutaravaggo

2. The Mudutara Chapter

1. Paṭilābhasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Acquisition

481. “Pañcimāni[T 5.0264], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ…pe…. Katamañca, bhikkhave, saddhindriyaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṃ – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, saddhindriyaṃ.

481. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of faith... the faculty of wisdom.... And what, Bhikkhus, is the faculty of faith? Here, Bhikkhus, a noble disciple has faith; he has faith in the enlightenment of the Tathāgata: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, the Well-Farer, the Knower of the worlds, the unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, the Teacher of gods and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ This, Bhikkhus, is called the faculty of faith.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, vīriyindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro sammappadhāne ārabbha vīriyaṃ paṭilabhati – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, vīriyindriyaṃ.

“And what, Bhikkhus, is the faculty of energy? Indeed, Bhikkhus, it is the energy that one acquires based on the four right strivings. This, Bhikkhus, is called the faculty of energy.”

“Katamañca[P 5.0200], bhikkhave, satindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro satipaṭṭhāne ārabbha satiṃ paṭilabhati – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, satindriyaṃ.

“And what, Bhikkhus, is the faculty of mindfulness? Indeed, Bhikkhus, it is the mindfulness that one acquires based on the four foundations of mindfulness. This, Bhikkhus, is called the faculty of mindfulness.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, samādhindriyaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako vossaggārammaṇaṃ karitvā labhati samādhiṃ, labhati cittassa ekaggataṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, samādhindriyaṃ.

“And what, Bhikkhus, is the faculty of concentration? Here, Bhikkhus, a noble disciple, having made relinquishment his object, gains concentration, gains one-pointedness of mind. This, Bhikkhus, is called the faculty of concentration.”

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, paññindriyaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā [V 3.0276] paññāya samannāgato ariyāya [T 5.0265] nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, paññindriyaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyānī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And what, Bhikkhus, is the faculty of wisdom? Here, Bhikkhus, a noble disciple is wise; he is endowed with wisdom that comprehends arising and cessation, which is noble, penetrative, and rightly leads to the complete destruction of suffering. This, Bhikkhus, is called the faculty of wisdom. Indeed, Bhikkhus, these are the five faculties.” The first.

2. Paṭhamasaṃkhittasuttaṃ

2. The First Concise Discourse

482. “Pañcimāni[M 3.0176], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samattā paripūrattā arahaṃ hoti, tato mudutarehi anāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi sotāpanno hoti, tato mudutarehi dhammānusārī hoti, tato mudutarehi saddhānusārī hotī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

482. Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These, bhikkhus, are the five faculties. Bhikkhus, through the completion and fulfillment of these five faculties, one becomes an Arahant. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Non-returner. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Once-returner. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Stream-enterer. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Dhamma-follower. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Faith-follower. The second.

3. Dutiyasaṃkhittasuttaṃ

3. The Second Concise Discourse

483. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samattā paripūrattā arahaṃ hoti, tato mudutarehi anāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi sotāpanno hoti, tato mudutarehi dhammānusārī hoti, tato mudutarehi saddhānusārī hoti. Iti kho, bhikkhave, indriyavemattatā phalavemattatā hoti, phalavemattatā puggalavemattatā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

483. Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These, bhikkhus, are the five faculties. Bhikkhus, through the completion and fulfillment of these five faculties, one becomes an Arahant. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Non-returner. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Once-returner. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Stream-enterer. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Dhamma-follower. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Faith-follower. Thus, bhikkhus, due to the difference in faculties, there is a difference in fruit; due to the difference in fruit, there is a difference in persons. The third.

4. Tatiyasaṃkhittasuttaṃ

4. The Third Concise Discourse

484. “Pañcimāni[P 5.0201], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samattā paripūrattā arahaṃ hoti, tato mudutarehi anāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmī [T 5.0266] hoti, tato mudutarehi sotāpanno hoti, tato mudutarehi dhammānusārī hoti, tato mudutarehi saddhānusārī hoti. Iti kho, bhikkhave, paripūraṃ paripūrakārī ārādheti, padesaṃ [V 3.0277] padesakārī ārādheti. ‘Avañjhāni tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcindriyānī’ti vadāmī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

484. Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These, bhikkhus, are the five faculties. Bhikkhus, through the completion and fulfillment of these five faculties, one becomes an Arahant. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Non-returner. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Once-returner. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Stream-enterer. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Dhamma-follower. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Faith-follower. Thus, bhikkhus, one who works for completion accomplishes the complete; one who works for a part accomplishes a part. I declare, bhikkhus, that these five faculties are not barren. The fourth.

5. Paṭhamavitthārasuttaṃ

5. The First Detailed Discourse

485. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samattā [M 3.0177] paripūrattā arahaṃ hoti, tato mudutarehi antarāparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi uddhaṃsoto hoti akaniṭṭhagāmī, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi sotāpanno hoti, tato mudutarehi dhammānusārī hoti, tato mudutarehi saddhānusārī hotī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

485. Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These, bhikkhus, are the five faculties. Bhikkhus, through the completion and fulfillment of these five faculties, one is an Arahant. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an antarāparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an upahaccaparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an upstream-goer bound for the Akaniṭṭha realm. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Once-returner. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Stream-enterer. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Dhamma-follower. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Faith-follower. The fifth.

6. Dutiyavitthārasuttaṃ

6. The Second Detailed Discourse

486. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samattā paripūrattā arahaṃ hoti, tato mudutarehi antarāparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi uddhaṃsoto hoti akaniṭṭhagāmī, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmī hoti[T 5.0267], tato mudutarehi sotāpanno hoti, tato mudutarehi dhammānusārī hoti, tato mudutarehi saddhānusārī hoti. Iti kho, bhikkhave, indriyavemattatā phalavemattatā hoti, phalavemattatā puggalavemattatā hotī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

486. Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These, bhikkhus, are the five faculties. Bhikkhus, through the completion and fulfillment of these five faculties, one becomes an Arahant. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an antarāparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an upahaccaparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an upstream-goer bound for the Akaniṭṭha realm. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Once-returner. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Stream-enterer. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Dhamma-follower. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Faith-follower. Thus, bhikkhus, due to the difference in faculties, there is a difference in fruit; due to the difference in fruit, there is a difference in persons. The sixth.

7. Tatiyavitthārasuttaṃ

7. The Third Detailed Discourse

487. “Pañcimāni[P 5.0202], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ [V 3.0278] samattā paripūrattā arahaṃ hoti, tato mudutarehi antarāparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi uddhaṃsoto hoti akaniṭṭhagāmī, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi sotāpanno hoti, tato mudutarehi dhammānusārī hoti, tato mudutarehi saddhānusārī hoti. Iti kho, bhikkhave, paripūraṃ [M 3.0178] paripūrakārī ārādheti, padesaṃ padesakārī ārādheti. ‘Avañjhāni tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcindriyānī’ti vadāmī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

487. Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These, bhikkhus, are the five faculties. Bhikkhus, through the completion and fulfillment of these five faculties, one becomes an Arahant. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an antarāparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an upahaccaparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes an upstream-goer bound for the Akaniṭṭha realm. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Once-returner. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Stream-enterer. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Dhamma-follower. With faculties weaker than that, one becomes a Faith-follower. Thus, bhikkhus, one who works for completion accomplishes the complete, and one who works for a part accomplishes a part. I declare, bhikkhus, that these five faculties are not barren. The seventh.

8. Paṭipannasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Those Practicing

488. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samattā paripūrattā arahaṃ hoti, tato mudutarehi arahattaphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno hoti, tato mudutarehi anāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya [T 5.0268] paṭipanno hoti, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno hoti, tato mudutarehi sotāpanno hoti, tato mudutarehi sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno hoti. Yassa kho, bhikkhave, imāni pañcindriyāni sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ natthi, tamahaṃ ‘bāhiro puthujjanapakkhe ṭhito’ti vadāmī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

488. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom—these, bhikkhus, are the five faculties. Bhikkhus, by virtue of the completion and fulfillment of these five faculties, one is an Arahant. If they are weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of Arahantship. If they are weaker than that, one is a non-returner. If they are weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of non-returning. If they are weaker than that, one is a once-returner. If they are weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of once-returning. If they are weaker than that, one is a stream-enterer. If they are weaker than that, one is practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry. But, bhikkhus, one in whom these five faculties are entirely and utterly absent in every way, I declare that person to be an outsider, one who stands in the faction of the worldling.”

9. Sampannasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Being Accomplished

489. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

489. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One, and having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:

“‘Indriyasampanno, indriyasampanno’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, indriyasampanno hotī”ti? “Idha[P 5.0203], bhikkhu, bhikkhu saddhindriyaṃ bhāveti upasamagāmiṃ sambodhagāmiṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ bhāveti upasamagāmiṃ sambodhagāmiṃ, satindriyaṃ bhāveti upasamagāmiṃ sambodhagāmiṃ[V 3.0279], samādhindriyaṃ bhāveti upasamagāmiṃ sambodhagāmiṃ, paññindriyaṃ bhāveti upasamagāmiṃ sambodhagāmiṃ. Ettāvatā kho, bhikkhu, bhikkhu indriyasampanno hotī”ti. Navamaṃ.

“Venerable sir, it is said, ‘one accomplished in the faculties, one accomplished in the faculties.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is one accomplished in the faculties?” “Here, bhikkhu, a bhikkhu develops the faculty of faith, which leads to peace, which leads to enlightenment; he develops the faculty of energy, which leads to peace, which leads to enlightenment; he develops the faculty of mindfulness, which leads to peace, which leads to enlightenment; he develops the faculty of concentration, which leads to peace, which leads to enlightenment; he develops the faculty of wisdom, which leads to peace, which leads to enlightenment. It is to this extent, bhikkhu, that a bhikkhu is one accomplished in the faculties.”

10. Āsavakkhayasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Destruction of the Taints

490. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā [M 3.0179] bahulīkatattā bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva [T 5.0269] dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

490. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom—these, bhikkhus, are the five faculties. Bhikkhus, it is due to the development and cultivation of these five faculties that a bhikkhu, through the destruction of the taints, in this very life, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, attains and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.”

Mudutaravaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter: On Weaker Faculties

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Paṭilābho tayo saṃkhittā, vitthārā apare tayo;

Paṭipanno ca sampanno paṭipanno cūpasamo (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), dasamaṃ āsavakkhayanti.

The Paṭilābha Sutta, three in brief, and another three in detail; the Paṭipanna Sutta and the Sampanna Sutta, and the tenth is the Āsavakkhaya Sutta.

3. Chaḷindriyavaggo

3. The Chapter on the Six Faculties

1. Punabbhavasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Renewed Existence

491. “Pañcimāni[T 5.0270], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ. Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ, neva [P 5.0204] tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ abhisambuddho paccaññāsiṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.). Yato ca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya [V 3.0280] ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti cetovimutti (sī. pī. ka.), ayamantimā jāti, natthidāni punabbhavo’”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

491. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. Bhikkhus, for as long as I did not directly know as it really is the arising, the ceasing, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these five faculties, for so long, bhikkhus, I did not claim to have awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. But, bhikkhus, when I directly knew as it really is the arising, the ceasing, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these five faculties, then, bhikkhus, I claimed to have awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘My liberation is unshakeable. This is the final birth. Now there is no renewed existence.’”

2. Jīvitindriyasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Life Faculty

492. “Tīṇimāni[M 3.0180], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni tīṇi? Itthindriyaṃ, purisindriyaṃ, jīvitindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi indriyānī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

492. “Bhikkhus, there are these three faculties. What three? The faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity, and the life faculty. These, bhikkhus, are the three faculties.”

3. Aññindriyasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Faculty of Final Knowledge

493. “Tīṇimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni tīṇi? Anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ[T 5.0271], aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, tīṇi indriyānī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

493. “Bhikkhus, there are these three faculties. What three? The faculty of ‘I will know what has not yet been known,’ the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has final knowledge. These, bhikkhus, are the three faculties.”

4. Ekabījīsuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Single-Seeder

494. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samattā paripūrattā arahaṃ hoti, tato mudutarehi antarāparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi [P 5.0205] sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, tato mudutarehi uddhaṃsoto hoti akaniṭṭhagāmī, tato mudutarehi sakadāgāmī hoti, tato mudutarehi ekabījī ekabīji (ka.) hoti, tato mudutarehi kolaṃkolo hoti, tato mudutarehi sattakkhattuparamo hoti, tato mudutarehi dhammānusārī hoti, tato mudutarehi saddhānusārī hotī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

494. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These, bhikkhus, are the five faculties. When, bhikkhus, these five faculties are fully developed and perfected, one is an arahant. If they are weaker than that, one is an antarāparinibbāyī. If they are weaker still, one is an upahaccaparinibbāyī. If they are weaker still, one is an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. If they are weaker still, one is a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī. If they are weaker still, one is an uddhaṃsoto, one who goes to Akaniṭṭha. If they are weaker still, one is a once-returner. If they are weaker still, one is a single-seeder. If they are weaker still, one is a family-to-family. If they are weaker still, one is a seven-times-at-most. If they are weaker still, one is a Dhamma-follower. If they are weaker still, one is a faith-follower.”

5. Suddhakasuttaṃ

5. The Simple Discourse

495. “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni cha? Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ[V 3.0281], jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, manindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, cha indriyānī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

495. “Bhikkhus, there are these six faculties. What six? The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, and the mind faculty—these, bhikkhus, are the six faculties.”

6. Sotāpannasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Stream-Enterer

496. “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni cha? Cakkhundriyaṃ…pe… manindriyaṃ. Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako imesaṃ channaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ [T 5.0272] pajānāti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

496. “Bhikkhus, there are these six faculties. What six? The eye faculty... the mind faculty. When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple understands as it truly is the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these six faculties, this noble disciple, bhikkhus, is called a stream-enterer, one not subject to falling into states of woe, certain, and bound for enlightenment.” Sixth.

7. Arahantasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Arahant

497. “Chayimāni[M 3.0181], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni cha? Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, manindriyaṃ. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imesaṃ channaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādāvimutto hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto’”ti. Sattamaṃ.

497. “Bhikkhus, there are these six faculties. What six? The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, and the mind faculty. When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, having understood as it truly is the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these six faculties, is liberated without clinging, this one is called, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who is an arahant, whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own true welfare, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and is liberated through perfect final knowledge.” Seventh.

8. Sambuddhasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Perfectly Enlightened One

498. “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni cha? Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, manindriyaṃ. Yāvakīvañcāhaṃ[P 5.0206], bhikkhave, imesaṃ channaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nābbhaññāsiṃ, neva tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassa maṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ. Yato ca khvāhaṃ, bhikkhave, imesaṃ channaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca [V 3.0282] yathābhūtaṃ abbhaññāsiṃ, athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti [T 5.0273] paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti, ayamantimā jāti, natthidāni punabbhavo’”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

498. “Bhikkhus, there are these six faculties. What six? The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, and the mind faculty. So long, bhikkhus, as I did not directly know as it truly is the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these six faculties, for so long I did not claim to have awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans. But when, bhikkhus, I directly knew as it truly is the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these six faculties, then I claimed to have awakened to the unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in this world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, in this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘My liberation is unshakeable; this is the last birth; now there is no further becoming.’” Eighth.

9. Paṭhamasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

499. “Chayimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni cha? Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, manindriyaṃ. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṃ channaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti, na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca panete āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā [M 3.0182] diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti”. “Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṃ channaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānanti, te kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Navamaṃ.

499. “Bhikkhus, there are these six faculties. What six? The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, and the mind faculty. Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand as it truly is the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these six faculties, I do not consider them to be ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones do not, in this very life, realize for themselves with direct knowledge the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood and dwell having attained it. But, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do understand as it truly is the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape concerning these six faculties, I consider them to be ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones, in this very life, realize for themselves with direct knowledge the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood and dwell having attained it.” Ninth.

10. Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

500. “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā cakkhundriyaṃ nappajānanti, cakkhundriyasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, cakkhundriyanirodhaṃ nappajānanti, cakkhundriyanirodhagāminiṃ [T 5.0274] paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti; sotindriyaṃ…pe… ghānindriyaṃ…pe… jivhindriyaṃ…pe… kāyindriyaṃ…pe… manindriyaṃ nappajānanti, manindriyasamudayaṃ nappajānanti[V 3.0283], manindriyanirodhaṃ nappajānanti, manindriyanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti. Na me te, bhikkhave…pe… sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.

500. “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand the eye faculty, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation; ...the ear faculty...; ...the nose faculty...; ...the tongue faculty...; ...the body faculty...; or the mind faculty, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation—I do not consider them to be ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones do not, in this very life, realize for themselves with direct knowledge the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood and dwell having attained it.

“Ye [P 5.0207] ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā cakkhundriyaṃ pajānanti, cakkhundriyasamudayaṃ pajānanti, cakkhundriyanirodhaṃ pajānanti, cakkhundriyanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti, sotindriyaṃ…pe… ghānindriyaṃ…pe… jivhindriyaṃ…pe… kāyindriyaṃ…pe… manindriyaṃ pajānanti, manindriyasamudayaṃ pajānanti, manindriyanirodhaṃ pajānanti, manindriyanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti, te kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“But, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins understand the eye faculty, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation; ...the ear faculty...; ...the nose faculty...; ...the tongue faculty...; ...the body faculty...; and the mind faculty, its origin, its cessation, and the path leading to its cessation—I consider them to be ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones, in this very life, realize for themselves with direct knowledge the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood and dwell having attained it.” Tenth.

Chaḷindriyavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on the Six Faculties, the Third.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Punabbhavo jīvitaññāya, ekabījī ca suddhakaṃ;

Soto arahasambuddho, dve ca samaṇabrāhmaṇāti.

The Punabbhava, Jīvita, and Aññā suttas; the Ekabījī and Suddhika suttas; the Soto, Araha, and Sambuddha suttas; and the two Samaṇabrāhmaṇa suttas.

4. Sukhindriyavaggo

4. The Chapter on the Faculty of Pleasure

1. Suddhikasuttaṃ

1. The Suddhika Sutta

501. “Pañcimāni[M 3.0183][T 5.0275], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyānī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

501. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of joy, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity. Indeed, bhikkhus, these are the five faculties.” First.

2. Sotāpannasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Stream-enterer

502. “Pañcimāni[V 3.0284], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ. Yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako imesaṃ pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

502. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of joy, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity. When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple understands as it really is the origin, the cessation, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in regard to these five faculties—this noble disciple, bhikkhus, is called a stream-enterer, one not subject to fall, fixed, and bound for enlightenment.” Second.

3. Arahantasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Arahant

503. “Pañcimāni[P 5.0208], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ. Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imesaṃ pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ viditvā anupādāvimutto hoti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

503. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of joy, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity. When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu understands as it really is the origination, cessation, gratification, danger, and escape in regard to these five faculties, and is liberated by non-clinging, he is called a bhikkhu who is an arahant, whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed, and who is liberated by perfect knowledge.” Third.

4. Paṭhamasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

4. The First Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

504. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ. Ye [T 5.0276] hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṃ pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti, na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca panete āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.

504. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of joy, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity. Whatever ascetics or brahmins, bhikkhus, do not understand as it really is the origination, cessation, gratification, danger, and escape in regard to these five faculties, I do not consider them to be ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins. Nor do these venerable ones, having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge, enter upon and abide in this very life in the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood.

“Ye [M 3.0184] ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā imesaṃ pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca assādañca ādīnavañca nissaraṇañca yathābhūtaṃ pajānanti, te kho me[V 3.0285], bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“But whatever ascetics or brahmins, bhikkhus, understand as it really is the origination, cessation, gratification, danger, and escape in regard to these five faculties, these, bhikkhus, I consider to be ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins. And these venerable ones, having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge, enter upon and abide in this very life in the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.” Fourth.

5. Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

5. The Second Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

505. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā sukhindriyaṃ nappajānanti, sukhindriyasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, sukhindriyanirodhaṃ nappajānanti, sukhindriyanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti; dukkhindriyaṃ nappajānanti…pe… somanassindriyaṃ nappajānanti…pe… domanassindriyaṃ nappajānanti [T 5.0277] …pe… upekkhindriyaṃ nappajānanti, upekkhindriyasamudayaṃ nappajānanti, upekkhindriyanirodhaṃ nappajānanti, upekkhindriyanirodhagāminiṃ [P 5.0209] paṭipadaṃ nappajānanti; na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca panete āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.

505. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of joy, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity. Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins do not understand the faculty of pleasure, do not understand the origin of the faculty of pleasure, do not understand the cessation of the faculty of pleasure, do not understand the path leading to the cessation of the faculty of pleasure; do not understand the faculty of pain… do not understand the faculty of joy… do not understand the faculty of displeasure… do not understand the faculty of equanimity, do not understand the origin of the faculty of equanimity, do not understand the cessation of the faculty of equanimity, do not understand the path leading to the cessation of the faculty of equanimity—I do not consider those ascetics or brahmins to be ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins. Nor do those venerable ones, in this very life, dwell having themselves realized with higher knowledge and attained the goal of asceticism or the goal of brahminhood.

“Ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā sukhindriyaṃ pajānanti, sukhindriyasamudayaṃ pajānanti, sukhindriyanirodhaṃ pajānanti, sukhindriyanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti; dukkhindriyaṃ pajānanti…pe… somanassindriyaṃ pajānanti… domanassindriyaṃ pajānanti… upekkhindriyaṃ pajānanti, upekkhindriyasamudayaṃ pajānanti, upekkhindriyanirodhaṃ pajānanti, upekkhindriyanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ pajānanti, te ca kho me, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu ceva samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu ca brāhmaṇasammatā, te ca panāyasmanto sāmaññatthañca brahmaññatthañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“But, bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins understand the faculty of pleasure, understand the origin of the faculty of pleasure, understand the cessation of the faculty of pleasure, understand the path leading to the cessation of the faculty of pleasure; understand the faculty of pain… understand the faculty of joy… understand the faculty of displeasure… understand the faculty of equanimity, understand the origin of the faculty of equanimity, understand the cessation of the faculty of equanimity, understand the path leading to the cessation of the faculty of equanimity—I consider those ascetics or brahmins to be ascetics among ascetics and brahmins among brahmins. And those venerable ones, in this very life, dwell having themselves realized with higher knowledge and attained the goal of asceticism and the goal of brahminhood.” Fifth.

6. Paṭhamavibhaṅgasuttaṃ

6. The First Discourse on Analysis

506. “Pañcimāni[V 3.0286], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ.

506. “Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of joy, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity.

“Katamañca[M 3.0185], bhikkhave, sukhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ[T 5.0278], kāyikaṃ sātaṃ, kāyasamphassajaṃ sukhaṃ sātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukhindriyaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the faculty of pleasure? Whatever, bhikkhus, is bodily pleasure, bodily agreeableness, the pleasant, agreeable feeling born of bodily contact—this, bhikkhus, is called the faculty of pleasure.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, dukkhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ, kāyikaṃ asātaṃ, kāyasamphassajaṃ dukkhaṃ asātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhindriyaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the faculty of pain? Whatever, bhikkhus, is bodily pain, bodily disagreeableness, the painful, disagreeable feeling born of bodily contact—this, bhikkhus, is called the faculty of pain.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, somanassindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ, cetasikaṃ sātaṃ, manosamphassajaṃ sukhaṃ sātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, somanassindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of gladness? Whatever, monks, is mental pleasure, mental satisfaction, the pleasant and satisfying feeling born of mind-contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of gladness.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, domanassindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ, cetasikaṃ asātaṃ, manosamphassajaṃ dukkhaṃ asātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, domanassindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of displeasure? Whatever, monks, is mental pain, mental disagreeableness, the painful, disagreeable feeling born of mind-contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of displeasure.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, upekkhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ vā cetasikaṃ vā nevasātaṃ nāsātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, upekkhindriyaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyānī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of equanimity? Whatever, monks, is feeling that is neither agreeable nor disagreeable, whether bodily or mental—this is called, monks, the faculty of equanimity. These, monks, are the five faculties.” Sixth.

7. Dutiyavibhaṅgasuttaṃ

7. The Second Discourse on Analysis

507. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ.

507. “Monks, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of gladness, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity.

“Katamañca[V 3.0287][P 5.0210], bhikkhave, sukhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ, kāyikaṃ sātaṃ, kāyasamphassajaṃ sukhaṃ sātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukhindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of pleasure? Whatever, monks, is bodily pleasure, bodily ease, the pleasant, agreeable feeling born of bodily contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of pleasure.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, dukkhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ[T 5.0279], kāyikaṃ asātaṃ, kāyasamphassajaṃ dukkhaṃ asātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of pain? Whatever, monks, is bodily pain, bodily unpleasantness, the painful, unpleasant feeling born of bodily contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of pain.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, somanassindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ, cetasikaṃ sātaṃ, manosamphassajaṃ sukhaṃ sātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, somanassindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of gladness? Whatever, monks, is mental pleasure, mental satisfaction, the pleasant, satisfying feeling born of mind-contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of gladness.

“Katamañca[M 3.0186], bhikkhave, domanassindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ, cetasikaṃ asātaṃ, manosamphassajaṃ dukkhaṃ asātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, domanassindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of displeasure? Whatever, monks, is mental pain, mental disagreeableness, the painful, disagreeable feeling born of mind-contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of displeasure.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, upekkhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ vā cetasikaṃ vā nevasātaṃ nāsātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, upekkhindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of equanimity? Whatever, monks, is bodily or mental feeling that is neither agreeable nor disagreeable—this is called, monks, the faculty of equanimity.

“Tatra, bhikkhave, yañca sukhindriyaṃ yañca somanassindriyaṃ, sukhā sā vedanā daṭṭhabbā. Tatra, bhikkhave, yañca dukkhindriyaṃ yañca domanassindriyaṃ, dukkhā sā vedanā daṭṭhabbā. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ, adukkhamasukhā sā vedanā daṭṭhabbā. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyānī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Among these, monks, the faculty of pleasure and the faculty of gladness should be seen as pleasant feeling. Among these, monks, the faculty of pain and the faculty of displeasure should be seen as painful feeling. Among these, monks, the faculty of equanimity should be seen as neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These, monks, are the five faculties.” Seventh.

8. Tatiyavibhaṅgasuttaṃ

8. The Third Discourse on Analysis

508. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ.

508. “Monks, there are these five faculties. What are the five? The faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of gladness, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity.

“Katamañca[V 3.0288], bhikkhave, sukhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ sukhaṃ[T 5.0280], kāyikaṃ sātaṃ, kāyasamphassajaṃ sukhaṃ sātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukhindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of pleasure? Whatever, monks, is bodily pleasure, bodily ease, the pleasant, agreeable feeling born of bodily contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of pleasure.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, dukkhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ dukkhaṃ, kāyikaṃ asātaṃ, kāyasamphassajaṃ dukkhaṃ asātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of pain? Whatever, monks, is bodily pain, bodily unpleasantness, the painful, unpleasant feeling born of bodily contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of pain.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, somanassindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, cetasikaṃ sukhaṃ, cetasikaṃ sātaṃ, manosamphassajaṃ sukhaṃ sātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, somanassindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of gladness? Whatever, monks, is mental pleasure, mental satisfaction, the pleasant and satisfying feeling born of mind-contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of gladness.

“Katamañca[P 5.0211], bhikkhave, domanassindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, cetasikaṃ dukkhaṃ, cetasikaṃ asātaṃ, manosamphassajaṃ dukkhaṃ asātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, domanassindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of displeasure? Whatever, monks, is mental pain, mental disagreeableness, the painful, disagreeable feeling born of mind-contact—this is called, monks, the faculty of displeasure.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, upekkhindriyaṃ? Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kāyikaṃ vā cetasikaṃ vā neva sātaṃ nāsātaṃ vedayitaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, upekkhindriyaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the faculty of equanimity? Whatever, monks, is feeling that is neither agreeable nor disagreeable, whether bodily or mental—this is called, monks, the faculty of equanimity.

“Tatra, bhikkhave, yañca sukhindriyaṃ yañca somanassindriyaṃ, sukhā sā vedanā daṭṭhabbā. Tatra, bhikkhave, yañca dukkhindriyaṃ yañca domanassindriyaṃ, dukkhā sā vedanā daṭṭhabbā. Tatra, bhikkhave, yadidaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ, adukkhamasukhā sā vedanā daṭṭhabbā[M 3.0187]. Iti kho, bhikkhave, imāni pañcindriyāni pañca hutvā [T 5.0281] tīṇi honti, tīṇi hutvā pañca honti pariyāyenā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Therein, monks, whatever is the faculty of pleasure and whatever is the faculty of gladness, that feeling should be seen as pleasant. Therein, monks, whatever is the faculty of pain and whatever is the faculty of displeasure, that feeling should be seen as painful. Therein, monks, whatever is this faculty of equanimity, that feeling should be seen as neither-painful-nor-pleasant. Thus, monks, these five faculties, being five, become three; being three, they become five by way of arrangement.” Eighth.

9. Kaṭṭhopamasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Simile of the Log

509. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Sukhindriyaṃ, dukkhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, domanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ. Sukhavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhave, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhindriyaṃ. So sukhitova samāno ‘sukhitosmī’ti pajānāti. Tasseva sukhavedaniyassa [V 3.0289] phassassa nirodhā ‘yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ sukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannaṃ sukhindriyaṃ taṃ nirujjhati, taṃ vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti”.

509. “Monks, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of pleasure, the faculty of pain, the faculty of gladness, the faculty of displeasure, and the faculty of equanimity. Monks, dependent on a contact to be felt as pleasant, the faculty of pleasure arises. He, being one who experiences pleasure, knows: ‘I am one who experiences pleasure.’ With the cessation of that very contact to be felt as pleasant, he knows: ‘The faculty of pleasure that arose in dependence on that contact, the feeling corresponding thereto, ceases and subsides.’

“Dukkhavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhave, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati dukkhindriyaṃ. So dukkhitova samāno ‘dukkhitosmī’ti pajānāti. Tasseva dukkhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā ‘yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ dukkhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ [P 5.0212] paṭicca uppannaṃ dukkhindriyaṃ taṃ nirujjhati, taṃ vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti”.

“Monks, dependent on a contact to be felt as painful, the faculty of pain arises. He, being one who experiences pain, knows: ‘I am one who experiences pain.’ With the cessation of that very contact to be felt as painful, he knows: ‘The faculty of pain that arose in dependence on that contact, the feeling corresponding thereto, ceases and subsides.’

“Somanassavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhave, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati somanassindriyaṃ. So sumanova samāno ‘sumanosmī’ti pajānāti. Tasseva somanassavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā ‘yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ somanassavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannaṃ somanassindriyaṃ taṃ nirujjhati, taṃ vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti”.

Bhikkhus, dependent on a contact productive of joy, the faculty of joy arises. Being joyful, one understands: ‘I am joyful.’ With the cessation of that same contact productive of joy, one understands: ‘That which is felt—the faculty of joy that arose dependent on that contact productive of joy—ceases and is pacified.’

“Domanassavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhave, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati domanassindriyaṃ. So dummanova samāno ‘dummanosmī’ti pajānāti. Tasseva domanassavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā ‘yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ domanassavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannaṃ domanassindriyaṃ taṃ nirujjhati, taṃ [T 5.0282] vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti”.

Bhikkhus, dependent on a contact productive of displeasure, the faculty of displeasure arises. Being displeased, one understands: ‘I am displeased.’ With the cessation of that same contact productive of displeasure, one understands: ‘That which is felt—the faculty of displeasure that arose dependent on that contact productive of displeasure—ceases and is pacified.’

“Upekkhāvedaniyaṃ, bhikkhave, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati upekkhindriyaṃ. So upekkhakova samāno ‘upekkhakosmī’ti pajānāti. Tasseva upekkhāvedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā ‘yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ upekkhāvedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppannaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ taṃ nirujjhati, taṃ vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti”.

Bhikkhus, dependent on a contact productive of equanimity, the faculty of equanimity arises. Being equanimous, one understands: ‘I am equanimous.’ With the cessation of that same contact productive of equanimity, one understands: ‘That which is felt—the faculty of equanimity that arose dependent on that contact productive of equanimity—ceases and is pacified.’

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, dvinnaṃ kaṭṭhānaṃ saṅghaṭṭanasamodhānā saṃghaṭṭanāsamodhānā (pī. ka.), saṃghaṭanasamodhānā (syā. kaṃ.) usmā jāyati, tejo abhinibbattati; tesaṃyeva kaṭṭhānaṃ nānābhāvāvinikkhepā yā [M 3.0188] nānābhāvanikkhepā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) tajjā usmā sā nirujjhati sā vūpasammati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, sukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhindriyaṃ. So sukhitova samāno ‘sukhitosmī’ti pajānāti. Tasseva sukhavedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā ‘yaṃ tajjaṃ [V 3.0290] vedayitaṃ sukhavedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhindriyaṃ taṃ nirujjhati[P 5.0213], taṃ vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti”.

Just as, bhikkhus, from the rubbing together and combining of two sticks, heat is generated and fire is produced; and from the separation and laying aside of those same sticks, the heat that arose from that ceases and is pacified; even so, bhikkhus, dependent on a contact productive of pleasure, the faculty of pleasure arises. Being pleased, one understands: ‘I am pleased.’ With the cessation of that same contact productive of pleasure, one understands: ‘That which is felt—the faculty of pleasure that arose dependent on that contact productive of pleasure—ceases and is pacified.’

“Dukkhavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhave, phassaṃ paṭicca…pe… somanassavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhave, phassaṃ paṭicca…pe… domanassavedaniyaṃ, bhikkhave, phassaṃ paṭicca…pe… upekkhāvedaniyaṃ, bhikkhave, phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati upekkhindriyaṃ. So upekkhakova samāno ‘upekkhakosmī’ti pajānāti. Tasseva upekkhāvedaniyassa phassassa nirodhā ‘yaṃ tajjaṃ vedayitaṃ upekkhāvedaniyaṃ phassaṃ paṭicca uppajjati upekkhindriyaṃ taṃ nirujjhati, taṃ vūpasammatī’ti pajānāti”. Navamaṃ.

Bhikkhus, dependent on a contact productive of pain… and so on… Bhikkhus, dependent on a contact productive of joy… and so on… Bhikkhus, dependent on a contact productive of displeasure… and so on… Bhikkhus, dependent on a contact productive of equanimity, the faculty of equanimity arises. Being equanimous, one understands: ‘I am equanimous.’ With the cessation of that same contact productive of equanimity, one understands: ‘That which is felt—the faculty of equanimity that arose dependent on that contact productive of equanimity—ceases and is pacified.’ The Ninth.

10. Uppaṭipāṭikasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Irregular Order

510. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Dukkhindriyaṃ[T 5.0283], domanassindriyaṃ, sukhindriyaṃ, somanassindriyaṃ, upekkhindriyaṃ. Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato uppajjati dukkhindriyaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ dukkhindriyaṃ, tañca kho sanimittaṃ sanidānaṃ sasaṅkhāraṃ sappaccayaṃ. Tañca animittaṃ anidānaṃ asaṅkhāraṃ appaccayaṃ dukkhindriyaṃ uppajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’. So dukkhindriyañca pajānāti, dukkhindriyasamudayañca pajānāti, dukkhindriyanirodhañca pajānāti, yattha cuppannaṃ dukkhindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati tañca pajānāti. Kattha cuppannaṃ dukkhindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ettha cuppannaṃ dukkhindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu aññāsi dukkhindriyassa nirodhaṃ, tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati’”.

510. Bhikkhus, there are these five faculties. Which five? The faculty of pain, the faculty of displeasure, the faculty of pleasure, the faculty of joy, and the faculty of equanimity. Here, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu dwells heedful, ardent, and resolute, the faculty of pain arises. He understands thus: ‘This faculty of pain has arisen in me, and it has a cause, a source, a formation, and a condition. That a faculty of pain could arise without a cause, without a source, without a formation, and without a condition—this is not possible.’ He understands the faculty of pain, he understands the origin of the faculty of pain, he understands the cessation of the faculty of pain, and he understands where the arisen faculty of pain ceases without remainder. And where does the arisen faculty of pain cease without remainder? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by initial application and sustained application, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. It is here that the arisen faculty of pain ceases without remainder. This, bhikkhus, is called a bhikkhu who has known the cessation of the faculty of pain and, for that purpose, directs his mind.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato uppajjati domanassindriyaṃ. So [P 5.0214] evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ domanassindriyaṃ, tañca kho sanimittaṃ sanidānaṃ sasaṅkhāraṃ sappaccayaṃ. Tañca animittaṃ anidānaṃ asaṅkhāraṃ appaccayaṃ domanassindriyaṃ uppajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’[T 5.0284]. So domanassindriyañca pajānāti, domanassindriyasamudayañca pajānāti, domanassindriyanirodhañca pajānāti, yattha cuppannaṃ [V 3.0291] domanassindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ [M 3.0189] nirujjhati tañca pajānāti. Kattha cuppannaṃ domanassindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodibhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhijaṃ pītisukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ettha cuppannaṃ domanassindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu aññāsi domanassindriyassa nirodhaṃ, tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati’”.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu dwells here heedful, ardent, and resolute, the faculty of displeasure arises. He understands thus: ‘This faculty of displeasure has arisen in me, and it has a cause, a source, a formation, and a condition. That a faculty of displeasure could arise without a cause, without a source, without a formation, and without a condition—this is not possible.’ He understands the faculty of displeasure, he understands the origin of the faculty of displeasure, he understands the cessation of the faculty of displeasure, and he understands where the arisen faculty of displeasure ceases without remainder. And where does the arisen faculty of displeasure cease without remainder? Here, bhikkhus, with the stilling of initial application and sustained application, a bhikkhu enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without initial application and sustained application, and is born of concentration, with rapture and happiness. It is here that the arisen faculty of displeasure ceases without remainder. This, bhikkhus, is called a bhikkhu who has known the cessation of the faculty of displeasure and, for that purpose, directs his mind.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato uppajjati sukhindriyaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ sukhindriyaṃ, tañca kho sanimittaṃ sanidānaṃ sasaṅkhāraṃ sappaccayaṃ. Tañca animittaṃ anidānaṃ asaṅkhāraṃ appaccayaṃ sukhindriyaṃ uppajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’. So sukhindriyañca pajānāti, sukhindriyasamudayañca pajānāti, sukhindriyanirodhañca pajānāti, yattha cuppannaṃ sukhindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati tañca pajānāti. Kattha cuppannaṃ sukhindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ettha [T 5.0285] cuppannaṃ sukhindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu aññāsi sukhindriyassa nirodhaṃ, tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati’”.

Here, monks, when a monk dwells heedful, ardent, and resolute, the faculty of pleasure arises. He understands thus: ‘This faculty of pleasure has indeed arisen in me, and it has a cause, a source, a formation, and a condition. That a faculty of pleasure would arise without a cause, without a source, without a formation, and without a condition—that is not possible.’ He understands the faculty of pleasure, the origin of the faculty of pleasure, the cessation of the faculty of pleasure, and where the arisen faculty of pleasure ceases without remainder. And where does the arisen faculty of pleasure cease without remainder? Here, monks, with the fading away of rapture, a monk dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending, and experiences pleasure with the body. It is of this that the noble ones declare: ‘Equanimous and mindful, he dwells happily.’ He enters and dwells in the third jhāna. Here the arisen faculty of pleasure ceases without remainder. This, monks, is called a monk who has understood the cessation of the faculty of pleasure and directs his mind toward that purpose.

“Idha [P 5.0215] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato uppajjati somanassindriyaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ somanassindriyaṃ, tañca kho sanimittaṃ sanidānaṃ sasaṅkhāraṃ sappaccayaṃ. Tañca animittaṃ anidānaṃ asaṅkhāraṃ appaccayaṃ somanassindriyaṃ uppajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’. So somanassindriyañca pajānāti, somanassindriyasamudayañca pajānāti, somanassindriyanirodhañca pajānāti, yattha cuppannaṃ somanassindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati tañca pajānāti. Kattha cuppannaṃ somanassindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati, ettha cuppannaṃ somanassindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu aññāsi somanassindriyassa nirodhaṃ, tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharati’”.

Furthermore, monks, when a monk dwells heedful, ardent, and resolute, the faculty of mental pleasure arises. He understands thus: ‘This faculty of mental pleasure has indeed arisen in me, and it has a cause, a source, a formation, and a condition. That a faculty of mental pleasure could arise without a cause, without a source, without a formation, and without a condition—this is not possible.’ He understands the faculty of mental pleasure, he understands the origin of the faculty of mental pleasure, he understands the cessation of the faculty of mental pleasure, and he understands where the arisen faculty of mental pleasure ceases without remainder. And where does the arisen faculty of mental pleasure cease without remainder? Here, monks, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of mental joy and sorrow, a monk enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. It is here that the arisen faculty of mental pleasure ceases without remainder. This, monks, is called a monk who has understood the cessation of the faculty of mental pleasure and directs his mind toward that purpose.

“Idha [V 3.0292][M 3.0190] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato uppajjati upekkhindriyaṃ. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘uppannaṃ kho me idaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ, tañca kho sanimittaṃ sanidānaṃ sasaṅkhāraṃ [T 5.0286] sappaccayaṃ. Tañca animittaṃ anidānaṃ asaṅkhāraṃ appaccayaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ uppajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati’. So upekkhindriyañca pajānāti, upekkhindriyasamudayañca pajānāti, upekkhindriyanirodhañca pajānāti, yattha cuppannaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati tañca pajānāti. Kattha cuppannaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati, ettha cuppannaṃ upekkhindriyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘bhikkhu aññāsi [P 5.0216] upekkhindriyassa nirodhaṃ, tadatthāya cittaṃ upasaṃharatī’”ti. Dasamaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, when a monk dwells heedful, ardent, and resolute, the faculty of equanimity arises. He understands thus: ‘This faculty of equanimity has arisen in me, and it has a cause, a source, a formation, and a condition. That a faculty of equanimity could arise without a cause, without a source, without a formation, and without a condition—this is not possible.’ He understands the faculty of equanimity, the origin of the faculty of equanimity, the cessation of the faculty of equanimity, and where the arisen faculty of equanimity ceases without remainder. And where does the arisen faculty of equanimity cease without remainder? Here, monks, a monk, by completely transcending the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, enters and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling. It is here that the arisen faculty of equanimity ceases without remainder. This, monks, is called a monk who has understood the cessation of the faculty of equanimity and directs his mind toward that purpose.” The tenth.

Sukhindriyavaggo catuttho.

The Chapter on the Faculty of Pleasure is the fourth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Suddhikañca soto arahā, duve samaṇabrāhmaṇā;

Vibhaṅgena tayo vuttā, kaṭṭho uppaṭipāṭikanti.

The Pure, the Stream-enterer, the Arahant; two on Ascetics and Brahmins; three taught with analysis; the Fire-stick, and the Arising.

5. Jarāvaggo

5. The Chapter on Aging

1. Jarādhammasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Nature of Aging

511. Evaṃ [T 5.0287] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito pacchātape nisinno hoti piṭṭhiṃ otāpayamāno.

511. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park, in the mansion of Migāra’s mother. Now at that time, the Blessed One, having arisen from seclusion in the evening, was sitting in the afternoon sun, warming his back.

Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā bhagavato gattāni pāṇinā anomajjanto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “acchariyaṃ, bhante[V 3.0293], abbhutaṃ, bhante! Na cevaṃ dāni, bhante, bhagavato tāva parisuddho chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto, sithilāni ca gattāni sabbāni valiyajātāni, purato pabbhāro [M 3.0191] ca kāyo, dissati ca indriyānaṃ aññathattaṃ – cakkhundriyassa sotindriyassa ghānindriyassa jivhindriyassa kāyindriyassā”ti.

Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, while massaging the Blessed One's limbs with his hand, he said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, it is wonderful! Venerable sir, it is marvelous! Venerable sir, the Blessed One's skin-complexion is no longer so pure and radiant. All his limbs are slack and have become wrinkled. His body is bent forward, and an alteration of the faculties is apparent—of the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, and the body faculty.'

“Evañhetaṃ[P 5.0217], ānanda, hoti – jarādhammo yobbaññe, byādhidhammo ārogye, maraṇadhammo jīvite. Na ceva tāva parisuddho hoti chavivaṇṇo pariyodāto, sithilāni ca honti gattāni sabbāni valiyajātāni, purato pabbhāro ca kāyo, dissati ca indriyānaṃ aññathattaṃ – cakkhundriyassa sotindriyassa ghānindriyassa jivhindriyassa kāyindriyassā”ti.

“So it is, Ānanda. The nature of aging is inherent in youth, the nature of sickness is inherent in health, the nature of death is inherent in life. The skin-complexion is no longer so pure and radiant. All the limbs are slack and have become wrinkled. The body is bent forward, and an alteration of the faculties is apparent—of the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, and the body faculty.”

“Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvā ca sugato [T 5.0288] athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, then said this further:

“Dhī taṃ jammi jare atthu, dubbaṇṇakaraṇī jare;

Tāva manoramaṃ bimbaṃ, jarāya abhimadditaṃ.

“Shame on you, wretched aging, you maker of ugliness! The once-delightful form is now crushed by aging.

“Yopi vassasataṃ jīve, sopi maccuparāyaṇo sabbe maccuparāyanā (syā. kaṃ. ka.);

Na kiñci parivajjeti, sabbamevābhimaddatī”ti. paṭhamaṃ;

Even one who lives for a hundred years has death as their final destination. It spares no one; it crushes all.” The first.

2. Uṇṇābhabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse to the Brahmin Uṇṇābha

512. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho uṇṇābho brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho uṇṇābho brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

512. The setting is Sāvatthī. Then the brahmin Uṇṇābha approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded the courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Uṇṇābha said this to the Blessed One:

“Pañcimāni, bho gotama, indriyāni nānāvisayāni nānāgocarāni, na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhonti. Katamāni pañca? Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ[P 5.0218]. Imesaṃ nu kho, bho gotama, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ nānāvisayānaṃ [V 3.0294] nānāgocarānaṃ na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhontānaṃ kiṃ paṭisaraṇaṃ, ko ca nesaṃ gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhotī”ti?

“Master Gotama, these five faculties have different domains and different ranges, and they do not experience one another's domain and range. Which five? The eye-faculty, the ear-faculty, the nose-faculty, the tongue-faculty, and the body-faculty. For these five faculties, Master Gotama, which have different domains and different ranges, and do not experience one another's domain and range, what is their refuge, and what experiences their domain and range?”

“Pañcimāni, brāhmaṇa, indriyāni nānāvisayāni nānāgocarāni na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhonti. Katamāni pañca? Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ[M 3.0192], ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ. Imesaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ nānāvisayānaṃ nānāgocarānaṃ [T 5.0289] na aññamaññassa gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhontānaṃ mano paṭisaraṇaṃ, manova nesaṃ gocaravisayaṃ paccanubhotī”ti.

“Brahmin, these five faculties have different domains and different ranges, and do not experience one another's domain and range. Which five? The eye-faculty, the ear-faculty, the nose-faculty, the tongue-faculty, and the body-faculty. For these five faculties, Brahmin, which have different domains and different ranges, and do not experience one another's domain and range, mind is their refuge, and mind experiences their domain and range.”

“Manassa pana, bho gotama, kiṃ paṭisaraṇa”nti? “Manassa kho, brāhmaṇa, sati paṭisaraṇa”nti. “Satiyā pana, bho gotama, kiṃ paṭisaraṇa”nti? “Satiyā kho, brāhmaṇa, vimutti paṭisaraṇa”nti. “Vimuttiyā pana, bho gotama, kiṃ paṭisaraṇa”nti? “Vimuttiyā kho, brāhmaṇa, nibbānaṃ paṭisaraṇa”nti. “Nibbānassa pana, bho gotama, kiṃ paṭisaraṇa”nti? “Accayāsi accasarā (sī. syā. kaṃ.), ajjhaparaṃ (pī. ka.), brāhmaṇa, pañhaṃ, nāsakkhi pañhassa pariyantaṃ gahetuṃ. Nibbānogadhañhi, brāhmaṇa, brahmacariyaṃ vussati nibbānaparāyaṇaṃ nibbānapariyosāna”nti.

“But, Master Gotama, what is the refuge for the mind?” “Mindfulness, Brahmin, is the refuge for the mind.” “But, Master Gotama, what is the refuge for mindfulness?” “Liberation, Brahmin, is the refuge for mindfulness.” “But, Master Gotama, what is the refuge for liberation?” “Nibbāna, Brahmin, is the refuge for liberation.” “But, Master Gotama, what is the refuge for Nibbāna?” “You have gone beyond the question, Brahmin; you were not able to grasp the limit of the question. For, Brahmin, the holy life is lived with Nibbāna as its immersion, Nibbāna as its destination, and Nibbāna as its final end.”

Atha kho uṇṇābho brāhmaṇo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Then the Brahmin Uṇṇābha, having delighted in and rejoiced at the Blessed One's words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him with his right side toward him, and departed.

Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante uṇṇābhe brāhmaṇe bhikkhū āmantesi – “seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kūṭāgāre vā kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ vā rasmiyo (syā. ka.) pācīnavātapānā sūriye uggacchante vātapānena rasmi kūṭāgāraṃ vā kūṭāgārasālaṃ vā uttarāya (ka. sī.) pavisitvā kvāssa kāya (syā. ka.) patiṭṭhitā”ti? “Pacchimāyaṃ, bhante, bhittiya”nti. “Evameva [P 5.0219] kho, bhikkhave, uṇṇābhassa brāhmaṇassa tathāgate saddhā [T 5.0290] niviṭṭhā mūlajātā patiṭṭhitā daḷhā asaṃhāriyā samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ. Imamhi ce, bhikkhave, samaye uṇṇābho brāhmaṇo kālaṅkareyya, natthi saṃyojanaṃ yena saṃyojanena saṃyutto uṇṇābho brāhmaṇo puna imaṃ lokaṃ āgaccheyyā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

Then, not long after the brahmin Uṇṇābha had departed, the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Monks, just as in a gabled house or a gabled hall, when the sun is rising, a ray of light having entered through an eastern window, where is it established?' 'Venerable sir, on the western wall.' 'Even so, monks, the faith of the brahmin Uṇṇābha in the Tathāgata is settled, rooted, established, firm, and not to be carried away by any ascetic or brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or by anyone in the world. If, monks, at this time the brahmin Uṇṇābha were to pass away, there is no fetter, being bound by which, the brahmin Uṇṇābha would come again to this world.' The second.

3. Sāketasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse at Sāketa

513. Evaṃ [V 3.0295] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sākete viharati añjanavane migadāye. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “atthi nu kho, bhikkhave[M 3.0193], pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma yāni pañcindriyāni tāni pañca balāni honti, yāni pañca balāni tāni pañcindriyāni hontī”ti?

513. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāketa, in the Añjana Grove, the sanctuary for deer. There the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Monks, is there a way, relying on which the five faculties become the five powers, and the five powers become the five faculties?'

“Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṃyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti. “Atthi, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma yāni pañcindriyāni tāni pañca balāni honti, yāni pañca balāni tāni pañcindriyāni honti”.

“Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One, guided by the Blessed One, and have the Blessed One as their refuge. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One himself would illuminate the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the monks will bear it in mind.” “There is, monks, a way, relying on which the five faculties become the five powers, and the five powers become the five faculties.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma yāni pañcindriyāni tāni pañca balāni honti, yāni pañca balāni tāni pañcindriyāni honti? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, saddhindriyaṃ taṃ saddhābalaṃ, yaṃ saddhābalaṃ taṃ saddhindriyaṃ; yaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ taṃ vīriyabalaṃ, yaṃ vīriyabalaṃ taṃ vīriyindriyaṃ; yaṃ satindriyaṃ taṃ satibalaṃ, yaṃ satibalaṃ taṃ satindriyaṃ; yaṃ samādhindriyaṃ taṃ [T 5.0291] samādhibalaṃ, yaṃ samādhibalaṃ taṃ samādhindriyaṃ; yaṃ paññindriyaṃ taṃ paññābalaṃ, yaṃ paññābalaṃ taṃ paññindriyaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā, tassa majjhe dīpo. Atthi, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma tassā nadiyā eko soto tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati saṅkhaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.). Atthi pana, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma tassā nadiyā dve sotāni tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchanti.

“And what, monks, is the way, relying on which the five faculties become the five powers, and the five powers become the five faculties? Whatever, monks, is the faculty of faith, that is the power of faith; whatever is the power of faith, that is the faculty of faith. Whatever is the faculty of energy, that is the power of energy; whatever is the power of energy, that is the faculty of energy. Whatever is the faculty of mindfulness, that is the power of mindfulness; whatever is the power of mindfulness, that is the faculty of mindfulness. Whatever is the faculty of concentration, that is the power of concentration; whatever is the power of concentration, that is the faculty of concentration. Whatever is the faculty of wisdom, that is the power of wisdom; whatever is the power of wisdom, that is the faculty of wisdom. Just as, monks, a river slopes to the east, inclines to the east, tends towards the east, and in its middle there is an island. There is, monks, a way, relying on which that river is reckoned as just one stream. And there is, monks, a way, relying on which that river is reckoned as two streams.

“Katamo [P 5.0220] ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma tassā nadiyā eko soto tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati? Yañca, bhikkhave, tassa dīpassa purimante puratthimante (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) udakaṃ, yañca pacchimante udakaṃ – ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma tassā nadiyā eko soto tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

“And what, monks, is the way, relying on which that river is reckoned as just one stream? The water at the eastern end of that island, monks, and the water at the western end—this, monks, is the way, relying on which that river is reckoned as just one stream.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma tassā nadiyā dve sotāni tveva [V 3.0296] saṅkhyaṃ gacchanti? Yañca, bhikkhave, tassa dīpassa uttarante udakaṃ, yañca dakkhiṇante udakaṃ – ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma tassā nadiyā dve sotāni tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchanti.
