Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yaṃ saddhindriyaṃ taṃ saddhābalaṃ, yaṃ saddhābalaṃ taṃ saddhindriyaṃ; yaṃ vīriyindriyaṃ taṃ vīriyabalaṃ, yaṃ vīriyabalaṃ taṃ vīriyindriyaṃ; yaṃ satindriyaṃ taṃ satibalaṃ[M 3.0194], yaṃ satibalaṃ taṃ satindriyaṃ; yaṃ [T 5.0292] samādhindriyaṃ taṃ samādhibalaṃ, yaṃ samādhibalaṃ taṃ samādhindriyaṃ; yaṃ paññindriyaṃ taṃ paññābalaṃ, yaṃ paññābalaṃ taṃ paññindriyaṃ. Pañcannaṃ, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the reason by which that river comes to be reckoned as ‘two streams’? The water, bhikkhus, at the northern end of that island and the water at the southern end—this, indeed, bhikkhus, is the reason by which that river comes to be reckoned as ‘two streams’. In this very same way, bhikkhus, that which is the faculty of faith is the power of faith; that which is the power of faith is the faculty of faith. That which is the faculty of energy is the power of energy; that which is the power of energy is the faculty of energy. That which is the faculty of mindfulness is the power of mindfulness; that which is the power of mindfulness is the faculty of mindfulness. That which is the faculty of concentration is the power of concentration; that which is the power of concentration is the faculty of concentration. That which is the faculty of wisdom is the power of wisdom; that which is the power of wisdom is the faculty of wisdom. Bhikkhus, due to having developed and frequently practiced the five faculties, a bhikkhu, through the destruction of the taints, dwells having attained the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge in this very life.” The third.

4. Pubbakoṭṭhakasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse at the Eastern Gatehouse

514. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbakoṭṭhake. Tatra kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “saddahasi saddahāsi (sī. pī.) tvaṃ, sāriputta – saddhindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosāna”nti?

514. Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī at the Eastern Gatehouse. There, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta: ‘Sāriputta, do you have faith that the faculty of faith, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination… and that the faculty of wisdom, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination?’”

“Na [P 5.0221] khvāhaṃ ettha, bhante, bhagavato saddhāya gacchāmi – saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Yesañhetaṃ, bhante, aññātaṃ assa adiṭṭhaṃ aviditaṃ asacchikataṃ aphassitaṃ apassitaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. ka.), aphusitaṃ (pī.) paññāya, te tattha paresaṃ saddhāya gaccheyyuṃ – saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Yesañca kho etaṃ, bhante, ñātaṃ diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phassitaṃ paññāya, nikkaṅkhā te tattha nibbicikicchā – saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Mayhañca kho etaṃ, bhante, ñātaṃ diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phassitaṃ paññāya. Nikkaṅkhavāhaṃ [T 5.0293] tattha nibbicikiccho saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosāna”nti.

“Venerable Sir, I do not proceed by faith in the Blessed One in this matter—that the faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination. For those, Venerable Sir, for whom this is not known, not seen, not comprehended, not realized, and not contacted by wisdom, they might proceed by faith in others—that the faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination. But for those, Venerable Sir, for whom this is known, seen, comprehended, realized, and contacted by wisdom, they are without doubt and uncertainty in this matter—that the faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination. And for me, Venerable Sir, this is known, seen, comprehended, realized, and contacted by wisdom. I am without doubt and uncertainty in this matter—that the faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination.”

“Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yesañhetaṃ, sāriputta, aññātaṃ assa adiṭṭhaṃ aviditaṃ asacchikataṃ [V 3.0297] aphassitaṃ paññāya, te tattha paresaṃ saddhāya gaccheyyuṃ – saddhindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Yesañca kho etaṃ, sāriputta, ñātaṃ diṭṭhaṃ viditaṃ sacchikataṃ phassitaṃ paññāya, nikkaṅkhā te tattha nibbicikicchā [M 3.0195] – saddhindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ [P 5.0222] amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosāna”nti. Catutthaṃ.

“Good, good, Sāriputta! For those, Sāriputta, for whom this is not known, not seen, not comprehended, not realized, and not contacted by wisdom, they might proceed by faith in others—that the faculty of faith, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination… the faculty of wisdom, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination. But for those, Sāriputta, for whom this is known, seen, comprehended, realized, and contacted by wisdom, they are without doubt and uncertainty—that the faculty of faith, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination… the faculty of wisdom, when developed and frequently practiced, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and the Deathless as its culmination.” The fourth.

5. Paṭhamapubbārāmasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse at Pubbārāma

515. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “katinaṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti?

515. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in the Eastern Park, in the mansion of Migāra's mother. There, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, due to having developed and frequently practiced how many faculties does a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declare final knowledge, saying: “I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is no further existence for this state of being”'?

Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “ekassa kho, bhikkhave, indriyassa bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti. Katamassa ekassa paññindriyassa paññavato[T 5.0294], bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa tadanvayā saddhā saṇṭhāti, tadanvayaṃ vīriyaṃ saṇṭhāti, tadanvayā sati saṇṭhāti, tadanvayo samādhi saṇṭhāti. Imassa kho, bhikkhave, ekassa indriyassa bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Venerable sir, for us, the teachings are rooted in the Blessed One...” “Indeed, bhikkhus, it is due to having developed and frequently practiced one faculty that a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares final knowledge, saying: 'I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is no further existence for this state of being.' Of which one? The faculty of wisdom. Bhikkhus, for a wise noble disciple, faith is established in accordance with that wisdom, energy is established in accordance with that wisdom, mindfulness is established in accordance with that wisdom, and concentration is established in accordance with that wisdom. Indeed, bhikkhus, it is due to having developed and frequently practiced this one faculty that a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares final knowledge, saying: 'I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what was to be done has been done, there is no further existence for this state of being.'” The fifth.

6. Dutiyapubbārāmasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse at Pubbārāma

516. Taṃyeva nidānaṃ. “Katinaṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “dvinnaṃ [P 5.0223] kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti [V 3.0298] – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti. Katamesaṃ dvinnaṃ? Ariyāya ca paññāya, ariyāya ca vimuttiyā. Yā hissa, bhikkhave, ariyā paññā tadassa paññindriyaṃ. Yā hissa, bhikkhave, ariyā vimutti tadassa samādhindriyaṃ. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dvinnaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ [M 3.0196] brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

516. The same setting. “Bhikkhus, through the development and cultivation of how many faculties does a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declare final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” “Bhikkhus, it is through the development and cultivation of two faculties that a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’ Which two? Noble wisdom and noble freedom. For him, bhikkhus, that which is noble wisdom is the faculty of wisdom. For him, bhikkhus, that which is noble freedom is the faculty of concentration. It is through the development and cultivation of these two faculties that a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’” The sixth.

7. Tatiyapubbārāmasuttaṃ

7. The Third Discourse in the Eastern Park

517. Taṃyeva nidānaṃ. “Katinaṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā [T 5.0295] bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “catunnaṃ kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Vīriyindriyassa, satindriyassa, samādhindriyassa, paññindriyassa – imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

517. The same setting. “Bhikkhus, through the development and cultivation of how many faculties does a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declare final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” “Bhikkhus, it is through the development and cultivation of four faculties that a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’ Which four? The faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. Bhikkhus, it is through the development and cultivation of these four faculties that a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’” The seventh.

8. Catutthapubbārāmasuttaṃ

8. The Fourth Discourse in the Eastern Park

518. Taṃyeva nidānaṃ. “Katinaṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “pañcannaṃ kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti. Katamesaṃ pañcannaṃ? Saddhindriyassa[P 5.0224], vīriyindriyassa, satindriyassa, samādhindriyassa, paññindriyassa – imesaṃ [T 5.0296] kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā [V 3.0299] khīṇāsavo bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

518. The same setting. “Bhikkhus, through the development and cultivation of how many faculties does a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declare final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being’?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One…” “Bhikkhus, it is through the development and cultivation of five faculties that a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’ Which five? The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. Bhikkhus, it is through the development and cultivation of these five faculties that a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’” The eighth.

9. Piṇḍolabhāradvājasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja

519. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmatā piṇḍolabhāradvājena aññā byākatā hoti – “khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ[M 3.0197], nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī”ti. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ –

519. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Kosambi, in Ghosita’s Park. Now at that time, the Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja had declared final knowledge, saying: “I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.” Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:

“Āyasmatā, bhante, piṇḍolabhāradvājena aññā byākatā – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti. Kiṃ nu kho, bhante, atthavasaṃ sampassamānena āyasmatā piṇḍolabhāradvājena aññā byākatā – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti?

“Venerable sir, the Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja has declared final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’ Venerable sir, seeing what purpose did the Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja declare final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being’?”

“Tiṇṇannaṃ kho, bhikkhave, indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā piṇḍolabhāradvājena bhikkhunā aññā byākatā – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti. Katamesaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ? Satindriyassa, samādhindriyassa, paññindriyassa – imesaṃ [T 5.0297] kho, bhikkhave, tiṇṇannaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā piṇḍolabhāradvājena bhikkhunā aññā byākatā – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmīti. Imāni ca, bhikkhave, tīṇindriyāni kimantāni? Khayantāni. Kissa khayantāni? Jātijarāmaraṇassa. ‘Jātijarāmaraṇaṃ khaya’nti kho, bhikkhave, sampassamānena piṇḍolabhāradvājena [P 5.0225] bhikkhunā aññā byākatā – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāmī”ti. Navamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, it is through the development and cultivation of three faculties that the bhikkhu Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja declared final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’ Which three? The faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. Bhikkhus, it is through the development and cultivation of these three faculties that the bhikkhu Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja declared final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’ And what, bhikkhus, is the end of these three faculties? Their end is destruction. The destruction of what? The destruction of birth, aging, and death. Bhikkhus, it is by clearly seeing the destruction of birth, aging, and death that the bhikkhu Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja declared final knowledge, saying: ‘I know that birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, and there is no further state of being.’” The ninth.

10. Āpaṇasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse at Āpaṇa

520. Evaṃ [V 3.0300] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā aṅgesu viharati āpaṇaṃ nāma aṅgānaṃ nigamo. Tatra kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “yo so, sāriputta, ariyasāvako tathāgate ekantagato ekantigato (sī.) abhippasanno, na so tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā kaṅkheyya vā vicikiccheyya vā”ti?

520. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Aṅgas, at a market town of the Aṅgas named Āpaṇa. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta: “Sāriputta, a noble disciple who has arrived at certainty regarding the Tathāgata and is exceedingly confident would not have any doubt or uncertainty about the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata’s teaching.”

“Yo so, bhante, ariyasāvako tathāgate ekantagato abhippasanno, na so tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā kaṅkheyya vā vicikiccheyya vā. Saddhassa hi, bhante, ariyasāvakassa evaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ yaṃ [M 3.0198] āraddhavīriyo viharissati – akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu. Yaṃ hissa, bhante, vīriyaṃ tadassa vīriyindriyaṃ.

“Venerable sir, a noble disciple who has arrived at certainty regarding the Tathāgata and is exceedingly confident would not have any doubt or uncertainty about the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata’s teaching. For a faithful noble disciple, venerable sir, it is to be expected that they will dwell with aroused energy for the abandoning of unwholesome qualities and the undertaking of wholesome qualities, being strong, of steadfast exertion, not shirking the burden regarding wholesome qualities. Whatever energy is theirs, venerable sir, that is their faculty of energy.”

“Saddhassa hi[T 5.0298], bhante, ariyasāvakassa āraddhavīriyassa etaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ yaṃ satimā bhavissati, paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā. Yā hissa, bhante, sati tadassa satindriyaṃ.

“Venerable sir, for a faithful noble disciple with aroused energy, it is to be expected that they will be mindful, possessed of supreme maturity of mindfulness, able to remember and recollect what was done long ago and what was said long ago. Venerable sir, whatever mindfulness is theirs, that is their faculty of mindfulness.”

“Saddhassa hi, bhante, ariyasāvakassa āraddhavīriyassa upaṭṭhitassatino etaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ yaṃ vossaggārammaṇaṃ karitvā labhissati samādhiṃ, labhissati cittassa ekaggataṃ. Yo hissa, bhante, samādhi tadassa samādhindriyaṃ.

“Venerable sir, for a faithful noble disciple with aroused energy and established mindfulness, it is to be expected that, having made relinquishment the object, they will gain concentration, they will gain unification of mind. Venerable sir, whatever concentration is theirs, that is their faculty of concentration.”

“Saddhassa hi, bhante, ariyasāvakassa āraddhavīriyassa upaṭṭhitassatino [P 5.0226] samāhitacittassa etaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ yaṃ evaṃ pajānissati – anamataggo kho saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Avijjāya tveva tamokāyassa asesavirāganirodho santametaṃ padaṃ paṇītametaṃ padaṃ, yadidaṃ – sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṃ nibbānanti (?). Yā hissa, bhante, paññā tadassa paññindriyaṃ.

“Venerable sir, for a faithful noble disciple with aroused energy, established mindfulness, and a concentrated mind, it is to be expected that they will understand thus: ‘Beginningless is this saṃsāra. A first point is not discerned of beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are roaming and wandering on. The remainderless fading away and cessation of this very mass of darkness that is ignorance is this peaceful state, this sublime state, namely: the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all substrates of existence, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.’ Venerable sir, whatever wisdom is theirs, that is their faculty of wisdom.”

“Saddho [V 3.0301] so sa kho so (sī. syā. kaṃ.), bhante, ariyasāvako evaṃ padahitvā padahitvā evaṃ saritvā saritvā evaṃ samādahitvā samādahitvā evaṃ pajānitvā pajānitvā evaṃ abhisaddahati – ‘ime kho te dhammā ye me pubbe sutavā ahesuṃ. Tenāhaṃ [T 5.0299] etarahi kāyena ca phusitvā viharāmi, paññāya ca ativijjha paṭivijjha (sī. ka.) tadaṭṭhakathāsu pana ativijjhitvāti vaṇṇitaṃ passāmī’ti. Yā hissa, bhante, saddhā tadassa saddhindriya”nti.

“Venerable sir, that faithful noble disciple, thus repeatedly applying effort, thus repeatedly recollecting, thus repeatedly concentrating, thus repeatedly understanding, has deep faith thus: ‘These are the very states that I had formerly only heard of. Now I dwell having experienced them with the body and, having penetrated them with wisdom, I see.’ Venerable sir, whatever faith is theirs, that is their faculty of faith.”

“Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yo so, sāriputta, ariyasāvako tathāgate ekantagato abhippasanno, na so tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā kaṅkheyya vā vicikiccheyya vā. Saddhassa hi, sāriputta, ariyasāvakassa etaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ yaṃ āraddhavīriyo viharissati – akusalānaṃ [M 3.0199] dhammānaṃ pahānāya, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu. Yaṃ hissa, sāriputta, vīriyaṃ tadassa vīriyindriyaṃ.

“Good, good, Sāriputta! A noble disciple, Sāriputta, who has arrived at certainty regarding the Tathāgata and is exceedingly confident would not have any doubt or uncertainty about the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata’s teaching. For a faithful noble disciple, Sāriputta, it is to be expected that they will dwell with aroused energy for the abandoning of unwholesome qualities and the undertaking of wholesome qualities, being strong, of steadfast exertion, not shirking the burden regarding wholesome qualities. Whatever energy is theirs, Sāriputta, that is their faculty of energy.”

“Saddhassa hi, sāriputta, ariyasāvakassa āraddhavīriyassa etaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ yaṃ satimā bhavissati, paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā. Yā hissa, sāriputta, sati tadassa satindriyaṃ.

“For a faithful noble disciple with aroused energy, Sāriputta, it is to be expected that they will be mindful, possessed of supreme maturity of mindfulness, able to remember and recollect what was done long ago and what was said long ago. Whatever mindfulness is theirs, Sāriputta, that is their faculty of mindfulness.”

“Saddhassa hi, sāriputta, ariyasāvakassa āraddhavīriyassa upaṭṭhitassatino etaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ yaṃ vossaggārammaṇaṃ karitvā labhissati samādhiṃ, labhissati cittassa ekaggataṃ. Yo hissa, sāriputta, samādhi tadassa samādhindriyaṃ.

“For a faithful noble disciple with aroused energy and established mindfulness, Sāriputta, it is to be expected that, having made relinquishment the object, they will gain concentration, they will gain unification of mind. Whatever concentration is theirs, Sāriputta, that is their faculty of concentration.”

“Saddhassa hi, sāriputta, ariyasāvakassa āraddhavīriyassa upaṭṭhitassatino samāhitacittassa [T 5.0300] etaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ yaṃ evaṃ pajānissati – anamataggo kho saṃsāro. Pubbā koṭi na paññāyati avijjānīvaraṇānaṃ sattānaṃ taṇhāsaṃyojanānaṃ sandhāvataṃ saṃsarataṃ. Avijjāya tveva tamokāyassa asesavirāganirodho santametaṃ padaṃ paṇītametaṃ padaṃ, yadidaṃ – sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṃ. Yā hissa, sāriputta, paññā tadassa paññindriyaṃ.

“For a faithful noble disciple with aroused energy, established mindfulness, and a concentrated mind, Sāriputta, it is to be expected that they will understand thus: ‘Beginningless is this saṃsāra. A first point is not discerned of beings hindered by ignorance and fettered by craving, who are roaming and wandering on. The remainderless fading away and cessation of this very mass of darkness that is ignorance is this peaceful state, this sublime state, namely: the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all substrates of existence, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.’ Whatever wisdom is theirs, Sāriputta, that is their faculty of wisdom.”

“Saddho so sa kho so (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), sāriputta, ariyasāvako evaṃ padahitvā padahitvā evaṃ saritvā saritvā evaṃ samādahitvā samādahitvā evaṃ pajānitvā pajānitvā evaṃ abhisaddahati – ‘ime kho te [V 3.0302] dhammā ye me pubbe sutavā ahesuṃ. Tenāhaṃ etarahi [P 5.0227] kāyena ca phusitvā viharāmi, paññāya ca ativijjha paṭivijjha (ka. sī. ka.) passāmī’ti. Yā hissa, sāriputta, saddhā tadassa saddhindriya”nti. Dasamaṃ.

“Sāriputta, that faithful noble disciple, thus repeatedly applying effort, thus repeatedly recollecting, thus repeatedly concentrating, thus repeatedly understanding, has deep faith thus: ‘These are the very states that I had formerly only heard of. Now I dwell having experienced them with the body and, having penetrated them with wisdom, I see.’ Whatever faith is theirs, Sāriputta, that is their faculty of faith. The tenth.”

Jarāvaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter on Old Age.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Jarā uṇṇābho brāhmaṇo, sāketo pubbakoṭṭhako;

Pubbārāme ca cattāri, piṇḍolo āpaṇena cāti saddhena te dasāti (syā. kaṃ. ka.).

Old Age, Uṇṇābha the Brahmin, Sāketa, Pubbakoṭṭhaka; and four at Pubbārāma, Piṇḍola, and with Āpaṇa.

6. Sūkarakhatavaggo

6. The Chapter on Sūkarakhata

1. Sālasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse at Sālā

521. Evaṃ [T 5.0301][M 3.0200] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu viharati sālāya brāhmaṇagāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci tiracchānagatā pāṇā, sīho migarājā tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – thāmena javena sūrena sūriyena (sī. syā. kaṃ.); evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāya”.

521. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kosalans at Sālā, a brahmin village. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, just as among whatever animals there are, the lion, the king of beasts, is declared the foremost—that is, in strength, speed, and courage—so too, bhikkhus, among whatever qualities are conducive to enlightenment, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for awakening.”

“Katame ca, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyā dhammā? Saddhindriyaṃ, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati; vīriyindriyaṃ bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati; satindriyaṃ bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati; samādhindriyaṃ bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati; paññindriyaṃ bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Seyyathāpi[P 5.0228], bhikkhave, ye keci tiracchānagatā pāṇā, sīho migarājā tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – thāmena javena sūrena; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāyā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, are the qualities conducive to enlightenment? The faculty of faith, bhikkhus, is a quality conducive to enlightenment; it conduces to awakening. The faculty of energy is a quality conducive to enlightenment; it conduces to awakening. The faculty of mindfulness is a quality conducive to enlightenment; it conduces to awakening. The faculty of concentration is a quality conducive to enlightenment; it conduces to awakening. The faculty of wisdom is a quality conducive to enlightenment; it conduces to awakening. Just as among whatever animals there are, the lion, the king of beasts, is declared the foremost—that is, in strength, speed, and courage—so too, bhikkhus, among whatever qualities are conducive to enlightenment, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for awakening.” The First.

2. Mallikasuttaṃ

2. The Mallikā Sutta

522. Evaṃ [V 3.0303] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā mallesu mallakesu (sī. syā. kaṃ.), mallikesu (ka.) viharati uruvelakappaṃ [T 5.0302] nāma mallānaṃ nigamo. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “yāvakīvañca, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa ariyañāṇaṃ na uppannaṃ hoti neva tāva catunnaṃ indriyānaṃ saṇṭhiti hoti, neva tāva catunnaṃ indriyānaṃ avaṭṭhiti hoti. Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa ariyañāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, atha catunnaṃ indriyānaṃ saṇṭhiti hoti, atha catunnaṃ indriyānaṃ avaṭṭhiti hoti”.

522. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling among the Mallas at a market town of the Mallas named Uruvelakappa. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, for as long as noble knowledge has not arisen for a noble disciple, for that long there is neither stability nor establishment of the four faculties. But when, bhikkhus, noble knowledge has arisen for a noble disciple, then there is stability of the four faculties, then there is establishment of the four faculties.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yāvakīvañca kūṭāgārassa kūṭaṃ na ussitaṃ hoti, neva tāva gopānasīnaṃ saṇṭhiti hoti, neva tāva gopānasīnaṃ avaṭṭhiti hoti. Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, kūṭāgārassa kūṭaṃ ussitaṃ [M 3.0201] hoti, atha gopānasīnaṃ saṇṭhiti hoti, atha gopānasīnaṃ avaṭṭhiti hoti. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, yāvakīvañca ariyasāvakassa ariyañāṇaṃ na uppannaṃ hoti, neva tāva catunnaṃ indriyānaṃ saṇṭhiti hoti, neva tāva catunnaṃ indriyānaṃ avaṭṭhiti hoti. Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa ariyañāṇaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, atha catunnaṃ indriyānaṃ…pe… avaṭṭhiti hoti.

“Bhikkhus, it is just as when the ridge-pole of a gabled house has not been raised, for that long there is neither stability nor establishment of the rafters. But when, bhikkhus, the ridge-pole of a gabled house has been raised, then there is stability of the rafters, then there is establishment of the rafters. So too, bhikkhus, for as long as noble knowledge has not arisen for a noble disciple, for that long there is neither stability nor establishment of the four faculties. But when, bhikkhus, noble knowledge has arisen for a noble disciple, then there is stability of the four faculties… then there is establishment of the four faculties.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Saddhindriyassa[P 5.0229], vīriyindriyassa, satindriyassa, samādhindriyassa. Paññavato, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa tadanvayā saddhā saṇṭhāti, tadanvayaṃ vīriyaṃ saṇṭhāti, tadanvayā sati saṇṭhāti, tadanvayo samādhi saṇṭhātī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Of which four? The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, and the faculty of concentration. Bhikkhus, for a wise noble disciple, faith is established in conformity with that wisdom, energy is established in conformity with that wisdom, mindfulness is established in conformity with that wisdom, and concentration is established in conformity with that wisdom.” The Second.

3. Sekhasuttaṃ

3. The Sekha Sutta

523. Evaṃ [T 5.0303] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “atthi nu kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajāneyya, asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajāneyyā”ti?

523. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Kosambi, in Ghosita’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Is there, bhikkhus, a way by which a trainee bhikkhu, standing on the trainee’s level, might understand, ‘I am a trainee,’ and an adept, standing on the adept’s level, might understand, ‘I am an adept’?”

Bhagavaṃmūlakā [V 3.0304] no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “atthi, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajāneyya, asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajāneyya”.

“Venerable sir, our teachings have the Blessed One as their root…” “Bhikkhus, there is a way by which a trainee bhikkhu, standing on the trainee’s level, might understand, ‘I am a trainee,’ and an adept, standing on the adept’s level, might understand, ‘I am an adept.’”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti – ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajānāti”.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the way by which a trainee bhikkhu, standing on the trainee’s level, understands, ‘I am a trainee’? Here, bhikkhus, a trainee bhikkhu understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering,’ ‘This is the origin of suffering,’ ‘This is the cessation of suffering,’ ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ This too, bhikkhus, is a way by which a trainee bhikkhu, standing on the trainee’s level, understands, ‘I am a trainee.’”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘atthi nu kho ito bahiddhā añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yo evaṃ bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ tathaṃ dhammaṃ [M 3.0202] deseti [P 5.0230] yathā bhagavā’ti? So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘natthi kho ito bahiddhā añño samaṇo vā [T 5.0304] brāhmaṇo vā yo evaṃ bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ tathaṃ dhammaṃ deseti yathā bhagavā’ti. Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajānāti”.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a trainee bhikkhu reflects thus: ‘Is there outside of this Dispensation any other ascetic or brahmin who teaches a Dhamma that is true, real, and unerring just as the Blessed One does?’ He understands thus: ‘There is no other ascetic or brahmin outside of this Dispensation who teaches a Dhamma that is true, real, and unerring just as the Blessed One does.’ This too, bhikkhus, is a way by which a trainee bhikkhu, standing on the trainee’s level, understands, ‘I am a trainee.’”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, sekho bhikkhu pañcindriyāni pajānāti – saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ – yaṃgatikāni yaṃparamāni yaṃphalāni yaṃpariyosānāni. Na heva kho kāyena phusitvā viharati; paññāya ca ativijjha passati. Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma sekho bhikkhu sekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘sekhosmī’ti pajānāti”.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a trainee bhikkhu understands the five faculties—the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom—what their destination is, what their supreme object is, what their fruit is, and what their final consummation is. He does not, however, dwell having realized them with the body, but he sees by penetrating them with wisdom. This too, bhikkhus, is a way by which a trainee bhikkhu, standing on the trainee’s level, understands, ‘I am a trainee.’”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajānāti? Idha, bhikkhave, asekho bhikkhu pañcindriyāni pajānāti – saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ – yaṃgatikāni yaṃparamāni yaṃphalāni yaṃpariyosānāni. Kāyena ca phusitvā viharati; paññāya ca ativijjha [V 3.0305] passati. Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajānāti”.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the way by which a bhikkhu beyond training, standing on the level of one beyond training, understands, ‘I am one beyond training’? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu beyond training understands the five faculties—the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom—what their destination is, what their supreme object is, what their fruit is, and what their final consummation is. And he dwells having realized them with the body; and he sees by penetrating them with wisdom. This too, bhikkhus, is a way by which a bhikkhu beyond training, standing on the level of one beyond training, understands, ‘I am one beyond training.’”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, asekho bhikkhu cha indriyāni pajānāti. ‘Cakkhundriyaṃ, sotindriyaṃ, ghānindriyaṃ, jivhindriyaṃ, kāyindriyaṃ, manindriyaṃ – imāni kho cha indriyāni sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ [T 5.0305] aparisesaṃ nirujjhissanti, aññāni ca cha indriyāni na kuhiñci kismiñci uppajjissantī’ti pajānāti. Ayampi kho, bhikkhave, pariyāyo yaṃ pariyāyaṃ āgamma asekho bhikkhu asekhabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito ‘asekhosmī’ti pajānātī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu beyond training understands the six faculties. He understands: ‘The eye-faculty, the ear-faculty, the nose-faculty, the tongue-faculty, the body-faculty, and the mind-faculty—these six faculties will utterly and in every way cease without remainder, and no other six faculties will arise anywhere, in any respect.’ This too, bhikkhus, is a way by which a bhikkhu beyond training, standing on the level of one beyond training, understands, ‘I am one beyond training.’”

4. Padasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Footprint

524. “Seyyathāpi[P 5.0231], bhikkhave, yāni kānici jaṅgalānaṃ jaṅgamānaṃ (sī. pī.) pāṇānaṃ padajātāni sabbāni tāni hatthipade samodhānaṃ gacchanti, hatthipadaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – mahantattena; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yāni kānici padāni bodhāya saṃvattanti[M 3.0203], paññindriyaṃ padaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāya. Katamāni ca, bhikkhave, padāni bodhāya saṃvattanti? Saddhindriyaṃ, bhikkhave, padaṃ, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati; vīriyindriyaṃ padaṃ, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati; satindriyaṃ padaṃ, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati; samādhindriyaṃ padaṃ, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati; paññindriyaṃ padaṃ, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yāni kānici jaṅgalānaṃ pāṇānaṃ padajātāni sabbāni tāni hatthipade samodhānaṃ gacchanti, hatthipadaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – mahantattena; evameva kho, bhikkhave, yāni kānici padāni bodhāya saṃvattanti, paññindriyaṃ padaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāyā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

524. “Bhikkhus, just as the footprints of any land-dwelling creatures are all encompassed by an elephant's footprint, and the elephant's footprint is declared foremost among them on account of its great size; even so, bhikkhus, of any factors that conduce to enlightenment, the faculty of wisdom is declared foremost among them, that is, for the sake of enlightenment. And what, bhikkhus, are the factors that conduce to enlightenment? The faculty of faith, bhikkhus, is a factor that conduces to enlightenment; the faculty of energy is a factor that conduces to enlightenment; the faculty of mindfulness is a factor that conduces to enlightenment; the faculty of concentration is a factor that conduces to enlightenment; the faculty of wisdom is a factor that conduces to enlightenment. Bhikkhus, just as the footprints of any land-dwelling creatures are all encompassed by an elephant's footprint, and the elephant's footprint is declared foremost among them on account of its great size; even so, bhikkhus, of any factors that conduce to enlightenment, the faculty of wisdom is declared foremost among them, that is, for the sake of enlightenment.” The fourth.

5. Sārasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Essence

525. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci sāragandhā, lohitacandanaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā[T 5.0306], paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāya. Katame ca, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyā dhammā? Saddhindriyaṃ, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Vīriyindriyaṃ…pe… satindriyaṃ [V 3.0306] …pe… samādhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci sāragandhā, lohitacandanaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāyā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

525. “Bhikkhus, just as, of all fragrant heartwoods, red sandalwood is declared to be the foremost; even so, bhikkhus, of all factors of enlightenment, the faculty of wisdom is declared to be the foremost, that is, for the sake of enlightenment. And what, bhikkhus, are the factors of enlightenment? The faculty of faith, bhikkhus, is a factor of enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment. The faculty of energy… the faculty of mindfulness… the faculty of concentration… the faculty of wisdom is a factor of enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment. Bhikkhus, just as, of all fragrant heartwoods, red sandalwood is declared to be the foremost; even so, bhikkhus, of all factors of enlightenment, the faculty of wisdom is declared to be the foremost, that is, for the sake of enlightenment.” The fifth.

6. Patiṭṭhitasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Being Established

526. “Ekadhamme [P 5.0232] patiṭṭhitassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni honti subhāvitāni. Katamasmiṃ ekadhamme? Appamāde. Katamo ca bhikkhave, appamādo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cittaṃ rakkhati āsavesu ca sāsavesu ca dhammesu. Tassa cittaṃ rakkhato āsavesu ca sāsavesu ca dhammesu saddhindriyampi bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Vīriyindriyampi bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Satindriyampi bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Samādhindriyampi bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Paññindriyampi bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Evampi kho, bhikkhave, ekadhamme patiṭṭhitassa bhikkhuno pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni honti subhāvitānī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

526. “Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu established in one quality, the five faculties are developed and well-developed. In what one quality? In heedfulness. And what, bhikkhus, is heedfulness? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu guards his mind in regard to the taints and qualities connected with the taints. For one who guards his mind in regard to the taints and qualities connected with the taints, the faculty of faith comes to fulfillment through development. The faculty of energy comes to fulfillment through development. The faculty of mindfulness comes to fulfillment through development. The faculty of concentration comes to fulfillment through development. The faculty of wisdom comes to fulfillment through development. Thus, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu established in one quality, the five faculties are developed and well-developed.” The sixth.

7. Sahampatibrahmasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse with Brahmā Sahampati

527. Ekaṃ [M 3.0204] samayaṃ bhagavā uruvelāyaṃ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre ajapālanigrodhe paṭhamābhisambuddho. Atha kho [T 5.0307] bhagavato rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni amatogadhāni honti amataparāyaṇāni amatapariyosānāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Vīriyindriyaṃ…pe… satindriyaṃ…pe… samādhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Imāni pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni amatogadhāni honti amataparāyaṇāni amatapariyosānānī”ti.

527. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in Uruvelā on the bank of the river Nerañjarā at the Ajapāla Banyan Tree, having just attained full enlightenment. Then, while the Blessed One was alone in seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind: ‘These five faculties, when developed and cultivated, plunge into the Deathless, have the Deathless as their destination, and have the Deathless as their final end. Which five? The faculty of faith, when developed and cultivated, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and has the Deathless as its final end. The faculty of energy… the faculty of mindfulness… the faculty of concentration… the faculty of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and has the Deathless as its final end. These five faculties, when developed and cultivated, plunge into the Deathless, have the Deathless as their destination, and have the Deathless as their final end.’”

Atha kho brahmā sahampati bhagavato cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā [V 3.0307] puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya; evameva brahmaloke antarahito bhagavato purato pāturahosi. Atha [P 5.0233] kho brahmā sahampati ekaṃsaṃ uttarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ sugata! Pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni amatogadhāni honti amataparāyaṇāni amatapariyosānāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāvitaṃ bahulīkataṃ amatogadhaṃ hoti amataparāyaṇaṃ amatapariyosānaṃ. Imāni pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni amatogadhāni honti amataparāyaṇāni amatapariyosānāni”.

Then Brahmā Sahampati, having known with his mind the thought in the Blessed One's mind—just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm—disappeared from the Brahmā world and appeared before the Blessed One. Then Brahmā Sahampati, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder and extended his joined palms in salutation toward the Blessed One, said to him: 'So it is, Blessed One! So it is, Well-Farer! These five faculties, when developed and cultivated, plunge into the Deathless, have the Deathless as their destination, and have the Deathless as their final end. Which five? The faculty of faith, when developed and cultivated, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and has the Deathless as its final end... the faculty of wisdom, when developed and cultivated, plunges into the Deathless, has the Deathless as its destination, and has the Deathless as its final end. These five faculties, when developed and cultivated, plunge into the Deathless, have the Deathless as their destination, and have the Deathless as their final end.'

“Bhūtapubbāhaṃ[T 5.0308], bhante, kassape sammāsambuddhe brahmacariyaṃ acariṃ. Tatrapi maṃ evaṃ jānanti – ‘sahako bhikkhu, sahako bhikkhū’ti. So khvāhaṃ, bhante, imesaṃyeva pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā kāmesu kāmacchandaṃ virājetvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ brahmalokaṃ upapanno. Tatrapi maṃ evaṃ jānanti – ‘brahmā sahampati, brahmā sahampatī’”ti. “Evametaṃ, bhagavā, evametaṃ sugata! Ahametaṃ jānāmi, ahametaṃ passāmi yathā imāni pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni amatogadhāni honti amataparāyaṇāni amatapariyosānānī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Venerable Sir, formerly, I practiced the holy life under the Perfectly Enlightened One Kassapa. There, too, they knew me thus: ‘the monk Sahaka, the monk Sahaka.’ Indeed, Venerable Sir, because of having developed and cultivated these very five faculties, and having caused sensual desire to fade away, with the breakup of the body, after death, I was reborn in a good destination, the Brahma world. There, too, they knew me thus: ‘Brahmā Sahampati, Brahmā Sahampati.’ So it is, Blessed One! So it is, Well-Farer! I know this, I see this: how these five faculties, when developed and cultivated, plunge into the Deathless, have the Deathless as their destination, and have the Deathless as their final end.”

8. Sūkarakhatasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse at the Boar's Cave

528. Ekaṃ [M 3.0205] samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate sūkarakhatāyaṃ. Tatra kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho, sāriputta, atthavasaṃ sampassamāno khīṇāsavo bhikkhu tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā paramanipaccakāraṃ pavattamāno pavattatī”ti pavattetīti (sī.)? “Anuttarañhi[P 5.0234], bhante, yogakkhemaṃ sampassamāno khīṇāsavo bhikkhu tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā paramanipaccakāraṃ pavattamāno pavattatī”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Anuttarañhi, sāriputta, yogakkhemaṃ sampassamāno khīṇāsavo bhikkhu tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā paramanipaccakāraṃ pavattamāno pavattatī”ti.

528. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha on Vulture Peak, in the Boar's Cave. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Sāriputta: 'For what reason, Sāriputta, does a monk whose taints are destroyed conduct himself with the highest reverence toward the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata's teaching?' 'It is, venerable sir, because he sees the unsurpassed security from bondage that a monk whose taints are destroyed conducts himself with the highest reverence toward the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata's teaching.' 'Good, good, Sāriputta! It is indeed because he sees the unsurpassed security from bondage that a monk whose taints are destroyed conducts himself with the highest reverence toward the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata's teaching.'

“Katamo ca, sāriputta, anuttaro yogakkhemo yaṃ sampassamāno [T 5.0309] khīṇāsavo bhikkhu tathāgate [V 3.0308] vā tathāgatasāsane vā paramanipaccakāraṃ pavattamāno pavattatī”ti? “Idha, bhante, khīṇāsavo bhikkhu saddhindriyaṃ bhāveti upasamagāmiṃ sambodhagāmiṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ bhāveti…pe… satindriyaṃ bhāveti…pe… samādhindriyaṃ bhāveti…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāveti upasamagāmiṃ sambodhagāmiṃ. Ayaṃ kho, bhante, anuttaro yogakkhemo yaṃ sampassamāno khīṇāsavo bhikkhu tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā paramanipaccakāraṃ pavattamāno pavattatī”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Eso hi, sāriputta, anuttaro yogakkhemo yaṃ sampassamāno khīṇāsavo bhikkhu tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā paramanipaccakāraṃ pavattamāno pavattatī”ti.

“And what, Sāriputta, is that unsurpassed security from bondage, seeing which a monk whose taints are destroyed conducts himself with the highest reverence toward the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata’s teaching?” “Here, venerable sir, a monk whose taints are destroyed develops the faculty of faith, which is conducive to peace, conducive to enlightenment. He develops the faculty of energy… the faculty of mindfulness… the faculty of concentration… he develops the faculty of wisdom, which is conducive to peace, conducive to enlightenment. This, venerable sir, is the unsurpassed security from bondage, seeing which a monk whose taints are destroyed conducts himself with the highest reverence toward the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata’s teaching.” “Good, good, Sāriputta! This, Sāriputta, is indeed the unsurpassed security from bondage, seeing which a monk whose taints are destroyed conducts himself with the highest reverence toward the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata’s teaching.”

“Katamo ca, sāriputta, paramanipaccakāro yaṃ khīṇāsavo bhikkhu tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā paramanipaccakāraṃ pavattamāno pavattatī”ti? “Idha, bhante, khīṇāsavo bhikkhu satthari sagāravo viharati sappatisso sappaṭisso (syā. kaṃ. ka.), dhamme sagāravo viharati sappatisso, saṅghe sagāravo viharati sappatisso, sikkhāya sagāravo viharati sappatisso, samādhismiṃ sagāravo viharati sappatisso. Ayaṃ kho, bhante, paramanipaccakāro yaṃ khīṇāsavo bhikkhu tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā paramanipaccakāraṃ pavattamāno pavattatī”ti. “Sādhu [T 5.0310][P 5.0235] sādhu, sāriputta! Eso hi[M 3.0206], sāriputta, paramanipaccakāro yaṃ khīṇāsavo bhikkhu tathāgate vā tathāgatasāsane vā paramanipaccakāraṃ pavattamāno pavattatī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“And what, Sāriputta, is that highest reverence with which a monk whose taints are destroyed conducts himself toward the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata’s teaching?” “Here, venerable sir, a monk whose taints are destroyed dwells reverential and deferential toward the Teacher; he dwells reverential and deferential toward the Dhamma; he dwells reverential and deferential toward the Saṅgha; he dwells reverential and deferential toward the training; he dwells reverential and deferential toward concentration. This, venerable sir, is that highest reverence with which a monk whose taints are destroyed conducts himself toward the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata’s teaching.” “Good, good, Sāriputta! This, Sāriputta, is indeed that highest reverence with which a monk whose taints are destroyed conducts himself toward the Tathāgata or the Tathāgata’s teaching.”

9. Paṭhamauppādasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on Arising

529. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni anuppannāni uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni anuppannāni uppajjanti, nāññatra tathāgatassa pātubhāvā arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti. Navamaṃ.

529. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, these five faculties, previously unarisen, arise only with the appearance of a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, and not otherwise. What five? The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. Monks, these five faculties, previously unarisen, arise only with the appearance of a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, and not otherwise.”

10. Dutiyauppādasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on Arising

530. “Pañcimāni[V 3.0309], bhikkhave, indriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni anuppannāni uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni anuppannāni uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

530. “Monks, these five unarisen faculties, when developed and cultivated, arise only in the discipline of the Sugata. What five? The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. Monks, these five unarisen faculties, when developed and cultivated, arise only in the discipline of the Sugata.” The tenth.

Sūkarakhatavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Sukarakhata Chapter, the sixth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that:

Sālaṃ mallikaṃ sekho ca, padaṃ sāraṃ patiṭṭhitaṃ;

Brahmasūkarakhatāyo, uppādā apare duveti.

The Sāla, Mallikā, and Sekha, Pada, Sāra, and Paṭiṭṭhita; Brahma, Sukarakhata, and two other Uppāda suttas.

7. Bodhipakkhiyavaggo

7. The Chapter on the Aids to Enlightenment

1. Saṃyojanasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Fetters

531. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0311][P 5.0236]. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni saṃyojanappahānāya saṃyojanānaṃ pahānāya (syā. ka.) saṃvattanti. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni saṃyojanappahānāya saṃvattantī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

531. At Sāvatthī. “Monks, these five faculties, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the abandonment of the fetters. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. Monks, these five faculties, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the abandonment of the fetters.” The first.

2. Anusayasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Underlying Tendencies

532. “Pañcimāni[M 3.0207], bhikkhave, indriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni anusayasamugghātāya saṃvattanti. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho[V 3.0310], bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni anusayasamugghātāya saṃvattantī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

532. “Monks, these five faculties, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the uprooting of the underlying tendencies. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. Monks, these five faculties, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the uprooting of the underlying tendencies.” The second.

3. Pariññāsuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Full Comprehension

533. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni addhānapariññāya saṃvattanti. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni addhānapariññāya saṃvattantī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

533. “Monks, these five faculties, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the full comprehension of the long course of saṃsāra. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These five faculties, monks, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the full comprehension of the long course of saṃsāra.” The third.

4. Āsavakkhayasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Destruction of the Taints

534. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattanti. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattantī”ti.

534. “Monks, these five faculties, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the destruction of the taints. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These five faculties, monks, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the destruction of the taints.”

“Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni saṃyojanappahānāya saṃvattanti, anusayasamugghātāya saṃvattanti, addhānapariññāya [T 5.0312] saṃvattanti, āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattanti. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni bhāvitāni bahulīkatāni saṃyojanappahānāya saṃvattanti, anusayasamugghātāya saṃvattanti, addhānapariññāya saṃvattanti, āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattantī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Monks, these five faculties, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the abandoning of the fetters, to the uprooting of the underlying tendencies, to the full comprehension of the long course of saṃsāra, and to the destruction of the taints. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. These five faculties, monks, when developed and cultivated, conduce to the abandoning of the fetters, to the uprooting of the underlying tendencies, to the full comprehension of the long course of saṃsāra, and to the destruction of the taints.” The fourth.

5. Paṭhamaphalasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on the Fruit

535. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā dvinnaṃ phalānaṃ aññataraṃ phalaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

535. “Monks, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom—these, monks, are the five faculties. Monks, because these five faculties have been developed and cultivated, one of two fruits is to be expected: either final knowledge in this very life or, if there is a remaining substratum of existence, the state of a non-returner.” The fifth.

6. Dutiyaphalasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on the Fruit

536. “Pañcimāni[V 3.0311][M 3.0208][P 5.0237], bhikkhave, indriyāni. Katamāni pañca? Saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcindriyāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā satta phalā sattānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā. Katame satta phalā sattānisaṃsā? Diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti, atha maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti. No ce diṭṭheva dhamme aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti, atha pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti, upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī [T 5.0313] hoti, uddhaṃsoto hoti akaniṭṭhagāmī. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ indriyānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ime satta phalā sattānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

536. “Monks, there are these five faculties. What five? The faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom—these, monks, are the five faculties. Monks, because these five faculties have been developed and cultivated, seven fruits and seven benefits are to be expected. What seven fruits and seven benefits? One attains final knowledge beforehand in this very life. If one does not attain final knowledge beforehand in this very life, then one attains final knowledge at the time of death. If one does not attain final knowledge beforehand in this very life and does not attain final knowledge at the time of death, then with the destruction of the five lower fetters, one becomes one who attains final Nibbāna in the interval, one who attains final Nibbāna upon approach, one who attains final Nibbāna without exertion, one who attains final Nibbāna with exertion, or one who is an upstream-goer, heading for the Akaniṭṭha realm. Monks, because these five faculties have been developed and cultivated, these seven fruits and seven benefits are to be expected.” The sixth.

7. Paṭhamarukkhasuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse on the Tree

537. “Seyyathāpi bhikkhave, ye keci jambudīpakā rukkhā, jambū tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāya. Katame ca, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyā dhammā? Saddhindriyaṃ, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Vīriyindriyaṃ…pe… satindriyaṃ…pe… samādhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci jambudīpakā rukkhā, jambū tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāyā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

537. “Monks, just as among whatever trees there are in Jambudīpa, the rose-apple tree is declared the foremost, so too, monks, among whatever qualities that are aids to enlightenment there are, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for enlightenment. And what, monks, are the qualities that are aids to enlightenment? The faculty of faith, monks, is a quality that is an aid to enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment. The faculty of energy… the faculty of mindfulness… the faculty of concentration… the faculty of wisdom is a quality that is an aid to enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment. Just as, monks, among whatever trees there are in Jambudīpa, the rose-apple tree is declared the foremost, so too, monks, among whatever qualities that are aids to enlightenment there are, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for enlightenment.” The seventh.

8. Dutiyarukkhasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse on the Tree

538. “Seyyathāpi[P 5.0238], bhikkhave, ye keci devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ rukkhā, pārichattako tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāya. Katame ca, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyā dhammā? Saddhindriyaṃ[V 3.0312], bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Vīriyindriyaṃ…pe… satindriyaṃ…pe… [T 5.0314] samādhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave[M 3.0209], ye keci devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ rukkhā, pārichattako tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāyā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

538. “Just as, monks, among whatever trees there are of the Tāvatiṃsa devas, the Pāricchattaka tree is declared the foremost; just so, monks, among whatever qualities that are factors of enlightenment there are, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for enlightenment. And what, monks, are the qualities that are factors of enlightenment? The faculty of faith, monks, is a quality that is a factor of enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment. The faculty of energy… the faculty of mindfulness… the faculty of concentration… the faculty of wisdom is a quality that is a factor of enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment. Just as, monks, among whatever trees there are of the Tāvatiṃsa devas, the Pāricchattaka tree is declared the foremost; just so, monks, among whatever qualities that are factors of enlightenment there are, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for enlightenment.” The eighth.

9. Tatiyarukkhasuttaṃ

9. The Third Discourse on the Tree

539. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci asurānaṃ rukkhā, cittapāṭali tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāya. Katame ca, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyā dhammā? Saddhindriyaṃ, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati…pe… paññindriyaṃ bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Seyyathāpi bhikkhave, ye keci asurānaṃ rukkhā, cittapāṭali tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāyā”ti. Navamaṃ.

539. “Just as, monks, among whatever trees there are of the asuras, the Cittapāṭali tree is declared the foremost; even so, monks, among whatever qualities that are factors of enlightenment there are, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for enlightenment. And what, monks, are the qualities that are factors of enlightenment? The faculty of faith, monks, is a quality that is a factor of enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment… the faculty of wisdom is a quality that is a factor of enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment. Just as, monks, among whatever trees there are of the asuras, the Cittapāṭali tree is declared the foremost; even so, monks, among whatever qualities that are factors of enlightenment there are, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for enlightenment.” The ninth.

10. Catuttharukkhasuttaṃ

10. The Fourth Discourse on the Tree

540. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci supaṇṇānaṃ rukkhā, kūṭasimbalī koṭasimbali (syā. kaṃ.) tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāya. Katame [P 5.0239] ca, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyā dhammā? Saddhindriyaṃ, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyo dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati…pe… paññindriyaṃ bodhipakkhiyo [T 5.0315] dhammo, taṃ bodhāya saṃvattati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci supaṇṇānaṃ rukkhā, kūṭasimbalī tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññindriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ – bodhāyā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

540. “Just as, monks, among whatever trees there are of the supaṇṇas, the silk-cotton tree is declared the foremost; even so, monks, among whatever qualities that are factors of enlightenment there are, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for enlightenment. And what, monks, are the qualities that are factors of enlightenment? The faculty of faith, monks, is a quality that is a factor of enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment… the faculty of wisdom is a quality that is a factor of enlightenment; it conduces to enlightenment. Just as, monks, among whatever trees there are of the supaṇṇas, the silk-cotton tree is declared the foremost; even so, monks, among whatever qualities that are factors of enlightenment there are, the faculty of wisdom is declared the foremost, that is, for enlightenment.” The tenth.

Bodhipakkhiyavaggo sattamo.

The Chapter on the Factors of Enlightenment, the Seventh.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Saṃyojanā [V 3.0313] anusayā, pariññā āsavakkhayā;

Dve phalā caturo rukkhā, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

Fetters, latent tendencies, full understanding, destruction of taints; two on fruits, four on trees—by this the chapter is called.

8. Gaṅgāpeyyālavaggo

8. 8. The Chapter on the Ganges Repetition Series

1-12. Pācīnādisuttadvādasakaṃ

1–12. The Twelve Discourses Beginning with the East

541-552. “Seyyathāpi[T 5.0316][M 3.0210], bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcindriyāni bhāvento pañcindriyāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcindriyāni bhāvento pañcindriyāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhindriyaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ…pe… satindriyaṃ… samādhindriyaṃ… paññindriyaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcindriyāni bhāvento pañcindriyāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

541–552. “Just as, monks, the river Ganges slopes, tends, and gravitates to the east, so too, a monk who develops and cultivates the five faculties slopes, tends, and gravitates to Nibbāna. And how, monks, does a monk who develops and cultivates the five faculties slope, tend, and gravitate to Nibbāna? Here, monks, a monk develops the faculty of faith, which is based upon seclusion, based upon dispassion, based upon cessation, culminating in relinquishment. He develops the faculty of energy… the faculty of mindfulness… the faculty of concentration… the faculty of wisdom, which is based upon seclusion, based upon dispassion, based upon cessation, culminating in relinquishment. It is in this way, monks, that a monk who develops and cultivates the five faculties slopes, tends, and gravitates to Nibbāna.” The twelfth.

Gaṅgāpeyyālavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Chapter on the Ganges Repetition Series, the Eighth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Cha [P 5.0240] pācīnato ninnā, cha ninnā ca samuddato;

Dvete cha dvādasa honti, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

Six sloping to the east, and six sloping to the ocean; these two sets of six make twelve, thus the chapter is called.

Appamādavaggo [V 3.0314] vitthāretabbo.

The Chapter on Heedfulness should be expanded.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Tathāgataṃ padaṃ kūṭaṃ, mūlaṃ sārena vassikaṃ;

Rājā candimasūriyā, vatthena dasamaṃ padanti.

The Tathāgata, foot, peak, root, heartwood, jasmine; king, moon and sun, with the cloth as the tenth.

Balakaraṇīyavaggo vitthāretabbo.

10. The Chapter on Things to be Done with Strength (To be elaborated in full).

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Balaṃ bījañca nāgo ca, rukkho kumbhena sūkiyā;

Ākāsena ca dve meghā, nāvā āgantukā nadīti.

Strength, seed, and nāga, tree, pot, and needle; with the sky, two clouds, boat, visitor, and river.

Esanāvaggo vitthāretabbo.

11. The Chapter on Searches (To be elaborated in full).

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Esanā [M 3.0211] vidhā āsavo, bhavo ca dukkhatā tisso;

Khilaṃ malañca nīgho ca, vedanā taṇhā tasinā cāti.

Searches, kinds, taints, existence, and the three sufferings; barrenness, stain, and trouble, feeling, craving, and thirst.

12. Oghavaggo

12. 12. The Chapter on Floods

1-10. Oghādisuttadasakaṃ

1–10. The Ten Discourses Beginning with the Flood

587-596. “Pañcimāni[V 3.0315][P 5.0241], bhikkhave, uddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Katamāni pañca? Rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya pañcindriyāni bhāvetabbāni. Katamāni pañca? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhindriyaṃ bhāveti [T 5.0317] vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya imāni pañcindriyāni bhāvetabbānī”ti. Dasamaṃ. (Yathā maggasaṃyuttaṃ, tathā vitthāretabbaṃ.)

587–596. “Bhikkhus, there are these five higher fetters. Which five? Lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance. These, bhikkhus, are the five higher fetters. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandoning of these five higher fetters, the five faculties should be developed. Which five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the faculty of faith, which is based upon seclusion, based upon dispassion, based upon cessation, culminating in relinquishment… he develops the faculty of wisdom, which is based upon seclusion, based upon dispassion, based upon cessation, culminating in relinquishment. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandoning of these five higher fetters, these five faculties should be developed.” The tenth. (This should be elaborated as in the Connected Discourses on the Path.)

Oghavaggo dvādasamo.

The Chapter on Floods is the twelfth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Ogho yogo upādānaṃ, ganthā anusayena ca;

Kāmaguṇā nīvaraṇā, khandhā oruddhambhāgiyāti.

The flood, yoke, clinging, bond, and latent tendency; sensual pleasures, hindrances, aggregates, and the lower and higher fetters.

13. Gaṅgāpeyyālavaggo

13. The Chapter on the Ganges Repetition Section

1-12. Pācīnādisuttadvādasakaṃ

1–12. The Dozen Discourses Beginning with the Eastern Direction

597-608. “Seyyathāpi[M 3.0212], bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcindriyāni bhāvento pañcindriyāni bahulīkaronto [V 3.0316] nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcindriyāni bhāvento pañcindriyāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhindriyaṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcindriyāni bhāvento pañcindriyāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

597–608. “Just as, bhikkhus, the river Ganges slopes, inclines, and gravitates to the east, so too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the five faculties slopes, inclines, and gravitates to Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the five faculties slope, incline, and gravitate to Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the faculty of faith, which has the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion as its culmination… he develops the faculty of wisdom, which has the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion as its culmination. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the five faculties slopes, inclines, and gravitates to Nibbāna.” The twelfth.

Gaṅgāpeyyālavaggo terasamo.

The Chapter on the Ganges Repetition Section is the thirteenth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Cha [P 5.0242] pācīnato ninnā, cha ninnā ca samuddato;

Dvete cha dvādasa honti, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

Six slope to the east, and six slope to the ocean; these two sixes become twelve, therefore it is called a chapter.

Appamādavagga-balakaraṇīyavagga-esanāvaggā vitthāretabbā.

The Chapter on Heedfulness, the Chapter on What is to be Done by Strength, and the Chapter on Searches should be elaborated.

17. Oghavaggo

17. The Chapter on Floods

1-10. Oghādisuttadasakaṃ

1–10. The Ten Suttas beginning with the Flood.

641-650. “Pañcimāni[V 3.0317], bhikkhave, uddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Katamāni pañca? Rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni [T 5.0318] kho, bhikkhave, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya pañcindriyāni bhāvetabbāni. Katamāni pañca? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhindriyaṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ. Vīriyindriyaṃ [M 3.0213] …pe… satindriyaṃ… samādhindriyaṃ [P 5.0243] … paññindriyaṃ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṃ dosavinayapariyosānaṃ mohavinayapariyosānaṃ. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya imāni pañcindriyāni bhāvetabbānī”ti.

641–650. “Bhikkhus, there are these five higher fetters. What five? Lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance—these, bhikkhus, are the five higher fetters. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandoning of these five higher fetters, the five faculties should be developed. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the faculty of faith, which culminates in the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion. He develops the faculty of energy... the faculty of mindfulness... the faculty of concentration... he develops the faculty of wisdom, which culminates in the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandoning of these five higher fetters, these five faculties should be developed.”

Oghavaggo sattarasamo.

The Chapter on the Floods is the seventeenth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Ogho yogo upādānaṃ, ganthā anusayena ca;

Kāmaguṇā nīvaraṇā, khandhā oruddhambhāgiyāti.

The flood, yoke, clinging, knots, and latent tendencies; sensual pleasures, hindrances, aggregates, the lower and higher fetters.

Indriyasaṃyuttaṃ catutthaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Faculties is the fourth.
