And through the development and cultivation of these four bases of psychic power, the monk Moggallāna experiences the various kinds of psychic power… even up to the Brahmā world, he wields mastery with his body… And through the development and cultivation of these four bases of psychic power, the monk Moggallāna, by the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life enters and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom.” The fourth.

5. Uṇṇābhabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse to Uṇṇābha the Brahmin

827. Evaṃ [T 5.0349] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ānando kosambiyaṃ viharati ghositārāme. Atha [P 5.0272] kho uṇṇābho brāhmaṇo yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho uṇṇābho brāhmaṇo āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “kimatthiyaṃ nu kho, bho ānanda, samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti? “Chandappahānatthaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, bhagavati brahmacariyaṃ vussatī”ti.

827. Thus have I heard. On one occasion, the Venerable Ānanda was dwelling in Kosambī at Ghosita's Park. Then the brahmin Uṇṇābha approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, he exchanged joyful greetings with the Venerable Ānanda. Having concluded a joyful and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Uṇṇābha said this to the Venerable Ānanda: 'For what purpose, good Ānanda, is the holy life lived under the ascetic Gotama?' 'Brahmin, it is for the purpose of abandoning desire that the holy life is lived under the Blessed One.'

“Atthi [V 3.0344] pana, bho ānanda, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa chandassa pahānāyā”ti? “Atthi kho, brāhmaṇa, maggo atthi paṭipadā etassa chandassa pahānāyā”ti.

'But, good Ānanda, is there a path, is there a practice for the abandoning of this desire?' 'Brahmin, there is a path, there is a practice for the abandoning of this desire.'

“Katamo pana, bho ānanda, maggo katamā paṭipadā etassa chandassa pahānāyā”ti? “Idha, brāhmaṇa, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ayaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, maggo ayaṃ paṭipadā etassa chandassa pahānāyā”ti.

'And what, good Ānanda, is the path, what is the practice for the abandoning of this desire?' 'Here, brahmin, a monk develops the base of psychic power that is endowed with concentration founded on desire and with striving formations. He develops the base of psychic power that is endowed with concentration founded on energy... concentration founded on mind... concentration founded on investigation and with striving formations. This, brahmin, is the path, this is the practice for the abandoning of this desire.'

“Evaṃ [M 3.0238] sante, bho ānanda, santakaṃ hoti no asantakaṃ. Chandeneva chandaṃ pajahissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati”. “Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, taññevettha paṭipucchissāmi. Yathā te khameyya tathā taṃ byākareyyāsi. Taṃ [T 5.0350] kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, ahosi te pubbe chando ‘ārāmaṃ gamissāmī’ti? Tassa te ārāmagatassa yo tajjo chando so paṭippassaddho”ti? “Evaṃ[P 5.0273], bho”. “Ahosi te pubbe vīriyaṃ ‘ārāmaṃ gamissāmī’ti? Tassa te ārāmagatassa yaṃ tajjaṃ vīriyaṃ taṃ paṭippassaddha”nti? “Evaṃ, bho”. “Ahosi te pubbe cittaṃ ‘ārāmaṃ gamissāmī’ti? Tassa te ārāmagatassa yaṃ tajjaṃ cittaṃ taṃ paṭippassaddha”nti? “Evaṃ, bho”. “Ahosi te pubbe vīmaṃsā ‘ārāmaṃ gamissāmī’ti? Tassa te ārāmagatassa yā tajjā vīmaṃsā sā paṭippassaddhā”ti? “Evaṃ, bho”.

“If that is so, good Ānanda, then it has an end; it is not without an end. That one will abandon desire by means of desire—this is not possible.” “Well then, brahmin, I shall question you in return on this very matter. You should answer as you see fit. What do you think, brahmin? Did you previously have the desire, ‘I will go to the park’? When you had gone to the park, was that corresponding desire pacified?” “Yes, good sir.” “Did you previously have the energy, ‘I will go to the park’? When you had gone to the park, was that corresponding energy pacified?” “Yes, good sir.” “Did you previously have the thought, ‘I will go to the park’? When you had gone to the park, was that corresponding thought pacified?” “Yes, good sir.” “Did you previously have the investigation, ‘I will go to the park’? When you had gone to the park, was that corresponding investigation pacified?” “Yes, good sir.”

“Evameva kho, brāhmaṇa, yo so bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto, tassa yo pubbe chando ahosi arahattappattiyā, arahattappatte arahatte patte (sī. syā. kaṃ.) yo tajjo chando so paṭippassaddho; yaṃ pubbe vīriyaṃ ahosi arahattappattiyā, arahattappatte yaṃ tajjaṃ vīriyaṃ taṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ; yaṃ pubbe cittaṃ ahosi arahattappattiyā, arahattappatte yaṃ tajjaṃ cittaṃ taṃ paṭippassaddhaṃ; yā pubbe vīmaṃsā ahosi arahattappattiyā, arahattappatte yā tajjā vīmaṃsā sā paṭippassaddhā. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, brāhmaṇa, iti evaṃ sante, santakaṃ vā hoti no asantakaṃ vā”ti?

“Just so, brahmin, for the bhikkhu who is an Arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, utterly destroyed the fetter of existence, and is liberated through right final knowledge: the desire he previously had for the attainment of Arahantship—upon attaining Arahantship, that corresponding desire is pacified; the effort he previously had for the attainment of Arahantship—upon attaining Arahantship, that corresponding effort is pacified; the thought he previously had for the attainment of Arahantship—upon attaining Arahantship, that corresponding thought is pacified; the investigation he previously had for the attainment of Arahantship—upon attaining Arahantship, that corresponding investigation is pacified. What do you think, brahmin? This being so, does it have an end, or does it not have an end?”

“Addhā, bho ānanda, evaṃ sante, santakaṃ hoti [T 5.0351] no asantakaṃ. Abhikkantaṃ, bho ānanda, abhikkantaṃ, bho ānanda! Seyyathāpi, bho ānanda, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ [V 3.0345] vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya – cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantīti; evamevaṃ bhotā ānandena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bho ānanda, taṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ ānando dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Certainly, Venerable Ānanda, when it is so, it has an end; it is not without an end. Excellent, Venerable Ānanda! Excellent, Venerable Ānanda! Just as, Venerable Ānanda, one might turn upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or point out the way to one who was lost, or hold up an oil lamp in the darkness, thinking, ‘Those with eyes will see forms’—in this very way, the Dhamma has been declared by the Venerable Ānanda in many ways. I, Venerable Ānanda, go for refuge to that Venerable Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May the Venerable Ānanda remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life lasts.”

6. Paṭhamasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

6. The First Discourse on Recluses and Brahmins

828. “Ye [M 3.0239] hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā mahiddhikā ahesuṃ mahānubhāvā, sabbe te catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā mahiddhikā bhavissanti mahānubhāvā, sabbe te catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā mahiddhikā mahānubhāvā, sabbe te catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā.

828. “Bhikkhus, whatever recluses or brahmins in the past were of great psychic power and great might, all of them were so because they had developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power. Whatever recluses or brahmins in the future will be of great psychic power and great might, all of them will be so because they will have developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power. Whatever recluses or brahmins at present are of great psychic power and great might, all of them are so because they have developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idha[P 5.0274], bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā [T 5.0352] mahiddhikā ahesuṃ mahānubhāvā, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā mahiddhikā bhavissanti mahānubhāvā, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā mahiddhikā mahānubhāvā, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Which four? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the basis of psychic power that possesses concentration of desire, accompanied by the volitional formations of striving. He develops the basis of psychic power that possesses concentration of energy… concentration of mind… concentration of investigation, accompanied by the volitional formations of striving. Bhikkhus, whatever recluses or brahmins in the past were of great psychic power and great might, all of them were so because they had developed and cultivated these same four bases of psychic power. Whatever recluses or brahmins in the future will be of great psychic power and great might, all of them will be so because they will have developed and cultivated these same four bases of psychic power. Whatever recluses or brahmins at present are of great psychic power and great might, all of them are so because they have developed and cultivated these same four bases of psychic power.”

7. Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

7. The Second Discourse on Recluses and Brahmins

829. “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhosuṃ – ekopi hutvā bahudhā ahesuṃ, bahudhāpi hutvā eko ahesuṃ; āvibhāvaṃ, tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamānā agamaṃsu, seyyathāpi [V 3.0346] ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ akaṃsu, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne abhijjamānā (sī. pī. ka.) agamaṃsu, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamiṃsu, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasiṃsu parāmasiṃsu (syā. kaṃ. ka.) parimajjiṃsu; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattesuṃ, sabbe te catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā.

829. “Bhikkhus, whatever recluses or brahmins in the past wielded various kinds of psychic power—being one, they became many; being many, they became one; they appeared and vanished; they went unhindered through walls, ramparts, and mountains as if through space; they emerged from and submerged into the earth as if it were water; they walked on water without breaking through as if it were earth; they traveled through the sky while sitting cross-legged like a winged bird; they even touched and stroked with their hand the moon and sun, so mighty and powerful; they exercised mastery with their body even as far as the Brahmā world—all of them did so because of having developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power.

“Ye [M 3.0240] hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhossanti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā bhavissanti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko bhavissanti; āvibhāvaṃ, tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamānā gamissanti[T 5.0353], seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ karissanti, seyyathāpi [P 5.0275] udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gamissanti, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamissanti, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasissanti parimajjissanti; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattissanti, sabbe te catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā.

“Bhikkhus, whatever recluses or brahmins in the future will experience various kinds of psychic power—having been one, they will become many; having been many, they will become one; they will manifest and vanish; they will go unhindered through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; in the earth, they will perform diving up and down as if in water; on water, they will go without breaking through as if on earth; in the sky, they will travel cross-legged like a winged bird; these moon and sun, so mighty and powerful, they will touch and stroke with their hand; they will wield mastery with their body even as far as the Brahmā world—all of them will do so because they will have developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power.”

“Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhonti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā honti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko honti; āvibhāvaṃ, tirobhāvaṃ; tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamānā gacchanti, seyyathāpi ākāse; pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ karonti, seyyathāpi udake; udakepi abhijjamāne gacchanti, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ; ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamanti, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo; imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parimasanti parāmasanti (syā. kaṃ.) parimajjanti; yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattenti, sabbe te catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattāti.

“Monks, whatever ascetics or brahmins at present experience various kinds of psychic power—having been one, they become many; having been many, they become one; they appear and disappear; they go unhindered through a wall, a rampart, or a mountain as if through space; they dive in and out of the earth as if it were water; they walk on water without breaking through as if on earth; they travel through the sky cross-legged like a winged bird; they touch and stroke with their hand these moon and sun, so mighty and powerful; they wield mastery with their body even as far as the Brahmā world—all of them do so because the four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhosuṃ – ekopi hutvā bahudhā ahesuṃ…pe… [T 5.0354] yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattesuṃ, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā.

“Of which four? Here, monks, a monk develops the basis of psychic power that is endowed with concentration founded on desire and the formations of striving. He develops the basis of psychic power… with concentration founded on energy… with concentration founded on mind… he develops the basis of psychic power that is endowed with concentration founded on investigation and the formations of striving. Monks, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past experienced various kinds of psychic power—having been one, they became many… they wielded mastery with their body even as far as the Brahmā world—all of them did so because of having developed and cultivated these same four bases of psychic power.

“Ye [V 3.0347] hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhossanti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā bhavissanti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattissanti, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā.

“Monks, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will experience various kinds of psychic power—having been one, they will become many... they will exercise mastery with their bodies even as far as the Brahmā world—all of them will do so because of having developed and cultivated these same four bases of psychic power.”

“Ye [M 3.0241] hi keci bhikkhave etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhonti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā honti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattenti, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Monks, whatever ascetics or brahmins at present experience various kinds of psychic power—having been one, they become many... they exercise mastery with their bodies even as far as the Brahmā world—all of them do so because of having developed and cultivated these same four bases of psychic power.” The seventh.

8. Bhikkhusuttaṃ

8. 8. The Monk

830. “Catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.

830. “Monks, because of having developed and cultivated the four bases of psychic power, a monk, through the destruction of the taints, attains and abides in the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge and made it manifest in this very life.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā [P 5.0276] anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Of which four? Here, monks, a monk develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration founded on desire and the formations of striving. He develops the basis of psychic power… with concentration founded on energy… with concentration founded on mind… with concentration founded on investigation and the formations of striving. Monks, it is because these four bases of psychic power have been developed and cultivated that a monk, through the destruction of the taints, attains and abides in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge and made it manifest in this very life.” The eighth.

9. Iddhādidesanāsuttaṃ

9. 9. Discourse on the Exposition of Psychic Power and Related Topics

831. “Iddhiṃ vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi iddhipādañca iddhipādabhāvanañca [T 5.0355] iddhipādabhāvanāgāminiñca paṭipadaṃ. Taṃ suṇātha.

831. “Monks, I will teach you psychic power, the basis of psychic power, the development of the basis of psychic power, and the practice leading to the development of the basis of psychic power. Listen to that.”

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, iddhi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhi.

“And what, monks, is psychic power? Here, monks, a monk experiences various kinds of psychic power: having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one… he wields mastery with his body even as far as the Brahmā world. This, monks, is called psychic power.”

“Katamo [V 3.0348] ca, bhikkhave, iddhipādo? Yo so, bhikkhave, maggo yā paṭipadā iddhilābhāya iddhipaṭilābhāya saṃvattati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhipādo.

“And what, monks, is the basis of psychic power? Monks, that path, that practice which leads to the gaining of psychic power, to the acquisition of psychic power—this, monks, is called the basis of psychic power.”

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi …pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanā.

“And what, monks, is the development of the basis of psychic power? Here, monks, a monk develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration founded on desire and the formations of striving; he develops the basis of psychic power… with concentration founded on energy… with concentration founded on mind… with concentration founded on investigation and the formations of striving. This, monks, is called the development of the basis of psychic power.”

“Katamā [M 3.0242] ca, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā”ti. Navamaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the practice leading to the development of the basis of psychic power? It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, monks, is called the practice leading to the development of the basis of psychic power.” The ninth.

10. Vibhaṅgasuttaṃ

10. 10. The Analysis

832. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, iddhipādā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṃsā”.

832. “Monks, these four bases of psychic power, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit and great benefit.”

“Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, cattāro iddhipādā kathaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṃsā? Idha, bhikkhave[T 5.0356], bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ‘iti me chando na [P 5.0277] ca atilīno bhavissati, na ca atippaggahito bhavissati, na ca ajjhattaṃ saṃkhitto bhavissati, na ca bahiddhā vikkhitto bhavissati’. Pacchāpuresaññī ca viharati – ‘yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā [V 3.0349] tathā pure; yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho; yathā divā tathā rattiṃ yathā rattiṃ tathā divā’. Iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ‘iti me vīmaṃsā na ca atilīnā bhavissati, na ca atippaggahitā bhavissati, na ca ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittā bhavissati, na ca bahiddhā vikkhittā bhavissati’. Pacchāpuresaññī ca viharati – ‘yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā tathā pure; yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho; yathā divā tathā rattiṃ, yathā rattiṃ tathā divā’. Iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti.

And how, monks, are the four bases of power, when developed and cultivated, of great fruit and great benefit? Here, monks, a monk develops the basis of power that is endowed with concentration founded on desire and the formations of striving, thinking: 'Thus my desire will be neither too slack nor too exerted, neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.' And he dwells perceiving what is after as what is before: 'As before, so after; as after, so before. As below, so above; as above, so below. As by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.' Thus, with an open and unenveloped mind, he develops a luminous mind. He develops the basis of power that is endowed with concentration founded on energy... concentration founded on mind... concentration founded on investigation and the formations of striving, thinking: 'Thus my investigation will be neither too slack nor too exerted, neither constricted internally nor scattered externally.' And he dwells perceiving what is after as what is before: 'As before, so after; as after, so before. As below, so above; as above, so below. As by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.' Thus, with an open and unenveloped mind, he develops a luminous mind.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, atilīno chando? Yo, bhikkhave, chando kosajjasahagato kosajjasampayutto – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atilīno chando.

And what, monks, is desire that is too slack? Whatever desire is accompanied by laziness, associated with laziness—this, monks, is called desire that is too slack.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, atippaggahito chando? Yo, bhikkhave, chando uddhaccasahagato uddhaccasampayutto – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atippaggahito chando.

And what, monks, is desire that is too exerted? Whatever desire is accompanied by restlessness, associated with restlessness—this, monks, is called desire that is too exerted.

“Katamo [T 5.0357][M 3.0243] ca, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ saṃkhitto chando? Yo, bhikkhave, chando thinamiddhasahagato thinamiddhasampayutto – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ saṃkhitto chando.

And what, monks, is internally constricted desire? Whatever desire is accompanied by sloth and torpor, associated with sloth and torpor—this, monks, is called internally constricted desire.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, bahiddhā vikkhitto chando? Yo, bhikkhave, chando bahiddhā pañca kāmaguṇe ārabbha anuvikkhitto anuvisaṭo – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bahiddhā vikkhitto chando.

And what, monks, is externally scattered desire? Whatever desire, taking the five strands of sensual pleasure as its object, is scattered and dispersed externally—this, monks, is called externally scattered desire.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pacchāpuresaññī ca viharati – yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā tathā pure? Idha[P 5.0278], bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pacchāpuresaññā suggahitā hoti sumanasikatā sūpadhāritā suppaṭividdhā paññāya. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pacchāpuresaññī ca viharati – yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā tathā pure.

And how, monks, does a monk dwell perceiving what is after as what is before: as before, so after; as after, so before? Here, monks, for a monk, the perception of what is after as what is before is well grasped, well attended to, well considered, and well penetrated by wisdom. Thus, monks, a monk dwells perceiving what is after as what is before: as before, so after; as after, so before.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho viharati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṃ uddhaṃ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṃ pūraṃ nānappakārassa asucino paccavekkhati – ‘atthi imasmiṃ kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā mutta’nti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho viharati.

And how, monks, does a monk dwell so that as it is below, so it is above; as it is above, so it is below? Here, monks, a monk reviews this very body, upwards from the soles of the feet, downwards from the top of the hair, enclosed by skin and full of various kinds of impurity: 'In this body there are head-hairs, body-hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, pleura, spleen, lungs, large intestines, small intestines, stomach contents, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, solid fat, tears, liquid fat, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, and urine.' Thus, monks, a monk dwells so that as it is below, so it is above; as it is above, so it is below.

“Kathañca[V 3.0350][T 5.0358], bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathā divā tathā rattiṃ, yathā rattiṃ tathā divā viharati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yehi ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi nimittehi divā chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, so tehi ākārehi tehi liṅgehi tehi nimittehi rattiṃ chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti; yehi vā pana ākārehi yehi liṅgehi yehi nimittehi rattiṃ chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, so tehi ākārehi tehi liṅgehi tehi nimittehi divā chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathā divā tathā rattiṃ, yathā rattiṃ tathā divā viharati.

And how, monks, does a monk dwell as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day? Here, monks, with whatever modes, signs, and indications a monk develops by day the basis of power endowed with concentration founded on desire and the formations of striving, with those same modes, signs, and indications he develops it by night. And with whatever modes, signs, and indications he develops by night the basis of power endowed with concentration founded on desire and the formations of striving, with those same modes, signs, and indications he develops it by day. In this way, monks, a monk dwells as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.

“Kathañca[M 3.0244], bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ālokasaññā suggahitā hoti divāsaññā svādhiṭṭhitā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti.

And how, monks, does a monk develop a luminous mind with a mind that is open and unenveloped? Here, monks, a monk's perception of light is well grasped, and the perception of daytime is well established. In this way, monks, a monk develops a luminous mind with a mind that is open and unenveloped.

“Katamañca[P 5.0279], bhikkhave, atilīnaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, vīriyaṃ kosajjasahagataṃ kosajjasampayuttaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atilīnaṃ vīriyaṃ.

And what, monks, is energy that is too slack? Whatever energy, monks, is accompanied by laziness, associated with laziness—this, monks, is called energy that is too slack.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, atippaggahitaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, vīriyaṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ uddhaccasampayuttaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atippaggahitaṃ vīriyaṃ.

And what, monks, is energy that is too exerted? Whatever energy, monks, is accompanied by restlessness, associated with restlessness—this, monks, is called energy that is too exerted.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, vīriyaṃ [T 5.0359] thinamiddhasahagataṃ thinamiddhasampayuttaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittaṃ vīriyaṃ.

And what, monks, is internally constricted energy? Whatever energy, monks, is accompanied by sloth and torpor, associated with sloth and torpor—this, monks, is called internally constricted energy.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, bahiddhā vikkhittaṃ vīriyaṃ? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, vīriyaṃ bahiddhā pañca kāmaguṇe ārabbha anuvikkhittaṃ anuvisaṭaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bahiddhā vikkhittaṃ vīriyaṃ…pe….

And what, bhikkhus, is externally scattered energy? That energy, bhikkhus, which is scattered forth and spread out externally with regard to the five strands of sensual pleasure—this, bhikkhus, is called externally scattered energy... and so on...

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti[V 3.0351]? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ālokasaññā suggahitā hoti divāsaññā svādhiṭṭhitā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti.

And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu develop a mind that is open, uncovered, and luminous? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has well-grasped the perception of light, and the perception of daytime is well-established. Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops a mind that is open, uncovered, and luminous.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, atilīnaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ kosajjasahagataṃ kosajjasampayuttaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atilīnaṃ cittaṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is an overly sluggish mind? That mind, bhikkhus, which is accompanied by laziness, conjoined with laziness—this, bhikkhus, is called an overly sluggish mind.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, atippaggahitaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ uddhaccasahagataṃ uddhaccasampayuttaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atippaggahitaṃ cittaṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is an over-exerted mind? That mind, bhikkhus, which is accompanied by restlessness, conjoined with restlessness—this, bhikkhus, is called an over-exerted mind.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ thinamiddhasahagataṃ thinamiddhasampayuttaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittaṃ cittaṃ.

And what, bhikkhus, is the internally constricted mind? That mind, bhikkhus, which is accompanied by sloth and torpor, conjoined with sloth and torpor—this, bhikkhus, is called the internally constricted mind.

“Katamañca[P 5.0280], bhikkhave, bahiddhā vikkhittaṃ cittaṃ? Yaṃ, bhikkhave, cittaṃ bahiddhā pañca kāmaguṇe ārabbha anuvikkhittaṃ anuvisaṭaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bahiddhā vikkhittaṃ cittaṃ…pe… evaṃ [T 5.0360] kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti.

And what, bhikkhus, is an externally scattered mind? That mind, bhikkhus, which is scattered forth and spread out externally with regard to the five strands of sensual pleasure—this, bhikkhus, is called an externally scattered mind... and so on... Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops a mind that is open, uncovered, and luminous.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, atilīnā vīmaṃsā? Yā, bhikkhave, vīmaṃsā kosajjasahagatā kosajjasampayuttā – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atilīnā vīmaṃsā.

And what, bhikkhus, is excessively sluggish investigation? That investigation, bhikkhus, which is accompanied by laziness, conjoined with laziness—this, bhikkhus, is called excessively sluggish investigation.

“Katamā [M 3.0245] ca, bhikkhave, atippaggahitā vīmaṃsā? Yā, bhikkhave, vīmaṃsā uddhaccasahagatā uddhaccasampayuttā – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atippaggahitā vīmaṃsā.

And what, bhikkhus, is over-exerted investigation? That investigation, bhikkhus, which is accompanied by restlessness, conjoined with restlessness—this, bhikkhus, is called over-exerted investigation.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittā vīmaṃsā? Yā, bhikkhave, vīmaṃsā thinamiddhasahagatā thinamiddhasampayuttā – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittā vīmaṃsā.

And what, bhikkhus, is the internally constricted investigation? That investigation, bhikkhus, which is accompanied by sloth and torpor, conjoined with sloth and torpor—this is called, bhikkhus, the internally constricted investigation.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, bahiddhā vikkhittā vīmaṃsā? Yā, bhikkhave, vīmaṃsā bahiddhā pañca kāmaguṇe ārabbha anuvikkhittā anuvisaṭā – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bahiddhā [V 3.0352] vikkhittā vīmaṃsā…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, cattāro iddhipādā evaṃ bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṃsā.

And what, bhikkhus, is externally scattered investigation? That investigation, bhikkhus, which, taking as its object the five strands of sensual pleasure, is scattered about and dispersed externally—this is called, bhikkhus, externally scattered investigation. … Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops a luminous mind with a consciousness that is open and unwrapped. When the four bases for spiritual power are thus developed and cultivated, they are of great fruit and great benefit.

“Evaṃ bhāvitesu kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu catūsu iddhipādesu evaṃ bahulīkatesu, anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi [T 5.0361] kāyena vasaṃ vatteti. Evaṃ bhāvitesu kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu catūsu iddhipādesu evaṃ bahulīkatesu, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ [P 5.0281] paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

When these four bases for spiritual power have been thus developed and cultivated, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu experiences various kinds of spiritual power: having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one… he wields mastery with his body even as far as the Brahmā world. When these four bases for spiritual power have been thus developed and cultivated, bhikkhus, with the destruction of the taints, he dwells having realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and having entered upon it. The tenth.

Pāsādakampanavaggo dutiyo.

The Pāsādakampana Chapter, the Second.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this chapter:

Pubbaṃ mahapphalaṃ chandaṃ, moggallānañca uṇṇābhaṃ;

Dve samaṇabrāhmaṇā bhikkhu, desanā vibhaṅgena cāti.

Pubba, Mahapphala, Chanda, Moggallāna, and Uṇṇābha the Brahmin; Two Samaṇabrāhmaṇas, Bhikkhu, Desanā, and Vibhaṅga.

3. Ayoguḷavaggo

3. 3. The Iron Ball Chapter

1. Maggasuttaṃ

1. 1. The Path Discourse

833. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0362]. “Pubbeva me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattasseva sato etadahosi – ‘ko nu kho maggo, kā paṭipadā iddhipādabhāvanāyā’ti[M 3.0246]? Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, etadahosi – ‘idha bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – iti me chando na ca atilīno bhavissati, na ca atippaggahito bhavissati, na ca ajjhattaṃ saṃkhitto bhavissati, na ca bahiddhā vikkhitto bhavissati. Pacchāpuresaññī ca viharati – yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā tathā pure; yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho; yathā divā tathā rattiṃ, yathā rattiṃ tathā divā. Iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti[V 3.0353]. Vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – iti me vīmaṃsā na ca atilīnā bhavissati, na ca atippaggahitā bhavissati, na ca ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittā bhavissati, na ca bahiddhā vikkhittā bhavissati. Pacchāpuresaññī ca viharati – yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā tathā pure; yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho; yathā divā tathā rattiṃ yathā rattiṃ tathā divā’ – iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti.

833. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment, while I was not yet fully enlightened and was still a Bodhisatta, this thought occurred to me: ‘What is the path, what is the way for the development of the bases of spiritual power?’ Then, bhikkhus, this thought occurred to me: ‘Here, a bhikkhu develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to desire and volitional formations of striving, thinking: “Thus my desire will be neither too sluggish nor too exerted; it will be neither internally constricted nor externally scattered.” And he dwells perceiving what is after and what is before: as before, so after; as after, so before; as below, so above; as above, so below; as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day. Thus, with an open and unconfined mind, he develops a luminous mind. He develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to energy… concentration due to mind… He develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration due to investigation and volitional formations of striving, thinking: “Thus my investigation will be neither too sluggish nor too exerted; it will be neither internally constricted nor externally scattered.” And he dwells perceiving what is after and what is before: as before, so after; as after, so before; as below, so above; as above, so below; as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.’ Thus, with an open and unconfined mind, he develops a luminous mind.”

“Evaṃ [P 5.0282] bhāvitesu kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu catūsu iddhipādesu evaṃ [T 5.0363] bahulīkatesu anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti. Evaṃ bhāvitesu kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu catūsu iddhipādesu evaṃ bahulīkatesu, āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Monks, when these four bases of psychic power are thus developed and cultivated, a monk experiences various kinds of psychic power: having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one… he wields mastery with his body even as far as the Brahmā world. When these four bases of psychic power are thus developed and cultivated, a monk, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for himself with direct knowledge, attains and abides in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, in this very life.” The first.

(Chapi abhiññāyo vitthāretabbā).

(The six direct knowledges should be elaborated upon.)

2. Ayoguḷasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Iron Ball

834. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhijānāti nu kho, bhante, bhagavā iddhiyā manomayena kāyena brahmalokaṃ upasaṅkamitā”ti? “Abhijānāmi khvāhaṃ, ānanda, iddhiyā manomayena kāyena brahmalokaṃ upasaṅkamitā”ti. “Abhijānāti pana, bhante, bhagavā iminā cātumahābhūtikena kāyena iddhiyā brahmalokaṃ upasaṅkamitā”ti[M 3.0247]? “Abhijānāmi khvāhaṃ, ānanda, iminā cātumahābhūtikena cātummahābhūtikena (sī. syā. kaṃ.) kāyena iddhiyā brahmalokaṃ upasaṅkamitā”ti.

834. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, does the Blessed One know directly of having approached the Brahmā world by means of psychic power with a mind-made body?” “Ānanda, I do know directly of having approached the Brahmā world by means of psychic power with a mind-made body.” “But, venerable sir, does the Blessed One know directly of having approached the Brahmā world by means of psychic power with this body composed of the four great elements?” “Ānanda, I do know directly of having approached the Brahmā world by means of psychic power with this body composed of the four great elements.”

“Yañca kho, omāti, bhante, bhagavā iddhiyā manomayena kāyena brahmalokaṃ upasaṅkamituṃ, yañca [P 5.0283] kho abhijānāti, bhante, bhagavā iminā cātumahābhūtikena kāyena iddhiyā brahmalokaṃ upasaṅkamitā[T 5.0364], tayidaṃ, bhante, bhagavato acchariyañceva abbhutañcā”ti. “Acchariyā [V 3.0354] ceva, ānanda, tathāgatā acchariyadhammasamannāgatā ca, abbhutā ceva, ānanda, tathāgatā abbhutadhammasamannāgatā ca”.

“Venerable sir, that the Blessed One is able to approach the Brahmā world by means of psychic power with a mind-made body, and that the Blessed One knows directly of having approached the Brahmā world by means of psychic power with this body composed of the four great elements—this, venerable sir, is a marvelous and astonishing quality of the Blessed One.” “Ānanda, Tathāgatas are indeed marvelous and endowed with marvelous qualities; Ānanda, Tathāgatas are indeed astonishing and endowed with astonishing qualities.”

“Yasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye tathāgato kāyampi citte samodahati samādahati (sī. syā. pī.) cittampi kāye samodahati, sukhasaññañca lahusaññañca kāye okkamitvā viharati; tasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye tathāgatassa kāyo lahutaro ceva hoti mudutaro ca kammaniyataro ca pabhassarataro ca.

“Ānanda, at a time when the Tathāgata establishes the body in the mind and establishes the mind in the body, and dwells having caused the perception of pleasure and the perception of lightness to enter the body; at that time, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s body becomes lighter, softer, more workable, and more radiant.

“Seyyathāpi, ānanda, ayoguḷo divasaṃ santatto lahutaro ceva hoti mudutaro ca kammaniyataro ca pabhassarataro ca; evameva kho, ānanda, yasmiṃ samaye tathāgato kāyampi citte samodahati, cittampi kāye samodahati, sukhasaññañca lahusaññañca kāye okkamitvā viharati; tasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye tathāgatassa kāyo lahutaro ceva hoti mudutaro ca kammaniyataro ca pabhassarataro ca.

“Just as, Ānanda, an iron ball heated for a day becomes lighter, softer, more workable, and more radiant; even so, Ānanda, at a time when the Tathāgata establishes the body in the mind and establishes the mind in the body, and dwells having caused the perception of pleasure and the perception of lightness to enter the body; at that time, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s body becomes lighter, softer, more workable, and more radiant.

“Yasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye tathāgato kāyampi citte samodahati, cittampi kāye samodahati, sukhasaññañca lahusaññañca kāye okkamitvā viharati; tasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye tathāgatassa kāyo appakasireneva pathaviyā vehāsaṃ abbhuggacchati, so anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti.

“Ānanda, at a time when the Tathāgata establishes the body in the mind and establishes the mind in the body, and dwells having caused the perception of pleasure and the perception of lightness to enter the body; at that time, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s body rises from the earth into the air with little effort. He experiences the various kinds of psychic power: having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one… and he exercises mastery with the body even as far as the Brahmā world.

“Seyyathāpi[P 5.0284][T 5.0365], ānanda, tūlapicu vā kappāsapicu vā lahuko vātūpādāno appakasireneva pathaviyā vehāsaṃ abbhuggacchati; evameva kho, ānanda, yasmiṃ samaye tathāgato kāyampi citte samodahati, cittampi [M 3.0248] kāye samodahati, sukhasaññañca lahusaññañca kāye okkamitvā viharati; tasmiṃ, ānanda, samaye tathāgatassa kāyo appakasireneva pathaviyā vehāsaṃ abbhuggacchati, so anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vattetī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Just as, Ānanda, a light tuft of silk-cotton or a tuft of cotton, borne by the wind, rises from the earth into the air with little effort; even so, Ānanda, at a time when the Tathāgata establishes the body in the mind and establishes the mind in the body, and dwells having caused the perception of pleasure and the perception of lightness to enter the body; at that time, Ānanda, the Tathāgata’s body rises from the earth into the air with little effort. He experiences the various kinds of psychic power: having been one, he becomes many… and he exercises mastery with the body even as far as the Brahmā world.” The second.

3. Bhikkhusuttaṃ

3. 3. The Discourse on the Bhikkhu

835. “Cattārome[V 3.0355], bhikkhave, iddhipādā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi …pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro iddhipādā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

835. “Monks, there are these four bases of spiritual power. What four? Here, monks, a monk develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on desire and with striving formations; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on energy… with concentration founded on mind… with concentration founded on investigation and with striving formations. These, monks, are the four bases of spiritual power. Monks, because these four bases of spiritual power have been developed and cultivated, a monk, through the destruction of the taints, in this very life realizes for himself with direct knowledge the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and having attained it, abides therein.” The third.

4. Suddhikasuttaṃ

4. The Simple Discourse

836. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, iddhipādā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ [T 5.0366] iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro iddhipādā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

836. “Monks, there are these four bases of spiritual power. What four? Here, monks, a monk develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on desire and with striving formations; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on energy… with concentration founded on mind… with concentration founded on investigation and with striving formations. These, monks, are the four bases of spiritual power.” The fourth.

5. Paṭhamaphalasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on the Fruit

837. “Cattārome[P 5.0285], bhikkhave, iddhipādā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi …pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro iddhipādā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā bhikkhunā dvinnaṃ phalānaṃ aññataraṃ phalaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

837. “Monks, there are these four bases of spiritual power. What four? Here, monks, a monk develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on desire and with striving formations; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on energy… with concentration founded on mind… with concentration founded on investigation and with striving formations. These, monks, are the four bases of spiritual power. Monks, because these four bases of spiritual power have been developed and cultivated by a monk, one of two fruits is to be expected: either final knowledge in this very life, or, if there is a residue remaining, the state of non-returning.” The fifth.

6. Dutiyaphalasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on the Fruit

838. “Cattārome[M 3.0249], bhikkhave, iddhipādā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ [V 3.0356] iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi …pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro iddhipādā. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā satta phalā sattānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā.

838. “Monks, there are these four bases of spiritual power. What four? Here, monks, a monk develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on desire and with striving formations; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on energy… with concentration founded on mind… with concentration founded on investigation and with striving formations. These, monks, are the four bases of spiritual power. When these four bases of spiritual power have been developed and frequently practiced, seven fruits and seven benefits are to be expected.

“Katame satta phalā sattānisaṃsā? Diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca paṭigacca (sī.), paṭihacca (pī.) aññaṃ ārādheti no ce diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti; atha maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce diṭṭheva dhamme paṭikacca aññaṃ ārādheti, no ce maraṇakāle aññaṃ ārādheti; atha pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti, upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, uddhaṃsoto hoti akaniṭṭhagāmī. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ime satta phalā sattānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“What are the seven fruits and seven benefits? One attains final knowledge beforehand in this very life. If one does not attain final knowledge beforehand in this very life, then one attains final knowledge at the time of death. If one does not attain final knowledge beforehand in this very life, and does not attain final knowledge at the time of death, then with the utter destruction of the five lower fetters, one becomes an antarāparinibbāyī, an upahaccaparinibbāyī, an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī, or one who is heading upstream, bound for the Akaniṭṭha realm. Monks, when these four bases of spiritual power have been developed and frequently practiced, these seven fruits and seven benefits are to be expected.” The sixth.

7. Paṭhamaānandasuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse to Ānanda

839. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā [T 5.0367] tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

839. The setting is Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Ānanda went to the Blessed One, and after approaching, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:

“Katamā nu kho, bhante[P 5.0286], iddhi, katamo iddhipādo, katamā iddhipādabhāvanā, katamā iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā”ti? “Idhānanda, bhikkhu anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, iddhi”.

“Venerable sir, what is spiritual power, what is the basis of spiritual power, what is the development of the basis of spiritual power, and what is the practice leading to the development of the basis of spiritual power?” “Here, Ānanda, a monk experiences various kinds of spiritual power: having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one… he wields mastery with his body even as far as the Brahmā world. This, Ānanda, is called spiritual power.”

“Katamo cānanda, iddhipādo? Yo, ānanda, maggo yā paṭipadā iddhilābhāya iddhipaṭilābhāya saṃvattati – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, iddhipādo.

“And what, Ānanda, is the basis of spiritual power? It is, Ānanda, the path, the practice that leads to the acquisition of spiritual power, to the re-acquisition of spiritual power. This, Ānanda, is called the basis of spiritual power.”

“Katamā [M 3.0250] cānanda, iddhipādabhāvanā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ [V 3.0357] bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, iddhipādabhāvanā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the development of the basis of spiritual power? Here, Ānanda, a monk develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on desire and with striving formations; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on energy… with concentration founded on mind… with concentration founded on investigation and with striving formations. This, Ānanda, is called the development of the basis of spiritual power.”

“Katamā cānanda, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“And what, Ānanda, is the practice leading to the development of the basis of spiritual power? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path; that is, right view… right concentration. This, Ānanda, is called the practice leading to the development of the basis of spiritual power.” The seventh.

8. Dutiyaānandasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse to Ānanda

840. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “katamā nu kho, ānanda, iddhi, katamo iddhipādo, katamā [T 5.0368] iddhipādabhāvanā, katamā iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā…pe….

840. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Ānanda who was seated to one side: “Ānanda, what is spiritual power, what is the basis of spiritual power, what is the development of the basis of spiritual power, and what is the practice leading to the development of the basis of spiritual power?” “Venerable sir, for us, the teachings have the Blessed One as their root, the Blessed One as their guide…”

“Idhānanda, bhikkhu anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, iddhi.

“Here, Ānanda, a monk experiences the various kinds of spiritual power: having been one, he becomes many… he wields mastery with his body even as far as the Brahmā world. This, Ānanda, is called spiritual power.”

“Katamo cānanda, iddhipādo? Yo, ānanda, maggo yā paṭipadā iddhilābhāya iddhipaṭilābhāya saṃvattati – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, iddhipādo.

“And what, Ānanda, is the basis of spiritual power? It is, Ānanda, the path, the practice that leads to the acquisition of spiritual power, to the re-acquisition of spiritual power. This, Ānanda, is called the basis of spiritual power.”

“Katamā cānanda, iddhipādabhāvanā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, iddhipādabhāvanā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the development of the basis of spiritual power? Here, Ānanda, a monk develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on desire and with striving formations; he develops the basis of spiritual power endowed with concentration founded on energy… with concentration founded on mind… with concentration founded on investigation and with striving formations. This, Ānanda, is called the development of the basis of spiritual power.”

“Katamā cānanda, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccatānanda, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“And what, Ānanda, is the practice leading to the development of the basis of spiritual power? It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view…right concentration. This, Ānanda, is called the practice leading to the development of the basis of spiritual power.” The eighth.

9. Paṭhamabhikkhusuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse to the Monks

841. Atha [V 3.0358][P 5.0287] kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho [M 3.0251] te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “katamā nu kho, bhante, iddhi, katamo iddhipādo, katamā iddhipādabhāvanā, katamā iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī [T 5.0369] paṭipadā”ti?

841. Then a number of monks approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. When they had sat down to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is spiritual power? What is the basis for spiritual power? What is the development of the basis for spiritual power? And what is the practice leading to the development of the basis for spiritual power?”

“Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhi.

“Here, Monks, a monk experiences the various kinds of spiritual power: having been one, he becomes many… he wields mastery with his body even as far as the Brahmā world. This, Monks, is called spiritual power.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, iddhipādo? Yo, bhikkhave, maggo, yā paṭipadā iddhilābhāya iddhipaṭilābhāya saṃvattati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhipādo.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the basis for spiritual power? Whatever path, bhikkhus, whatever practice leads to the attainment and re-attainment of spiritual power—this, bhikkhus, is called the basis for spiritual power.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanā.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the development of the basis for spiritual power? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the basis for spiritual power that is endowed with concentration founded on desire and with the formations of striving. He develops the basis for spiritual power that is endowed with concentration founded on energy… endowed with concentration founded on mind… endowed with concentration founded on investigation and with the formations of striving. This, bhikkhus, is called the development of the basis for spiritual power.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā”ti. Navamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the practice leading to the development of the basis for spiritual power? It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view… right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called the practice leading to the development of the basis for spiritual power.” Ninth.

10. Dutiyabhikkhusuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse to the Bhikkhus

842. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca – “katamā nu kho, bhikkhave, iddhi, katamo iddhipādo, katamā iddhipādabhāvanā, katamā iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā…pe….

842. Then, a number of bhikkhus went to the Blessed One... and sat down to one side. To those bhikkhus seated to one side, the Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, what, now, is psychic power? What is the basis of psychic power? What is the development of the basis of psychic power? And what is the practice leading to the development of the basis of psychic power?” “Venerable Sir, for us, the teachings have the Blessed One as their root, the Blessed One as their guide…”

“Katamā [T 5.0370][V 3.0359] ca, bhikkhave, iddhi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti…pe… yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhi.

“And what, bhikkhus, is psychic power? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu experiences the various kinds of psychic power: having been one, he becomes many… he wields mastery with his body even as far as the Brahmā world. This, bhikkhus, is called psychic power.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, iddhipādo? Yo, bhikkhave, maggo, yā paṭipadā iddhilābhāya iddhipaṭilābhāya saṃvattati – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhipādo.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the basis of psychic power? That path, bhikkhus, that practice which leads to the acquisition of psychic power, to the re-acquisition of psychic power—this, bhikkhus, is called the basis of psychic power.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanā? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ [M 3.0252] iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanā.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the development of the basis of psychic power? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the basis of psychic power possessed of concentration due to desire and formations of striving; he develops the basis of psychic power possessed of concentration due to energy… possessed of concentration due to mind… possessed of concentration due to investigation and formations of striving. This, bhikkhus, is called the development of the basis of psychic power.

“Katamā [P 5.0288] ca, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, iddhipādabhāvanāgāminī paṭipadā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the practice leading to the development of the basis of psychic power? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path; that is: right view… right concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called the practice leading to the development of the basis of psychic power.” Tenth.

11. Moggallānasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse with Moggallāna

843. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā moggallāno bhikkhu evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā…pe… “catunnaṃ kho, bhikkhave, iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā [T 5.0371] moggallāno bhikkhu evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo”.

843. There, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “What do you think, bhikkhus? Due to developing and cultivating which qualities is the bhikkhu Moggallāna of such great psychic power, of such great might?” “Venerable Sir, for us, the teachings have the Blessed One as their root, the Blessed One as their guide…” “Bhikkhus, it is due to developing and cultivating the four bases of psychic power that the bhikkhu Moggallāna is of such great psychic power, of such great might.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, moggallāno bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ‘iti me chando na ca atilīno bhavissati, na ca atippaggahito bhavissati, na ca ajjhattaṃ saṃkhitto bhavissati, na ca bahiddhā vikkhitto bhavissati’. Pacchāpuresaññī ca viharati – ‘yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā tathā pure; yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho; yathā divā tathā rattiṃ, yathā rattiṃ tathā divā’. Iti [V 3.0360] vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ‘iti me vīmaṃsā na ca atilīnā bhavissati, na ca atippaggahitā bhavissati, na ca ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittā bhavissati, na ca bahiddhā vikkhittā bhavissati’…pe… iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā moggallāno bhikkhu evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo.

“Which four? Here, bhikkhus, the bhikkhu Moggallāna develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of desire and the formations of striving, thinking: ‘Thus my desire will be neither too slack nor too tense, neither inwardly constricted nor outwardly scattered.’ He dwells perceiving what is behind and what is in front: ‘As in front, so behind; as behind, so in front. As below, so above; as above, so below. As by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.’ Thus, with an open and unconfined mind, he develops a luminous mind. He develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of energy… concentration of mind… he develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of investigation and the formations of striving, thinking: ‘Thus my investigation will be neither too slack nor too tense, neither inwardly constricted nor outwardly scattered’… Thus, with an open and unconfined mind, he develops a luminous mind. It is, bhikkhus, because of having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power that the bhikkhu Moggallāna is of such great psychic power and might.”

“Imesañca pana, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā moggalāno bhikkhu evaṃ anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti…pe… yāva [M 3.0253] brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti. Imesañca [P 5.0289] pana, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā [T 5.0372] moggallāno bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

“Moreover, bhikkhus, because of having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power, the bhikkhu Moggallāna experiences various kinds of psychic power: being one, he becomes many; being many, he becomes one… he wields bodily mastery even as far as the Brahmā world. And moreover, bhikkhus, because of having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power, the bhikkhu Moggallāna, through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, enters and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, in this very life.” Eleventh.

12. Tathāgatasuttaṃ

12. The Discourse on the Tathāgata

844. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamesaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā tathāgato evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo”ti? Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “catunnaṃ kho, bhikkhave, iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā tathāgato evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo”.

844. At that time, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “What do you think, bhikkhus? By developing and cultivating which dhammas is the Tathāgata of such great psychic power and of such great might?” “Venerable Sir, for us, the dhammas are rooted in the Blessed One… “Bhikkhus, it is by developing and cultivating the four bases of psychic power that the Tathāgata is of such great psychic power and of such great might.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, tathāgato chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ‘iti me chando na ca atilīno bhavissati, na ca atippaggahito bhavissati, na ca ajjhattaṃ saṃkhitto bhavissati, na ca bahiddhā vikkhitto bhavissati’. Pacchāpuresaññī ca viharati – ‘yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā tathā pure; yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho; yathā divā tathā rattiṃ, yathā rattiṃ tathā divā’. Iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti – ‘iti me vīmaṃsā [V 3.0361] na ca atilīnā bhavissati, na ca atipaggahitā bhavissati, na ca ajjhattaṃ saṃkhittā bhavissati, na ca bahiddhā vikkhittā bhavissati’. Pacchāpuresaññī ca viharati – ‘yathā pure tathā pacchā, yathā pacchā tathā pure; yathā adho tathā uddhaṃ, yathā uddhaṃ tathā adho; yathā divā tathā rattiṃ, yathā rattiṃ tathā divā’. Iti vivaṭena cetasā apariyonaddhena sappabhāsaṃ cittaṃ bhāveti. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā tathāgato evaṃmahiddhiko [T 5.0373] evaṃmahānubhāvo.

“Which four? Here, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata develops the basis of psychic power that possesses concentration due to desire and the volitional formations of striving, thinking: ‘Thus my desire will be neither too slack nor too tense, neither inwardly constricted nor outwardly scattered.’ He dwells perceiving what is after and what is before: ‘As before, so after; as after, so before; as below, so above; as above, so below; as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.’ Thus, with an open, unconfined mind, he develops a luminous mind. He develops the basis of psychic power that possesses concentration due to energy… and so on… He develops the basis of psychic power that possesses concentration due to mind… and so on… He develops the basis of psychic power that possesses concentration due to investigation and the volitional formations of striving, thinking: ‘Thus my investigation will be neither too slack nor too tense, neither inwardly constricted nor outwardly scattered.’ He dwells perceiving what is after and what is before: ‘As before, so after; as after, so before; as below, so above; as above, so below; as by day, so by night; as by night, so by day.’ Thus, with an open, unconfined mind, he develops a luminous mind. It is by developing and cultivating these four bases of psychic power, bhikkhus, that the Tathāgata is of such great psychic power and of such great might.”

“Imesañca pana, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā tathāgato anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti – ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti…pe… [P 5.0290] yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti. Imesañca pana, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā tathāgato āsavānaṃ [M 3.0254] khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

“Moreover, bhikkhus, because of having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power, the Tathāgata experiences various kinds of psychic power: being one, he becomes many… he wields bodily mastery as far as the Brahmā world. And moreover, bhikkhus, because of having developed and cultivated these four bases of psychic power, the Tathāgata, through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, enters and dwells in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, in this very life.”

(Chapi abhiññāyo vitthāretabbā).

(The six direct knowledges should also be elaborated.)

Ayoguḷavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on the Iron Ball, the Third.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Maggo ayoguḷo bhikkhu, suddhikañcāpi dve phalā;

Dve cānandā duve bhikkhū, moggallāno tathāgatoti.

The Path, the Iron Ball, the Bhikkhu, Suddhika, and two on the Fruits; two Ānandas, two Bhikkhus, Moggallāna, and the Tathāgata.

4. Gaṅgāpeyyālavaggo

4. The Chapter on the Ganges Repetition Series

1-12. Gaṅgānadīādisuttadvādasakaṃ

1-12. The Twelve Discourses Beginning with the River Ganges

845-856. “Seyyathāpi[T 5.0374], bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā; evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cattāro iddhipāde bhāvento cattāro iddhipāde bahulīkaronto [V 3.0362] nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cattāro iddhipāde bhāvento cattāro iddhipāde bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi…pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti.

“Just as, bhikkhus, the river Ganges slopes, tends, and inclines to the east, so too, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the four bases of psychic power slopes, tends, and inclines to Nibbāna. And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the four bases of psychic power slope, tend, and incline to Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to desire and the volitional formations of striving. He develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to energy... the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to mind... He develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to investigation and the volitional formations of striving.

“Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cattāro iddhipāde [P 5.0291] bhāvento cattāro iddhipāde bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

“Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who develops and cultivates the four bases of psychic power slopes, tends, and inclines to Nibbāna.”

Gaṅgāpeyyālavaggo catuttho.

The Chapter on the Ganges Repetition Series, the Fourth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Cha pācīnato ninnā, cha ninnā ca samuddato;

Dvete cha dvādasa honti, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

Six sloping to the east, and six sloping to the sea; these two sixes make twelve, thus is the chapter called.

Appamādavaggo vitthāretabbo.

The Chapter on Heedfulness should be elaborated.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Tathāgataṃ [M 3.0255] padaṃ kūṭaṃ, mūlaṃ sāro ca vassikaṃ;

Rājā candimasūriyā, vatthena dasamaṃ padanti.

The Tathāgata, the Footprint, the Peak, the Root, the Heartwood, and the Jasmine; the King, the Moon, and the Sun, with Cloth as the tenth item.

Balakaraṇīyavaggo [V 3.0363] vitthāretabbo.

The Chapter on What is to be Done by Strength should be elaborated.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Balaṃ bījañca nāgo ca, rukkho kumbhena sūkiyā;

Ākāsena ca dve meghā, nāvā āgantukā nadīti.

Strength, the Seed, and the Elephant, the Tree, the Pot, and the Winnower; the Sky and the Two Clouds, the Boat, the Newcomer, and the River.

Esanāvaggo vitthāretabbo.

The Chapter on Searches should be elaborated.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Esanā [P 5.0292] vidhā āsavo, bhavo ca dukkhatā tisso;

Khilaṃ malañca nīgho ca, vedanā taṇhā tasinā cāti.

Searches, Modes, Taints, Becoming, and the Three Kinds of Suffering; Barrenness, Stain, Distress, Feeling, Craving, and Thirst.

8. Oghavaggo

8. The Chapter on Floods

1-10. Oghādisuttadasakaṃ

1-10. The Ten Discourses Beginning with Floods

889-898. “Pañcimāni, bhikkhave, uddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Katamāni pañca[V 3.0364]? Rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni kho, bhikkhave, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya cattāro iddhipādā bhāvetabbā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ [T 5.0375] iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhi…pe… cittasamādhi [M 3.0256] …pe… vīmaṃsāsamādhippadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ uddhambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ abhiññāya pariññāya parikkhayāya pahānāya ime cattāro iddhipādā bhāvetabbā”ti.

“Bhikkhus, there are these five higher fetters. Which five? Lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance. These, bhikkhus, are the five higher fetters. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandoning of these five higher fetters, the four bases of psychic power should be developed. Which four? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to desire and the volitional formations of striving. He develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to energy... the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to mind... He develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration due to investigation and the volitional formations of striving. For the direct knowledge, full understanding, utter destruction, and abandoning of these five higher fetters, these four bases of psychic power should be developed.”

(Yathā [P 5.0293] maggasaṃyuttaṃ tathā vitthāretabbaṃ).

(As with the Connected Discourses on the Path, so should it be elaborated.)

Oghavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Chapter on Floods, the Eighth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its Summary:

Ogho yogo upādānaṃ, ganthā anusayena ca;

Kāmaguṇā nīvaraṇā, khandhā oruddhambhāgiyāti.

Floods, Yokes, Clinging, Bonds, and Latent Tendencies; Strands of Sensual Pleasure, Hindrances, Aggregates, and Lower Fetters.

Iddhipādasaṃyuttaṃ sattamaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Bases of Psychic Power, the Seventh.

8. Anuruddhasaṃyuttaṃ

8. The Connected Discourses with Anuruddha

1. Rahogatavaggo

1. The Chapter on Solitude

1. Paṭhamarahogatasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on Solitude

899. Evaṃ [T 5.0376][V 3.0365][M 3.0257][P 5.0294] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā anuruddho sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmato anuruddhassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṃ cetaso parivitakko udapādi – “yesaṃ kesañci cattāro satipaṭṭhānā viraddhā, viraddho tesaṃ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī. Yesaṃ kesañci cattāro satipaṭṭhānā āraddhā, āraddho tesaṃ ariyo maggo sammā dukkhakkhayagāmī”ti.

899. Thus have I heard. At one time, the Venerable Anuruddha was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then, while the Venerable Anuruddha was in seclusion and solitude, this thought arose in his mind: 'For whomever the four establishments of mindfulness are neglected, for them the noble path that rightly leads to the destruction of suffering is neglected. For whomever the four establishments of mindfulness are undertaken, for them the noble path that rightly leads to the destruction of suffering is undertaken.'

Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno āyasmato anuruddhassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – āyasmato anuruddhassa sammukhe pāturahosi. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ etadavoca – “kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso anuruddha, bhikkhuno cattāro satipaṭṭhānā āraddhā hontī”ti?

Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, having known with his own mind the thought in the Venerable Anuruddha's mind, just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm, even so, appeared before the Venerable Anuruddha. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to the Venerable Anuruddha: 'To what extent, friend Anuruddha, are the four establishments of mindfulness undertaken by a bhikkhu?'

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu ajjhattaṃ kāye samudayadhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattaṃ kāye vayadhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattaṃ kāye [T 5.0377] samudayavayadhammānupassī viharati [P 5.0295] ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Bahiddhā kāye samudayadhammānupassī viharati, bahiddhā kāye vayadhammānupassī viharati, bahiddhā kāye samudayavayadhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Ajjhattabahiddhā kāye samudayadhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā kāye vayadhammānupassī viharati, ajjhattabahiddhā [V 3.0366] kāye samudayavayadhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“Here, friend, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the nature of arising in the body internally; he dwells contemplating the nature of passing away in the body internally; he dwells contemplating the nature of arising and passing away in the body internally—ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in the world.
