I am not to be approached by anyone, except for the one who brings my alms-food.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One, and no one approached the Blessed One, except for the one who brought his alms-food.

Atha [M 3.0279] kho te bhikkhū – “bhagavā anekapariyāyena asubhakathaṃ katheti, asubhāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati[V 3.0391], asubhabhāvanāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsatī”ti anekākāravokāraṃ asubhabhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti. Te iminā kāyena aṭṭīyamānā aṭṭiyamānā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) harāyamānā jigucchamānā satthahārakaṃ pariyesanti. Dasapi bhikkhū ekāhena satthaṃ āharanti, vīsampi…pe… tiṃsampi bhikkhū ekāhena satthaṃ āharanti.

Then those monks, thinking, 'The Blessed One speaks in many ways a discourse on foulness, speaks in praise of foulness, and speaks in praise of the development of foulness,' dwelt, having applied themselves in many and various ways to the practice of developing foulness. Being distressed by, ashamed of, and disgusted with this body, they searched for a weapon. Ten monks in a single day took the knife, as did twenty... as did thirty monks in a single day.

Atha [T 5.0406] kho bhagavā tassa aḍḍhamāsassa accayena paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ āmantesi – “kiṃ nu kho, ānanda, tanubhūto viya bhikkhusaṅgho”ti? “Tathā hi pana, bhante, ‘bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ anekapariyāyena asubhakathaṃ katheti, asubhāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati[P 5.0321], asubhabhāvanāya vaṇṇaṃ bhāsatī’ti anekākāravokāraṃ asubhabhāvanānuyogamanuyuttā viharanti. Te iminā kāyena aṭṭīyamānā harāyamānā jigucchamānā satthahārakaṃ pariyesanti. Dasapi bhikkhū ekāhena satthaṃ āharanti, vīsampi bhikkhū… tiṃsampi bhikkhū ekāhena satthaṃ āharanti. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā aññaṃ pariyāyaṃ ācikkhatu yathāyaṃ bhikkhusaṅgho aññāya saṇṭhaheyyā”ti.

Then the Blessed One, having arisen from seclusion after the passing of that half-month, addressed the Venerable Ānanda: 'Why is it, Ānanda, that the Saṅgha of monks seems to be diminished?' 'It is because, Venerable Sir, the Blessed One speaks to the monks in many ways a discourse on foulness, speaks in praise of foulness, and speaks in praise of the development of foulness. They dwell, having applied themselves in many and various ways to the practice of developing foulness. Being distressed by, ashamed of, and disgusted with this body, they search for a weapon. Ten monks in a single day took the knife, as did twenty monks... as did thirty monks in a single day. It would be good, Venerable Sir, if the Blessed One would teach another method, so that this Saṅgha of monks might be established in final knowledge.'

“Tenahānanda, yāvatikā bhikkhū vesāliṃ upanissāya viharanti te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātehī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paṭissutvā yāvatikā bhikkhū vesāliṃ upanissāya viharanti te sabbe upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannipātetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sannipatito sannipātito (sī.), bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho. Yassa dāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī”ti.

'Well then, Ānanda, assemble in the assembly hall all the monks who are dwelling in dependence on Vesālī.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable Ānanda replied in assent to the Blessed One. Having assembled in the assembly hall all the monks who were dwelling in dependence on Vesālī, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, the Saṅgha of monks is assembled. Now, Blessed One, is the time for that which you deem fit.'

Atha kho bhagavā yena upaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [T 5.0407] paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “ayampi kho, bhikkhave, ānāpānassatisamādhi bhāvito bahulīkato santo ceva paṇīto ca asecanako ca sukho ca vihāro uppannuppanne ca pāpake akusale dhamme ṭhānaso antaradhāpeti vūpasameti”.

Then the Blessed One approached the assembly hall. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the monks: 'Monks, this concentration due to mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, is peaceful and sublime, unadulterated, and a pleasant abiding; and it instantly causes evil, unwholesome states that have arisen to disappear and be pacified.'

“Seyyathāpi[M 3.0280], bhikkhave, gimhānaṃ pacchime māse ūhataṃ rajojallaṃ, tamenaṃ mahāakālamegho ṭhānaso antaradhāpeti vūpasameti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ānāpānassatisamādhi bhāvito bahulīkato santo ceva paṇīto ca [P 5.0322] asecanako ca sukho ca [V 3.0392] vihāro uppannuppanne ca pāpake akusale dhamme ṭhānaso antaradhāpeti vūpasameti. Kathaṃ bhāvito ca, bhikkhave, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṃ bahulīkato santo ceva paṇīto ca asecanako ca sukho ca vihāro uppannuppanne ca pāpake akusale dhamme ṭhānaso antaradhāpeti vūpasameti?

Just as, monks, in the last month of the hot season, stirred-up dust and dirt is instantly made to disappear and is pacified by a great, unseasonal rain cloud; in the very same way, monks, concentration due to mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, is peaceful and sublime, unadulterated, and a pleasant abiding; and it instantly causes evil, unwholesome states that have arisen to disappear and be pacified. And how, monks, is concentration due to mindfulness of breathing developed, how is it cultivated, so that it is peaceful and sublime, unadulterated, and a pleasant abiding, and instantly causes evil, unwholesome states that have arisen to disappear and be pacified?

“Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So satova assasati, satova passasati…pe… ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. Evaṃ bhāvito kho, bhikkhave, ānāpānassatisamādhi evaṃ bahulīkato santo ceva paṇīto ca asecanako ca [T 5.0408] sukho ca vihāro uppannuppanne ca pāpake akusale dhamme ṭhānaso antaradhāpeti vūpasametī”ti. Navamaṃ.

Here, monks, a monk—having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling—sits down, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him. Mindful he breathes out, mindful he breathes in... He trains thus: 'Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe out.' He trains thus: 'Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe in.' Monks, when concentration due to mindfulness of breathing is developed and cultivated in this way, it is peaceful and sublime, unadulterated, and a pleasant abiding; and it instantly causes evil, unwholesome states that have arisen to disappear and be pacified.” The ninth.

10. Kimilasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse to Kimila

986. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kimilāyaṃ kimbilāyaṃ (sī. pī.) viharati veḷuvane. Tatra kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ kimilaṃ āmantesi – “kathaṃ bhāvito nu kho, kimila, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṃ bahulīkato mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso”ti?

986. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Kimilā, in the Bamboo Grove. There the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Kimila: “Kimila, how is concentration due to mindfulness of breathing developed, how is it cultivated, so that it is of great fruit and great benefit?”

Evaṃ vutte āyasmā kimilo tuṇhī ahosi. Dutiyampi kho bhagavā…pe… tatiyampi kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ kimilaṃ āmantesi – “kathaṃ bhāvito nu kho, kimila, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṃ bahulīkato mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso”ti? Tatiyampi kho āyasmā kimilo tuṇhī ahosi.

When this was said, the Venerable Kimila remained silent. For a second time, the Blessed One… For a third time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Kimila: “Kimila, how is concentration due to mindfulness of breathing developed, how is it cultivated, so that it is of great fruit and great benefit?” For a third time, the Venerable Kimila remained silent.

Evaṃ [P 5.0323] vutte āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “etassa, bhagavā, kālo; etassa, sugata, kālo! Yaṃ bhagavā ānāpānassatisamādhiṃ bhāseyya[M 3.0281]. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.

When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, this is the time! Sugata, this is the time for the Blessed One to speak on concentration due to mindfulness of breathing. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the monks will bear it in mind.”

“Tenahānanda, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho [V 3.0393] āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca – “kathaṃ bhāvito ca, ānanda, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṃ bahulīkato mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso? Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So satova assasati, satova passasati…pe… ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī [T 5.0409] passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. Evaṃ bhāvito kho, ānanda, ānāpānassatisamādhi evaṃ bahulīkato mahapphalo hoti mahānisaṃso”.

“Then, Ānanda, listen and attend carefully; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this: “And how, Ānanda, is concentration due to mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so that it is of great fruit and great benefit? Here, Ānanda, a monk, having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, sits down, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him. Mindful he breathes out, mindful he breathes in… He trains himself: ‘Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe out.’ He trains himself: ‘Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe in.’ Indeed, Ānanda, it is when concentration due to mindfulness of breathing is developed in this way and cultivated in this way that it is of great fruit and great benefit.”

“Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṃ vā passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; ‘sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – kāye kāyānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Kāyaññatarāhaṃ, ānanda, etaṃ vadāmi yadidaṃ – assāsapassāsaṃ. Tasmātihānanda, kāye kāyānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“Ānanda, at a time when a bhikkhu, breathing out long, knows, ‘I am breathing out long,’ or breathing in long, knows, ‘I am breathing in long’; breathing out short, knows, ‘I am breathing out short,’ or breathing in short, knows, ‘I am breathing in short’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the entire body’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing the entire body’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe out, calming the bodily formation’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in, calming the bodily formation’—Ānanda, at that time, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. For what reason? I say, Ānanda, that this—that is, the in-breath and the out-breath—is a certain body among the bodies. Therefore, Ānanda, at that time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.”

“Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu ‘pītippaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘pītippaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘sukhappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘sukhappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī [P 5.0324] assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; ‘passambhayaṃ [T 5.0410] cittasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – vedanāsu vedanānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno [M 3.0282] satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Vedanāññatarāhaṃ, ānanda, etaṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – assāsapassāsānaṃ assāsapassāsaṃ (pī. ka.) ma. ni. 3.145 sādhukaṃ manasikāraṃ. Tasmātihānanda, vedanāsu vedanānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“Ānanda, at a time when a bhikkhu trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing rapture’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing rapture’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing pleasure’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing pleasure’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the mental formation’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing the mental formation’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe out, calming the mental formation’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in, calming the mental formation’—Ānanda, at that time, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. For what reason? I say, Ānanda, that this—that is, the careful attention to the in-breaths and out-breaths—is a certain feeling among the feelings. Therefore, Ānanda, at that time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.”

“Yasmiṃ [V 3.0394] samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu ‘cittappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘cittappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ…pe… samādahaṃ cittaṃ…pe… ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – citte cittānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Nāhaṃ, ānanda, muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa ānāpānassatisamādhibhāvanaṃ vadāmi. Tasmātihānanda, citte cittānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“Ānanda, at a time when a bhikkhu trains thus: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in experiencing the mind’; …gladdening the mind… …concentrating the mind… he trains thus: ‘I will breathe out liberating the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in liberating the mind’—Ānanda, at that time, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. For what reason? I do not say, Ānanda, that there is the development of concentration through mindfulness of breathing for one who is unmindful and not clearly comprehending. Therefore, Ānanda, at that time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.”

“Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu ‘aniccānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati…pe… virāgānupassī…pe… nirodhānupassī…pe… ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – dhammesu [T 5.0411] dhammānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. So yaṃ taṃ hoti abhijjhādomanassānaṃ pahānaṃ taṃ paññāya disvā sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti. Tasmātihānanda, dhammesu dhammānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“Ānanda, at a time when a bhikkhu trains thus: ‘I will breathe out contemplating impermanence’… contemplating dispassion… contemplating cessation… he trains thus: ‘I will breathe out contemplating relinquishment’; he trains thus: ‘I will breathe in contemplating relinquishment’—Ānanda, at that time, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. He, having seen with wisdom the abandonment of that covetousness and displeasure, becomes one who regards it well with equanimity. Therefore, Ānanda, at that time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.”

“Seyyathāpi[P 5.0325], ānanda, catumahāpathe cātummahāpathe (sī. syā. kaṃ.) mahāpaṃsupuñjo. Puratthimāya cepi disāyaṃ āgaccheyya sakaṭaṃ vā ratho vā, upahanateva taṃ paṃsupuñjaṃ; pacchimāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya…pe… uttarāya cepi disāya…pe… dakkhiṇāya cepi disāya āgaccheyya sakaṭaṃ vā ratho vā, upahanateva taṃ paṃsupuñjaṃ. Evameva kho, ānanda, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharantopi upahanateva [M 3.0283] pāpake akusale dhamme; vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharantopi upahanateva pāpake akusale dhamme”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Just as, Ānanda, there might be a great pile of dust at a major crossroads. If a cart or a chariot should come from the eastern direction, it would surely strike that pile of dust; if it should come from the western direction… from the northern direction… if a cart or a chariot should come from the southern direction, it would surely strike that pile of dust. In the very same way, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, while dwelling contemplating the body in the body, surely strikes down evil, unwholesome states; while dwelling contemplating feelings… mind… while dwelling contemplating phenomena in phenomena, he surely strikes down evil, unwholesome states.” Tenth.

Ekadhammavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on a Single Thing.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Ekadhammo [V 3.0395] ca bojjhaṅgo, suddhikañca duve phalā;

Ariṭṭho kappino dīpo, vesālī kimilena cāti.

A Single Thing and the Factors of Enlightenment, the Pure and the two Fruits; Ariṭṭha, Kappina, Dīpa, Vesālī, and Kimila.

2. Dutiyavaggo

2. The Second Chapter

1. Icchānaṅgalasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse at Icchānaṅgala

987. Ekaṃ [T 5.0412] samayaṃ bhagavā icchānaṅgale viharati icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍe. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “icchāmahaṃ, bhikkhave, temāsaṃ paṭisallīyituṃ. Nāmhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakenā”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā nāssudha koci bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamati, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakena.

987. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Icchānaṅgala in the Icchānaṅgala forest grove. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, I wish to go into seclusion for three months. I am not to be approached by anyone, except for the one who brings my alms-food.” “Very well, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One, and then no one approached the Blessed One, except for the one who brought his alms-food.

Atha [P 5.0326] kho bhagavā tassa temāsassa accayena paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito bhikkhū āmantesi – “sace kho, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘katamenāvuso, vihārena samaṇo gotamo vassāvāsaṃ bahulaṃ vihāsī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘ānāpānassatisamādhinā kho, āvuso, bhagavā vassāvāsaṃ bahulaṃ vihāsī’ti. Idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sato assasāmi, sato passasāmi. Dīghaṃ assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāmi, dīghaṃ passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāmi; rassaṃ assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāmi, rassaṃ passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāmi; ‘sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti pajānāmi…pe… ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti pajānāmi, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti [T 5.0413] pajānāmi”.

Then the Blessed One, having emerged from seclusion after those three months, addressed the monks: ‘Monks, if wanderers of other sects were to ask you, “Friends, with what abiding did the ascetic Gotama mostly dwell for the rains-residence?”—being asked thus, monks, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: “Friends, the Blessed One mostly dwelt for the rains-residence with concentration due to mindfulness of breathing.” Here, monks, being mindful, I breathe out; being mindful, I breathe in. Breathing out long, I understand, ‘I breathe out long’; breathing in long, I understand, ‘I breathe in long.’ Breathing out short, I understand, ‘I breathe out short’; breathing in short, I understand, ‘I breathe in short.’ I understand, ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body’… I understand, ‘I shall breathe out contemplating relinquishment’; I understand, ‘I shall breathe in contemplating relinquishment.’”

“Yañhi [M 3.0284] taṃ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘ariyavihāro’ itipi, ‘brahmavihāro’ [V 3.0396] itipi, ‘tathāgatavihāro’ itipi. Ānāpānassatisamādhiṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘ariyavihāro’ itipi, ‘brahmavihāro’ itipi, ‘tathāgatavihāro’ itipi. Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sekhā appattamānasā anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ patthayamānā viharanti tesaṃ ānāpānassatisamādhi bhāvito bahulīkato āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattati. Ye ca kho te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā tesaṃ ānāpānassatisamādhi bhāvito bahulīkato diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāya ceva saṃvattati satisampajaññāya ca.

“Monks, if one, speaking rightly, were to speak of a ‘noble abiding,’ a ‘sublime abiding,’ or a ‘Tathāgata’s abiding,’ it is of concentration due to mindfulness of breathing that one would rightly speak, calling it a ‘noble abiding,’ a ‘sublime abiding,’ or a ‘Tathāgata’s abiding.’ For those monks who are trainees, who have not attained their goal, aspiring to the unsurpassed security from bondage, concentration due to mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, leads to the destruction of the taints. And for those monks who are Arahants—whose taints are destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own welfare, whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed, and who are completely liberated through right knowledge—concentration due to mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, leads both to a pleasant abiding in this very life and to mindfulness and clear comprehension.”

“Yañhi taṃ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘ariyavihāro’ itipi, ‘brahmavihāro’ itipi, ‘tathāgatavihāro’ itipi. Ānāpānassatisamādhiṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘ariyavihāro’ itipi, ‘brahmavihāro’ itipi, ‘tathāgatavihāro’ itipī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Monks, if one, speaking rightly, were to speak of a ‘noble abiding,’ a ‘sublime abiding,’ or a ‘Tathāgata’s abiding,’ it is of concentration due to mindfulness of breathing that one would rightly speak, calling it a ‘noble abiding,’ a ‘sublime abiding,’ or a ‘Tathāgata’s abiding.’ First.”

2. Kaṅkheyyasuttaṃ

2. 2. The Kaṅkheyya Sutta

988. Ekaṃ [P 5.0327] samayaṃ āyasmā lomasakaṃbhiyo lomasavaṅgiso (sī. pī.) sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yenāyasmā lomasakaṃbhiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ lomasakaṃbhiyaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko āyasmantaṃ lomasakaṃbhiyaṃ etadavoca – “so eva nu kho, bhante, sekho [T 5.0414] vihāro so tathāgatavihāro, udāhu aññova añño (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) sekho vihāro añño tathāgatavihāro”ti?

988. At one time the Venerable Lomasakaṃbhiya was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Park. Then Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the Venerable Lomasakaṃbhiya, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said to the Venerable Lomasakaṃbhiya: “Venerable Sir, is the abiding of a trainee the very same as the abiding of the Tathāgata, or is the abiding of a trainee one thing and the abiding of the Tathāgata another?”

“Na kho, āvuso mahānāma, sveva sekho vihāro, so tathāgatavihāro. Añño kho, āvuso mahānāma, sekho vihāro, añño tathāgatavihāro. Ye te, āvuso mahānāma, bhikkhū sekhā appattamānasā anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ patthayamānā viharanti, te pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya viharanti. Katame pañca? Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ pahāya viharanti, byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ…pe… thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ…pe… uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ…pe… vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ pahāya viharanti.

“Indeed not, friend Mahānāma, the abiding of a trainee is not the very same as the abiding of the Tathāgata. The abiding of a trainee, friend Mahānāma, is one thing, and the abiding of the Tathāgata is another. Those monks, friend Mahānāma, who are trainees, who have not yet attained their goal, aspiring to the unsurpassed security from bondage, dwell having abandoned the five hindrances. What five? They dwell having abandoned the hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, and the hindrance of doubt.”

“Yepi [M 3.0285][V 3.0397] te, āvuso mahānāma, bhikkhū sekhā appattamānasā anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ patthayamānā viharanti, te ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya viharanti.

“Friend Mahānāma, those monks who are trainees, who have not yet attained their goal, aspiring to the unsurpassed security from bondage, dwell having abandoned these five hindrances.”

“Ye ca kho te, āvuso mahānāma, bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā, tesaṃ pañca nīvaraṇā pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā anabhāvakatā (sī. pī.) āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Katame pañca? Kāmacchandanīvaraṇaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ anuppādadhammaṃ; byāpādanīvaraṇaṃ pahīnaṃ…pe… thinamiddhanīvaraṇaṃ…pe… uddhaccakukkuccanīvaraṇaṃ…pe… vicikicchānīvaraṇaṃ pahīnaṃ ucchinnamūlaṃ tālāvatthukataṃ anabhāvaṃkataṃ āyatiṃ [P 5.0328] anuppādadhammaṃ.

“And, friend Mahānāma, for those monks who are Arahants—whose taints are destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own welfare, whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed, and who are completely liberated through right knowledge—for them, the five hindrances are abandoned, their roots cut off, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to a state of non-arising, and are of the nature not to arise in the future. What five? The hindrance of sensual desire is abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to a state of non-arising, and is of the nature not to arise in the future; the hindrance of ill will is abandoned... the hindrance of sloth and torpor... the hindrance of restlessness and remorse... the hindrance of doubt is abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to a state of non-arising, and is of the nature not to arise in the future.”

“Ye te, āvuso mahānāma, bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto [T 5.0415] katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā, tesaṃ ime pañca nīvaraṇā pahīnā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṃkatā āyatiṃ anuppādadhammā. Tadamināpetaṃ, āvuso mahānāma, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ yathā – aññova sekho vihāro, añño tathāgatavihāro.

“Friend Mahānāma, for those monks who are Arahants—whose taints are destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own welfare, whose fetters of existence are utterly destroyed, and who are completely liberated through right knowledge—for them, these five hindrances are abandoned, their roots cut off, made like a palm-tree stump, brought to a state of non-arising, and are of the nature not to arise in the future. By this method, friend Mahānāma, it should be understood how the abiding of a trainee is one thing, and the abiding of the Tathāgata is another.”

“Ekamidaṃ, āvuso mahānāma, samayaṃ bhagavā icchānaṅgale viharati icchānaṅgalavanasaṇḍe. Tatra kho, āvuso mahānāma, bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘icchāmahaṃ, bhikkhave, temāsaṃ paṭisallīyituṃ. Nāmhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakenā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante’ti kho, āvuso mahānāma, te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā nāssudha koci bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamati, aññatra ekena piṇḍapātanīhārakena.

“At one time, friend Mahānāma, the Blessed One was dwelling at Icchānaṅgala in the Icchānaṅgala forest grove. There, friend Mahānāma, the Blessed One addressed the monks: ‘Monks, I wish to enter into seclusion for three months. I am not to be approached by anyone, except for the one who brings the alms-food.’ ‘So be it, Venerable Sir.’ And so, friend Mahānāma, those monks assented to the Blessed One, and no one at all approached the Blessed One, except for the one who brings the alms-food.”

“Atha kho, āvuso, bhagavā tassa temāsassa accayena paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘sace kho, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – katamenāvuso, vihārena samaṇo gotamo vassāvāsaṃ bahulaṃ vihāsīti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ [M 3.0286] aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ānāpānassatisamādhinā kho, āvuso, bhagavā vassāvāsaṃ bahulaṃ vihāsīti. Idhāhaṃ, bhikkhave[V 3.0398], sato assasāmi, sato passasāmi. Dīghaṃ assasanto dīghaṃ assasāmīti pajānāmi, dīghaṃ passasanto dīghaṃ passasāmīti pajānāmi…pe… paṭinissaggānupassī [T 5.0416] assasissāmīti pajānāmi, paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti pajānāmi”.

Then, indeed, the Blessed One, at the end of those three months, having emerged from seclusion, addressed the monks: 'Monks, if indeed wanderers of other sects should ask you thus: “Friends, by what abiding did the recluse Gotama mostly dwell during the rains-retreat?”—being asked thus, monks, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: “Friends, the Blessed One indeed mostly dwelt during the rains-retreat with the concentration of mindfulness of in-and-out breathing.” Here, monks, I, being mindful, breathe out; being mindful, I breathe in. Breathing out long, I know, “I am breathing out long”; breathing in long, I know, “I am breathing in long.” … I know, “Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe out”; I know, “Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe in.”'

“Yañhi taṃ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ariyavihāro itipi, brahmavihāro itipi, tathāgatavihāro itipi. Ānāpānassatisamādhiṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ariyavihāro itipi, brahmavihāro itipi, tathāgatavihāro itipi.

Monks, if one were to rightly speak of 'a noble abiding,' 'a sublime abiding,' or 'a Tathāgata's abiding,' it is the concentration of mindfulness of in-and-out breathing that one would rightly call 'a noble abiding,' 'a sublime abiding,' or 'a Tathāgata's abiding'.

“Ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sekhā appattamānasā anuttaraṃ yogakkhemaṃ patthayamānā viharanti, tesaṃ ānāpānassatisamādhi bhāvito bahulīkato āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattati.

Monks, for those monks who are trainees, who have not attained the goal, aspiring to the unsurpassed security from bondage, the concentration of mindfulness of in-and-out breathing, when developed and cultivated, leads to the destruction of the taints.

“Ye ca kho te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū arahanto khīṇāsavā vusitavanto katakaraṇīyā ohitabhārā anuppattasadatthā parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā, tesaṃ ānāpānassatisamādhi bhāvito bahulīkato diṭṭheva dhamme sukhavihārāya ceva saṃvattati satisampajaññāya ca.

But, monks, for those monks who are arahants, whose taints are destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own welfare, utterly destroyed the fetters of being, and are liberated through perfect knowledge, the concentration of mindfulness of in-and-out breathing, when developed and cultivated, conduces to a pleasant abiding in this very life, and to mindfulness and clear comprehension.

“Yañhi taṃ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ariyavihāro itipi, brahmavihāro itipi, tathāgatavihāro itipi. Ānāpānassatisamādhiṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ariyavihāro itipi, brahmavihāro itipi, tathāgatavihāro itipī”ti. “Iminā kho etaṃ, āvuso mahānāma, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ, yathā – aññova sekho vihāro, añño tathāgatavihāro”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Monks, if one were to rightly speak of 'a noble abiding,' 'a sublime abiding,' or 'a Tathāgata's abiding,' it is the concentration of mindfulness of in-and-out breathing that one would rightly call 'a noble abiding,' 'a sublime abiding,' or 'a Tathāgata's abiding.' By this method, friend Mahānāma, it should be understood that the abiding of a trainee is one thing, and the abiding of a Tathāgata is another.” Second.

3. Paṭhamaānandasuttaṃ

3. The First Sutta on Ānanda

989. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[T 5.0417]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “atthi [P 5.0329] nu kho, bhante[M 3.0287], ekadhammo eko dhammo (sī.) bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro [V 3.0399] dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrentī”ti?

989. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting there, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, is there one quality which, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four qualities; four qualities which, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven qualities; and seven qualities which, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two qualities?”

“Atthi kho, ānanda, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrentī”ti.

“There is, Ānanda, one quality that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four qualities. Four qualities, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven qualities. Seven qualities, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two qualities.”

“Katamo pana, bhante, ekadhammo eko dhammo (sī.) bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrentī”ti? “Ānāpānassatisamādhi kho, ānanda, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti”.

“But what, venerable sir, is that one quality which, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four qualities? What are the four qualities which, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven qualities? And what are the seven qualities which, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two qualities?” “The concentration of mindfulness of in-and-out breathing, Ānanda, is the one quality which, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the four establishments of mindfulness. The four establishments of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment. The seven factors of enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, fulfill knowledge and liberation.”

“Kathaṃ bhāvito, ānanda, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṃ bahulīkato cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti? Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So satova assasati, satova passasati. Dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti [T 5.0418] pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti…pe… ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati”. “Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti; rassaṃ vā…pe… ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – kāye kāyānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Kāyaññatarāhaṃ, ānanda, etaṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – assāsapassāsaṃ[P 5.0330]. Tasmātihānanda, kāye kāyānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ”.

“How, Ānanda, is the concentration of mindfulness of in-and-out breathing developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the four establishments of mindfulness? Here, Ānanda, a monk, gone to the forest or to the root of a tree or to an empty dwelling, sits down cross-legged, keeps his body erect, and establishes mindfulness before him. Mindful, he breathes out; mindful, he breathes in. Breathing out long, he knows, ‘I am breathing out long’; or breathing in long, he knows, ‘I am breathing in long’… He trains, ‘I will breathe out contemplating relinquishment’; he trains, ‘I will breathe in contemplating relinquishment.’ “Ānanda, at the time when a monk, breathing out long, knows, ‘I am breathing out long,’ or breathing in long, knows, ‘I am breathing in long’; or breathing out short… he trains, ‘I will breathe out calming the bodily formation’; he trains, ‘I will breathe in calming the bodily formation’—at that time, Ānanda, the monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. For what reason? Ānanda, I say that this—that is, the in-breath and the out-breath—is a certain body among the bodies. Therefore, at that time, Ānanda, the monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.”

“Yasmiṃ [M 3.0288] samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu ‘pītippaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati [V 3.0400] …pe… sukhappaṭisaṃvedī…pe… cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī…pe… ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – vedanāsu vedanānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Vedanāññatarāhaṃ, ānanda, etaṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – assāsapassāsānaṃ sādhukaṃ manasikāraṃ. Tasmātihānanda, vedanāsu vedanānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno [T 5.0419] satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“Ānanda, at a time when a bhikkhu trains, thinking: ‘I will breathe out experiencing rapture,’ … ‘I will breathe out experiencing pleasure,’ … ‘I will breathe out experiencing the mental formation,’ … ‘I will breathe out calming the mental formation,’ and ‘I will breathe in calming the mental formation’—at that time, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. For what reason? For I say, Ānanda, that this is a certain kind of feeling, that is, the proper attention to in-breaths and out-breaths. Therefore, Ānanda, at that time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.”

“Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu ‘cittappaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘cittappaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati; abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ…pe… samādahaṃ cittaṃ…pe… ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – citte cittānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Nāhaṃ, ānanda, muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa ānāpānassatisamādhibhāvanaṃ vadāmi. Tasmātihānanda, citte cittānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“Ānanda, at a time when a bhikkhu trains, thinking: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the mind,’ and ‘I will breathe in experiencing the mind’; … ‘I will breathe out gladdening the mind,’ … ‘I will breathe out concentrating the mind,’ … ‘I will breathe out liberating the mind,’ and ‘I will breathe in liberating the mind’—at that time, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. For what reason? I do not say, Ānanda, that the development of concentration through mindfulness of breathing is for one who is unmindful and lacks clear comprehension. Therefore, Ānanda, at that time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.”

“Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu aniccānupassī…pe… virāgānupassī…pe… nirodhānupassī…pe… ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – dhammesu dhammānupassī, ānanda, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. So yaṃ taṃ hoti abhijjhādomanassānaṃ pahānaṃ taṃ paññāya disvā sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā [P 5.0331] hoti. Tasmātihānanda, dhammesu dhammānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“Ānanda, at a time when a bhikkhu trains, thinking: ‘I will breathe out contemplating impermanence,’ … ‘I will breathe out contemplating dispassion,’ … ‘I will breathe out contemplating cessation,’ … ‘I will breathe out contemplating relinquishment,’ and ‘I will breathe in contemplating relinquishment’—at that time, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. Having seen with wisdom that abandoning of covetousness and displeasure, he regards it well with equanimity. Therefore, Ānanda, at that time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.”

“Evaṃ bhāvito kho, ānanda, ānāpānassatisamādhi evaṃ bahulīkato cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti.

“Thus developed, Ānanda, and thus frequently practiced, concentration through mindfulness of breathing fulfills the four establishments of mindfulness.”

“Kathaṃ [T 5.0420][V 3.0401] bhāvitā cānanda, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā kathaṃ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti? Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī [M 3.0289] viharati – upaṭṭhitāssa upaṭṭhitassati (pī. ka.) tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno tasmiṃ samaye ānanda bhikkhuno (pī. ka.), tasmiṃ samaye (ma. ni. 3.149) sati hoti asammuṭṭhā. Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhuno upaṭṭhitā sati hoti asammuṭṭhā – satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, satisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

“And how, Ānanda, when developed and frequently practiced, do the four establishments of mindfulness fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment? Ānanda, at a time when a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, then mindfulness is established in that bhikkhu, unforgotten. Ānanda, at a time when mindfulness is established in the bhikkhu, unforgotten, then the mindfulness enlightenment factor is aroused in that bhikkhu; at that time the bhikkhu develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor, and at that time the mindfulness enlightenment factor in that bhikkhu reaches the culmination of its development.”

“So tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati. Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati – dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

“Dwelling thus mindful, he investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, examines it, and arrives at a thorough inquiry. Ānanda, at a time when a bhikkhu, dwelling thus mindful, investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, examines it, and arrives at a thorough inquiry—the investigation-of-dhammas enlightenment factor is aroused in him at that time. At that time, the bhikkhu develops the investigation-of-dhammas enlightenment factor, and at that time, the investigation-of-dhammas enlightenment factor in him reaches the culmination of its development.”

“Tassa taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato pavicarato parivīmaṃsamāpajjato āraddhaṃ hoti vīriyaṃ asallīnaṃ. Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhuno taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato pavicarato parivīmaṃsamāpajjato āraddhaṃ [P 5.0332] hoti vīriyaṃ asallīnaṃ – vīriyasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye [T 5.0421] bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

“For one who investigates that Dhamma with wisdom, examines it, and arrives at a thorough inquiry, energy is aroused and unwavering. Ānanda, at a time when the energy of a bhikkhu who is investigating that Dhamma with wisdom, examining it, and arriving at a thorough inquiry is aroused and unwavering—at that time, the energy enlightenment factor is aroused in that bhikkhu. At that time, the bhikkhu develops the energy enlightenment factor, and at that time, the energy enlightenment factor in that bhikkhu reaches the culmination of its development.”

“Āraddhavīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā. Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhuno āraddhavīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā – pītisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, pītisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

“For one with aroused energy, unworldly rapture arises. Ānanda, at a time when unworldly rapture arises in a bhikkhu with aroused energy—at that time, the rapture enlightenment factor is aroused in that bhikkhu. At that time, the bhikkhu develops the rapture enlightenment factor, and at that time, the rapture enlightenment factor in that bhikkhu reaches the culmination of its development.”

“Pītimanassa kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati. Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhuno pītimanassa kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati – passaddhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

“For one with a rapturous mind, the body becomes tranquil and the mind becomes tranquil. Ānanda, at a time when the body and mind of a bhikkhu with a rapturous mind become tranquil—at that time, the tranquility enlightenment factor is aroused in that bhikkhu. At that time, the bhikkhu develops the tranquility enlightenment factor, and at that time, the tranquility enlightenment factor in that bhikkhu reaches the culmination of its development.”

“Passaddhakāyassa [V 3.0402][M 3.0290] sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati. Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhuno passaddhakāyassa sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati – samādhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, samādhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

“For one whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. Ānanda, at a time when the mind of a happy bhikkhu whose body is tranquil becomes concentrated—at that time, the concentration enlightenment factor is aroused in that bhikkhu. At that time, the bhikkhu develops the concentration enlightenment factor, and at that time, the concentration enlightenment factor in that bhikkhu reaches the culmination of its development.”

“So tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti. Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti – upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti[T 5.0422], upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

He well regards with equanimity the mind that is thus concentrated. When, Ānanda, a bhikkhu well regards with equanimity the mind that is thus concentrated—at that time the enlightenment factor of equanimity is aroused for the bhikkhu. At that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, and at that time for that bhikkhu, the enlightenment factor of equanimity reaches the culmination of its development.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati – upaṭṭhitāssa tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno sati hoti asammuṭṭhā. Yasmiṃ [P 5.0333] samaye, ānanda, bhikkhuno upaṭṭhitā sati hoti asammuṭṭhā – satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, satisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. (Yathā paṭhamaṃ satipaṭṭhānaṃ, evaṃ vitthāretabbaṃ).

When, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in mind... dhammas in dhammas—at that time the bhikkhu's mindfulness is established and unmuddled. When, Ānanda, the bhikkhu's mindfulness is established and unmuddled—at that time the enlightenment factor of mindfulness is aroused for the bhikkhu. At that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, and at that time for that bhikkhu, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness reaches the culmination of its development. (This should be elaborated in the same way as the first foundation of mindfulness.)

“So tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti. Yasmiṃ samaye, ānanda, bhikkhu tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti – upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, ānanda, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā evaṃ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti.

He well regards with equanimity the mind that is thus concentrated. When, Ānanda, a bhikkhu well regards with equanimity the mind that is thus concentrated—at that time the enlightenment factor of equanimity is aroused for the bhikkhu. At that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, and at that time for that bhikkhu, the enlightenment factor of equanimity reaches the culmination of its development. Indeed, Ānanda, when the four foundations of mindfulness are thus developed and thus frequently practiced, they bring the seven factors for enlightenment to fulfillment.

“Kathaṃ bhāvitā, ānanda, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti? Idhānanda, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti [M 3.0291] …pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ [T 5.0423] virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, ānanda, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

How, Ānanda, are the seven factors of enlightenment developed and cultivated so as to fulfill knowledge and liberation? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. He develops the enlightenment factor of the investigation of phenomena… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, culminating in relinquishment. Indeed, Ānanda, when the seven factors of enlightenment are developed and cultivated in this way, they fulfill knowledge and liberation.” The third.

4. Dutiyaānandasuttaṃ

4. The Second Discourse to Ānanda

990. Atha [V 3.0403] kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “atthi nu kho, ānanda, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā, satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrentī”ti. Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… “atthānanda, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme [P 5.0334] paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrenti.

990. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to the Venerable Ānanda: “Is there, Ānanda, one principle that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four principles; four principles that, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven principles; seven principles that, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two principles?” “Venerable sir, for us the teachings have the Blessed One as their root…” “There is, Ānanda, one principle that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four principles; four principles that, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven principles; seven principles that, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two principles.”

“Katamo cānanda, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrenti? Ānāpānassatisamādhi, ānanda, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī”ti. “Kathaṃ [T 5.0424] bhāvito cānanda, ānāpānassatisamādhi, kathaṃ bahulīkato cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti? Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā…pe… evaṃ bhāvitā kho, ānanda, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“And what, Ānanda, is the one thing that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four things; which four things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven things; and which seven things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two things? Concentration due to mindfulness of breathing, Ānanda, is the one thing that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the four establishments of mindfulness. The four establishments of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the seven factors for enlightenment. The seven factors for enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, fulfill knowledge and liberation. And how, Ānanda, is concentration due to mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so as to fulfill the four establishments of mindfulness? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest… and so on… Thus indeed, Ānanda, the seven factors for enlightenment, when developed and cultivated in this way, fulfill knowledge and liberation.” The fourth.

5. Paṭhamabhikkhusuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse to the Bhikkhus

991. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “atthi nu kho, bhante, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā [M 3.0292] bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrentī”ti? “Atthi kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme [P 5.0335] paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrentī”ti.

991. Then many bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, is there indeed one thing that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four things; which four things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven things; and which seven things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two things?” “There is indeed, bhikkhus, one thing that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four things; which four things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven things; and which seven things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two things.”

“Katamo [V 3.0404] pana, bhante, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrentī”ti? “Ānāpānassatisamādhi kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī”ti.

“Venerable sir, what is the one thing that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four things; which four things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven things; and which seven things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two things?” “Concentration through mindfulness of breathing, bhikkhus, is the one thing that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness. The four foundations of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment. The seven factors of enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, fulfill knowledge and liberation.”

“Kathaṃ bhāvito ca, bhikkhave, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṃ bahulīkato cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araññagato vā…pe… evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Monks, how is concentration through mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so that it fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness? Here, monks, a monk gone to the wilderness… and so on… Thus developed and cultivated, monks, the seven factors of enlightenment fulfill knowledge and liberation.” Fifth.

6. Dutiyabhikkhusuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse Concerning a Bhikkhu

992. Atha [T 5.0425] kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū bhagavā etadavoca – “atthi nu kho, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrentī”ti? “Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā…pe… bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti. “Atthi, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrenti”.

992. Then a number of bhikkhus approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. When they were seated, the Blessed One said to them: “Bhikkhus, is there one thing that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four things; four things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven things; and seven things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two things?” “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One… and so on… The bhikkhus will remember it after hearing it from the Blessed One.” “There is, bhikkhus, one thing that, when developed and cultivated, fulfills four things; four things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill seven things; and seven things, when developed and cultivated, fulfill two things.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro dhamme paripūreti, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta dhamme paripūrenti, satta dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā dve dhamme paripūrenti? Ānāpānassatisamādhi, bhikkhave, ekadhammo bhāvito bahulīkato cattāro [M 3.0293] satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti, satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentīti.

“And what, Bhikkhus, is that one thing which, when developed and frequently practiced, fulfills four things; when those four things are developed and frequently practiced, they fulfill seven things; and when those seven things are developed and frequently practiced, they fulfill two things? Bhikkhus, concentration due to mindfulness of breathing is the one thing that, when developed and frequently practiced, fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness. The four foundations of mindfulness, when developed and frequently practiced, fulfill the seven enlightenment factors. The seven enlightenment factors, when developed and frequently practiced, fulfill knowledge and liberation.”

“Kathaṃ [P 5.0336] bhāvito ca, bhikkhave, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṃ bahulīkato cattāro satipaṭṭhāne [V 3.0405] paripūreti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So satova assasati, satova passasati…pe… ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati”.

“And how, Bhikkhus, is concentration due to mindfulness of breathing developed and frequently practiced so that it fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness? Here, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu—having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling—sits down, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness directed towards the meditation subject. Mindful he breathes out, mindful he breathes in... He trains thus: ‘Contemplating relinquishment, I shall breathe out’; he trains thus: ‘Contemplating relinquishment, I shall breathe in.’”

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti…pe… sabbakāyappaṭisaṃvedī…pe… ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – kāye kāyānupassī, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Kāyaññatarāhaṃ, bhikkhave, etaṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – assāsapassāsaṃ. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, kāye kāyānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“At a time when, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu breathing out long knows, ‘I am breathing out long,’ or breathing in long knows, ‘I am breathing in long’; or breathing out short knows, ‘I am breathing out short,’ or breathing in short knows, ‘I am breathing in short’… experiencing the whole body… calming the bodily formation, he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out’; calming the bodily formation, he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in’—at that time, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. For what reason? I say, Bhikkhus, that this—the in-breath and the out-breath—is a certain body among bodies. Therefore, at that time, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pītippaṭisaṃvedī…pe… sukhappaṭisaṃvedī…pe… cittasaṅkhārappaṭisaṃvedī…pe… ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – vedanāsu vedanānupassī, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Vedanāññatarāhaṃ, bhikkhave, etaṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – assāsapassāsānaṃ sādhukaṃ manasikāraṃ. Tasmātiha[P 5.0337], bhikkhave, vedanāsu vedanānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“At a time when, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu trains thus: ‘Experiencing rapture… experiencing pleasure… experiencing the mental formation… calming the mental formation, I shall breathe out’; he trains thus: ‘Calming the mental formation, I shall breathe in’—at that time, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. For what reason? I say, Bhikkhus, that this—namely, the careful attention to in-breaths and out-breaths—is one among the feelings. Therefore, at that time, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cittappaṭisaṃvedī…pe… abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ…pe… ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘samādahaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti [M 3.0294] sikkhati; ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘vimocayaṃ cittaṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – citte cittānupassī, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, muṭṭhassatissa asampajānassa ānāpānassatisamādhibhāvanaṃ vadāmi. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave[V 3.0406], citte cittānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

“At a time when, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu trains thus: ‘Experiencing the mind… gladdening the mind… concentrating the mind, I shall breathe out’; he trains thus: ‘Concentrating the mind, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Liberating the mind, I shall breathe out’; he trains thus: ‘Liberating the mind, I shall breathe in’—at that time, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating mind in mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. For what reason? I do not say, Bhikkhus, that for one with lapsed mindfulness who lacks clear comprehension there is the development of concentration through mindfulness of breathing. Therefore, at that time, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating mind in mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aniccānupassī…pe… virāgānupassī…pe… nirodhānupassī…pe… ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati – dhammesu dhammānupassī, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. So yaṃ taṃ hoti abhijjhādomanassānaṃ pahānaṃ taṃ paññāya disvā sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti. Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, dhammesu dhammānupassī bhikkhu tasmiṃ samaye viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ.

Bhikkhus, at whatever time a bhikkhu trains, contemplating impermanence... contemplating dispassion... contemplating cessation... ‘Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe out,’ and trains, ‘Contemplating relinquishment, I will breathe in’—at that time, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world. That which is the abandoning of covetousness and displeasure, having seen it with wisdom, he regards with thorough equanimity. Therefore, herein, bhikkhus, at that time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having subdued covetousness and displeasure in the world.

“Evaṃ bhāvito kho, bhikkhave, ānāpānassatisamādhi evaṃ bahulīkato cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūreti.

Thus developed, bhikkhus, and thus cultivated, concentration through mindfulness of breathing fulfills the four establishments of mindfulness.

“Kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā kathaṃ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti? Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati – upaṭṭhitāssa tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno sati hoti asammuṭṭhā. Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno upaṭṭhitā [P 5.0338] sati hoti asammuṭṭhā – satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, satisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

And how, bhikkhus, when developed and cultivated, do the four establishments of mindfulness fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment? Bhikkhus, at whatever time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, at that time his mindfulness is established and unconfused. At whatever time, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu’s mindfulness is established and unconfused, at that time the enlightenment factor of mindfulness is aroused in him; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, and at that time, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness comes to the culmination of its development in him.

“So tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati. Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathā sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati pavicarati parivīmaṃsamāpajjati – dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

He, dwelling thus mindful, investigates that phenomenon with wisdom, examines it, and undertakes a thorough inquiry into it. At whatever time, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, dwelling thus mindful, investigates that phenomenon with wisdom, examines it, and undertakes a thorough inquiry into it, at that time the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena is aroused in him; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, and at that time, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena comes to the culmination of its development in him.

“Tassa [M 3.0295] taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato pavicarato parivīmaṃsamāpajjato āraddhaṃ hoti vīriyaṃ [V 3.0407] asallīnaṃ. Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato pavicarato parivīmaṃsamāpajjato āraddhaṃ hoti vīriyaṃ asallīnaṃ – vīriyasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, vīriyasambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, vīriyasambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

For him who investigates that phenomenon with wisdom, examines it, and undertakes a thorough inquiry into it, his energy is aroused and unflagging. At whatever time, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who investigates that phenomenon with wisdom, examines it, and undertakes a thorough inquiry into it, his energy is aroused and unflagging—at that time the enlightenment factor of energy is aroused in him; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of energy, and at that time, the enlightenment factor of energy comes to the culmination of its development in him.

“Āraddhavīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā. Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno āraddhavīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā – pītisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, pītisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, pītisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

For one with aroused energy, unworldly joy arises. At whatever time, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu with aroused energy, unworldly joy arises—at that time the enlightenment factor of joy is aroused in him; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of joy, and at that time, the enlightenment factor of joy comes to the culmination of its development in him.

“Pītimanassa kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati. Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pītimanassa kāyopi passambhati, cittampi passambhati – passaddhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, passaddhisambojjhaṅgaṃ [P 5.0339] tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, passaddhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

For one with a joyful mind, the body becomes tranquil and the mind also becomes tranquil. At whatever time, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu with a joyful mind, the body becomes tranquil and the mind also becomes tranquil—at that time the enlightenment factor of tranquility is aroused in him; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of tranquility, and at that time, the enlightenment factor of tranquility comes to the culmination of its development in him.

“Passaddhakāyassa sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati. Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno passaddhakāyassa sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati – samādhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, samādhisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, samādhisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

For one whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated. At whatever time, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated—at that time the enlightenment factor of concentration is aroused in him; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of concentration, and at that time, the enlightenment factor of concentration comes to the culmination of its development in him.

“So tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti. Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti – upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati.

He regards the mind thus concentrated well with equanimity. At whatever time, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu regards the mind thus concentrated well with equanimity—at that time the enlightenment factor of equanimity is aroused in him; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, and at that time, the enlightenment factor of equanimity comes to the culmination of its development in him.

“Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vedanāsu…pe… citte…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati – upaṭṭhitāssa tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno sati hoti [M 3.0296] asammuṭṭhā. Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno upaṭṭhitā sati hoti asammuṭṭhā – satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno [V 3.0408] āraddho hoti, satisambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti – satisambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati…pe….

Bhikkhus, at whatever time a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in mind... phenomena in phenomena, at that time his mindfulness is established and unconfused. At whatever time, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu’s mindfulness is established and unconfused—at that time the enlightenment factor of mindfulness is aroused in him; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, and at that time, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness comes to the culmination of its development in him....

So tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti. Yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāsamāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti – upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, upekkhāsambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchati. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā evaṃ bahulīkatā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti.

He regards the mind thus concentrated well with equanimity. At whatever time, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu regards the mind thus concentrated well with equanimity—at that time the enlightenment factor of equanimity is aroused in him; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, and at that time, the enlightenment factor of equanimity comes to the culmination of its development in him. Thus developed, bhikkhus, and thus cultivated, the four establishments of mindfulness fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment.

“Kathaṃ [P 5.0340] bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā kathaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satisambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ; dhammavicayasambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ…pe… upekkhāsambojjhaṅgaṃ bhāveti vivekanissitaṃ virāganissitaṃ nirodhanissitaṃ vossaggapariṇāmiṃ. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, satta bojjhaṅgā evaṃ bahulīkatā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrentī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

And how, monks, are the seven factors of enlightenment developed and cultivated so as to fulfill knowledge and liberation? Here, monks, a monk develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, and culminates in relinquishment. He develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, and culminates in relinquishment… He develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity, which is based upon seclusion, dispassion, and cessation, and culminates in relinquishment. Monks, thus developed and thus cultivated, the seven factors of enlightenment fulfill knowledge and liberation.” The Sixth.

7. Saṃyojanappahānasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Abandoning Fetters

993. Ānāpānassatisamādhi, bhikkhave, bhāvito bahulīkato saṃyojanappahānāya [T 5.0426] saṃvattati…pe…. Sattamaṃ.

993. Monks, concentration through mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, leads to the abandonment of the fetters… The Seventh.

8. Anusayasamugghātasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Eradication of Underlying Tendencies

994. …Anusayasamugghātāya saṃvattati…. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

994. …leads to the eradication of underlying tendencies…. The Eighth.

9. Addhānapariññāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Full Comprehension of the Course

995. …Addhānapariññāya saṃvattati…. Navamaṃ.

995. …leads to the full comprehension of the course…. The Ninth.

10. Āsavakkhayasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Destruction of the Taints

996. Āsavānaṃ [M 3.0297][V 3.0409] khayāya saṃvattati. Kathaṃ bhāvito ca, bhikkhave, ānāpānassatisamādhi kathaṃ bahulīkato saṃyojanappahānāya saṃvattati… anusayasamugghātāya saṃvattati… addhānapariññāya saṃvattati… āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattati? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā…pe. [P 5.0341]… paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmīti sikkhati, paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmīti sikkhati. Evaṃ bhāvito kho, bhikkhave, ānāpānassatisamādhi evaṃ bahulīkato saṃyojanappahānāya saṃvattati…pe… anusayasamugghātāya saṃvattati…pe… addhānapariññāya saṃvattati…pe… āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattatīti. Dasamaṃ.

996. …leads to the destruction of the taints. And how, monks, does concentration through mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, lead to the abandoning of the fetters… to the eradication of underlying tendencies… to the full comprehension of the course… to the destruction of the taints? Here, monks, a monk, gone to the wilderness, or to the foot of a tree… he trains, thinking: ‘I will breathe out, contemplating relinquishment.’ He trains, thinking: ‘I will breathe in, contemplating relinquishment.’ Thus developed and cultivated, monks, concentration through mindfulness of breathing leads to the abandoning of the fetters… to the eradication of underlying tendencies… to the full comprehension of the course… to the destruction of the taints.” The Tenth.

Dutiyo vaggo.

The Second Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Icchānaṅgalaṃ [T 5.0427] kaṅkheyyaṃ, ānandā apare duve;

Bhikkhū saṃyojanānusayā, addhānaṃ āsavakkhayanti.

Icchānaṅgala, Kaṅkheyya, two other Ānanda suttas; The Bhikkhu suttas, Fetters, Underlying Tendencies, The Course, and Destruction of the Taints.

Ānāpānasaṃyuttaṃ dasamaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Mindfulness of Breathing, the tenth.

11. Sotāpattisaṃyuttaṃ

11. Connected Discourses on Stream-Entry

1. Veḷudvāravaggo

1. The Chapter on Veḷudvāra

1. Cakkavattirājasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Wheel-Turning Monarch

997. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0428][M 3.0298][V 3.0410][P 5.0342]. Tatra kho bhagavā…pe… etadavoca – “kiñcāpi, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī cakkavatti (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) catunnaṃ dīpānaṃ issariyādhipaccaṃ rajjaṃ kāretvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati devānaṃ tāvatiṃsānaṃ sahabyataṃ, so tattha nandane vane accharāsaṅghaparivuto dibbehi ca pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti, so catūhi dhammehi asamannāgato, atha kho so aparimuttova aparimutto ca (syā. kaṃ. ka.) nirayā aparimutto tiracchānayoniyā aparimutto pettivisayā aparimutto apāyaduggativinipātā. Kiñcāpi, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako piṇḍiyālopena yāpeti, nantakāni ca dhāreti, so catūhi dhammehi samannāgato, atha kho so parimutto parimutto ca (syā. kaṃ. ka.) nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā”.

997. At Sāvatthī.
