There the Blessed One said this: “Even though, monks, a wheel-turning monarch rules, exercising sovereignty and dominion over the four continents, and after the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, in the company of the Tāvatiṃsa devas; and even though there in the Nandana Grove, surrounded by a host of celestial nymphs, he is furnished with the five divine strands of sensual pleasure and endowed with attendants; if he is not possessed of four qualities, then indeed he is not freed from hell, not freed from the animal realm, not freed from the realm of petas, not freed from the plane of misery, the bad destination, the state of ruin. But even though, monks, a noble disciple lives on almsfood and wears rag-robes, if he is possessed of four qualities, then indeed he is freed from hell, freed from the animal realm, freed from the realm of petas, freed from the plane of misery, the bad destination, the state of ruin.”

“Katamehi catūhi? Idha[P 5.0343], bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti[T 5.0429]. Dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti. Saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ – cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha [V 3.0411] purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti. Ariyakantehi sīlehi [M 3.0299] samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi catūhi dhammehi samannāgato hoti. Yo ca, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ dīpānaṃ paṭilābho, yo catunnaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭilābho catunnaṃ dīpānaṃ paṭilābho catunnaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭilābhassa kalaṃ nāgghati soḷasi”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“With what four? Here, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant, perfectly self-enlightened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-Farer, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: ‘The Dhamma is well expounded by the Blessed One, directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be personally experienced by the wise.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way, practicing the straight way, practicing the true way, practicing the proper way; that is, the four pairs of persons, the eight individual types—this Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken, unblemished, unspotted, unmottled, liberating, praised by the wise, ungrasped, and conducive to concentration. He is endowed with these four qualities. And, monks, the gain of the four continents is not worth a sixteenth part of the gain of these four qualities.” This is the first.

2. Brahmacariyogadhasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Foundation of the Holy Life

998. “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.

998. “Monks, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into states of woe, certain, with enlightenment as his destination.

“Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā’ti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi [T 5.0430] samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi [P 5.0344] kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.

“With what four? Here, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant, perfectly self-enlightened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, the Well-Farer, knower of the world, unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… conducive to concentration. Monks, a noble disciple who is endowed with these four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into states of woe, fixed in destiny, with enlightenment as his destination.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna vatvā (sī. pī.) evamīdisesu ṭhānesu sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-Farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Yesaṃ saddhā ca sīlañca, pasādo dhammadassanaṃ;

Te ve kālena paccenti, brahmacariyogadhaṃ sukha”nti. dutiyaṃ;

“Those for whom there is faith and virtue, confidence and vision of the Dhamma, they indeed, in due time, attain the happiness immersed in the holy life.”

3. Dīghāvuupāsakasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse to Dīghāvu the Lay Follower

999. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena dīghāvu upāsako ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho dīghāvu upāsako [V 3.0412] pitaraṃ jotikaṃ gahapatiṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, gahapati, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vanda – ‘dīghāvu, bhante[M 3.0300], upāsako ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, bhagavā yena dīghāvussa upāsakassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’”ti. “Evaṃ, tātā”ti kho jotiko gahapati dīghāvussa upāsakassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jotiko gahapati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “dīghāvu, bhante, upāsako ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno[T 5.0431]. So bhagavato pāde sirasā vandati. Evañca vadeti – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, bhagavā yena dīghāvussa upāsakassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’”ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.

999. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary. Now at that time the lay follower Dīghāvu was sick, suffering, and gravely ill. Then the lay follower Dīghāvu addressed his father, the householder Jotika: “Come, householder, go to the Blessed One and, having approached, pay homage with your head at the Blessed One’s feet in my name and say: ‘Venerable sir, the lay follower Dīghāvu is sick, suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet.’ And say this: ‘It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would come to the residence of the lay follower Dīghāvu out of compassion.’” “Yes, dear,” replied the householder Jotika to the lay follower Dīghāvu, and he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the householder Jotika said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the lay follower Dīghāvu is sick, suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head at the Blessed One’s feet. And he says this: ‘It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would come to the residence of the lay follower Dīghāvu out of compassion.’” The Blessed One consented by remaining silent.

Atha kho bhagavā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena dīghāvussa upāsakassa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [P 5.0345] paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā dīghāvuṃ upāsakaṃ etadavoca – “kacci te, dīghāvu, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ? Kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti? “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti. “Tasmātiha te, dīghāvu, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato bhavissāmi – itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato bhavissāmi akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi’. Evañhi te, dīghāvu, sikkhitabba”nti.

Then the Blessed One, having put on his under-robe, taking his bowl and robe, went to the residence of the lay follower Dīghāvu. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One said this to the lay follower Dīghāvu: “Dīghāvu, are you keeping well? Are you able to manage? Are your painful feelings subsiding and not increasing? Is their subsiding apparent, and not their increasing?” “Venerable sir, I am not keeping well; I am not able to manage. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increasing is apparent, not their subsiding.” “Therefore, Dīghāvu, you should train yourself thus: ‘I will be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: “Indeed, that Blessed One is an Arahant, perfectly enlightened, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, an unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.” In the Dhamma… In the Saṅgha… I will be endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones, unbroken… conducive to concentration.’ Indeed, Dīghāvu, you should train yourself thus.”

“Yānimāni, bhante, bhagavatā cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni desitāni, saṃvijjante te dhammā mayi, ahañca tesu dhammesu sandissāmi. Ahañhi, bhante, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato – itipi [T 5.0432] so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehī”ti[V 3.0413]. “Tasmātiha tvaṃ, dīghāvu, imesu catūsu sotāpattiyaṅgesu patiṭṭhāya cha vijjābhāgiye dhamme uttari bhāveyyāsi. Idha tvaṃ, dīghāvu, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī [M 3.0301] viharāhi, anicce dukkhasaññī, dukkhe anattasaññī pahānasaññī virāgasaññī nirodhasaññīti. Evañhi te, dīghāvu, sikkhitabba”nti.

“Venerable sir, these four factors of stream-attainment have been taught by the Blessed One; these qualities are present in me, and I am seen in these qualities. Indeed, venerable sir, I am endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Indeed, that Blessed One is… teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ In the Dhamma… In the Saṅgha… I am endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones, unbroken… conducive to concentration.” “Therefore, Dīghāvu, being established in these four factors of stream-attainment, you should further develop the six qualities that are portions of true knowledge. Here, Dīghāvu, you should dwell contemplating impermanence in all conditioned formations, perceiving suffering in what is impermanent, perceiving not-self in what is suffering, perceiving abandoning, perceiving dispassion, and perceiving cessation. Indeed, Dīghāvu, you should train yourself thus.”

“Yeme, bhante, bhagavatā cha vijjābhāgiyā dhammā desitā, saṃvijjante te dhammā mayi, ahañca tesu dhammesu sandissāmi. Ahañhi, bhante, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī viharāmi, anicce dukkhasaññī, dukkhe anattasaññī pahānasaññī virāgasaññī nirodhasaññī. Api ca me, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘mā hevāyaṃ jotiko gahapati mamaccayena vighātaṃ āpajjī’”ti āpajjati (ka.). “Mā [P 5.0346] tvaṃ, tāta dīghāvu, evaṃ manasākāsi. Iṅgha tvaṃ, tāta dīghāvu, yadeva te bhagavā āha, tadeva tvaṃ sādhukaṃ manasi karohī”ti.

“Venerable sir, those six qualities that are portions of true knowledge that the Blessed One has taught—those qualities are found in me, and I am seen in those qualities. For, venerable sir, I dwell contemplating impermanence in all conditioned formations, perceiving suffering in what is impermanent, perceiving not-self in what is suffering, perceiving abandoning, perceiving dispassion, and perceiving cessation. And yet, venerable sir, this thought occurs to me: ‘May this householder Jotika not fall into distress upon my passing away.’” “Do not think in that way, dear Dīghāvu. Come now, dear Dīghāvu, carefully attend to what the Blessed One has taught.”

Atha kho bhagavā dīghāvuṃ upāsakaṃ iminā ovādena ovaditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho dīghāvu upāsako acirapakkantassa bhagavato kālamakāsi. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā [T 5.0433] kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “yo so, bhante, dīghāvu nāma upāsako bhagavatā saṃkhittena ovādena ovadito so kālaṅkato. Tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo”ti? “Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, dīghāvu upāsako, paccapādi ahosi saccavādī (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) dhammassānudhammaṃ, na ca maṃ dhammādhikaraṇaṃ na ca dhammādhikaraṇaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) vihesesi viheṭhesi (itipi aññattha). Dīghāvu, bhikkhave, upāsako pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

Then the Blessed One, having advised Dīghāvu the lay follower with this instruction, rose from his seat and departed. Then, not long after the Blessed One had left, Dīghāvu the lay follower passed away. Then several monks approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, those monks said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, that lay follower named Dīghāvu, who was instructed with brief advice by the Blessed One, has passed away. What is his destiny, what is his future state?” “Monks, the lay follower Dīghāvu was wise; he practiced the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and did not trouble me regarding the Dhamma. Monks, the lay follower Dīghāvu, with the destruction of the five lower fetters, has arisen spontaneously and will attain final Nibbāna there, not subject to returning from that world.”

4. Paṭhamasāriputtasuttaṃ

4. The First Discourse concerning Sāriputta

1000. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca ānando sāvatthiyaṃ viharanti jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā ānando sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca – “katinaṃ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, dhammānaṃ samannāgamanahetu evamayaṃ pajā [V 3.0414] bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti[M 3.0302]? “Catunnaṃ [P 5.0347] kho, āvuso, dhammānaṃ samannāgamanahetu evamayaṃ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”.

1000. At one time the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Ānanda were dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then in the evening, the Venerable Ānanda arose from seclusion... and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Venerable Sāriputta: “Friend Sāriputta, due to being endowed with how many dhammas is this populace declared by the Blessed One to be a stream-enterer, not subject to perdition, assured, and destined for enlightenment?” “Friend, it is due to being endowed with four dhammas that this populace is declared by the Blessed One to be a stream-enterer, not subject to perdition, assured, and destined for enlightenment.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Idhāvuso, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi [T 5.0434] sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imesaṃ kho, āvuso, catunnaṃ dhammānaṃ samannāgamanahetu evamayaṃ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Which four? Here, friend, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, that Blessed One is an Arahant, perfectly enlightened, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma... He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha... He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken... conducive to concentration. Friend, it is due to being endowed with these four dhammas that this populace is declared by the Blessed One to be a stream-enterer, not subject to perdition, assured, and destined for enlightenment.” The fourth.

5. Dutiyasāriputtasuttaṃ

5. The Second Sāriputta Sutta

1001. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “‘sotāpattiyaṅgaṃ, sotāpattiyaṅga’nti hidaṃ, sāriputta, vuccati. Katamaṃ nu kho sāriputta, sotāpattiyaṅga”nti? “Sappurisasaṃsevo hi, bhante, sotāpattiyaṅgaṃ, saddhammassavanaṃ sotāpattiyaṅgaṃ, yonisomanasikāro sotāpattiyaṅgaṃ, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti sotāpattiyaṅga”nti. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Sappurisasaṃsevo hi, sāriputta, sotāpattiyaṅgaṃ, saddhammassavanaṃ sotāpattiyaṅgaṃ, yonisomanasikāro sotāpattiyaṅgaṃ, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti sotāpattiyaṅgaṃ”.

1001. Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to the Venerable Sāriputta: “‘Factor for stream-entry, factor for stream-entry,’ it is said, Sāriputta. What now, Sāriputta, is a factor for stream-entry?” “Venerable sir, association with good persons is a factor for stream-entry; hearing the true Dhamma is a factor for stream-entry; wise attention is a factor for stream-entry; practice in accordance with the Dhamma is a factor for stream-entry.” “Good, good, Sāriputta! Association with good persons, Sāriputta, is a factor for stream-entry; hearing the true Dhamma is a factor for stream-entry; wise attention is a factor for stream-entry; practice in accordance with the Dhamma is a factor for stream-entry.”

“‘Soto, soto’ti hidaṃ, sāriputta, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, sāriputta, soto”ti? “Ayameva hi, bhante, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo soto, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhī”ti. “Sādhu [T 5.0435] sādhu, sāriputta! Ayameva hi, sāriputta, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo soto, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi”.

“‘The stream, the stream,’ it is said, Sāriputta. What now, Sāriputta, is the stream?” “Venerable sir, this very Noble Eightfold Path is the stream; that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.” “Good, good, Sāriputta! This very Noble Eightfold Path, Sāriputta, is the stream; that is: right view… right concentration.”

“‘Sotāpanno[P 5.0348], sotāpanno’ti hidaṃ, sāriputta, vuccati. Katamo nu kho, sāriputta, sotāpanno”ti[V 3.0415]? “Yo hi, bhante, iminā ariyena aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena samannāgato ayaṃ vuccati sotāpanno, svāyaṃ āyasmā [M 3.0303] evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto”ti. “Sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yo hi, sāriputta, iminā ariyena aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena samannāgato ayaṃ vuccati sotāpanno, svāyaṃ āyasmā evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“‘A stream-enterer, a stream-enterer,’ it is said, Sāriputta. What, Sāriputta, is a stream-enterer?” “Venerable sir, whoever is endowed with this Noble Eightfold Path is called a stream-enterer; that venerable one is of such a name and of such a clan.” “Good, good, Sāriputta! Whoever is endowed with this Noble Eightfold Path is called a stream-enterer; that venerable one is of such a name and of such a clan.” The fifth.

6. Thapatisuttaṃ

6. The Carpenters Sutta

1002. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṃ karonti – “niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṃ pakkamissatī”ti. Tena kho pana samayena isidattapurāṇā thapatayo sādhuke paṭivasanti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Assosuṃ kho isidattapurāṇā thapatayo – “sambahulā kira bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṃ karonti – ‘niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’”ti.

1002. At Sāvatthī. At that time, many monks were making a robe for the Blessed One, thinking: “When the Blessed One’s robe is finished, he will set out on a journey after the passing of the three months.” At that time, the carpenters Isidatta and Purāṇa were dwelling in Sādhuka on some business. The carpenters Isidatta and Purāṇa heard: “It is said that many monks are making a robe for the Blessed One, thinking: ‘When the Blessed One’s robe is finished, he will set out on a journey after the passing of the three months.’”

Atha kho isidattapurāṇā thapatayo magge purisaṃ ṭhapesuṃ – “yadā tvaṃ, ambho purisa, passeyyāsi bhagavantaṃ āgacchantaṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ, atha amhākaṃ āroceyyāsī”ti. Dvīhatīhaṃ ṭhito kho so [T 5.0436] puriso addasa bhagavantaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna yena isidattapurāṇā thapatayo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā isidattapurāṇe thapatayo etadavoca – “ayaṃ so, bhante, bhagavā āgacchati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho. Yassa dāni kālaṃ maññathā”ti.

Then Isidatta and Purāṇa, the carpenters, stationed a man on the road, saying: “Good man, when you see the Blessed One coming, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha, then inform us.” After standing for two or three days, that man saw the Blessed One coming from afar. Having seen him, he approached Isidatta and Purāṇa, the carpenters, and said: “Venerable sirs, the Blessed One is coming, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha. Now is the time for whatever you think fit.”

Atha kho isidattapurāṇā thapatayo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā bhagavantaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma yena aññataraṃ rukkhamūlaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane [P 5.0349] nisīdi. Isidattapurāṇā thapatayo bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te isidattapurāṇā thapatayo bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ –

Then Isidatta and Purāṇa, the carpenters, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and followed right behind him. Then the Blessed One left the road and went to the foot of a certain tree. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Isidatta and Purāṇa, the carpenters, paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Isidatta and Purāṇa, the carpenters, said this to the Blessed One:

“Yadā mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘sāvatthiyā kosalesu cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘sāvatthiyā kosalesu cārikaṃ pakkanto’ti[V 3.0416], hoti no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā’”ti.

“Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will depart from Sāvatthī for a journey in the Kosala country,’ at that time there is displeasure for us and there is sadness, thinking: ‘Our Blessed One will be far away.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One has departed from Sāvatthī for a journey in the Kosala country,’ at that time there is displeasure for us and there is sadness, thinking: ‘Our Blessed One is far away.’”

“Yadā [M 3.0304] pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘kosalehi mallesu cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante[T 5.0437], bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘kosalehi mallesu cārikaṃ pakkanto’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā’”ti.

Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will set out on a journey from the Kosalas to the Mallas,’ at that time we feel displeasure and sadness, thinking: ‘The Blessed One will be far from us.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One has set out on a journey from the Kosalas to the Mallas,’ at that time we feel displeasure and sadness, thinking: ‘The Blessed One is far from us.’”

“Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘mallehi vajjīsu cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘mallehi vajjīsu cārikaṃ pakkanto’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā’”ti.

Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will set out on a journey from the Mallas to the Vajjis,’ at that time we feel displeasure and sadness, thinking: ‘The Blessed One will be far from us.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One has set out on a journey from the Mallas to the Vajjis,’ at that time we feel displeasure and sadness, thinking: ‘The Blessed One is far from us.’”

“Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘vajjīhi kāsīsu cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘vajjīhi kāsīsu cārikaṃ pakkanto’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā’”ti.

Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will set out on a journey from the Vajjis to the Kāsīs,’ at that time we feel displeasure and sadness, thinking: ‘The Blessed One will be far from us.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One has set out on a journey from the Vajjis to the Kāsīs,’ at that time we feel displeasure and sadness, thinking: ‘The Blessed One is far from us.’”

“Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘kāsīhi māgadhe cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā [P 5.0350] hoti domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘kāsīhi māgadhe cārikaṃ pakkanto’ti, hoti anappakā no tasmiṃ samaye anattamanatā hoti anappakaṃ domanassaṃ – ‘dūre no bhagavā’”ti.

Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will set out on a journey from the Kāsīs to Magadha,’ at that time we feel displeasure and sadness, thinking: ‘The Blessed One will be far from us.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One has set out on a journey from the Kāsīs to Magadha,’ at that time we feel no small displeasure and no small sadness, thinking: ‘The Blessed One is far from us.’”

“Yadā [T 5.0438] pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘māgadhehi kāsīsu cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti[V 3.0417], hoti no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā hoti somanassaṃ – ‘āsanne no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘māgadhehi kāsīsu cārikaṃ pakkanto’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā hoti somanassaṃ – ‘āsanne no bhagavā’”ti.

Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will set out on a journey from Magadha to the Kāsīs,’ at that time we feel gladness and joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One will be near us.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One has set out on a journey from Magadha to the Kāsīs,’ at that time we feel gladness and joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One is near us.’”

“Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘kāsīhi vajjīsu cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā hoti somanassaṃ [M 3.0305] – ‘āsanne no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘kāsīhi vajjīsu cārikaṃ pakkanto’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā hoti somanassaṃ – ‘āsanne no bhagavā’”ti.

Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will set out on a journey from the Kāsīs to the Vajjis,’ at that time we feel gladness and joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One will be near us.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One has set out on a journey from the Kāsīs to the Vajjis,’ at that time we feel gladness and joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One is near us.’”

“Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘vajjīhi mallesu cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā hoti somanassaṃ – ‘āsanne no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘vajjīhi mallesu cārikaṃ pakkanto’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā hoti somanassaṃ – ‘āsanne no bhagavā’”ti.

Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will set out on a journey from the Vajjis to the Mallas,’ at that time we feel gladness and joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One will be near us.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One has set out on a journey from the Vajjis to the Mallas,’ at that time we feel gladness and joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One is near us.’”

“Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘mallehi kosale cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā [T 5.0439] hoti somanassaṃ – ‘āsanne no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘mallehi kosale cārikaṃ pakkanto’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā hoti somanassaṃ – ‘āsanne no bhagavā’”ti.

Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will set out on a journey from the Mallas to the Kosalas,’ at that time we feel gladness and joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One will be near us.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One has set out on a journey from the Mallas to the Kosalas,’ at that time we feel gladness and joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One is near us.’”

“Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘kosalehi sāvatthiṃ cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā hoti somanassaṃ – ‘āsanne no bhagavā bhavissatī’ti. Yadā pana mayaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ suṇāma – ‘sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme’ti, hoti anappakā no tasmiṃ samaye attamanatā hoti anappakaṃ somanassaṃ – ‘āsanne no bhagavā’”ti.

Venerable Sir, when we hear, ‘The Blessed One will set out on a journey from the Kosalas to Sāvatthī,’ at that time we feel gladness and joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One will be near us.’ And when, Venerable Sir, we hear, ‘The Blessed One is dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park,’ at that time we feel no small gladness and no small joy, thinking: ‘The Blessed One is near us.’”

“Tasmātiha, thapatayo, sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho, abbhokāso pabbajjā. Alañca pana [V 3.0418] vo, thapatayo, appamādāyā”ti. “Atthi kho no, bhante, etamhā sambādhā añño sambādho sambādhataro ceva sambādhasaṅkhātataro cā”ti. “Katamo [P 5.0351] pana vo, thapatayo, etamhā sambādhā añño sambādho sambādhataro ceva sambādhasaṅkhātataro cā”ti?

“Therefore, carpenters, the household life is confining, a path of dust; the going forth is like the open air. It is fitting for you, carpenters, to be diligent.” “Indeed, Venerable Sir, there is for us another confinement than this—one more confining and reckoned as more confining.” “And what, carpenters, is that other confinement for you, which is more confining and reckoned as more confining than this?”

“Idha mayaṃ, bhante, yadā rājā pasenadi kosalo uyyānabhūmiṃ niyyātukāmo hoti, ye te rañño pasenadissa kosalassa nāgā opavayhā te kappetvā, yā tā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa pajāpatiyo piyā manāpā tā ekaṃ purato ekaṃ [M 3.0306] pacchato [T 5.0440] nisīdāpema. Tāsaṃ kho pana, bhante, bhaginīnaṃ evarūpo gandho hoti, seyyathāpi nāma gandhakaraṇḍakassa tāvadeva vivariyamānassa, yathā taṃ rājakaññānaṃ gandhena vibhūsitānaṃ. Tāsaṃ kho pana, bhante, bhaginīnaṃ evarūpo kāyasamphasso hoti, seyyathāpi nāma tūlapicuno vā kappāsapicuno vā, yathā taṃ rājakaññānaṃ sukhedhitānaṃ. Tasmiṃ kho pana, bhante, samaye nāgopi rakkhitabbo hoti, tāpi bhaginiyo rakkhitabbā honti, attāpi rakkhitabbo hoti. Na kho pana mayaṃ, bhante, abhijānāma tāsu bhaginīsu pāpakaṃ cittaṃ uppādetā. Ayaṃ kho no, bhante, etamhā sambādhā añño sambādho sambādhataro ceva sambādhasaṅkhātataro cā”ti.

“Here, venerable sir, when King Pasenadi of Kosala wishes to go to the pleasure grounds, we prepare the royal elephants of King Pasenadi of Kosala that are fit to be ridden. Then we seat the consorts of King Pasenadi of Kosala, who are beloved and pleasing, one in front and one behind. And, venerable sir, these ladies have such a fragrance, like a perfume casket just being opened—like that of royal maidens adorned with perfumes. And, venerable sir, these ladies have such a bodily touch, like a tuft of silk-cotton or a tuft of cotton—like that of royal maidens brought up in luxury. At that time, venerable sir, the elephant must be guarded, those ladies must be guarded, and we ourselves must be guarded. But, venerable sir, we do not recall an evil thought arising in us toward those ladies. This, venerable sir, is for us another constraint, more confining and considered even more confining than that.”

“Tasmātiha, thapatayo, sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho, abbhokāso pabbajjā. Alañca pana vo, thapatayo, appamādāya. Catūhi kho, thapatayo, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.

“Therefore, carpenters, the household life is confining, a path of dust; the going forth is like the open air. It is indeed proper for you, carpenters, to be diligent. A noble disciple endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into the lower realms, assured, and destined for enlightenment.

“Katamehi catūhi? Idha, thapatayo, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… vigatamalamaccherena cetasā ajjhāgāraṃ vasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Imehi kho, thapatayo, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato [P 5.0352] ariyasāvako [T 5.0441] sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.

“With which four? Here, carpenters, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ In the Dhamma… In the Saṅgha… He dwells at home with a mind free from the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, delighting in relinquishment, responsive to requests, and delighting in giving and sharing. A noble disciple endowed with these four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into the lower realms, assured, and destined for enlightenment.

“Tumhe kho, thapatayo, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… yaṃ kho pana kiñci kule deyyadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ appaṭivibhattaṃ sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehi. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, thapatayo, katividhā [V 3.0419] te kosalesu manussā ye tumhākaṃ samasamā, yadidaṃ – dānasaṃvibhāge”ti? “Lābhā no, bhante, suladdhaṃ no, bhante! Yesaṃ no bhagavā evaṃ pajānātī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Indeed, carpenters, you are endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Thus is the Blessed One… teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ In the Dhamma… In the Saṅgha… And whatever gift-worthy thing there is in your family, all of it is shared unreservedly with the virtuous, those of good character. What do you think, carpenters? How many people are there in Kosala who are your equals in this matter of giving and sharing?” “It is a gain for us, venerable sir, a great gain for us, that the Blessed One knows us thus!” The sixth.

7. Veḷudvāreyyasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse at Veḷudvāra

1003. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena veḷudvāraṃ nāma kosalānaṃ brāhmaṇagāmo [M 3.0307] tadavasari. Assosuṃ kho te veḷudvāreyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā – “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ veḷudvāraṃ anuppatto. Taṃ kho pana bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ evaṃ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato – ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā bhagavāti (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti. So [T 5.0442] dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti’. Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṃ arahataṃ dassanaṃ hotī”ti.

1003. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was wandering on tour in the Kosalan country together with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus, and he arrived at a brahmin village of the Kosalans named Veḷudvāra. The brahmin householders of Veḷudvāra heard: “The ascetic Gotama, it seems, a Sakyan son gone forth from the Sakyan clan, is wandering on tour in the Kosalan country together with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus and has arrived at Veḷudvāra. Now, a good report concerning the venerable Gotama has spread thus: ‘Thus is the Blessed One an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, consummate in knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, knower of the world, an unsurpassed trainer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One. He makes known this world with its devas, its Māra, and its Brahmā, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, having realized it himself through direct knowledge. He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with its meaning and phrasing; he proclaims the holy life, utterly complete and pure.’ Indeed, it is good to see such Arahants.”

Atha [P 5.0353] kho te veḷudvāreyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu; sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce bhagavato santike nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te veḷudvāreyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “mayaṃ, bho gotama, evaṃkāmā evaṃchandā evaṃadhippāyā – puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvaseyyāma, kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhaveyyāma, mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhāreyyāma, jātarūparajataṃ sādiyeyyāma, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyāma. Tesaṃ no bhavaṃ gotamo amhākaṃ evaṃkāmānaṃ evaṃchandānaṃ evaṃadhippāyānaṃ tathā dhammaṃ desetu yathā mayaṃ puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvaseyyāma…pe… sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjeyyāmā”ti.

Then the brahmin householders of Veḷudvāra approached the Blessed One. Having approached, some paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One and, after concluding endearing and memorable talk, sat down to one side; some extended their hands in reverential salutation toward the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some announced their name and clan in the presence of the Blessed One and sat down to one side; some sat down to one side in silence. Seated to one side, the brahmin householders of Veḷudvāra said to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, we have such desires, such wishes, such intentions—we wish to dwell in a residence crowded with children, to enjoy sandalwood from Kāsi, to wear garlands, perfumes, and unguents, to delight in gold and silver, and after the breakup of the body, after death, to be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world. Let Master Gotama teach us the Dhamma in such a way that we, who have such desires, such wishes, and such intentions, may dwell in a residence crowded with children… and be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.”

“Attūpanāyikaṃ [V 3.0420] vo, gahapatayo, dhammapariyāyaṃ desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho te [T 5.0443] veḷudvāreyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“Householders, I will teach you a discourse on the Dhamma applicable to yourselves. Listen to it and attend carefully; I will speak.” “Yes, Master,” replied the brahmin householders of Veḷudvāra to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamo [M 3.0308] ca, gahapatayo, attupanāyiko dhammapariyāyo? Idha, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘ahaṃ khosmi jīvitukāmo amaritukāmo sukhakāmo dukkhappaṭikūlo. Yo kho maṃ jīvitukāmaṃ amaritukāmaṃ sukhakāmaṃ dukkhappaṭikūlaṃ jīvitā voropeyya, na metaṃ assa piyaṃ manāpaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana paraṃ jīvitukāmaṃ amaritukāmaṃ sukhakāmaṃ dukkhappaṭikūlaṃ jīvitā voropeyyaṃ, parassapi taṃ assa appiyaṃ amanāpaṃ. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo [P 5.0354] appiyo amanāpo. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṃ paraṃ tena saṃyojeyya’nti! So iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, parañca pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Evamassāyaṃ kāyasamācāro tikoṭiparisuddho hoti.

And what, householders, is the discourse on the Dhamma applicable to oneself? Here, householders, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘I am one who desires to live, who does not desire to die, who desires happiness, and who is averse to suffering. If someone were to deprive me of life—I who desire to live, do not desire to die, desire happiness, and am averse to suffering—that would not be pleasing or agreeable to me. And if I were to deprive another of life—one who desires to live, does not desire to die, desires happiness, and is averse to suffering—that would not be pleasing or agreeable to that other. The state that is unpleasing and disagreeable to me is also unpleasing and disagreeable to another. Since this state is unpleasing and disagreeable to me, how could I associate another with it?’ Having reflected thus, he himself abstains from the destruction of life, he encourages others to abstain from the destruction of life, and he speaks in praise of abstaining from the destruction of life. In this way, his bodily conduct is purified in three aspects.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yo kho me adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyeyya, na metaṃ assa piyaṃ manāpaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana parassa adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyeyyaṃ, parassapi taṃ assa appiyaṃ amanāpaṃ. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo appiyo amanāpo. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṃ paraṃ tena saṃyojeyya’nti[T 5.0444]! So iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, parañca adinnādānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, adinnādānā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Evamassāyaṃ kāyasamācāro tikoṭiparisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘If someone were to take from me what is not given, which is reckoned as theft, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to me. And if I were to take from another what is not given, which is reckoned as theft, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to that other. The state that is unpleasing and disagreeable to me is also unpleasing and disagreeable to another. Since this state is unpleasing and disagreeable to me, how could I associate another with it?’ Having reflected thus, he himself abstains from taking what is not given, he encourages others to abstain from taking what is not given, and he speaks in praise of abstaining from taking what is not given. In this way, his bodily conduct is purified in three aspects.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yo kho me dāresu cārittaṃ āpajjeyya, na metaṃ assa piyaṃ manāpaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana parassa dāresu cārittaṃ āpajjeyyaṃ, parassapi taṃ assa appiyaṃ amanāpaṃ. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo appiyo amanāpo. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṃ paraṃ tena saṃyojeyya’nti! So iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato [V 3.0421] hoti, parañca kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ [M 3.0309] bhāsati. Evamassāyaṃ kāyasamācāro tikoṭiparisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘If someone were to commit a transgression against my wives, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to me. And if I were to commit a transgression against another’s wives, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to that other. The state that is unpleasing and disagreeable to me is also unpleasing and disagreeable to another. Since this state is unpleasing and disagreeable to me, how could I associate another with it?’ Having reflected thus, he himself abstains from misconduct in sensual pleasures, he encourages others to abstain from misconduct in sensual pleasures, and he speaks in praise of abstaining from misconduct in sensual pleasures. In this way, his bodily conduct is purified in three aspects.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yo kho me musāvādena atthaṃ bhañjeyya, na metaṃ assa piyaṃ manāpaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana parassa musāvādena atthaṃ bhañjeyyaṃ, parassapi taṃ assa appiyaṃ amanāpaṃ. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo appiyo amanāpo. Yo [P 5.0355] kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṃ paraṃ tena saṃyojeyya’nti! So [T 5.0445] iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, parañca musāvādā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, musāvādā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Evamassāyaṃ vacīsamācāro tikoṭiparisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘If someone were to destroy my welfare with false speech, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to me. And if I were to destroy another’s welfare with false speech, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to that other. The state that is unpleasing and disagreeable to me is also unpleasing and disagreeable to another. Since this state is unpleasing and disagreeable to me, how could I associate another with it?’ Having reflected thus, he himself abstains from false speech, he encourages others to abstain from false speech, and he speaks in praise of abstaining from false speech. In this way, his verbal conduct is purified in three aspects.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – yo kho maṃ pisuṇāya vācāya mitte bhindeyya mittehi bhedeyya (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.), na metaṃ assa piyaṃ manāpaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana paraṃ pisuṇāya vācāya mitte bhindeyyaṃ, parassapi taṃ assa appiyaṃ amanāpaṃ…pe… evamassāyaṃ vacīsamācāro tikoṭiparisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘If someone were to divide me from my friends with slanderous speech, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to me. And if I were to divide another from their friends with slanderous speech, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to that other... and so on... In this way, his verbal conduct is purified in three aspects.’

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – yo kho maṃ pharusāya vācāya samudācareyya, na metaṃ assa piyaṃ manāpaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana paraṃ pharusāya vācāya samudācareyyaṃ, parassapi taṃ assa appiyaṃ amanāpaṃ. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo…pe… evamassāyaṃ vacīsamācāro tikoṭiparisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘If someone were to address me with harsh speech, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to me. And if I were to address another with harsh speech, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to that other. That principle which for me... and so on... In this way, his verbal conduct is purified in three aspects.’

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘yo kho maṃ samphabhāsena samphappalāpabhāsena samudācareyya, na metaṃ assa piyaṃ manāpaṃ. Ahañceva kho pana paraṃ samphabhāsena samphappalāpabhāsena samudācareyyaṃ, parassapi taṃ assa appiyaṃ amanāpaṃ. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo appiyo amanāpo. Yo kho myāyaṃ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṃ paraṃ tena saṃyojeyya’nti! So iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti[M 3.0310], parañca samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, samphappalāpā [V 3.0422] veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Evamassāyaṃ vacīsamācāro tikoṭiparisuddho hoti.

Furthermore, householders, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘If someone were to address me with idle chatter, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to me. And if I were to address another with idle chatter, that would not be pleasing or agreeable to that other. The state that is unpleasing and disagreeable to me is also unpleasing and disagreeable to another. Since this state is unpleasing and disagreeable to me, how could I associate another with it?’ Having reflected thus, he himself abstains from idle chatter, he encourages others to abstain from idle chatter, and he speaks in praise of abstaining from idle chatter. In this way, his verbal conduct is purified in three aspects.

“So buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti; dhamme [P 5.0356] …pe… saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Yato kho, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako imehi sattahi saddhammehi dhammehi (sī.) samannāgato hoti imehi catūhi ākaṅkhiyehi ṭhānehi, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇatiracchānayoniyo (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.), khīṇatiracchānayoniko (ka.) khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti.

He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Thus is the Blessed One… teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha: ‘The community of the Blessed One’s disciples has practiced well… it is the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration. When, householders, a noble disciple is endowed with these seven good qualities, he may, if he wishes, declare of himself by means of these four desirable states: ‘Hell is destroyed for me, the animal realm is destroyed, the realm of ghosts is destroyed, the states of woe, bad destinations, and downfall are destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to downfall, assured, and destined for enlightenment.’

Evaṃ vutte veḷudvāreyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – “abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… ete mayaṃ bhavantaṃ gotamaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca. Upāsake no bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete pāṇupetaṃ (ka.) saraṇaṃ gate”ti. Sattamaṃ.

When this was said, the brahmins and householders of Veḷudvāra said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, Master Gotama!… We go for refuge to Master Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. May Master Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.” Seventh.

8. Paṭhamagiñjakāvasathasuttaṃ

8. The First Discourse at the Brick Hall

1004. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā ñātike viharati giñjakāvasathe. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami[T 5.0447]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

1004. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was staying at Ñātika in the Brick Hall. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, and having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:

“Sāḷho nāma, bhante, bhikkhu kālaṅkato; tassa kā gati ko abhisamparāyo? Nandā nāma, bhante, bhikkhunī kālaṅkatā; tassā kā gati ko abhisamparāyo? Sudatto nāma, bhante, upāsako kālaṅkato; tassa kā gati ko abhisamparāyo? Sujātā nāma, bhante, upāsikā kālaṅkatā; tassā kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo”ti?

“Venerable sir, the monk named Sāḷha has passed away. What is his destination, what is his future state? Venerable sir, the bhikkhunī named Nandā has passed away. What is her destination, what is her future state? Venerable sir, the lay follower named Sudatta has passed away. What is his destination, what is his future state? Venerable sir, the laywoman named Sujātā has passed away. What is her destination, what is her future state?”

“Sāḷho[M 3.0311], ānanda, bhikkhu kālaṅkato āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ [V 3.0423] diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi. Nandā, ānanda, bhikkhunī kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ [P 5.0357] parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyinī anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sudatto, ānanda, upāsako kālaṅkato tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī; sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissati. Sujātā, ānanda, upāsikā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā.

“Ānanda, the bhikkhu Sāḷha, having passed away, due to the destruction of the taints, dwelt having for himself directly known, realized, and attained the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in this very life. Ānanda, the bhikkhunī Nandā, having passed away, due to the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, was of spontaneous rebirth, destined to attain final Nibbāna there, being of the nature not to return from that world. Ānanda, the upāsaka Sudatta, having passed away, due to the complete destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, became a once-returner; having come to this world only once, he will make an end of suffering. Ānanda, the upāsikā Sujātā, having passed away, due to the complete destruction of the three fetters, became a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into states of woe, assured, and destined for enlightenment.”

“Anacchariyaṃ kho panetaṃ, ānanda, yaṃ manussabhūto kālaṃ kareyya; tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ce maṃ kālaṅkate upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipucchissatha. Vihesā pesā, ānanda, assa tathāgatassa. Tasmātihānanda[T 5.0448], dhammādāsaṃ nāma dhammapariyāyaṃ desessāmi; yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”.

“Indeed, Ānanda, it is not astonishing that a human being should pass away. If, each time someone has passed away, you were to approach me and ask about this matter, that would be a vexation for the Tathāgata. Therefore, Ānanda, I shall teach the discourse on the Dhamma named the Mirror of the Dhamma, endowed with which a noble disciple, if he so wishes, could declare of himself: ‘Hell is destroyed for me, the animal realm is destroyed, the realm of ghosts is destroyed, the planes of misery, the bad destinations, the lower worlds are destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into states of woe, assured, and destined for enlightenment.’”

“Katamo ca so, ānanda, dhammādāso dhammapariyāyo; yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”?

“And what, Ānanda, is that discourse on the Dhamma, the Mirror of the Dhamma, endowed with which a noble disciple, if he so wishes, could declare of himself: ‘Hell is destroyed for me, the animal realm is destroyed, the realm of ghosts is destroyed, the planes of misery, the bad destinations, the lower worlds are destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into states of woe, assured, and destined for enlightenment’?”

“Idha, ānanda, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ayaṃ kho so, ānanda, dhammādāso dhammapariyāyo; yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Here, Ānanda, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Thus is that Blessed One… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… and he is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration. This, Ānanda, is that teaching, the Mirror of the Dhamma, endowed with which a noble disciple, should he wish, could declare of himself by himself: ‘Hell is destroyed for me; the animal realm is destroyed for me; the realm of ghosts is destroyed for me; the plane of misery, the bad destination, and the lower world are destroyed for me. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to downfall, assured, and destined for enlightenment.’” The eighth.

(Tīṇipi suttantāni ekanidānāni).

(The three discourses have a single introduction.)

9. Dutiyagiñjakāvasathasuttaṃ

9. The Second Discourse at the Brick Hall

1005. Ekamantaṃ [M 3.0312][V 3.0424][P 5.0358] nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “asoko nāma, bhante, bhikkhu kālaṅkato; tassa kā gati, ko [T 5.0449] abhisamparāyo? Asokā nāma, bhante, bhikkhunī kālaṅkatā…pe… asoko nāma, bhante, upāsako kālaṅkato…pe… asokā nāma, bhante, upāsikā kālaṅkatā; tassā kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo”ti?

1005. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, the monk named Asoka has passed away. What is his destination, what is his future state? Venerable Sir, the bhikkhunī named Asokā has passed away… Venerable Sir, the layman named Asoka has passed away… Venerable Sir, the laywoman named Asokā has passed away. What is her destination, what is her future state?”

“Asoko, ānanda, bhikkhu kālaṅkato āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi…pe… (purimaveyyākaraṇena ekanidānaṃ).

“Ānanda, the monk Asoka, having passed away, through the destruction of the taints, realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having attained it, he dwelled therein… (The introduction is the same as in the previous explanation.)”

“Ayaṃ kho so, ānanda, dhammādāso dhammapariyāyo; yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti. Navamaṃ.

“This, Ānanda, is that teaching, the Mirror of the Dhamma, endowed with which a noble disciple, should he wish, could declare of himself by himself: ‘Hell is destroyed for me; the animal realm is destroyed for me; the realm of ghosts is destroyed for me; the plane of misery, the bad destination, and the lower world are destroyed for me. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to downfall, assured, and destined for enlightenment.’” Ninth.

10. Tatiyagiñjakāvasathasuttaṃ

10. The Third Discourse at the Brick Hall

1006. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kakkaṭo nāma, bhante, ñātike upāsako kālaṅkato; tassa kā gati, ko abhisamparāyo? Kaḷibho nāma, bhante, ñātike upāsako…pe… nikato nāma, bhante, ñātike upāsako…pe… kaṭissaho nāma, bhante, ñātike upāsako…pe… tuṭṭho nāma, bhante, ñātike upāsako…pe… santuṭṭho nāma, bhante, ñātike upāsako…pe… bhaddo nāma, bhante, ñātike upāsako…pe… subhaddo nāma, bhante, ñātike upāsako kālaṅkato; tassa kā gati ko abhisamparāyo”ti?

1006. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, the lay follower named Kakkaṭa in Ñātika has passed away. What is his destination, what is his future state? The lay follower named Kaḷibha, Venerable Sir, in Ñātika… Nikata… Kaṭissaha… Tuṭṭha… Santuṭṭha… Bhadda… and the lay follower named Subhadda in Ñātika has passed away. What is his destination, what is his future state?'

“Kakkaṭo[T 5.0450], ānanda, upāsako kālaṅkato pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Kaḷibho, ānanda [V 3.0425][P 5.0359] …pe… nikato, ānanda…pe… kaṭissaho, ānanda [M 3.0313] …pe… tuṭṭho, ānanda…pe… santuṭṭho, ānanda…pe… bhaddo, ānanda…pe… subhaddo, ānanda, upāsako kālaṅkato pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. (Sabbe ekagatikā kātabbā).

“Ānanda, the lay follower Kakkaṭa, having passed away, due to the destruction of the five lower fetters, is one of spontaneous arising and will attain Parinibbāna there, being one who does not return from that world. Kaḷibha, Ānanda… Nikata, Ānanda… Kaṭissaha, Ānanda… Tuṭṭha, Ānanda… Santuṭṭha, Ānanda… Bhadda, Ānanda… and the lay follower Subhadda, Ānanda, having passed away, due to the destruction of the five lower fetters, is one of spontaneous arising and will attain Parinibbāna there, being one who does not return from that world.”

“Paropaññāsa, ānanda, ñātike upāsakā kālaṅkatā pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Sādhikanavuti, ānanda, ñātike upāsakā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino; sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Chātirekāni kho, ānanda, pañcasatāni ñātike upāsakā kālaṅkatā tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā.

“Ānanda, more than fifty lay followers in Ñātika have passed away; due to the destruction of the five lower fetters, they are of spontaneous arising and will attain Parinibbāna there, being ones who do not return from that world. More than ninety lay followers in Ñātika, Ānanda, have passed away; due to the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, they are once-returners who, having come to this world only once, will make an end of suffering. Indeed, Ānanda, five hundred and six lay followers in Ñātika have passed away; due to the destruction of the three fetters, they are stream-enterers, not subject to fall into states of woe, assured, and bound for enlightenment.”

“Anacchariyaṃ kho panetaṃ, ānanda, yaṃ manussabhūto kālaṃ kareyya; tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ce maṃ kālaṅkate upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipucchissatha. Vihesā pesā, ānanda, assa tathāgatassa. Tasmātihānanda, dhammādāsaṃ nāma dhammapariyāyaṃ desessāmi; yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi [T 5.0451] khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”.

“Ānanda, it is not astonishing that a human being should die. If, whenever someone dies, you were to approach me and ask about this matter, this would be a weariness for the Tathāgata. Therefore, Ānanda, I shall teach a discourse on the Dhamma called the Mirror of the Dhamma, endowed with which a noble disciple, should he so desire, may declare of himself by himself: ‘For me, hell is destroyed, the animal realm is destroyed, the sphere of petas is destroyed, the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower world is destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to fall into states of woe, assured, with enlightenment as my final destination.’”

“Katamo ca so, ānanda, dhammādāso dhammapariyāyo; yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”.

“And what, Ānanda, is that discourse on the Dhamma called the Mirror of the Dhamma, endowed with which a noble disciple, should he so desire, may declare of himself by himself: ‘For me, hell is destroyed, the animal realm is destroyed, the sphere of petas is destroyed, the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower world is destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to fall into states of woe, assured, with enlightenment as my final destination’?”

“Idhānanda[P 5.0360], ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ayaṃ kho so, ānanda, dhammādāso dhammapariyāyo; yena samannāgato ariyasāvako ākaṅkhamāno attanāva [V 3.0426] attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo [M 3.0314] khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Here, Ānanda, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Thus indeed is the Blessed One… Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken… conducive to concentration. This, Ānanda, is that discourse on the Dhamma called the Mirror of the Dhamma, endowed with which a noble disciple, should he so desire, may declare of himself by himself: ‘For me, hell is destroyed, the animal realm is destroyed, the sphere of petas is destroyed, the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower world is destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to fall into states of woe, assured, with enlightenment as my final destination.’” The tenth.

Veḷudvāravaggo paṭhamo.

The Veḷudvāra Chapter, the First.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Rājā ogadhadīghāvu, sāriputtāpare duve;

Thapatī veḷudvāreyyā, giñjakāvasathe tayoti.

The Rāja, Ogadha, Dīghāvu, two other Sāriputta suttas, the Thapati, the Veḷudvāreyya, and three at the Giñjakāvasatha.

2. Rājakārāmavaggo

2. The Rājakārāma Chapter

1. Sahassabhikkhunisaṅghasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Community of a Thousand Nuns

1007. Ekaṃ [T 5.0452] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati rājakārāme. Atha kho sahassabhikkhunisaṅgho sahasso bhikkhunisaṃgho (sī.) yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhagavā etadavoca –

1007. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Rājakārāma. Then a community of a thousand bhikkhunīs approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. The Blessed One spoke these words to those bhikkhunīs standing to one side:

“Catūhi kho, bhikkhuniyo, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhikkhuniyo, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme [P 5.0361] …pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti, akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, bhikkhuniyo, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhunīs, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer, not of a nature to fall into the lower realms, assured, and destined for enlightenment. With what four? Here, bhikkhunīs, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, too, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken… conducive to concentration. Bhikkhunīs, a noble disciple endowed with these four qualities is a stream-enterer, not of a nature to fall into the lower realms, assured, and destined for enlightenment.” The first.

2. Brāhmaṇasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Brahmins

1008. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0427]. “Brāhmaṇā, bhikkhave, udayagāminiṃ nāma paṭipadaṃ paññapenti. Te sāvakaṃ evaṃ samādapenti – ‘ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, kālasseva uṭṭhāya pācīnamukho yāhi. So tvaṃ mā sobbhaṃ parivajjehi, mā [M 3.0315] papātaṃ, mā khāṇuṃ, mā kaṇḍakaṭhānaṃ kaṇḍakaṃ ṭhānaṃ (pī. ka.), mā candaniyaṃ, mā oḷigallaṃ. Yattha yattheva (syā. kaṃ.), yāni vā (sī.) papateyyāsi tattheva maraṇaṃ āgameyyāsi. Evaṃ tvaṃ, ambho purisa, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjissasī’”ti.

1008. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, the brahmins prescribe a practice called ‘leading to growth.’ They instruct their disciple thus: ‘Come, O man, rise early and go forth facing east. You should not avoid a pit, you should not avoid a precipice, you should not avoid a tree stump, you should not avoid a thorny place, you should not avoid a cesspool, you should not avoid a sewer pit. Wherever you might fall, right there you should meet death. Thus, O man, with the breakup of the body, after death, you will be reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world.’”

“Taṃ [T 5.0453] kho panetaṃ, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇānaṃ bālagamanametaṃ bālānaṃ gamanametaṃ (sī.) mūḷhagamanametaṃ na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati. Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, ariyassa vinaye udayagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ paññapemi; yā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

“But, bhikkhus, that course of the brahmins is a foolish course, a deluded course. It does not lead to disenchantment, not to dispassion, not to cessation, not to peace, not to direct knowledge, not to enlightenment, not to Nibbāna. And I, bhikkhus, in the discipline of the noble ones, make known the practice that leads to growth, which leads exclusively to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, and to Nibbāna.

“Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, udayagāminī paṭipadā; yā ekantanibbidāya…pe… nibbānāya saṃvattati? Idha[P 5.0362], bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti; dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ayaṃ kho sā, bhikkhave, udayagāminī paṭipadā ekantanibbidāya…pe… nibbānāya saṃvattatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is that practice leading to growth, which leads exclusively to disenchantment… to Nibbāna? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant, perfectly self-enlightened… teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ They are endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… They are endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. This, bhikkhus, is that practice leading to growth, which leads exclusively to disenchantment… to Nibbāna.”

3. Ānandattherasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse concerning the Elder Ānanda

1009. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā ca ānando āyasmā ca sāriputto sāvatthiyaṃ viharanti jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṃ [T 5.0454] ānandaṃ etadavoca – “katinaṃ kho, āvuso ānanda[V 3.0428], dhammānaṃ pahānā, katinaṃ dhammānaṃ samannāgamanahetu, evamayaṃ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti? “Catunnaṃ kho, āvuso, dhammānaṃ pahānā, catunnaṃ dhammānaṃ samannāgamanahetu, evamayaṃ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti.

1009. On one occasion the Venerable Ānanda and the Venerable Sāriputta were dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then, in the evening, the Venerable Sāriputta arose from his seclusion and approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Ānanda. Having exchanged courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “Friend Ānanda, by abandoning how many qualities and by being endowed with how many qualities is a person declared by the Blessed One to be a stream-enterer, not subject to falling away, assured, and destined for enlightenment?” “Friend, by abandoning four qualities and by being endowed with four qualities, a person is declared by the Blessed One to be a stream-enterer, not subject to falling away, assured, and destined for enlightenment.”

“Katamesaṃ [M 3.0316] catunnaṃ? Yathārūpena kho, āvuso, buddhe appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati tathārūpassa [P 5.0363] buddhe appasādo na hoti. Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato sutavā ariyasāvako kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati tathārūpassa buddhe aveccappasādo hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā”ti.

“Of which four? Friend, whatever kind of lack of confidence in the Buddha an uninstructed worldling is endowed with, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell—that kind of lack of confidence in the Buddha is not present in the noble disciple. And, friend, whatever kind of unwavering confidence in the Buddha an instructed noble disciple is endowed with, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world—that kind of unwavering confidence in the Buddha is present in them: ‘Thus is that Blessed One… a teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Bhagavā.’

“Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, dhamme appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati tathārūpassa dhamme appasādo na hoti. Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato sutavā ariyasāvako kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati tathārūpassa dhamme aveccappasādo [T 5.0455] hoti – svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… viññūhīti.

“And, friend, whatever kind of lack of confidence in the Dhamma an uninstructed worldling is endowed with, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell—that kind of lack of confidence in the Dhamma is not present in the noble disciple. And, friend, whatever kind of unwavering confidence in the Dhamma an instructed noble disciple is endowed with, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world—that kind of unwavering confidence in the Dhamma is present in them: ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One… to be realized by the wise.’

“Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, saṅghe appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati tathārūpassa saṅghe appasādo na hoti. Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato sutavā ariyasāvako kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati tathārūpassa saṅghe aveccappasādo hoti – suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti.

“And, friend, whatever kind of lack of confidence in the Saṅgha an uninstructed worldling is endowed with, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell—that kind of lack of confidence in the Saṅgha is not present in the noble disciple. And, friend, whatever kind of unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha an instructed noble disciple is endowed with, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world—that kind of unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha is present in them: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is of good conduct… an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’

“Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, dussīlyena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati tathārūpassa dussīlyaṃ na hoti. Yathārūpehi ca kho, āvuso, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato sutavā ariyasāvako [V 3.0429] kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati tathārūpāni ariyakantāni sīlāni honti akhaṇḍāni…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikāni. Imesaṃ [P 5.0364] kho, āvuso, catunnaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānā imesaṃ catunnaṃ [M 3.0317] dhammānaṃ samannāgamanahetu evamayaṃ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“And, friend, whatever kind of immorality an uninstructed worldling is endowed with, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell—that kind of immorality is not present in the noble disciple. And, friend, whatever kind of virtues dear to the noble ones an instructed noble disciple is endowed with, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world—those virtues dear to the noble ones are present in them, unbroken… conducive to concentration. It is, friend, through the abandoning of these four qualities and through being endowed with these four qualities that this person has been declared by the Blessed One to be a stream-enterer, not subject to falling away, assured, and destined for enlightenment.”

4. Duggatibhayasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Fear of a Bad Destination

1010. “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sabbaduggatibhayaṃ samatikkanto hoti. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako [T 5.0456] buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sabbaduggatibhayaṃ samatikkanto hotī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

1010. “Bhikkhus, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities has overcome all fear of a bad destination. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is... the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ They are endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma... in the Saṅgha... and are endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken... conducive to concentration. Bhikkhus, a noble disciple endowed with these four qualities has overcome all fear of a bad destination.”

5. Duggativinipātabhayasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Fear of a Bad Destination and Downfall

1011. “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sabbaduggativinipātabhayaṃ samatikkanto hoti. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sabbaduggativinipātabhayaṃ samatikkanto hotī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

1011. Monks, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities has completely overcome all fear of bad destinations and states of woe. What four? Here, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: 'For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant... the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.' He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma... in the Sangha... and is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken... and conducive to concentration. Monks, a noble disciple endowed with these four qualities has completely overcome all fear of bad destinations and states of woe." The fifth.

6. Paṭhamamittāmaccasuttaṃ

6. The First Discourse on Friends and Companions

1012. “Ye te, bhikkhave, anukampeyyātha, ye ca sotabbaṃ maññeyyuṃ – mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā – te, bhikkhave, catūsu sotāpattiyaṅgesu samādapetabbā[V 3.0430], nivesetabbā, patiṭṭhāpetabbā.
