Katamesu catūsu? Buddhe [P 5.0365] aveccappasāde samādapetabbā, nivesetabbā, patiṭṭhāpetabbā – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantesu sīlesu samādapetabbā, nivesetabbā, patiṭṭhāpetabbā akhaṇḍesu…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikesu. Ye te, bhikkhave, anukampeyyātha[T 5.0457], ye ca sotabbaṃ maññeyyuṃ – mittā vā amaccā [M 3.0318] vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā – te, bhikkhave, imesu catūsu sotāpattiyaṅgesu samādapetabbā, nivesetabbā, patiṭṭhāpetabbā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

1012. Monks, those for whom you would have compassion, and who would think it worth listening to—whether friends, companions, relatives, or kinsmen—they, monks, should be encouraged in, settled in, and established in the four factors of stream-entry. In which four? They should be encouraged in, settled in, and established in unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant … the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ They should be encouraged in, settled in, and established in unwavering confidence in the Dhamma … in the Sangha … They should be encouraged in, settled in, and established in virtues dear to the noble ones—which are unbroken … and conducive to concentration. Monks, those for whom you would have compassion, and who would think it worth listening to—whether friends, companions, relatives, or kinsmen—they, monks, should be encouraged in, settled in, and established in these four factors of stream-entry.” The sixth.

7. Dutiyamittāmaccasuttaṃ

7. The Second Discourse on Friends and Companions

1013. “Ye te, bhikkhave, anukampeyyātha, ye ca sotabbaṃ maññeyyuṃ – mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā – te, bhikkhave, catūsu sotāpattiyaṅgesu samādapetabbā, nivesetabbā, patiṭṭhāpetabbā. Katamesu catūsu? Buddhe aveccappasāde samādapetabbā, nivesetabbā, patiṭṭhāpetabbā – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā”ti.

1013. “Monks, those for whom you would have compassion, and those who would think they should listen—whether friends, companions, relatives, or kinsmen by blood—they, monks, should be encouraged to undertake, settled, and established in the four factors of stream-entry. In which four? They should be encouraged to undertake, settled, and established in unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: 'For this reason, that Blessed One is... the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.'”

“Siyā, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ aññathattaṃ – pathavīdhātuyā, āpodhātuyā, tejodhātuyā, vāyodhātuyā – na tveva buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa siyā aññathattaṃ. Tatridaṃ aññathattaṃ – so vata buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato ariyasāvako nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā pettivisayaṃ vā upapajjissatī”ti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. “Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantesu sīlesu samādapetabbā, nivesetabbā, patiṭṭhāpetabbā akhaṇḍesu…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikesu. Siyā, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ mahābhūtānaṃ aññathattaṃ – pathavīdhātuyā, āpodhātuyā, tejodhātuyā, vāyodhātuyā – na tveva ariyakantehi [P 5.0366] sīlehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa siyā aññathattaṃ. Tatridaṃ aññathattaṃ – so vata ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato ariyasāvako [T 5.0458] nirayaṃ vā tiracchānayoniṃ vā pettivisayaṃ vā upapajjissatīti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Ye te, bhikkhave, anukampeyyātha, ye ca sotabbaṃ maññeyyuṃ – mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā – te, bhikkhave[V 3.0431], imesu catūsu sotāpattiyaṅgesu samādapetabbā, nivesetabbā, patiṭṭhāpetabbā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Monks, there might be an alteration of the four great elements—the earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the air element—but there would not be an alteration for a noble disciple who is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha. This would be the alteration in that case: that a noble disciple endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha would be reborn in hell, or in the animal realm, or in the sphere of the petas. This situation does not exist. They should be encouraged to undertake, settled, and established in unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in unwavering confidence in the Sangha… and in the virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… conducive to concentration. Monks, there might be an alteration of the four great elements—the earth element, the water element, the fire element, and the air element—but there would not be an alteration for a noble disciple who is endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones. This would be the alteration in that case: that a noble disciple endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones would be reborn in hell, or in the animal realm, or in the sphere of the petas. This situation does not exist. Monks, those for whom you would have compassion, and those who would think they should listen—whether friends, companions, relatives, or kinsmen by blood—they, monks, should be encouraged to undertake, settled, and established in these four factors of stream-entry.” The seventh.

8. Paṭhamadevacārikasuttaṃ

8. The First Discourse on Wandering Among the Devas

1014. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā [M 3.0319] bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – jetavane antarahito devesu tāvatiṃsesu pāturahosi. Atha kho sambahulā tāvatiṃsakāyikā devatāyo yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho tā devatāyo āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

1014. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, in this very way—vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared among the Tāvatiṃsa devas. Then many devas of the Tāvatiṃsa realm approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna; having approached, they paid homage to the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna and stood to one side. To those devas standing to one side, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this:

“Sādhu kho, āvuso, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, āvuso, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sādhu kho, āvuso, dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… sādhu kho, āvuso, ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… [T 5.0459] samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi [P 5.0367] sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, āvuso, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

“Friends, it is indeed good to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: 'For this reason, that Blessed One is... the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.' Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, friends, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Friends, it is indeed good to be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Sangha… Friends, it is indeed good to be endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… conducive to concentration. Because of being endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, friends, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘He is indeed the Blessed One… a Teacher of devas and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is being endowed with… the Dhamma… the Saṅgha… with the virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. Because of being endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.” The Eighth.

9. Dutiyadevacārikasuttaṃ

9. The Second Discourse on Wandering Among the Devas

1015. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0432]. Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – jetavane antarahito devesu tāvatiṃsesu pāturahosi. Atha kho sambahulā tāvatiṃsakāyikā devatāyo yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ [M 3.0320] ṭhitā kho tā devatāyo āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

1015. At Sāvatthī. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm, vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared among the Tāvatiṃsa devas. Then a large number of Tāvatiṃsa devas approached the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this to those devas:

“Sādhu [T 5.0460] kho, āvuso, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, āvuso, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā. Sādhu kho, āvuso, dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, āvuso, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā”ti.

“Good indeed, friends, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘He is indeed the Blessed One… a Teacher of devas and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, friends, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, friends, is being endowed with… the Dhamma… the Saṅgha… with the virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. Because of being endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, friends, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā. Sādhu kho, mārisa moggallāna, dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa moggallāna, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā”ti. Navamaṃ.

“Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘He is indeed the Blessed One… a Teacher of devas and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Good indeed, Venerable Moggallāna, is being endowed with… the Dhamma… the Saṅgha… with the virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. Because of being endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, Venerable Moggallāna, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.” The Ninth.

10. Tatiyadevacārikasuttaṃ

10. The Third Discourse on Wandering Among the Devas

1016. Atha kho bhagavā – seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṃ vā bāhaṃ pasāreyya, pasāritaṃ vā bāhaṃ samiñjeyya, evameva – jetavane antarahito devesu tāvatiṃsesu pāturahosi. Atha [T 5.0461] kho sambahulā tāvatiṃsakāyikā devatāyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā [V 3.0433] bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā [P 5.0368] ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho tā devatāyo bhagavā etadavoca –

1016. Then the Blessed One—just as a strong man might extend his flexed arm or flex his extended arm—vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared among the Tāvatiṃsa devas. Then many devas of the Tāvatiṃsa realm approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and stood to one side. To those devas standing to one side, the Blessed One said this:

“Sādhu kho, āvuso, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, āvuso, evamidhekacce sattā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā. Sādhu kho, āvuso[M 3.0321], dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, āvuso, evamidhekacce sattā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti.

“Good indeed, friends, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘He is indeed the Blessed One… a Teacher of devas and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, friends, some beings here become stream-enterers, not subject to falling into the lower realms, certain, and destined for enlightenment. Good indeed, friends, is being endowed with… the Dhamma… the Saṅgha… with virtues cherished by the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration. Because of being endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones, friends, some beings here become stream-enterers, not subject to falling into the lower realms, certain, and destined for enlightenment.”

“Sādhu kho, mārisa, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanaṃ hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa, evamayaṃ pajā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā. Sādhu kho, mārisa, dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanaṃ hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgamanahetu kho, mārisa, evamayaṃ pajā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Good indeed, venerable sir, is being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘He is indeed the Blessed One… a Teacher of devas and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.’ Because of being endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, venerable sir, this populace becomes stream-enterers, not subject to falling into the lower realms, certain, and destined for enlightenment. Good indeed, venerable sir, is being endowed with… the Dhamma… the Saṅgha… with virtues cherished by the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration. Because of being endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones, venerable sir, this populace becomes stream-enterers, not subject to falling into the lower realms, certain, and destined for enlightenment.” The Tenth.

Rājakārāmavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Rājakārāma Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Sahassabrāhmaṇānanda[T 5.0462], duggati apare duve;

Mittāmaccā duve vuttā, tayo ca devacārikāti.

Sahassa, Brāhmaṇa, and Ānanda; two other suttas on states of woe; two spoken on friends and ministers; and three on wandering among devas.

3. Saraṇānivaggo

3. The Chapter on the Refuges

1. Paṭhamamahānāmasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse to Mahānāma

1017. Evaṃ [T 5.0463][V 3.0434][P 5.0369] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ, bhante, kapilavatthu iddhañceva phītañca bāhujaññaṃ ākiṇṇamanussaṃ sambādhabyūhaṃ. So khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ vā payirupāsitvā manobhāvanīye vā bhikkhū sāyanhasamayaṃ kapilavatthuṃ pavisanto; bhantenapi vibbhantenapi (sī.), bhamantenapi (ka.) hatthinā samāgacchāmi[M 3.0322]; bhantenapi assena samāgacchāmi; bhantenapi rathena samāgacchāmi; bhantenapi sakaṭena samāgacchāmi; bhantenapi purisena samāgacchāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, tasmiṃ samaye mussateva musateva (?) bhagavantaṃ ārabbha sati, mussati musati (?) dhammaṃ ārabbha sati, mussati saṅghaṃ ārabbha sati. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘imamhi cāhaṃ samaye kālaṃ kareyyaṃ, kā mayhaṃ gati, ko abhisamparāyo’”ti?

1017. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans in Kapilavatthu, in the Banyan Grove Monastery. Then Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this Kapilavatthu is rich, prosperous, populous, crowded with people, and with congested streets. When I, venerable sir, having attended upon the Blessed One or upon monks who are inspiring to the mind, enter Kapilavatthu in the evening, I encounter a roaming elephant, a roaming horse, a roaming chariot, a roaming cart, or a roaming man. At that time, venerable sir, my mindfulness directed towards the Blessed One indeed lapses, my mindfulness directed towards the Dhamma lapses, and my mindfulness directed towards the Saṅgha lapses. Then, venerable sir, this thought occurs to me: ‘If I were to pass away at this time, what would be my destination? What would be my future state?’”

“Mā bhāyi, mahānāma, mā bhāyi, mahānāma! Apāpakaṃ te maraṇaṃ bhavissati apāpikā kālaṃkiriyā kālakiriyā (sī. syā. kaṃ.). Yassa kassaci, mahānāma, dīgharattaṃ saddhāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sīlaparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ sutaparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ cāgaparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ, tassa yo hi khvāyaṃ kāyo rūpī cātumahābhūtiko cātummahābhūtiko (sī. syā. kaṃ.) mātāpettikasambhavo [P 5.0370] odanakummāsūpacayo [T 5.0464] aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammo. Taṃ idheva kākā vā khādanti gijjhā vā khādanti kulalā vā khādanti sunakhā vā khādanti siṅgālā sigālā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) vā khādanti vividhā vā pāṇakajātā khādanti; yañca khvassa cittaṃ dīgharattaṃ saddhāparibhāvitaṃ…pe… paññāparibhāvitaṃ taṃ uddhagāmi hoti visesagāmi.

“Do not fear, Mahānāma, do not fear, Mahānāma! Your death will not be a bad one, your passing will not be a bad one. For anyone, Mahānāma, whose mind has long been imbued with faith, imbued with virtue, imbued with learning, imbued with generosity, and imbued with wisdom, this body of his—which has form, is made of the four great elements, is born of mother and father, is built up by rice and gruel, and is subject to impermanence, to being scrubbed and massaged, to breaking apart and dispersal—is eaten right here by crows, vultures, hawks, dogs, jackals, or various kinds of creatures. But that mind of his which has long been imbued with faith… imbued with wisdom—that goes upwards, it goes to a superior state.”

“Seyyathāpi, mahānāma, puriso sappikumbhaṃ vā telakumbhaṃ vā gambhīraṃ udakarahadaṃ ogāhitvā bhindeyya. Tatra yā assa sakkharā vā kaṭhalā kathalā (pī. ka.) vā sā adhogāmī assa, yañca khvassa tatra sappi vā telaṃ vā taṃ uddhagāmi assa visesagāmi. Evameva kho, mahānāma, yassa [V 3.0435] kassaci dīgharattaṃ saddhāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ…pe… paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ tassa yo hi khvāyaṃ kāyo rūpī cātumahābhūtiko mātāpettikasambhavo odanakummāsūpacayo aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṃsanadhammo taṃ idheva kākā vā khādanti gijjhā vā khādanti kulalā vā khādanti sunakhā vā khādanti siṅgālā vā khādanti vividhā vā pāṇakajātā khādanti; yañca khvassa cittaṃ dīgharattaṃ saddhāparibhāvitaṃ…pe… paññāparibhāvitaṃ taṃ uddhagāmi hoti visesagāmi. Tuyhaṃ kho pana, mahānāma, dīgharattaṃ saddhāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ…pe… paññāparibhāvitaṃ cittaṃ[P 5.0371]. Mā bhāyi, mahānāma[M 3.0323], mā bhāyi, mahānāma! Apāpakaṃ te maraṇaṃ bhavissati, apāpikā kālaṃkiriyā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Suppose, Mahānāma, a man were to plunge a pot of ghee or a pot of oil into a deep pool of water and break it. Any gravel or potsherds from it would sink downwards, but the ghee or oil in it would rise upwards and go to a superior state. In the same way, Mahānāma, for anyone whose mind has long been imbued with faith… imbued with wisdom, this body of his—which has form, is made of the four great elements, is born of mother and father, is built up by rice and gruel, and is subject to impermanence, to being scrubbed and massaged, to breaking apart and dispersal—is eaten right here by crows, vultures, hawks, dogs, jackals, or various kinds of creatures. But that mind of his which has long been imbued with faith… imbued with wisdom—that goes upwards, it goes to a superior state. Now, Mahānāma, your mind has long been imbued with faith… imbued with wisdom. Do not fear, Mahānāma, do not fear, Mahānāma! Your death will not be a bad one, your passing will not be a bad one.” First.

2. Dutiyamahānāmasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse to Mahānāma

1018. Evaṃ [T 5.0465] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idaṃ, bhante, kapilavatthu iddhañceva phītañca bāhujaññaṃ ākiṇṇamanussaṃ sambādhabyūhaṃ. So khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ vā payirupāsitvā manobhāvanīye vā bhikkhū sāyanhasamayaṃ kapilavatthuṃ pavisanto; bhantenapi hatthinā samāgacchāmi; bhantenapi assena samāgacchāmi; bhantenapi rathena samāgacchāmi; bhante, napi sakaṭena samāgacchāmi; bhante, napi purisena samāgacchāmi. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, tasmiṃ samaye mussateva bhagavantaṃ ārabbha sati, mussati dhammaṃ ārabbha sati, mussati saṅghaṃ ārabbha sati. Tassa mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti – ‘imamhi cāhaṃ samaye kālaṃ kareyyaṃ, kā mayhaṃ gati, ko abhisamparāyo’”ti?

1018. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans in Kapilavatthu, in the Banyan Grove Monastery. Then Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, this Kapilavatthu is rich, prosperous, populous, crowded with people, and with congested streets. When I, venerable sir, having attended upon the Blessed One or upon monks who are inspiring to the mind, enter Kapilavatthu in the evening, I encounter a roaming elephant, a roaming horse, a roaming chariot, a roaming cart, or a roaming man. At that time, venerable sir, my mindfulness directed towards the Blessed One indeed lapses, my mindfulness directed towards the Dhamma lapses, and my mindfulness directed towards the Saṅgha lapses. Then, venerable sir, this thought occurs to me: ‘If I were to pass away at this time, what would be my destination? What would be my future state?’”

“Mā bhāyi, mahānāma, mā bhāyi, mahānāma! Apāpakaṃ te maraṇaṃ bhavissati apāpikā kālaṃkiriyā. Catūhi kho, mahānāma, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe [T 5.0466] …pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi.

“Do not fear, Mahānāma, do not fear, Mahānāma! Your death will not be a bad one; your passing will not be a bad one. A noble disciple, Mahānāma, who is endowed with four qualities is inclined towards Nibbāna, slopes towards Nibbāna, and heads towards Nibbāna. With which four? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Such is the Blessed One: he is an Arahant… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with the virtues cherished by the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration.”

“Seyyathāpi[V 3.0436], mahānāma, rukkho pācīnaninno pācīnapoṇo pācīnapabbhāro, so mūlacchinno katamena papateyyā”ti? “Yena, bhante, ninno yena poṇo yena pabbhāro”ti. “Evameva kho, mahānāma, imehi catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Suppose, Mahānāma, there is a tree inclined towards the east, sloped towards the east, and tending towards the east. If it were cut at the root, in which direction would it fall?” “Venerable sir, it would fall in the direction towards which it is inclined, sloped, and tending.” “Just so, Mahānāma, a noble disciple endowed with these four qualities is inclined towards Nibbāna, sloped towards Nibbāna, and tending towards Nibbāna.”

3. Godhasakkasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse with Godha the Sakyan

1019. Kapilavatthunidānaṃ[M 3.0324]. Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena godhā sakko tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā godhaṃ sakkaṃ etadavoca – “katihi [P 5.0372] katīhi (pī. ka.) rūpasiddhi oloketabbā tvaṃ, godhe, dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāsi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇa”nti?

1019. At Kapilavatthu. Then Mahānāma the Sakyan approached Godha the Sakyan. Having approached, he said to him: ‘Godha, by how many qualities do you recognize a person to be a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination?’”

“Tīhi khvāhaṃ, mahānāma, dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāmi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇaṃ. Katamehi tīhi? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti. Imehi khvāhaṃ, mahānāma, tīhi dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāmi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇaṃ.

“Mahānāma, I recognize a person who is endowed with three qualities as a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination. What three? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha thus: ‘The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way… an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ By these three qualities, Mahānāma, I recognize a person as a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination.”

“Tvaṃ pana, mahānāma, katihi dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ [T 5.0467] ājānāsi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇa”nti? “Catūhi khvāhaṃ, godhe, dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāmi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇaṃ. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, godhe, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi khvāhaṃ, godhe, catūhi dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāmi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇa”nti.

“But you, Mahānāma, by how many qualities do you recognize a person as a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination?” “Godha, I recognize a person endowed with four qualities as a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination. With what four? Here, Godha, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘That Blessed One is… the Teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration. By these four qualities, Godha, I recognize a person as a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination.”

“Āgamehi tvaṃ, mahānāma, āgamehi tvaṃ, mahānāma! Bhagavāva etaṃ jāneyya etehi dhammehi samannāgataṃ vā asamannāgataṃ vā”ti. “Āyāma, godhe, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā [V 3.0437] bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocessāmā”ti. Atha [P 5.0373] kho mahānāmo sakko godhā ca sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

“Wait, Mahānāma, wait, Mahānāma! Only the Blessed One would know of this, whether one is endowed with these qualities or not.” “Let us go, Godha, to where the Blessed One is and approach him. Having approached, we will report this matter to the Blessed One.” Then Mahānāma the Sakyan and Godha the Sakyan went to where the Blessed One was. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said this to the Blessed One:

“Idhāhaṃ[M 3.0325], bhante, yena godhā sakko tenupasaṅkamiṃ; upasaṅkamitvā godhaṃ sakkaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘katihi tvaṃ, godhe, dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāsi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇaṃ’? Evaṃ [T 5.0468] vutte, bhante, godhā sakko maṃ etadavoca –

“Venerable sir, I approached Godha the Sakyan and said this to him: ‘Godha, by how many qualities do you recognize a person as a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination?’ When this was said, venerable sir, Godha the Sakyan said this to me:”

“Tīhi khvāhaṃ, mahānāma, dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāmi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇaṃ. Katamehi tīhi? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti. Imehi khvāhaṃ, mahānāma, tīhi dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāmi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇaṃ. Tvaṃ pana, mahānāma, katamehi dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāsi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇa”nti?

“‘Mahānāma, I know a person endowed with three qualities to be a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination. With what three? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: “Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant… a Teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.” They are endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… They are endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: “The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples has practiced well… it is the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.” Mahānāma, I know a person endowed with these three qualities to be a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination. But you, Mahānāma, with what qualities do you know a person to be a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination?’”

“Evaṃ vuttāhaṃ, bhante, godhaṃ sakkaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘catūhi khvāhaṃ, godhe, dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāmi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇaṃ. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, godhe, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi khvāhaṃ, godhe, catūhi dhammehi samannāgataṃ sotāpannapuggalaṃ ājānāmi avinipātadhammaṃ niyataṃ sambodhiparāyaṇa’”nti.

“When this was said, venerable sir, I spoke thus to Godha the Sakyan: ‘Godha, I know a person endowed with four qualities to be a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination. With what four? Here, Godha, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: “Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant… a Teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.” They are endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… and they are endowed with virtues cherished by the noble ones, which are unbroken… conducive to concentration. Godha, I know a person endowed with these four qualities to be a stream-enterer, one not of a nature to fall into a woeful state, who is assured, and has the higher stages of enlightenment as his destination.’”

“Evaṃ [T 5.0469] vutte, bhante, godhā sakko maṃ etadavoca – ‘āgamehi tvaṃ, mahānāma, āgamehi tvaṃ, mahānāma! Bhagavāva etaṃ jāneyya etehi dhammehi samannāgataṃ vā asamannāgataṃ vā’”ti. “Idha[P 5.0374], bhante, kocideva dhammo samuppādo uppajjeyya, ekato assa bhagavā ekato bhikkhusaṅgho [V 3.0438] ca. Yeneva bhagavā tenevāhaṃ assaṃ. Evaṃ pasannaṃ maṃ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu. Idha, bhante, kocideva dhammo samuppādo uppajjeyya, ekato assa bhagavā ekato bhikkhusaṅgho bhikkhunisaṅgho ca. Yeneva bhagavā tenevāhaṃ assaṃ. Evaṃ pasannaṃ maṃ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu. Idha, bhante, kocideva dhammo samuppādo uppajjeyya, ekato assa bhagavā ekato bhikkhusaṅgho [M 3.0326] bhikkhunisaṅgho ca upāsakā ca. Yeneva bhagavā tenevāhaṃ assaṃ. Evaṃ pasannaṃ maṃ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu. Idha, bhante, kocideva dhammo samuppādo uppajjeyya, ekato assa bhagavā ekato bhikkhusaṅgho bhikkhunisaṅgho upāsakā upāsikāyo ca. Yeneva bhagavā tenevāhaṃ assaṃ. Evaṃ pasannaṃ maṃ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu. Idha, bhante, kocideva dhammo samuppādo uppajjeyya, ekato assa bhagavā ekato bhikkhusaṅgho bhikkhunisaṅgho upāsakā upāsikāyo sadevako ca loko samārako sabrahmako sassamaṇabrāhmaṇī [T 5.0470] pajā sadevamanussā. Yeneva bhagavā tenevāhaṃ assaṃ. Evaṃ pasannaṃ maṃ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretū”ti. “Evaṃvādī tvaṃ, godhe, mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ kiṃ vadesī”ti? “Evaṃvādāhaṃ, bhante, mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ na kiñci vadāmi, aññatra kalyāṇā aññatra kusalā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“When this was said, venerable sir, Godhā the Sakyan said this to me: ‘Wait, Mahānāma, wait, Mahānāma! Only the Blessed One would know whether one is endowed with these qualities or not.’ Here, venerable sir, if any occasion for a dispute were to arise, with the Blessed One on one side and the Saṅgha of monks on the other, I would be on the side of the Blessed One. May the Blessed One remember me as one with such confidence. Here, venerable sir, if any occasion for a dispute were to arise, with the Blessed One on one side and the Saṅgha of monks and nuns on the other, I would be on the side of the Blessed One. May the Blessed One remember me as one with such confidence. Here, venerable sir, if any occasion for a dispute were to arise, with the Blessed One on one side and the Saṅgha of monks, nuns, and male lay followers on the other, I would be on the side of the Blessed One. May the Blessed One remember me as one with such confidence. Here, venerable sir, if any occasion for a dispute were to arise, with the Blessed One on one side and the Saṅgha of monks, nuns, male and female lay followers on the other, I would be on the side of the Blessed One. May the Blessed One remember me as one with such confidence. Here, venerable sir, if any occasion for a dispute were to arise, with the Blessed One on one side and the Saṅgha of monks, nuns, male and female lay followers, the world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans on the other, I would be on the side of the Blessed One. May the Blessed One remember me as one with such confidence.” “Godhe, when you speak thus, what do you say to Mahānāma the Sakyan?” “Venerable sir, when I speak thus, I say nothing to Mahānāma the Sakyan other than what is good, other than what is wholesome.” The third.

4. Paṭhamasaraṇānisakkasuttaṃ

4. The First Discourse on Saraṇāni the Sakyan

1020. Kapilavatthunidānaṃ[P 5.0375]. Tena kho pana samayena saraṇāni sarakāni (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) sakko kālaṅkato hoti. So bhagavatā byākato – “sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Tatra sudaṃ sambahulā sakkā saṅgamma samāgamma ujjhāyanti khīyanti vipācenti – “acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ettha dāni ko na sotāpanno bhavissati! Yatra hi nāma saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato – ‘sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. Saraṇāni sakko sikkhādubbalyamāpādi, majjapānaṃ apāyī”ti.

1020. The origin at Kapilavatthu. At that time, Saraṇāni the Sakyan had passed away. He was declared by the Blessed One: 'A stream-enterer, not subject to falling into a woeful state, assured, destined for enlightenment.' Then, many Sakyans, having gathered and assembled, complained, were disdainful, and spoke disparagingly: 'Sirs, it is indeed astonishing! Sirs, it is indeed wonderful! At this rate, who will not become a stream-enterer? For Saraṇāni the Sakyan has passed away, and he was declared by the Blessed One: “A stream-enterer, not subject to falling into a woeful state, assured, destined for enlightenment.” Saraṇāni the Sakyan was weak in the training; he drank intoxicating liquor.'

Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “idha, bhante, saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato. So bhagavatā byākato – ‘sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. Tatra sudaṃ, bhante, sambahulā sakkā saṅgamma samāgamma ujjhāyanti khīyanti vipācenti – “acchariyaṃ [T 5.0471] vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho! Ettha dāni [V 3.0439] ko na sotapanno bhavissati! Yatra hi nāma saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato; so bhagavatā byākato [M 3.0327] – ‘sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. Saraṇāni sakko sikkhādubbalyamāpādi, majjapānaṃ apāyī”ti.

Then, Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the place where the Blessed One was. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said this to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, here Saraṇāni the Sakyan has passed away. He was declared by the Blessed One: “A stream-enterer, not subject to falling into a woeful state, assured, destined for enlightenment.” At that, Venerable Sir, many Sakyans, having gathered and assembled, complain, are disdainful, and speak disparagingly: “Sirs, it is indeed astonishing! Sirs, it is indeed wonderful! At this rate, who will not become a stream-enterer? For Saraṇāni the Sakyan has passed away, and he was declared by the Blessed One: ‘A stream-enterer, not subject to falling into a woeful state, assured, destined for enlightenment.’ Saraṇāni the Sakyan was weak in the training; he drank intoxicating liquor.”'

“Yo so, mahānāma, dīgharattaṃ upāsako buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato, so kathaṃ vinipātaṃ gaccheyya! Yañhi taṃ, mahānāma, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘dīgharattaṃ upāsako buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato’ti, saraṇāni sakkaṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya. Saraṇāni[P 5.0376], mahānāma, sakko dīgharattaṃ upāsako buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato. So kathaṃ vinipātaṃ gaccheyya!

“Mahānāma, that lay follower who for a long time has gone for refuge to the Buddha, gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and gone for refuge to the Saṅgha, how could he go to a state of ruin? Mahānāma, if one were to speak rightly, one would say: ‘A lay follower has for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and gone for refuge to the Saṅgha.’ Speaking of Saraṇāni the Sakyan, one would speak rightly. Mahānāma, Saraṇāni the Sakyan was a lay follower who for a long time had gone for refuge to the Buddha, gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and gone for refuge to the Saṅgha. How could he go to a state of ruin!”

“Idha, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… hāsapañño javanapañño vimuttiyā ca samannāgato. So āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.

“Here, Mahānāma, a certain person is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He has joyful wisdom, swift wisdom, and is endowed with liberation. Through the destruction of the taints, he has realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and dwells having attained it. This person also, Mahānāma, is freed from hell, freed from the animal realm, freed from the realm of ghosts, freed from the plane of misery, the bad destination, and the state of ruin.”

“Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe aveccappasādena [T 5.0472] samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… hāsapañño javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato. So pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā asmā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) lokā. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.

“But here, Mahānāma, a certain person is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He does not have joyful wisdom, does not have swift wisdom, and is not endowed with liberation. Through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, he is one of spontaneous birth, due to attain final Nibbāna there, not liable to return from that world. This person also, Mahānāma, is freed from hell, freed from the animal realm, freed from the realm of ghosts, freed from the plane of misery, the bad destination, and the state of ruin.”

“Idha [P 5.0377] pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… na hāsapañño na javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato. So tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī hoti, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ [V 3.0440] karoti[M 3.0328]. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.

Furthermore, Mahānāma, a certain person is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He is not endowed with joyful wisdom nor swift wisdom, and is not endowed with liberation. Through the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, he becomes a once-returner, returning only once to this world to make an end of suffering. This person, Mahānāma, is freed from hell, freed from the animal realm, freed from the realm of ghosts, freed from the plane of misery, the bad destination, the state of ruin.

“Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti; dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… na hāsapañño na javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato. So tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇoti[T 5.0473]. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.

Furthermore, Mahānāma, a certain person is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One’; he is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He is not endowed with joyful wisdom nor swift wisdom, and is not endowed with liberation. Through the destruction of the three fetters, he becomes a stream-enterer, is of a nature not to fall into the lower realms, is certain, and is destined for enlightenment. This person too, Mahānāma, is freed from hell, freed from the animal realm, freed from the realm of ghosts, freed from the plane of misery, the bad destination, the state of ruin.

“Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo na heva kho buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti… na dhamme…pe… na saṅghe…pe… na hāsapañño na javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato. Api cassa ime dhammā honti – saddhindriyaṃ, vīriyindriyaṃ, satindriyaṃ, samādhindriyaṃ, paññindriyaṃ. Tathāgatappaveditā cassa dhammā paññāya mattaso nijjhānaṃ khamanti. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo agantā nirayaṃ agantā tiracchānayoniṃ agantā pettivisayaṃ agantā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ.

Furthermore, Mahānāma, a certain person is not endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha… nor in the Dhamma… nor in the Saṅgha… nor is he endowed with joyful wisdom nor swift wisdom, and is not endowed with liberation. However, he has these qualities: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom. And the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata are, to a certain measure, acceptable to his contemplation with wisdom. This person too, Mahānāma, will not go to hell, will not go to the animal realm, will not go to the realm of ghosts, will not go to the plane of misery, the bad destination, the state of ruin.

“Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo na heva kho buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti… na dhamme…pe… na saṅghe…pe… na hāsapañño na javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato, api cassa ime dhammā honti saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ. Tathāgate cassa saddhāmattaṃ hoti pemamattaṃ. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo agantā nirayaṃ agantā tiracchānayoniṃ agantā pettivisayaṃ agantā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ. Ime cepi, mahānāma, mahāsālā subhāsitaṃ dubbhāsitaṃ ājāneyyuṃ, ime cāhaṃ imevāhaṃ (syā. kaṃ.), imesāhaṃ (ka.) mahāsāle byākareyyaṃ – ‘sotāpannā avinipātadhammā [T 5.0474] niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’ti; kimaṅgaṃ kimaṅga (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pana saraṇāniṃ sakkaṃ. Saraṇāni, mahānāma, sakko maraṇakāle sikkhaṃ samādiyī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

Furthermore, Mahānāma, a certain person is not endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha… nor in the Dhamma… nor in the Saṅgha… he is not possessed of joyful wisdom nor of swift wisdom, and is not endowed with liberation. Yet he has these qualities: the controlling faculty of faith… the controlling faculty of wisdom. And he has mere faith and mere affection for the Tathāgata. This person too, Mahānāma, will not go to hell, the animal realm, the sphere of ghosts, or to a state of deprivation, a woeful course, a place of ruin. Mahānāma, if these great sāla trees could know what is well-spoken and what is ill-spoken, I would declare of these great sāla trees: ‘They are stream-enterers, of a nature not to fall into states of woe, assured, with enlightenment as their destination.’ How much more so Saraṇāni the Sakyan? Mahānāma, Saraṇāni the Sakyan undertook the training at the time of death.”

5. Dutiyasaraṇānisakkasuttaṃ

5. The Second Discourse on Saraṇāni the Sakyan

1021. Kapilavatthunidānaṃ[V 3.0441][M 3.0329][P 5.0378]. Tena kho pana samayena saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato hoti. So bhagavatā byākato – “sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Tatra sudaṃ sambahulā sakkā saṅgamma samāgamma ujjhāyanti khīyanti vipācenti – “acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ettha dāni ko na sotāpanno bhavissati! Yatra hi nāma saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato. So bhagavatā byākato – ‘sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. Saraṇāni sakko sikkhāya aparipūrakārī ahosī”ti. Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

1021. At Kapilavatthu. At that time Saraṇāni the Sakyan had passed away. The Blessed One had declared about him: “He was a stream-enterer, not liable to fall into states of woe, assured, destined for enlightenment.” There, numerous Sakyans gathered and complained, grumbled, and criticized: “It is astonishing, friends, it is amazing! Who now will not be a stream-enterer? For Saraṇāni the Sakyan has passed away, and he was declared by the Blessed One as a stream-enterer, not liable to fall into states of woe, assured, destined for enlightenment. Saraṇāni the Sakyan was one who did not fulfill the training.” Then Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said to the Blessed One:

“Idha, bhante, saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato. So bhagavatā byākato – ‘sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. Tatra sudaṃ, bhante, sambahulā sakkā saṅgamma samāgamma ujjhāyanti khīyanti vipācenti – ‘acchariyaṃ vata, bho, abbhutaṃ vata, bho! Ettha dāni ko na sotāpanno bhavissati! Yatra hi nāma saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato. So bhagavatā byākato – sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇoti. Saraṇāni sakko sikkhāya aparipūrakārī ahosī’”ti.

“Here, venerable sir, Saraṇāni the Sakyan has passed away. He was declared by the Blessed One thus: ‘A stream-enterer, not subject to fall into states of woe, assured, and destined for enlightenment.’ Therein, venerable sir, many Sakyans, having gathered and assembled, complain, grumble, and criticize thus: ‘It is indeed astonishing, friends, it is indeed amazing! Who now will not become a stream-enterer? For Saraṇāni the Sakyan has passed away, and he was declared by the Blessed One thus: “A stream-enterer, not subject to fall into states of woe, assured, and destined for enlightenment.” Saraṇāni the Sakyan was one who did not fulfill the training!’”

“Yo [T 5.0475] so, mahānāma, dīgharattaṃ upāsako buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato, so kathaṃ vinipātaṃ gaccheyya! Yañhi taṃ, mahānāma, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘dīgharattaṃ upāsako buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato’, saraṇāniṃ sakkaṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya. Saraṇāni, mahānāma, sakko dīgharattaṃ upāsako buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato saṅghaṃ saraṇaṃ gato, so kathaṃ vinipātaṃ gaccheyya!

“Mahānāma, how could that lay follower who for a long time has gone for refuge to the Buddha, gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and gone for refuge to the Saṅgha, go to a state of ruin? Mahānāma, if one wished to say rightly, ‘For a long time a lay follower has gone for refuge to the Buddha, gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and gone for refuge to the Saṅgha,’ one would be speaking rightly of Saraṇāni the Sakyan. Mahānāma, Saraṇāni the Sakyan, a lay follower, for a long time had gone for refuge to the Buddha, gone for refuge to the Dhamma, and gone for refuge to the Saṅgha. How could he go to a state of ruin?”

“Idha, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe ekantagato hoti abhippasanno – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… hāsapañño javanapañño vimuttiyā ca samannāgato[M 3.0330]. So āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Ayampi kho, mahānāma[V 3.0442], puggalo parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.

“Here, Mahānāma, a certain person has perfect confidence in the Buddha and is extremely devout, reflecting: ‘Thus is the Blessed One… Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He has perfect confidence in the Dhamma… He has perfect confidence in the Saṅgha… He is joyful in wisdom, swift in wisdom, and is endowed with liberation. Through the destruction of the taints, in this very life, he realizes for himself with direct knowledge the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and abides having attained it. This person too, Mahānāma, is freed from hell, freed from the animal realm, freed from the realm of ghosts, freed from the planes of misery, bad destinations, and states of ruin.”

“Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe ekantagato hoti abhippasanno – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… hāsapañño javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato. So pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti, upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti, asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti, uddhaṃsoto hoti [T 5.0476] akaniṭṭhagāmī. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.

“Furthermore, Mahānāma, a certain person here is decisively confident and exceedingly pleased in the Buddha: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant... the Teacher of gods and humans... the Blessed One.’ They are decisively confident and exceedingly pleased in the Dhamma... and in the Saṅgha... They have joyful wisdom and swift wisdom, but are not endowed with liberation. With the destruction of the five lower fetters, they are an antarāparinibbāyin, an upahaccaparinibbāyin, an asaṅkhāraparinibbāyin, a sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyin, or one who goes upstream, bound for the Akaniṭṭha realm. This person too, Mahānāma, is freed from hell, freed from the animal realm, freed from the sphere of spirits, and from states of deprivation, bad destinations, and ruin.”

“Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe ekantagato hoti abhippasanno – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… na hāsapañño na javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato. So tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī hoti, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karoti. Ayampi kho, mahānāma[P 5.0379], puggalo parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.

“Furthermore, Mahānāma, a certain person here is decisively confident and exceedingly pleased in the Buddha: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant... the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ They are decisively confident and exceedingly pleased in the Dhamma... and in the Saṅgha... They have neither joyful wisdom nor swift wisdom, and are not endowed with liberation. With the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion, they are a once-returner, returning to this world just once to make an end of suffering. This person too, Mahānāma, is freed from hell, freed from the animal realm, freed from the sphere of spirits, and from states of deprivation, bad destinations, and ruin.”

“Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe ekantagato hoti abhippasanno – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… na hāsapañño na javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato. So tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.

“Furthermore, Mahānāma, a certain person here is decisively confident and exceedingly pleased in the Buddha: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant... the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ They are decisively confident and exceedingly pleased in the Dhamma... and in the Saṅgha... They have neither joyful wisdom nor swift wisdom, and are not endowed with liberation. With the destruction of the three fetters, they are a stream-enterer, not liable to fall into states of woe, assured, and destined for enlightenment. This person too, Mahānāma, is freed from hell, freed from the animal realm, freed from the sphere of spirits, and from states of deprivation, bad destinations, and ruin.”

“Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo na heva kho buddhe ekantagato hoti abhippasanno…pe… na dhamme…pe… na saṅghe…pe… na [T 5.0477] hāsapañño na javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato; api cassa ime dhammā honti – saddhindriyaṃ [M 3.0331] …pe… paññindriyaṃ. Tathāgatappaveditā [V 3.0443] cassa dhammā paññāya mattaso nijjhānaṃ khamanti. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo agantā nirayaṃ agantā tiracchānayoniṃ agantā pettivisayaṃ agantā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ.

“Furthermore, Mahānāma, here a certain person is not decisively established and exceedingly confident in the Buddha… nor in the Dhamma… nor in the Saṅgha… he is not of joyful wisdom nor of swift wisdom, and is not endowed with liberation. However, he has these qualities: the faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. And the teachings proclaimed by the Tathāgata are acceptable for contemplation by his wisdom to a certain measure. This person also, Mahānāma, will not go to hell, the animal realm, the sphere of petas, or any state of deprivation, bad destination, or downfall.”

“Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo na heva kho buddhe ekantagato hoti abhippasanno… na dhamme…pe… na saṅghe…pe… na hāsapañño na javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato; api cassa ime dhammā honti – saddhindriyaṃ…pe… paññindriyaṃ. Tathāgate cassa saddhāmattaṃ hoti pemamattaṃ. Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo agantā nirayaṃ agantā tiracchānayoniṃ agantā pettivisayaṃ agantā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ.

“Furthermore, Mahānāma, here a certain person is not decisively established and exceedingly confident in the Buddha… nor in the Dhamma… nor in the Saṅgha… he is not of joyful wisdom nor of swift wisdom, and is not endowed with liberation. However, he has these qualities: the faculty of faith… the faculty of wisdom. And he has mere faith and mere affection for the Tathāgata. This person also, Mahānāma, will not go to hell, the animal realm, the sphere of petas, or any state of deprivation, bad destination, or downfall.”

“Seyyathāpi, mahānāma, dukkhettaṃ dubbhūmaṃ avihatakhāṇukaṃ, bījāni cassu khaṇḍāni pūtīni vātātapahatāni asārādāni asukhasayitāni asukhāpassayitāni (ka.), devo ca na sammā devo pana sammā (syā. kaṃ.), devo na sammā (ka.) dī. ni. 2.438 dhāraṃ anuppaveccheyya. Api nu tāni bījāni vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyyu”nti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Evameva kho, mahānāma, idha dhammo durakkhāto dvākkhāto (pī. ka.) hoti duppavedito aniyyāniko anupasamasaṃvattaniko asammāsambuddhappavedito – idamahaṃ dukkhettasmiṃ vadāmi. Tasmiñca [P 5.0380] dhamme sāvako viharati dhammānudhammappaṭipanno [T 5.0478] sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī – idamahaṃ dubbījasmiṃ vadāmi”.

“Suppose, Mahānāma, there is a bad field, with bad soil, and with stumps not removed. And the seeds are broken, rotten, damaged by wind and heat, without essence, and not properly stored. And the rain does not fall properly. Would those seeds grow, increase, and thrive?” “No, venerable sir.” “Just so, Mahānāma, here the Dhamma is poorly taught, poorly proclaimed, not leading to deliverance, not conducive to peace, not proclaimed by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One—this I call the bad field. And in this Dhamma, a disciple dwells practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing properly, living in line with the Dhamma—this I call the bad seed.”

“Seyyathāpi, mahānāma, sukhettaṃ subhūmaṃ suvihatakhāṇukaṃ, bījāni cassu akhaṇḍāni apūtīni avātātapahatāni sārādāni sukhasayitāni; devo ca devo cassa (syā. kaṃ. ka.) sammā dhāraṃ anuppaveccheyya. Api nu tāni bījāni vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjeyyu”nti? “Evaṃ, bhante”. “Evameva kho, mahānāma, idha dhammo svākkhāto hoti suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito – idamahaṃ sukhettasmiṃ vadāmi. Tasmiñca dhamme sāvako viharati dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī – idamahaṃ subījasmiṃ vadāmi. Kimaṅgaṃ pana saraṇāniṃ sakkaṃ! Saraṇāni, mahānāma, sakko maraṇakāle sikkhāya paripūrakārī ahosī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Suppose, Mahānāma, there is a good field with good soil, with stumps well-removed, and the seeds are unbroken, not rotten, undamaged by wind and sun, fertile, and well-kept; and the rain should fall with a proper shower. Would those seeds attain growth, increase, and abundance?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Just so, Mahānāma, here the Dhamma is well-expounded, well-proclaimed, leading to liberation, conducive to peace, proclaimed by the Perfectly Enlightened One—this I say is like a good field. And in that Dhamma, a disciple dwells practicing in accordance with the Dhamma, practicing properly, living in conformity with the Dhamma—this I say is like good seed. What then to say of Saraṇāni the Sakyan! Mahānāma, Saraṇāni the Sakyan, at the time of his death, was a fulfiller of the training.” The fifth.

6. Paṭhamaanāthapiṇḍikasuttaṃ

6. The First Anāthapiṇḍika Sutta.

1022. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[V 3.0444][M 3.0332]. Tena kho pana samayena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vanda – ‘anāthapiṇḍiko, bhante, gahapati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’”ti.

1022. At Sāvatthī. At that time, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika addressed a certain man: "Come, good man, go to the Venerable Sāriputta; having approached, bow down with your head at the feet of the Venerable Sāriputta with my words, saying: 'Venerable sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. He bows down with his head at the feet of the Venerable Sāriputta.' And also say this: 'It would be good, venerable sir, if the Venerable Sāriputta would approach the dwelling of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, out of compassion.'"

“Evaṃ[P 5.0381], bhante”ti kho so [T 5.0479] puriso anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa paṭissutvā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca –

"Very well, sir." Having replied in assent to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, that man approached the place where the Venerable Sāriputta was. Having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Sāriputta, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that man said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“Anāthapiṇḍiko, bhante, gahapati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandati. Evañca vadati – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’”ti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā sāriputto tuṇhībhāvena.

“Venerable sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head at the feet of the Venerable Sāriputta and says this: ‘Venerable sir, it would be good if the Venerable Sāriputta would approach the dwelling of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, out of compassion.’” The Venerable Sāriputta consented by remaining silent.

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āyasmatā ānandena pacchāsamaṇena yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho āyasmā sāriputto anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “kacci te, gahapati, khamanīyaṃ kacci yāpanīyaṃ? Kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti? “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṃ, na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.

Then, in the morning, the Venerable Sāriputta, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, went with the Venerable Ānanda as his attendant to the dwelling of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika. On arrival, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Venerable Sāriputta said to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: ‘Householder, are you bearing up? Are you getting by? Are your painful feelings subsiding and not increasing? Is their subsiding apparent, and not their increasing?’ ‘Venerable sir, I am not bearing up; I am not getting by. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding; their increase is apparent, not their subsiding.’”

“Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, buddhe appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā [V 3.0445] paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati [M 3.0333] tathārūpo te buddhe appasādo natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, buddhe aveccappasādo – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Tañca pana te buddhe aveccappasādaṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

“Householder, with whatever kind of lack of faith in the Buddha an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell. You do not have that kind of lack of faith in the Buddha. But you, householder, have unwavering faith in the Buddha: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… a teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ And for you, contemplating that unwavering faith in the Buddha within yourself, the painful feelings might be pacified on the spot.

“Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, dhamme appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā [P 5.0382] apāyaṃ duggatiṃ [T 5.0480] vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpo te dhamme appasādo natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, dhamme aveccappasādo – svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhīti. Tañca pana te dhamme aveccappasādaṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

“Householder, with whatever kind of lack of faith in the Dhamma an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell. You do not have that kind of lack of faith in the Dhamma. But you, householder, have unwavering faith in the Dhamma: 'The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One... to be realized for oneself by the wise.' And for you, contemplating that unwavering faith in the Dhamma within yourself, the painful feelings might be pacified on the spot.

“Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, saṅghe appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpo te saṅghe appasādo natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, saṅghe aveccappasādo – suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti. Tañca pana te saṅghe aveccappasādaṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

“Householder, with whatever kind of lack of faith in the Saṅgha an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell. You do not have that kind of lack of faith in the Saṅgha. But you, householder, have unwavering faith in the Saṅgha: 'The Saṅgha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way... the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.' And for you, contemplating that unwavering faith in the Saṅgha within yourself, the painful feelings might be pacified on the spot.

“Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, dussīlyena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpaṃ te dussīlyaṃ natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, ariyakantāni sīlāni…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikāni. Tāni ca pana te ariyakantāni sīlāni attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

“Householder, with whatever kind of immorality an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell. You do not have that kind of immorality. But you, householder, have the virtues dear to the noble ones... conducive to concentration. And for you, contemplating those virtues dear to the noble ones within yourself, the painful feelings might be pacified on the spot.

“Yathārūpāya kho, gahapati, micchādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato assutavā puthujjano [T 5.0481] kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpā te micchādiṭṭhi natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammādiṭṭhi. Tañca pana te sammādiṭṭhiṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

“Householder, with whatever kind of wrong view an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell. You do not have that kind of wrong view. But you, householder, have right view. And for you, contemplating that right view within yourself, the painful feelings might be pacified on the spot.

“Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, micchāsaṅkappena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā [V 3.0446] paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati[M 3.0334], tathārūpo te micchāsaṅkappo natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāsaṅkappo. Tañca pana te sammāsaṅkappaṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

“Householder, with whatever kind of wrong intention an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell. You do not have that kind of wrong intention. But you, householder, have right intention. And for you, contemplating that right intention within yourself, the painful feelings might be pacified on the spot.

“Yathārūpāya [P 5.0383] kho, gahapati, micchāvācāya samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpā te micchāvācā natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāvācā. Tañca pana te sammāvācaṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

Householder, that kind of wrong speech with which an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell—that kind of wrong speech is not found in you. Indeed, householder, you have right speech. And for you, while clearly discerning that right speech within yourself, the feelings should be calmed on the spot.

“Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, micchākammantena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpo te micchākammanto natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammākammanto. Tañca pana te sammākammantaṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

Householder, that kind of wrong action with which an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell—that kind of wrong action is not found in you. Indeed, householder, you have right action. And for you, while clearly discerning that right action within yourself, the feelings should be calmed on the spot.

“Yathārūpena [T 5.0482] kho, gahapati, micchāājīvena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpo te micchāājīvo natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāājīvo. Tañca pana te sammāājīvaṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

Householder, that kind of wrong livelihood with which an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell—that kind of wrong livelihood is not found in you. Indeed, householder, you have right livelihood. And for you, while clearly discerning that right livelihood within yourself, the feelings should be calmed on the spot.

“Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, micchāvāyāmena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpo te micchāvāyāmo natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāvāyāmo. Tañca pana te sammāvāyāmaṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

Householder, that kind of wrong effort with which an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell—that kind of wrong effort is not found in you. Indeed, householder, you have right effort. And for you, while clearly discerning that right effort within yourself, the feelings should be calmed on the spot.

“Yathārūpāya kho, gahapati, micchāsatiyā samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpā te micchāsati natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāsati. Tañca pana te sammāsatiṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

Householder, that kind of wrong mindfulness with which an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell—that kind of wrong mindfulness is not found in you. Indeed, householder, you have right mindfulness. And for you, while clearly discerning that right mindfulness within yourself, the feelings should be calmed on the spot.

“Yathārūpena [V 3.0447] kho, gahapati, micchāsamādhinā samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati[M 3.0335], tathārūpo te micchāsamādhi natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāsamādhi. Tañca pana te sammāsamādhiṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

Householder, that kind of wrong concentration with which an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell—that kind of wrong concentration is not found in you. Indeed, householder, you have right concentration. And for you, while clearly discerning that right concentration within yourself, the feelings should be calmed on the spot.

“Yathārūpena [T 5.0483][P 5.0384] kho, gahapati, micchāñāṇena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpaṃ te micchāñāṇaṃ natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāñāṇaṃ. Tañca pana te sammāñāṇaṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.

Householder, that kind of wrong knowledge with which an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell—that kind of wrong knowledge is not found in you. Indeed, householder, you have right knowledge. And for you, while clearly discerning that right knowledge within yourself, the feelings should be calmed on the spot.

“Yathārūpāya kho, gahapati, micchāvimuttiyā samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati, tathārūpā te micchāvimutti natthi. Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāvimutti. Tañca pana te sammāvimuttiṃ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyyā”ti.

Householder, that kind of wrong release with which an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed, on account of which, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell—that kind of wrong release is not found in you. Indeed, householder, you have right release. And for you, while clearly discerning that right release within yourself, the feelings should be calmed on the spot.”

Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambhiṃsu. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati āyasmantañca sāriputtaṃ āyasmantañca ānandaṃ sakeneva thālipākena parivisi. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ aññataraṃ nīcāsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [T 5.0484] nisinnaṃ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ āyasmā sāriputto imāhi gāthāhi anumodi –

Then the feelings of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika were calmed on the spot. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika served the Venerable Sāriputta and the Venerable Ānanda from his own cooking pot. Then, when the Venerable Sāriputta had finished his meal and withdrawn his hand from the bowl, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika took a certain low seat and sat down to one side. To the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, who was sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta expressed his appreciation with these verses:

“Yassa saddhā tathāgate, acalā suppatiṭṭhitā;

Sīlañca yassa kalyāṇaṃ, ariyakantaṃ pasaṃsitaṃ.

‘He whose faith in the Tathāgata is unwavering and well-established; and whose virtuous conduct is excellent, beloved by the noble ones, and praised;

“Saṅghe pasādo yassatthi, ujubhūtañca dassanaṃ;

Adaliddoti adaḷiddoti (sī. syā. kaṃ.) taṃ āhu, amoghaṃ tassa jīvitaṃ.

He who has confidence in the Saṅgha, and whose view has been made upright; ‘He is not poor,’ they say, his life is not in vain.

“Tasmā [V 3.0448] saddhañca sīlañca, pasādaṃ dhammadassanaṃ;

Anuyuñjetha medhāvī, saraṃ buddhānasāsana”nti.

Therefore, let the wise one, remembering the teaching of the Buddhas, devote himself to faith and virtue, to confidence and the vision of the Dhamma.’”

Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

Then, having expressed his appreciation to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika with these verses, the Venerable Sāriputta rose from his seat and departed.

Atha [M 3.0336][P 5.0385] kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “handa! Kuto nu tvaṃ, ānanda, āgacchasi divādivassā”ti? “Āyasmatā, bhante, sāriputtena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati iminā ca iminā ca ovādena ovadito”ti. “Paṇḍito, ānanda, sāriputto; mahāpañño, ānanda, sāriputto, yatra hi nāma cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni dasahākārehi vibhajissatī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

Then the Venerable Ānanda went to the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. As the Venerable Ānanda was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said to him: “Well now, Ānanda, from where do you come in the middle of the day?” “Venerable sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was instructed by the Venerable Sāriputta with such and such an exhortation.” “Sāriputta is wise, Ānanda; Sāriputta has great wisdom, in that he will analyze the four factors of stream-entry in ten ways.”

7. Dutiyaanāthapiṇḍikasuttaṃ

7. The Second Discourse to Anāthapiṇḍika
