1023. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko [T 5.0485] gahapati aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – “ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vanda – ‘anāthapiṇḍiko, bhante, gahapati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Evañca vadehi – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā ānando yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’”ti.

1023. The setting is Sāvatthī. At that time the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika addressed a certain man: “Come, good man, approach the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, pay homage with your head to the feet of the Venerable Ānanda in my name, saying: ‘Venerable sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head to the feet of the Venerable Ānanda.’ And say this: ‘It would be good, venerable sir, if the Venerable Ānanda would approach the residence of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika out of compassion.’”

“Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho so puriso anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa paṭissutvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so puriso āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – “anāthapiṇḍiko, bhante, gahapati ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. So āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vandati. Evañca vadati – ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā ānando yena anāthapiṇḍikassa [V 3.0449] gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā’”ti. Adhivāsesi kho āyasmā ānando tuṇhībhāvena.

“Very well, master,” that man replied to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika. Then he approached the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, that man said this to the Venerable Ānanda: “Venerable sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill. He pays homage with his head to the feet of the Venerable Ānanda. And he says this: ‘It would be good, venerable sir, if the Venerable Ānanda would approach the residence of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika out of compassion.’” The Venerable Ānanda consented through silence.

Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho āyasmā ānando anāthapiṇḍikaṃ [M 3.0337] gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “kacci te, gahapati, khamanīyaṃ, kacci yāpanīyaṃ? Kacci dukkhā [T 5.0486] vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti? “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṃ na yāpanīyaṃ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṃ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.

Then, in the morning, the Venerable Ānanda dressed, took his bowl and robe, and approached the residence of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “Householder, are you enduring? Are you managing? Are your painful feelings subsiding and not increasing? Is their subsiding apparent, and not their increasing?” “Venerable sir, I am not enduring, I am not managing. My severe painful feelings are increasing, not subsiding. Their increasing is apparent, and not their subsiding.”

“Catūhi [P 5.0386] kho, gahapati, dhammehi samannāgatassa assutavato puthujjanassa hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṃ, hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano buddhe appasādena samannāgato hoti. Tañca panassa buddhe appasādaṃ attani samanupassato hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṃ, hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ.

“Householder, for an uninstructed ordinary person who is endowed with four qualities, there is alarm, there is trepidation, and there is fear of death concerning the next world. With what four? Here, householder, an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed with a lack of confidence in the Buddha. And when that person perceives that lack of confidence in the Buddha within themselves, there is alarm, there is trepidation, and there is fear of death concerning the next world.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano dhamme appasādena samannāgato hoti. Tañca panassa dhamme appasādaṃ attani samanupassato hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṃ, hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ.

“Furthermore, householder, an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed with a lack of confidence in the Dhamma. When they perceive that lack of confidence in the Dhamma within themselves, they experience alarm, trepidation, and fear of death regarding the next world.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano saṅghe appasādena samannāgato hoti. Tañca panassa saṅghe appasādaṃ attani samanupassato hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṃ, hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ.

“Furthermore, householder, an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed with a lack of confidence in the Saṅgha. When they perceive that lack of confidence in the Saṅgha within themselves, they experience alarm, trepidation, and fear of death regarding the next world.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano dussīlyena samannāgato hoti. Tañca panassa dussīlyaṃ attani samanupassato hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṃ, hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ. Imehi kho, gahapati, catūhi dhammehi samannāgatassa assutavato [T 5.0487] puthujjanassa hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṃ, hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ.

“Furthermore, householder, an uninstructed ordinary person is endowed with immorality. When they perceive that immorality within themselves, they experience alarm, trepidation, and fear of death regarding the next world. Householder, an uninstructed ordinary person endowed with these four qualities experiences alarm, trepidation, and fear of death regarding the next world.

“Catūhi [V 3.0450] kho, gahapati, dhammehi samannāgatassa sutavato ariyasāvakassa na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṃ, na hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Tañca panassa buddhe aveccappasādaṃ attani samanupassato na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṃ, na hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ.

“Householder, an instructed noble disciple endowed with four qualities does not experience alarm, trepidation, or fear of death regarding the next world. What four? Here, householder, an instructed noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ When they perceive that unwavering confidence in the Buddha within themselves, they do not experience alarm, trepidation, or fear of death regarding the next world.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… paccattaṃ veditabbo [M 3.0338] viññūhīti. Tañca panassa dhamme aveccappasādaṃ attani samanupassato na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṃ, na hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ.

“Furthermore, householder, an instructed noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: ‘The Dhamma is well proclaimed by the Blessed One… to be personally experienced by the wise.’ When they perceive that unwavering confidence in the Dhamma within themselves, they do not experience alarm, trepidation, or fear of death regarding the next world.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti. Tañca panassa saṅghe aveccappasādaṃ attani samanupassato na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṃ, na hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ.

“Furthermore, householder, an instructed noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: ‘The community of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way… an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ When they perceive that unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha within themselves, they do not experience alarm, trepidation, or fear of death concerning the next world.

“Puna caparaṃ, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Tāni ca panassa ariyakantāni sīlāni [T 5.0488] attani samanupassato na [P 5.0387] hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṃ, na hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhayaṃ. Imehi kho, gahapati, catūhi dhammehi samannāgatassa sutavato ariyasāvakassa na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṃ, na hoti samparāyikaṃ maraṇabhaya”nti.

Furthermore, householder, a learned noble disciple is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. When he perceives these virtues dear to the noble ones within himself, there is no alarm, there is no trepidation, there is no fear of death concerning the next world. For a learned noble disciple who is endowed with these four qualities, householder, there is no alarm, there is no trepidation, there is no fear of death concerning the next world.

“Nāhaṃ, bhante ānanda, bhāyāmi. Kyāhaṃ bhāyissāmi! Ahañhi, bhante, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato homi – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato homi – suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti. Yāni cimāni, bhante, bhagavatā gihisāmīcikāni sikkhāpadāni desitāni, nāhaṃ tesaṃ kiñci attani khaṇḍaṃ samanupassāmī”ti[V 3.0451]. “Lābhā te, gahapati, suladdhaṃ te, gahapati! Sotāpattiphalaṃ tayā, gahapati, byākata”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“Venerable Ānanda, I am not afraid. Why should I be afraid? For I, venerable sir, am endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, too, the Blessed One is… a teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ …in the Dhamma… I am endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: ‘The community of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way… an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ And, venerable sir, as for these training rules proper for householders that have been taught by the Blessed One, I do not perceive any breach of them in myself.” “It is a gain for you, householder! It is a great gain for you, householder! The fruit of stream-entry has been declared by you, householder.” Seventh.

8. Paṭhamabhayaverūpasantasuttaṃ

8. The First Discourse on the Quelling of Fear and Enmity

1024. Sāvatthinidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni ca honti, catūhi ca sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ariyo cassa ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni [M 3.0339] khīṇatiracchānayoniyo (sabbattha) khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto; sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”.

1024. At Sāvatthī. The Blessed One said to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, who was seated to one side: 'Householder, when for a noble disciple five fears and enmities are allayed, and he is endowed with the four factors of stream-entry, and the noble method is well-seen and well-penetrated by him with wisdom, then, if he so wishes, he may declare of himself: “I am finished with hell, finished with the animal realm, finished with the realm of ghosts, finished with the states of deprivation, bad destinations, and perdition; I am a stream-enterer, not subject to perdition, assured, with enlightenment as my final destination.”'

“Katamāni [T 5.0489] pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti? Yaṃ, gahapati, pāṇātipātī pāṇātipātappaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṃ [P 5.0388] veraṃ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvediyati. Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa evaṃ taṃ bhayaṃ veraṃ vūpasantaṃ hoti. Yaṃ, gahapati, adinnādāyī…pe… yaṃ, gahapati, kāmesumicchācārī…pe… yaṃ, gahapati, musāvādī…pe… yaṃ, gahapati, surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhāyī surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānappaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvediyati. Surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratassa evaṃ taṃ bhayaṃ veraṃ vūpasantaṃ hoti. Imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti.

“What are the five fears and enmities that are allayed? Householder, one who destroys life, on account of destroying life, generates fear and enmity in this very life and generates fear and enmity in the life to come, and he experiences mental suffering and displeasure. For one who abstains from destroying life, that fear and enmity is thus allayed. Householder, one who takes what is not given… one who engages in sexual misconduct… one who speaks falsely… Householder, one who partakes of liquors, wines, and intoxicants which are the basis for heedlessness, on account of partaking of liquors, wines, and intoxicants which are the basis for heedlessness, generates fear and enmity in this very life and generates fear and enmity in the life to come, and he experiences mental suffering and displeasure. For one who abstains from partaking of liquors, wines, and intoxicants which are the basis for heedlessness, that fear and enmity is thus allayed. These are the five fears and enmities that are allayed.”

“Katamehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti? Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti.

“With which four factors of stream-entry is he endowed? Here, householder, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant… Teacher of gods and humans, the Enlightened One, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration. He is endowed with these four factors of stream-entry.”

“Katamo cassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho? Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako [V 3.0452] paṭiccasamuppādaññeva sādhukaṃ yoniso manasi karoti – iti imasmiṃ sati idaṃ hoti, imassuppādā [T 5.0490] idaṃ uppajjati; iti imasmiṃ asati idaṃ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṃ nirujjhati; yadidaṃ avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti. Avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho…pe… phassanirodhā vedanānirodho, vedanānirodhā taṇhānirodho… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa nirodho hoti. Ayamassa [P 5.0389] ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho.

And what, for him, is the noble principle that is well seen and well penetrated with wisdom? Here, householder, a noble disciple attends well and wisely to dependent origination itself thus: ‘When this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises. When this does not exist, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases.’ That is: with ignorance as condition, formations come to be; with formations as condition, consciousness comes to be… Thus is the origin of this whole mass of suffering. But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very ignorance, comes the cessation of formations… Thus is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering. This, for him, is the noble principle that is well seen and well penetrated with wisdom.

“Yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, imehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ayañcassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho[M 3.0340]. So ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto; sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

When, householder, for a noble disciple these five fears and enmities are allayed, when he is endowed with these four factors of stream-entry, and this noble principle has been well seen and well penetrated by him with wisdom, he may, if he wishes, declare of himself: ‘I am finished with hell, finished with the animal realm, finished with the sphere of ghosts, finished with the planes of misery, the bad destinations, and the states of ruin. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to the lower realms, assured, with enlightenment as my final destination.’ The eighth.

9. Dutiyabhayaverūpasantasuttaṃ

9. The Second Discourse on the Quelling of Fear and Enmity

1025. Sāvatthinidānaṃ…pe… “yato kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, imehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ayañcassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho; so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto; sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti. Navamaṃ.

1025. At Sāvatthī. … “When, bhikkhus, for a noble disciple these five fears and enmities are allayed, and he is endowed with these four factors of stream-entry, and this noble principle has been well seen and well penetrated by him with wisdom, then, if he wishes, he can declare of himself: ‘I am finished with hell, finished with the animal realm, finished with the sphere of ghosts, finished with the planes of misery, the bad destinations, and the states of ruin. I am a stream-enterer, not subject to the lower realms, assured, with enlightenment as my final destination.’” The ninth.

10. Nandakalicchavisuttaṃ

10. The Discourse to Nandaka the Licchavi

1026. Ekaṃ [T 5.0491] samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Atha kho nandako licchavimahāmatto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho nandakaṃ licchavimahāmattaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

1026. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof. Then Nandaka, the great Licchavi minister, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One then said this to Nandaka, the great Licchavi minister, who was sitting to one side:

“Catūhi [V 3.0453] kho, nandaka, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno [P 5.0390] hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, nandaka, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, nandaka, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.

“Nandaka, a noble disciple who is endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to perdition, assured, and destined for enlightenment. With which four? Here, Nandaka, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ …in the Dhamma… …in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken… conducive to concentration. Nandaka, a noble disciple who is endowed with these four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to perdition, assured, and destined for enlightenment.

“Imehi ca pana, nandaka, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako āyunā saṃyutto hoti dibbenapi mānusenapi; vaṇṇena saṃyutto hoti dibbenapi mānusenapi; sukhena saṃyutto hoti dibbenapi mānusenapi; yasena saṃyutto hoti dibbenapi mānusenapi; ādhipateyyena saṃyutto hoti dibbenapi mānusenapi. Taṃ kho panāhaṃ, nandaka[M 3.0341], nāññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā sutvā vadāmi. Api ca yadeva mayā sāmaṃ ñātaṃ sāmaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sāmaṃ viditaṃ, tadevāhaṃ vadāmī”ti.

“Furthermore, Nandaka, a noble disciple who is endowed with these four qualities is endowed with longevity, both divine and human; endowed with beauty, both divine and human; endowed with happiness, both divine and human; endowed with retinue, both divine and human; endowed with dominion, both divine and human. I do not say this, Nandaka, having heard it from another ascetic or brahmin. But rather, what I myself have known, myself have seen, myself have understood, that is what I declare.”

Evaṃ [T 5.0492] vutte aññataro puriso nandakaṃ licchavimahāmattaṃ etadavoca – “nahānakālo, bhante”ti. “Alaṃ dāni, bhaṇe, etena bāhirena nahānena. Alamidaṃ ajjhattaṃ nahānaṃ bhavissati, yadidaṃ – bhagavati pasādo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

When this was said, a certain man said to Nandaka, the great Licchavi minister: “It is time for your bath, venerable sir.” “Enough now, friend, with this external bath. This internal bath will suffice, that is, this confidence in the Blessed One.”

Saraṇānivaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on Refuges.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Mahānāmena dve vuttā, godhā ca saraṇā duve;

Duve anāthapiṇḍikā, duve verabhayena ca;

Licchavī dasamo vutto, vaggo tena pavuccatīti.

Two were taught concerning Mahānāma, and the Godhā and two Saraṇāni suttas; two concerning Anāthapiṇḍika, and two on enmity and fear. The Licchavi is spoken of as the tenth. Therefore, it is called a chapter.

4. Puññābhisandavaggo

4. The Chapter on the Streams of Merit

1. Paṭhamapuññābhisandasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on the Streams of Merit

1027. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0493][V 3.0454][P 5.0391]. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro.

1027. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, there are these four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nourishments for happiness. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: 'For this reason, the Blessed One is...the teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.' This is the first stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nourishment for happiness.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo…pe… paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhīti. Ayaṃ dutiyo puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: 'The Dhamma is well proclaimed by the Blessed One… to be personally experienced by the wise.' This is the second stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nourishment for happiness.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti. Ayaṃ tatiyo puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha thus: 'The Saṅgha of the Blessed One's disciples is practicing the good way... the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.' This is the third stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nourishment for happiness.

“Puna [M 3.0342] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ayaṃ catuttho puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. This is the fourth stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nourishment for happiness. These, bhikkhus, are the four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nourishments for happiness.”

2. Dutiyapuññābhisandasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on the Streams of Merit

1028. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so [V 3.0455] bhagavā…pe… [T 5.0494] satthā devamanussānaṃ [P 5.0392] buddho bhagavāti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro.

1028. “Bhikkhus, there are these four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nourishments for happiness. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: 'For this reason, the Blessed One is... the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.' This is the first stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nourishment for happiness.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe….

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma... in the Saṅgha...

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṃ ajjhāvasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Ayaṃ catuttho puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple dwells at home with a mind rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, delighting in relinquishing, responsive to requests, delighting in the sharing of gifts. This is the fourth stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nourishment for happiness. These, bhikkhus, are the four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nourishments for happiness.”

3. Tatiyapuññābhisandasuttaṃ

3. The Third Discourse on the Streams of Merit

1029. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro.

1029. “Bhikkhus, there are these four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nourishments for happiness. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: 'For this reason, the Blessed One is... the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.' This is the first stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nourishment for happiness.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe….

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma... in the Saṅgha...

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā. Ayaṃ catuttho puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is wise, endowed with wisdom that discerns arising and passing away—noble, penetrative, and rightly leading to the complete destruction of suffering. This is the fourth stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, nourishment for happiness. These, bhikkhus, are the four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nourishments for happiness.”

4. Paṭhamadevapadasuttaṃ

4. The First Discourse on the Divine States

1030. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[M 3.0343]. Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, devānaṃ devapadāni avisuddhānaṃ sattānaṃ visuddhiyā apariyodātānaṃ sattānaṃ pariyodapanāya.

1030. At Sāvatthī. "Bhikkhus, these are four divine states for the purification of impure beings, for the cleansing of uncleansed beings.

Katamāni [V 3.0456] cattāri? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho [T 5.0495] bhagavāti. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ devānaṃ devapadaṃ avisuddhānaṃ sattānaṃ visuddhiyā apariyodātānaṃ sattānaṃ pariyodapanāya.

What are the four? Here, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: 'For this reason, the Blessed One is... the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.' This is the first divine state for the purification of impure beings, for the cleansing of uncleansed beings.

“Puna [P 5.0393] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe….

Furthermore, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma... in the Saṅgha...

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Idaṃ catutthaṃ devānaṃ devapadaṃ avisuddhānaṃ sattānaṃ visuddhiyā apariyodātānaṃ sattānaṃ pariyodapanāya. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri devānaṃ devapadāni avisuddhānaṃ sattānaṃ visuddhiyā apariyodātānaṃ sattānaṃ pariyodapanāyā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken... conducive to concentration. This is the fourth divine state for the purification of impure beings, for the cleansing of uncleansed beings. These, monks, are the four divine states for the purification of impure beings, for the cleansing of uncleansed beings.” Fourth.

5. Dutiyadevapadasuttaṃ

5. The Second Discourse on the Divine States

1031. “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, devānaṃ devapadāni avisuddhānaṃ sattānaṃ visuddhiyā apariyodātānaṃ sattānaṃ pariyodapanāya.

1031. Monks, there are these four divine states for the purification of impure beings, for the cleansing of uncleansed beings.

“Katamāni cattāri? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘kiṃ nu kho devānaṃ devapada’nti? So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘abyābajjhaparame khvāhaṃ etarahi deve [T 5.0496] suṇāmi. Na ca kho panāhaṃ kiñci byābādhemi tasaṃ vā thāvaraṃ vā. Addhāhaṃ devapadadhammasamannāgato viharāmī’”ti. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ devānaṃ devapadaṃ avisuddhānaṃ sattānaṃ visuddhiyā apariyodātānaṃ sattānaṃ pariyodapanāya.

What four? Here, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He reflects thus: ‘What, indeed, is the divine state?’ He understands thus: ‘I hear that the devas are of limitless non-affliction. And I, for my part, do not afflict any being, whether trembling or steadfast. Surely, I dwell endowed with the quality of the divine state.’ This is the first divine state for the purification of impure beings, for the cleansing of uncleansed beings.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe….

Furthermore, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha….

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. So iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘kiṃ nu kho devānaṃ devapada’nti[V 3.0457]? So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘abyābajjhaparame [M 3.0344] khvāhaṃ etarahi deve suṇāmi. Na kho panāhaṃ kiñci byābādhemi tasaṃ vā thāvaraṃ vā. Addhāhaṃ devapadadhammasamannāgato viharāmī’ti. Idaṃ catutthaṃ [P 5.0394] devānaṃ devapadaṃ avisuddhānaṃ sattānaṃ visuddhiyā apariyodātānaṃ sattānaṃ pariyodapanāya. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri devānaṃ devapadāni avisuddhānaṃ sattānaṃ visuddhiyā apariyodātānaṃ sattānaṃ pariyodapanāyā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

Furthermore, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. He reflects thus: ‘What, indeed, is the divine state?’ He understands thus: ‘I hear that the devas are of limitless non-affliction. And I, for my part, do not afflict any being, whether trembling or steadfast. Surely, I abide endowed with the quality of the divine state.’ This is the fourth divine state for the purification of impure beings, for the cleansing of uncleansed beings. These, monks, are the four divine states for the purification of impure beings, for the cleansing of uncleansed beings.” Fifth.

6. Devasabhāgasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Being of the Same Kind as the Devas

1032. “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgataṃ attamanā devā sabhāgataṃ kathenti. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Yā tā devatā buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā ito cutā tatrūpapannā tāsaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘yathārūpena kho mayaṃ buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā tato cutā idhūpapannā, ariyasāvakopi tathārūpena buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato ehīti devānaṃ santike’”ti.

1032. “Monks, the devas, being pleased, speak of one endowed with four qualities as being of the same kind. With what four? Here, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ Those devas who, endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha, passed away from here and were reborn there, think thus: ‘Just as we, endowed with such unwavering confidence in the Buddha, passed away from there and have been reborn here, so too this noble disciple is endowed with such unwavering confidence in the Buddha. He will come into the presence of the devas.’”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Yā tā devatā ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā ito cutā tatrūpapannā tāsaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘yathārūpehi kho mayaṃ ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā tato cutā idhūpapannā, ariyasāvakopi tathārūpehi ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato ehīti devānaṃ santike’ti. Imehi [T 5.0497] kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgataṃ attamanā devā sabhāgataṃ kathentī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Furthermore, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… and is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken… conducive to concentration. Those devas who, endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, have passed away from here and been reborn there, think thus: ‘Just as we, being endowed with virtues of such a kind, passed away from there and have been reborn here, so too is this noble disciple endowed with virtues of such a kind; he will come into the presence of the devas.’ Monks, the devas, pleased, speak of one endowed with these four qualities as being of the same kind.” Sixth.

7. Mahānāmasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse to Mahānāma

1033. Ekaṃ [P 5.0395] samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

1033. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Park. Then Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said this to the Blessed One:

“Kittāvatā [V 3.0458] nu kho, bhante, upāsako hotī”ti? “Yato kho, mahānāma, buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gato hoti, dhammaṃ saraṇaṃ gato hoti, saṅghaṃ [M 3.0345] saraṇaṃ gato hoti – ettāvatā kho, mahānāma, upāsako hotī”ti.

“Venerable sir, to what extent is one a lay follower?” “Mahānāma, when one has gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Saṅgha—to that extent one is a lay follower.”

“Kittāvatā pana, bhante, upāsako sīlasampanno hotī”ti? “Yato kho, mahānāma, upāsako pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti, – ettāvatā kho, mahānāma, upāsako sīlasampanno hotī”ti.

“But, venerable sir, to what extent is a lay follower accomplished in virtue?” “Mahānāma, when a lay follower abstains from destroying life, from taking what is not given, from sexual misconduct, from false speech, and from consuming intoxicants which are the basis for heedlessness—to that extent a lay follower is accomplished in virtue.”

“Kittāvatā pana, bhante, upāsako saddhāsampanno hotī”ti? “Idha, mahānāma, upāsako saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṃ – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Ettāvatā kho, mahānāma, upāsako saddhāsampanno hotī”ti.

“Venerable sir, to what extent is a lay follower accomplished in faith?” “Here, Mahānāma, a lay follower has faith; he has confidence in the enlightenment of the Tathāgata: ‘For this reason, too, the Blessed One is an Arahant… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ To this extent, Mahānāma, a lay follower is accomplished in faith.”

“Kittāvatā pana, bhante, upāsako cāgasampanno hotī”ti? “Idha, mahānāma, upāsako vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṃ ajjhāvasati muttacāgo [T 5.0498] payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato – ettāvatā kho, mahānāma, upāsako cāgasampanno hotī”ti.

“Venerable sir, to what extent is a lay follower accomplished in generosity?” “Here, Mahānāma, a lay follower dwells at home with a mind devoid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, delighting in relinquishment, responsive to requests, delighting in giving and sharing. To this extent, Mahānāma, a lay follower is accomplished in generosity.”

“Kittāvatā pana, bhante, upāsako paññāsampanno hotī”ti? “Idha, mahānāma, upāsako paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā – ettāvatā kho, mahānāma, upāsako paññāsampanno hotī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Venerable sir, to what extent is a lay follower accomplished in wisdom?” “Here, Mahānāma, a lay follower is wise, possessing the wisdom that comprehends arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and rightly leads to the complete destruction of suffering. To this extent, Mahānāma, a lay follower is accomplished in wisdom.”

8. Vassasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Rain

1034. “Seyyathāpi[P 5.0396], bhikkhave, uparipabbate thullaphusitake deve vassante taṃ udakaṃ yathāninnaṃ pavattamānaṃ pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūreti, pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūrā kusobbhe paripūrenti, kusobbhā paripūrā mahāsobbhe paripūrenti, mahāsobbhā paripūrā kunnadiyo paripūrenti, kunnadiyo paripūrā mahānadiyo paripūrenti, mahānadiyo paripūrā mahāsamuddaṃ mahāsamuddasāgaraṃ (sabbattha) saṃ. ni. 4.70 paripūrenti; evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa yo ca buddhe aveccappasādo, yo ca dhamme [V 3.0459] aveccappasādo, yo ca saṅghe [M 3.0346] aveccappasādo, yāni ca ariyakantāni sīlāni – ime dhammā sandamānā pāraṃ gantvā āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

1034. “Just as, monks, when rain with large drops falls on a mountain top, the water, flowing to a low-lying place, fills the mountain clefts, fissures, and ravines. When these are filled, they fill the small pools. When the small pools are filled, they fill the large pools. When the large pools are filled, they fill the small rivers. When the small rivers are filled, they fill the great rivers. When the great rivers are filled, they fill the great ocean. In the very same way, monks, for a noble disciple, the unwavering confidence in the Buddha, the unwavering confidence in the Dhamma, the unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha, and the virtues dear to the noble ones—these qualities, flowing on, go to the further shore and conduce to the destruction of the taints.”

9. Kāḷigodhasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Kāḷigodhā

1035. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena kāḷigodhāya sākiyāniyā nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho kāḷigodhā sākiyānī [T 5.0499] yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho kāḷigodhaṃ sākiyāniṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

1035. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans, at Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Park. Then the Blessed One, having dressed in the morning, took his bowl and robe and went to the residence of Kāḷigodhā the Sakyan lady; having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then Kāḷigodhā the Sakyan lady approached the Blessed One; having approached, she paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to Kāḷigodhā the Sakyan lady who was sitting to one side:

“Catūhi kho, godhe, dhammehi samannāgatā ariyasāvikā sotāpannā hoti avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā. Katamehi catūhi? Idha, godhe, ariyasāvikā buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… vigatamalamaccherena [P 5.0397] cetasā agāraṃ ajjhāvasati muttacāgā payatapāṇinī payatapāṇī (sabbattha) 3.30 moggallānasuttaṃ oloketabbaṃ vossaggaratā yācayogā dānasaṃvibhāgaratā. Imehi kho, godhe, catūhi dhammehi samannāgatā ariyasāvikā sotāpannā hoti avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti.

“Godhā, a noble female disciple endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into states of woe, assured, and destined for enlightenment. With which four? Here, Godhā, a noble female disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant… a teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ She is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… and she dwells at home with a mind free from the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, delighting in relinquishment, responsive to requests, delighting in giving and sharing. Godhā, a noble female disciple endowed with these four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into states of woe, assured, and destined for enlightenment.”

“Yānimāni, bhante, bhagavatā cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni desitāni, saṃvijjante te dhammā mayi, ahañca tesu dhammesu sandissāmi. Ahañhi, bhante, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… yaṃ kho pana kiñci kule deyyadhammaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ appaṭivibhattaṃ sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehī”ti. “Lābhā te, godhe, suladdhaṃ te, godhe! Sotāpattiphalaṃ tayā, godhe, byākata”nti. Navamaṃ.

“Venerable sir, these four factors of stream-entry that the Blessed One has taught are found in me, and I am seen in those qualities. For I, venerable sir, am endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant… a teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ In the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… and whatever offering there is in the family, all of it is shared without reservation with those who are virtuous and of good character.” “It is a gain for you, Godhā! It is well-gained by you, Godhā! The fruit of stream-entry has been declared by you, Godhā.”

10. Nandiyasakkasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse to Nandiya the Sakyan

1036. Ekaṃ [V 3.0460] samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho nandiyo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā [T 5.0500] bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho [M 3.0347] nandiyo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “yasseva nu kho, bhante, ariyasāvakassa cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ natthi sveva nu kho, bhante, ariyasāvako pamādavihārī”ti.

1036. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Park. Then Nandiya the Sakyan approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, Nandiya the Sakyan said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, if a noble disciple is entirely and completely without the four factors of stream-entry, is that noble disciple, venerable sir, said to be one who dwells heedlessly?"

“‘Yassa kho, nandiya, cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni sabbena sabbaṃ sabbathā sabbaṃ natthi tamahaṃ bāhiro puthujjanapakkhe ṭhito’ti vadāmi. Api ca, nandiya, yathā ariyasāvako pamādavihārī ceva hoti, appamādavihārī ca taṃ suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ[P 5.0398], bhante”ti kho nandiyo sakko bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

"Nandiya, one who is without the four factors of stream-entry in every respect and in every way, I declare as an outsider, one who stands in the faction of the worldlings. Moreover, Nandiya, as to how a noble disciple is one who dwells heedlessly and one who dwells heedfully, listen to that and pay close attention; I will speak." "Yes, venerable sir," Nandiya the Sakyan replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Kathañca, nandiya, ariyasāvako pamādavihārī hoti? Idha nandiya, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. So tena buddhe aveccappasādena santuṭṭho na uttari vāyamati divā pavivekāya, rattiṃ paṭisallānāya. Tassa evaṃ pamattassa viharato pāmojjaṃ na hoti. Pāmojje asati, pīti na hoti. Pītiyā asati, passaddhi na hoti. Passaddhiyā asati, dukkhaṃ viharati. Dukkhino cittaṃ na samādhiyati. Asamāhite citte dhammā na pātubhavanti. Dhammānaṃ apātubhāvā pamādavihārī tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

"And how, Nandiya, is a noble disciple one who dwells heedlessly? Here, Nandiya, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He, being satisfied with that unwavering confidence in the Buddha, does not strive further for seclusion by day and for solitude by night. For him, dwelling thus heedlessly, joy does not arise. When there is no joy, rapture does not arise. When there is no rapture, tranquility does not arise. When there is no tranquility, he dwells in suffering. The mind of one who is suffering does not become concentrated. When the mind is not concentrated, dhammas do not become manifest. Because of the non-manifestation of the dhammas, he is reckoned as one who dwells heedlessly."

“Puna caparaṃ, nandiya, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti [T 5.0501] akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. So tehi ariyakantehi sīlehi santuṭṭho na uttari vāyamati divā pavivekāya rattiṃ paṭisallānāya. Tassa evaṃ pamattassa viharato pāmojjaṃ na hoti. Pāmojje asati, pīti na hoti. Pītiyā asati, passaddhi na hoti. Passaddhiyā asati, dukkhaṃ viharati. Dukkhino cittaṃ na samādhiyati[V 3.0461]. Asamāhite citte dhammā na pātubhavanti. Dhammānaṃ apātubhāvā pamādavihārī tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Evaṃ kho, nandiya, ariyasāvako pamādavihārī hoti.

Furthermore, Nandiya, a noble disciple is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken... conducive to concentration. Content with those virtues dear to the noble ones, he does not strive further for seclusion by day and for solitude by night. For him, dwelling thus in heedlessness, joy does not arise. When joy is absent, rapture does not arise. When rapture is absent, tranquility does not arise. When tranquility is absent, he dwells in suffering. The mind of one who suffers does not become concentrated. When the mind is unconcentrated, phenomena do not manifest. Because of the non-manifestation of phenomena, he is reckoned as one who dwells in heedlessness. Thus, Nandiya, a noble disciple is one who dwells in heedlessness.

“Kathañca, nandiya, ariyasāvako appamādavihārī hoti? Idha, nandiya, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. So tena buddhe aveccappasādena asantuṭṭho uttari vāyamati divā pavivekāya rattiṃ paṭisallānāya. Tassa evaṃ appamattassa viharato pāmojjaṃ jāyati. Pamuditassa [M 3.0348] pīti jāyati. Pītimanassa kāyo passambhati. Passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vediyati. Sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati. Samāhite citte dhammā pātubhavanti. Dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā appamādavihārī tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati[P 5.0399].

And how, Nandiya, is a noble disciple one who dwells heedfully? Here, Nandiya, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha: ‘Indeed, that Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ Not content with that unwavering confidence in the Buddha, he strives further for seclusion by day and for solitude by night. For him, dwelling thus heedfully, joy arises. For one who is joyful, rapture arises. For one whose mind is enraptured, the body becomes tranquil. One whose body is tranquil experiences happiness. The mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated. When the mind is concentrated, phenomena manifest. Because of the manifestation of phenomena, he is reckoned as one who dwells heedfully.

“Puna caparaṃ, nandiya, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. So tehi ariyakantehi sīlehi asantuṭṭho uttari vāyamati divā pavivekāya rattiṃ paṭisallānāya[T 5.0502]. Tassa evaṃ appamattassa viharato pāmojjaṃ jāyati. Pamuditassa pīti jāyati. Pītimanassa kāyo passambhati. Passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vediyati. Sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati. Samāhite citte dhammā pātubhavanti. Dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā appamādavihārī tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Evaṃ kho, nandiya, ariyasāvako appamādavihārī hotī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

Furthermore, Nandiya, a noble disciple is endowed with faith in the Dhamma...pe... in the Saṅgha...pe... and with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken... conducive to concentration. Not being content with those virtues dear to the noble ones, he strives further for seclusion by day and for solitude by night. For him, dwelling thus heedfully, joy arises. For one who is joyful, rapture arises. For one with a rapturous mind, the body becomes tranquil. One with a tranquil body experiences happiness. The mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated. When the mind is concentrated, phenomena manifest. Because of the manifestation of phenomena, he is indeed reckoned as one who dwells heedfully. Thus indeed, Nandiya, a noble disciple is one who dwells heedfully.” Tenth.

Puññābhisandavaggo catuttho.

The Fourth Chapter on the Outpouring of Merit.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Abhisandā tayo vuttā, duve devapadāni ca;

Sabhāgataṃ mahānāmo, vassaṃ kāḷī ca nandiyāti.

Three suttas on Outpourings are taught, and two on Divine States; Sabhāgata, Mahānāma, Vassa, Kāḷī, and Nandiya.

5. Sagāthakapuññābhisandavaggo

5. The Chapter on the Outpouring of Merit with Verses

1. Paṭhamaabhisandasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on the Outpouring

1037. “Cattārome[V 3.0462][T 5.0503], bhikkhave, puññābhisandā, kusalābhisandā, sukhassāhārā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo puññābhisando, kusalābhisando, sukhassāhāro.

1037. “Bhikkhus, there are these four outpourings of merit, outpourings of the wholesome, which are sources of happiness. What are the four? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, that Blessed One is an arahant... Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ This is the first outpouring of merit, outpouring of the wholesome, a source of happiness.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe….

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma...pe... in the Saṅgha...pe...

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Ayaṃ catuttho [M 3.0349] puññābhisando, kusalābhisando, sukhassāhāro. Ime kho, bhikkhave[P 5.0400], cattāro puññābhisandā, kusalābhisandā, sukhassāhārā.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with the virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken... conducive to concentration. This is the fourth outpouring of merit, outpouring of the wholesome, a source of happiness. These indeed, bhikkhus, are the four outpourings of merit, outpourings of the wholesome, sources of happiness.”

“Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi puññābhisandehi kusalābhisandehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa na sukaraṃ puññassa pamāṇaṃ gaṇetuṃ – ‘ettako puññābhisando, kusalābhisando, sukhassāhāro’ti. Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandho tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

“Bhikkhus, for a noble disciple who is endowed with these four outpourings of merit, these outpourings of the wholesome, it is not easy to reckon the measure of merit thus: ‘The outpouring of merit, the outpouring of the wholesome, a source of happiness, is of such a measure.’ Rather, it is reckoned simply as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde na sukaraṃ udakassa pamāṇaṃ gaṇetuṃ – ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasatānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasahassānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasatasahassānī’ti vāti. Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo [T 5.0504] appameyyo mahāudakakkhandho tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, imehi catūhi puññābhisandehi kusalābhisandehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa na sukaraṃ puññassa pamāṇaṃ gaṇetuṃ – ‘ettako puññābhisando, kusalābhisando, sukhassāhāro’ti. Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandho tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchatī”ti.

“Just as, bhikkhus, in the great ocean it is not easy to reckon the measure of water thus: ‘There are this many measures of water,’ or ‘this many hundreds of measures of water,’ or ‘this many thousands of measures of water,’ or ‘this many hundreds of thousands of measures of water.’ Rather, it is reckoned simply as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of water. In the same way, bhikkhus, for a noble disciple who is endowed with these four outpourings of merit, these outpourings of the wholesome, it is not easy to reckon the measure of merit thus: ‘The outpouring of merit, the outpouring of the wholesome, a source of happiness, is of such a measure.’ Rather, it is reckoned simply as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.”

Idamavoca [V 3.0463] bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

This the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, then further said this:

“Mahodadhiṃ aparimitaṃ mahāsaraṃ,

Bahubheravaṃ ratanagaṇānamālayaṃ;

Najjo yathā naragaṇasaṅghasevitā,

Puthū savantī upayanti sāgaraṃ.

“Just as rivers frequented by throngs of people, flowing widely, approach the ocean—the great water-container, immeasurable, a great lake, filled with many terrors, an abode for collections of gems—

“Evaṃ naraṃ annapānavatthadadaṃ,

Seyyāni paccattharaṇassa sajjattharaṇassa (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) dāyakaṃ;

Puññassa dhārā upayanti paṇḍitaṃ,

Najjo yathā vārivahāva sāgara”nti. paṭhamaṃ;

“So too, streams of merit approach the wise person who gives food, drink, and clothing, and is a giver of beds and coverings, just as rivers that are bearers of water approach the ocean.” The first.

2. Dutiyaabhisandasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on the Outpouring

1038. “Cattārome[M 3.0350][P 5.0401], bhikkhave, puññābhisandā, kusalābhisandā, sukhassāhārā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro.

1038. “Bhikkhus, there are these four outpourings of merit, outpourings of the wholesome, which are sources of happiness. What are the four? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, that Blessed One is an arahant... Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ This is the first outpouring of merit, outpouring of the wholesome, a source of happiness.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe….

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma...pe... in the Saṅgha...pe...

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṃ ajjhāvasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Ayaṃ catuttho puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro[T 5.0505]. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puññābhisandā, kusalābhisandā, sukhassāhārā.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple dwells at home with a mind devoid of the stain of stinginess, is freely generous, open-handed, delighting in relinquishment, amenable to requests, delighting in giving and sharing. This is the fourth stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, a nourishment of happiness. These, bhikkhus, are the four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nourishments of happiness.

“Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi puññābhisandehi kusalābhisandehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa na sukaraṃ puññassa pamāṇaṃ gaṇetuṃ – ‘ettako puññābhisando, kusalābhisando[V 3.0464], sukhassāhāro’ti. Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandho tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati.

“Bhikkhus, for a noble disciple endowed with these four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, it is not easy to reckon the measure of merit thus: ‘The stream of merit, the stream of the wholesome, the nourishment of happiness is of such a measure.’ Rather, it is reckoned simply as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yatthimā mahānadiyo saṃsandanti samenti, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, tattha na sukaraṃ udakassa pamāṇaṃ gaṇetuṃ – ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasatānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasahassānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasatasahassānī’ti vāti. Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāudakakkhandho tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, imehi catūhi puññābhisandehi kusalābhisandehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa na sukaraṃ puññassa pamāṇaṃ gaṇetuṃ – ‘ettako puññābhisando, kusalābhisando, sukhassāhāro’ti. Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandho tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchatī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā…pe… satthā –

“Just as, bhikkhus, where these great rivers flow together and meet—namely, the Ganges, Yamuna, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—it is not easy to reckon the measure of the water thus: ‘So many measures of water,’ or ‘so many hundreds of measures of water,’ or ‘so many thousands of measures of water,’ or ‘so many hundreds of thousands of measures of water.’ Rather, it is reckoned simply as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of water. In the same way, bhikkhus, for a noble disciple endowed with these four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, it is not easy to reckon the measure of merit thus: ‘The stream of merit, the stream of the wholesome, the nourishment of happiness is of such a measure.’ Rather, it is reckoned simply as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.” This the Blessed One said… the Teacher:

“Mahodadhiṃ aparimitaṃ mahāsaraṃ,

Bahubheravaṃ ratanagaṇānamālayaṃ;

Najjo yathā naragaṇasaṅghasevitā,

Puthū savantī upayanti sāgaraṃ.

“Just as rivers frequented by multitudes of people, flowing widely, approach the ocean—the great water-holder, immeasurable, a great lake, of many dangers, an abode for collections of jewels;

“Evaṃ [T 5.0506][M 3.0351] naraṃ annapānavatthadadaṃ,

Seyyāni paccattharaṇassa dāyakaṃ;

Puññassa dhārā upayanti paṇḍitaṃ,

Najjo yathā vārivahāva sāgara”nti. dutiyaṃ;

“Thus, to the person who gives food, drink, and clothing, and gives beds and coverings, streams of merit approach that wise one, just as rivers bearing water approach the ocean.” Second.

3. Tatiyaabhisandasuttaṃ

3. The Third Discourse on Streams of Merit

1039. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, puññābhisandā, kusalābhisandā, sukhassāhārā. Katame cattāro? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo puññābhisando, kusalābhisando, sukhassāhāro.

1039. “Bhikkhus, there are these four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nourishments of happiness. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ This is the first stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, a nourishment of happiness.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe….

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha….

“Puna [V 3.0465] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato [P 5.0402] ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā. Ayaṃ catuttho puññābhisando kusalābhisando sukhassāhāro. Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is wise, endowed with wisdom regarding arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and rightly leads to the complete destruction of suffering. This is the fourth stream of merit, stream of the wholesome, a nourishment of happiness. These, bhikkhus, are the four streams of merit, streams of the wholesome, nourishments of happiness.

“Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi puññābhisandehi kusalābhisandehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa na sukaraṃ puññassa pamāṇaṃ gaṇetuṃ – ‘ettako puññābhisando, kusalābhisando, sukhassāhāro’ti. Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandho tveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchatī”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā…pe… satthā –

“For a noble disciple endowed with these four streams of merit, these streams of the wholesome, bhikkhus, it is not easy to calculate the measure of merit thus: ‘So much is the stream of merit, the stream of the wholesome, a nourishment of happiness.’ Rather, it is reckoned only as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.” This the Blessed One said… the Teacher:

“Yo puññakāmo kusale patiṭṭhito,

Bhāveti maggaṃ amatassa pattiyā;

So dhammasārādhigamo khaye rato,

Na vedhati maccurājāgamanasmi”nti maccurājāgamissatīti (sī. pī.), maccujarākampisminti (ka.). tatiyaṃ;

“One who desires merit, established in the wholesome, develops the path for the attainment of the Deathless. That one, having attained the essence of the Dhamma, delights in destruction, and does not tremble at the coming of the King of Death.” Third.

4. Paṭhamamahaddhanasuttaṃ

4. The First Discourse on Being Greatly Wealthy

1040. “Catūhi[M 3.0352], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako ‘aḍḍho mahaddhano [T 5.0507] mahābhogo’ti mahābhogo mahāyasoti (syā. pī. ka.) vuccati.

1040. “Bhikkhus, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities is called ‘rich, greatly wealthy, and of great possessions.’”

“Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti; dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako ‘aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo’ti vuccatī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“With what four? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: 'Indeed, that Blessed One is... a Teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One'; he is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma...; he is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha...; he is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken... conducive to concentration. Bhikkhus, a noble disciple endowed with these four qualities is called 'rich, greatly wealthy, and of great possessions.' Fourth.

5. Dutiyamahaddhanasuttaṃ

5. The Second Discourse on the Greatly Wealthy

1041. “Catūhi[V 3.0466], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako ‘aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo mahāyaso’ti vuccati.

1041. “Bhikkhus, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities is called 'rich, greatly wealthy, of great possessions, and of great retinue.'”

“Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako ‘aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo mahāyaso’ti vuccatī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“With what four? Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: 'Indeed, that Blessed One is... a Teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One'; he is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma...; he is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha...; he is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken... conducive to concentration. Bhikkhus, a noble disciple endowed with these four qualities is called 'rich, greatly wealthy, of great possessions, and of great retinue.' Fifth.

6. Suddhakasuttaṃ

6. The Simple Discourse

1042. “Catūhi[P 5.0403], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.

1042. “Bhikkhus, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer, not destined for the lower realms, is assured, and is bound for enlightenment.

“Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi [T 5.0508] …pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

With what four? Here, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering faith in the Buddha thus: 'Indeed, that Blessed One is... a Teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One'; he is endowed with unwavering faith in the Dhamma...; he is endowed with unwavering faith in the Saṅgha...; he is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones—unbroken... conducive to concentration. Monks, a noble disciple endowed with these four qualities is a stream-enterer, not destined for the lower realms, is assured, and is bound for enlightenment. Sixth.

7. Nandiyasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse to Nandiya

1043. Kapilavatthunidānaṃ[M 3.0353]. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho nandiyaṃ sakkaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “catūhi kho, nandiya, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”.

1043. At Kapilavatthu. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to Nandiya the Sakyan: “Nandiya, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into the states of woe, assured, and destined for full awakening.”

“Katamehi [V 3.0467] catūhi? Idha, nandiya, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, nandiya, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“With what four? Here, Nandiya, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant… a teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration. Endowed with these four qualities, Nandiya, a noble disciple is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into the states of woe, assured, and destined for full awakening.” Seventh.

8. Bhaddiyasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse to Bhaddiya

1044. Kapilavatthunidānaṃ. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho bhaddiyaṃ sakkaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “catūhi kho, bhaddiya, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.

1044. At Kapilavatthu. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to Bhaddiya the Sakyan: “Bhaddiya, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into the states of woe, assured, and destined for full awakening.”

“Katamehi catūhi? Idha, bhaddiya, ariyasāvako buddhe…pe… dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, bhaddiya, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“With what four? Here, Bhaddiya, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha… in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration. Endowed with these four qualities, Bhaddiya, a noble disciple is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into the states of woe, assured, and destined for full awakening.” Eighth.

9. Mahānāmasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse to Mahānāma

1045. Kapilavatthunidānaṃ[T 5.0509][P 5.0404]. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho mahānāmaṃ sakkaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “catūhi kho, mahānāma, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti…pe… sambodhiparāyaṇo”.

1045. At Kapilavatthu. Seated to one side, the Blessed One said to Mahānāma the Sakyan: “Mahānāma, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer… destined for full awakening.”

“Katamehi catūhi? Idha, mahānāma, ariyasāvako buddhe…pe… dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, mahānāma, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Navamaṃ.

“By what four? Here, Mahānāma, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha… in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken… leading to concentration. Mahānāma, a noble disciple endowed with these four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into the lower realms, assured, and destined for enlightenment.” Ninth.

10. Aṅgasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Factors

1046. “Cattārimāni[M 3.0354][V 3.0468], bhikkhave, sotāpattiyaṅgāni. Katamāni cattāri? Sappurisasaṃsevo, saddhammassavanaṃ, yonisomanasikāro, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti – imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgānī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

1046. “Monks, there are these four factors of stream-entry. What four? Association with good persons, hearing the true Dhamma, appropriate attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma. These, monks, are the four factors of stream-entry.” Tenth.

Sagāthakapuññābhisandavaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter: With Verses on the Overflowing of Merit.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for that:

Abhisandā tayo vuttā, duve mahaddhanena ca;

Suddhaṃ nandiyaṃ bhaddiyaṃ, mahānāmaṅgena te dasāti.

Three are stated with ‘overflowing,’ and two with ‘great wealth’; Suddha, Nandiya, Bhaddiya, Mahānāma, and Aṅga—these are the ten.

6. Sappaññavaggo

6. The Chapter on the Wise

1. Sagāthakasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse with Verses

1047. “Catūhi[T 5.0510], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.

1047. “Monks, a noble disciple endowed with four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into the lower realms, assured, and destined for enlightenment.”

“Katamehi catūhi? Idha[P 5.0405], bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehi. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

“By what four? Here, monks, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is an Arahant… a teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken… leading to concentration. Monks, a noble disciple endowed with these four qualities is a stream-enterer, not subject to falling into the lower realms, assured, and destined for enlightenment.” This the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Well-Farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Yassa [V 3.0469] saddhā tathāgate, acalā suppatiṭṭhitā;

Sīlañca yassa kalyāṇaṃ, ariyakantaṃ pasaṃsitaṃ.

“One who has unshakable and well-established faith in the Tathāgata, and whose virtue is good, dear to the noble ones, and praised,

“Saṅghe pasādo yassatthi, ujubhūtañca dassanaṃ;

Adaliddoti taṃ āhu, amoghaṃ tassa jīvitaṃ.

who has confidence in the Saṅgha, and whose view has been straightened—the wise say that one is not poor; their life is not in vain.”

“Tasmā saddhañca sīlañca, pasādaṃ dhammadassanaṃ;

Anuyuñjetha medhāvī, saraṃ buddhānasāsana”nti. paṭhamaṃ;

“Therefore, let the wise devote themselves to faith, virtue, confidence, and the vision of the Dhamma, remembering the teaching of the Buddhas.” First.

2. Vassaṃvutthasuttaṃ

2. The Sutta on Having Completed the Rains Residence

1048. Ekaṃ [M 3.0355] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sāvatthiyaṃ vassaṃvuttho kapilavatthuṃ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Assosuṃ kho kāpilavatthavā sakyā – “aññataro kira bhikkhu [T 5.0511] sāvatthiyaṃ vassaṃvuttho kapilavatthuṃ anuppatto”ti.

1048. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's park. At that time a certain monk who had completed the rains residence at Sāvatthī arrived at Kapilavatthu on some business. The Sakyans of Kapilavatthu heard: "It is said that a certain monk who has completed the rains residence at Sāvatthī has arrived at Kapilavatthu."

Atha kho kāpilavatthavā sakyā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho kāpilavatthavā sakyā taṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavocuṃ – “kacci, bhante, bhagavā arogo ceva balavā cā”ti? “Arogo cāvuso, bhagavā balavā cā”ti. “Kacci [P 5.0406] pana, bhante, sāriputtamoggallānā arogā ceva balavanto cā”ti? “Sāriputtamoggallānāpi kho, āvuso, arogā ceva balavanto cā”ti. “Kacci pana, bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho arogo ca balavā cā”ti. “Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho, āvuso, arogo ca balavā cā”ti. “Atthi pana te, bhante, kiñci iminā antaravassena bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahita”nti? “Sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘appakā te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ye āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti. Atha kho eteva bahutarā bhikkhū ye pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā’”ti.

Then the Sakyans of Kapilavatthu approached that monk. Having approached, they paid homage to him and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Sakyans of Kapilavatthu said to that monk: "Venerable sir, is the Blessed One well and strong?" "The Blessed One is well and strong, friends." "And, venerable sir, are Sāriputta and Moggallāna well and strong?" "Sāriputta and Moggallāna are also well and strong, friends." "And, venerable sir, is the community of monks well and strong?" "The community of monks is also well and strong, friends." "But, venerable sir, have you heard anything in the Blessed One's presence that you have received directly from him during this rains-residence?" "I have heard this in the Blessed One's presence, friends, and received it directly from him: 'Bhikkhus, few are those monks who, through the destruction of the taints, having realized it for themselves with direct knowledge, in this very life enter and abide in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom. But far more numerous are those monks who, with the destruction of the five lower fetters, are of spontaneous birth, attaining final Nibbāna there, not liable to return from that world.'"

“Aparampi [V 3.0470] kho me, āvuso, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘appakā te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ye pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā. Atha kho eteva bahutarā bhikkhū [T 5.0512] ye tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissantī’”ti.

Furthermore, friends, I have heard and received this in the Blessed One's presence: 'Few are those monks, Bhikkhus, who, with the destruction of the five lower fetters, are of spontaneous birth, attaining final Nibbāna there, not liable to return from that world. But indeed, far more numerous are those monks who, with the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, are once-returners who, having come to this world only once, will make an end of suffering.'"

“Aparampi kho me, āvuso, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘appakā te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ye tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmino, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā [M 3.0356] dukkhassantaṃ karissanti. Atha kho eteva bahutarā bhikkhū ye tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

Furthermore, friends, I have heard and received this in the Blessed One's presence: 'Few are those monks, Bhikkhus, who, with the destruction of the three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hatred, and delusion, are once-returners who, having come to this world only once, will make an end of suffering. But indeed, far more numerous are those monks who, with the destruction of the three fetters, are stream-enterers, not liable to fall into the lower realms, assured, and destined for enlightenment.' The Second.

3. Dhammadinnasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse with Dhammadinna

1049. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye. Atha [P 5.0407] kho dhammadinno upāsako pañcahi upāsakasatehi saddhiṃ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho dhammadinno upāsako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ovadatu no, bhante, bhagavā; anusāsatu no, bhante, bhagavā yaṃ amhākaṃ assa dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.

1049. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Bārāṇasī in the deer park at Isipatana. Then the lay follower Dhammadinna, together with five hundred lay followers, approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the lay follower Dhammadinna said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One advise us; Venerable Sir, may the Blessed One instruct us in that which would be for our welfare and happiness for a long time.”

“Tasmātiha vo, dhammadinnaṃ, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘ye te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatapaṭisaṃyuttā te kālena kālaṃ upasampajja viharissāmā’ti. Evañhi vo, dhammadinna, sikkhitabba”nti. “Na kho netaṃ, bhante, sukaraṃ amhehi puttasambādhasayanaṃ ajjhāvasantehi kāsikacandanaṃ paccanubhontehi mālāgandhavilepanaṃ dhārayantehi jātarūparajataṃ sādiyantehi – ye te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā [T 5.0513] gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatapaṭisaṃyuttā te kālena kālaṃ upasampajja viharituṃ. Tesaṃ no, bhante, bhagavā amhākaṃ pañcasu sikkhāpadesu ṭhitānaṃ uttaridhammaṃ desetū”ti.

“Therefore, Dhammadinna, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will from time to time attain and abide in those discourses spoken by the Tathāgata that are deep, profound in meaning, supramundane, and connected with emptiness.’ Thus indeed, Dhammadinna, should you train yourselves.” “Venerable sir, it is not easy for us—who live in a home crowded with children, who enjoy sandalwood from Kasi, who wear garlands, perfumes, and cosmetics, and who delight in gold and silver—to from time to time attain and abide in those discourses spoken by the Tathāgata that are deep, profound in meaning, supramundane, and connected with emptiness. Venerable sir, may the Blessed One teach a further Dhamma to us who are established in the five training precepts.”

“Tasmātiha [V 3.0471] vo, dhammadinna, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā bhavissāma – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā bhavissāma akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehī’ti. Evañhi vo, dhammadinna, sikkhitabba”nti.
