“Therefore, Dhammadinna, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: “Indeed, that Blessed One is an Arahant… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.” We will be endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… We will be endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration.’ Thus indeed, Dhammadinna, should you train yourselves.”

“Yānimāni, bhante, bhagavatā cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni desitāni, saṃvijjante te dhammā amhesu, mayañca tesu dhammesu sandissāma. Mayañhi bhante, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā – itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho [P 5.0408] bhagavāti. Dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā akhaṇḍehi…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikehī”ti. “Lābhā vo[M 3.0357], dhammadinna, suladdhaṃ vo, dhammadinna! Sotāpattiphalaṃ tumhehi byākata”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Venerable sir, these four factors of stream-entry that have been taught by the Blessed One exist in us, and we are seen in these qualities. For, venerable sir, we are endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, that Blessed One is an Arahant… the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ We are endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… in the Saṅgha… We are endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, which are unbroken… and conducive to concentration.” “It is a gain for you, Dhammadinna! It is a great gain for you, Dhammadinna! The fruit of stream-entry has been declared by you.” The Third.

4. Gilānasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Sick Person

1050. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṃ karonti – “niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṃ pakkamissatī”ti. Assosi kho mahānāmo sakko – “sambahulā kira bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṃ karonti – ‘niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’”ti[T 5.0514]. Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “sutametaṃ, bhante – ‘sambahulā kira bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṃ karonti – niṭṭhitacīvaro bhagavā temāsaccayena cārikaṃ pakkamissatī’ti. Na kho netaṃ na kho te etaṃ (sī. pī.), bhante, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ sappaññena upāsakena sappañño upāsako ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno ovaditabbo”ti.

1050. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans in Kapilavatthu at the Nigrodha Park. Now at that time, many bhikkhus were doing robe-work for the Blessed One, thinking: 'When the robe-work is finished, the Blessed One will depart on a journey after the passing of three months.' Mahānāma the Sakyan heard: 'It is said that many bhikkhus are doing robe-work for the Blessed One, thinking: "When the robe-work is finished, the Blessed One will depart on a journey after the passing of three months."' Then Mahānāma the Sakyan approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, Mahānāma the Sakyan said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable Sir, I have heard this: "It is said that many bhikkhus are doing robe-work for the Blessed One, thinking: ‘When the robe-work is finished, the Blessed One will depart on a journey after the passing of three months.’" But, Venerable Sir, I have not heard in the Blessed One's presence, nor received in his presence, how a wise lay follower should instruct a wise lay follower who is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill.'

“Sappaññena mahānāma, upāsakena sappañño upāsako ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno catūhi assāsanīyehi dhammehi assāsetabbo – ‘assāsatāyasmā – atthāyasmato buddhe aveccappasādo itipi so bhagavā…pe… satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti[V 3.0472]. Assāsatāyasmā – atthāyasmato dhamme…pe… saṅghe…pe… ariyakantāni sīlāni akhaṇḍāni…pe… samādhisaṃvattanikānī’”ti.

“Mahānāma, a wise lay follower should reassure a wise lay follower who is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill with four grounds for reassurance: ‘Be reassured, venerable sir—you have unwavering confidence in the Buddha: “That Blessed One is an Arahant, perfectly enlightened, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, fortunate, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of devas and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One.” Be reassured, venerable sir—you have unwavering confidence in the Dhamma… Be reassured, venerable sir—you have unwavering confidence in the Saṅgha… Be reassured, venerable sir—you possess the virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken… conducive to concentration.’”

“Sappaññena[P 5.0409], mahānāma, upāsakena sappañño upāsako ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno imehi catūhi assāsanīyehi dhammehi assāsetvā evamassa vacanīyo – ‘atthāyasmato mātāpitūsu apekkhā’ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘atthi me mātāpitūsu apekkhā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmā kho māriso maraṇadhammo. Sace pāyasmā mātāpitūsu apekkhaṃ karissati, marissateva; no ce [T 5.0515] pāyasmā [M 3.0358] mātāpitūsu apekkhaṃ karissati, marissateva. Sādhāyasmā, yā te mātāpitūsu apekkhā taṃ pajahā’”ti.

“Mahānāma, a wise lay follower, having reassured a wise lay follower who is afflicted, suffering, and gravely ill with these four reassuring principles, should speak to him thus: ‘Venerable sir, do you have any longing for your parents?’ If he should say, ‘I have longing for my parents,’ he should be spoken to thus: ‘Good sir, you are of a mortal nature. Whether you, venerable sir, have longing for your parents or do not have longing for your parents, you will surely die. It is good, venerable sir; abandon that longing which you have for your parents.’”

“So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘yā me mātāpitūsu apekkhā sā pahīnā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘atthi panāyasmato puttadāresu apekkhā’ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘atthi me puttadāresu apekkhā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘āyasmā kho māriso maraṇadhammo. Sace pāyasmā puttadāresu apekkhaṃ karissati, marissateva; no ce pāyasmā puttadāresu apekkhaṃ karissati, marissateva. Sādhāyasmā, yā te puttadāresu apekkhā taṃ pajahā’”ti.

“If he should say, ‘That longing which I had for my parents has been abandoned,’ he should be spoken to thus: ‘But do you, venerable sir, have any longing for your children and spouse?’ If he should say, ‘I have longing for my children and spouse,’ he should be spoken to thus: ‘Good sir, you are of a mortal nature. Whether you, venerable sir, have longing for your children and spouse or do not have longing for your children and spouse, you will surely die. It is good, venerable sir; abandon that longing which you have for your children and spouse.’”

“So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘yā me puttadāresu apekkhā sā pahīnā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘atthi panāyasmato mānusakesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu apekkhā’ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘atthi me mānusakesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu apekkhā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘mānusakehi kho, āvuso, kāmehi dibbā kāmā abhikkantatarā ca paṇītatarā ca. Sādhāyasmā, mānusakehi kāmehi cittaṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā cātumahārājikesu cātummahārājikesu (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) devesu cittaṃ adhimocehī’”ti.

“If he should say, ‘That longing which I had for my children and spouse has been abandoned,’ he should be spoken to thus: ‘But do you, venerable sir, have any longing for the five cords of human sensual pleasure?’ If he should say, ‘I have longing for the five cords of human sensual pleasure,’ he should be spoken to thus: ‘Friend, divine sensual pleasures are superior and more refined than human sensual pleasures. It is good, venerable sir; raise your mind from human sensual pleasures and direct it towards the Cātumahārājika devas.’”

“So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘mānusakehi me kāmehi cittaṃ vuṭṭhitaṃ, cātumahārājikesu devesu cittaṃ adhimocita’nti, so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘cātumahārājikehi kho, āvuso[P 5.0410], devehi tāvatiṃsā devā abhikkantatarā ca paṇītatarā ca. Sādhāyasmā, cātumahārājikehi [T 5.0516] devehi cittaṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā tāvatiṃsesu devesu cittaṃ adhimocehī’”ti.

“If he should say: ‘My mind has been raised from human sensual pleasures and is directed towards the Cātumahārājika devas,’ he should be spoken to thus: ‘Friend, the Tāvatiṃsa devas are more excellent and more sublime than the Cātumahārājika devas. It is good, venerable sir; raise your mind from the Cātumahārājika devas and direct it towards the Tāvatiṃsa devas.’”

“So [V 3.0473] ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘cātumahārājikehi me devehi cittaṃ vuṭṭhitaṃ, tāvatiṃsesu devesu cittaṃ adhimocita’nti, so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘tāvatiṃsehi kho, āvuso, devehi yāmā devā…pe… tusitā devā…pe… nimmānaratī devā…pe… paranimmitavasavattī devā…pe… paranimmitavasavattīhi kho, āvuso, devehi brahmaloko abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca. Sādhāyasmā, paranimmitavasavattīhi devehi cittaṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā brahmaloke cittaṃ adhimocehī’ti. So [M 3.0359] ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘paranimmitavasavattīhi me devehi cittaṃ vuṭṭhitaṃ, brahmaloke cittaṃ adhimocita’nti, so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘brahmalokopi kho, āvuso, anicco addhuvo sakkāyapariyāpanno. Sādhāyasmā, brahmalokā cittaṃ vuṭṭhāpetvā sakkāyanirodhe cittaṃ upasaṃharāhī’”ti.

“If he should say: ‘My mind has been raised from the Cātumahārājika devas and is directed towards the Tāvatiṃsa devas,’ he should be spoken to thus: ‘Friend, the Yāma devas are more excellent and more sublime than the Tāvatiṃsa devas… the Tusita devas… the Nimmānaratī devas… the Paranimmitavasavattī devas… Friend, the Brahmā world is more excellent and more sublime than the Paranimmitavasavattī devas. It is good, venerable sir; raise your mind from the Paranimmitavasavattī devas and direct it towards the Brahmā world.’ If he should say: ‘My mind has been raised from the Paranimmitavasavattī devas and is directed towards the Brahmā world,’ he should be spoken to thus: ‘Friend, the Brahmā world is also impermanent, not lasting, and included within personality. It is good, venerable sir; raise your mind from the Brahmā world and apply it to the cessation of personality.’”

“So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘brahmalokā me cittaṃ vuṭṭhitaṃ, sakkāyanirodhe cittaṃ upasaṃharāmī’ti; evaṃ vimuttacittassa kho, mahānāma, upāsakassa āsavā vassasata (sī. syā.) vimuttacittena bhikkhunā na kiñci nānākaraṇaṃ vadāmi, yadidaṃ – vimuttiyā vimutta”nti. Catutthaṃ.

“If he should say: ‘My mind has been raised from the Brahmā world; I am applying my mind to the cessation of personality,’ then, Mahānāma, I do not declare any difference whatsoever between a lay follower whose mind is thus liberated and a bhikkhu whose mind is liberated from the taints, that is to say, with respect to liberation. Fourth.”

5. Sotāpattiphalasuttaṃ

5. The Sutta on the Fruit of Stream-Entry

1051. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti. Katame cattāro? Sappurisasaṃsevo[P 5.0411], saddhammassavanaṃ[T 5.0517], yonisomanasikāro, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti – ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

1051. “Bhikkhus, these four things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry. What four? Association with true persons, listening to the true Dhamma, wise attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma. These four things, bhikkhus, when developed and cultivated, lead to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry.” The fifth.

6. Sakadāgāmiphalasuttaṃ

6. The Sutta on the Fruit of Once-Returning

1052. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā sakadāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti. Katame cattāro? …Pe… saṃvattantī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

1052. “Bhikkhus, these four things, when developed and cultivated, lead to the realization of the fruit of once-returning. What four? … They lead to the realization of the fruit of once-returning.” The sixth.

7. Anāgāmiphalasuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on the Fruit of Non-Returning

1053. …Pe… [V 3.0474] anāgāmiphalasacchikiriyāya…pe… saṃvattantī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

1053. …lead to the realization of the fruit of non-returning… The seventh.

8. Arahattaphalasuttaṃ

8. The Sutta on the Fruit of Arahantship

1054. …Pe… arahattaphalasacchikiriyāya…pe… saṃvattantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

1054. …lead to the realization of the fruit of arahantship… The eighth.

9. Paññāpaṭilābhasuttaṃ

9. The Sutta on the Acquisition of Wisdom

1055. …Pe… paññāpaṭilābhāya…pe… saṃvattantī”ti. Navamaṃ.

1055. …lead to the acquisition of wisdom… The ninth.

10. Paññāvuddhisuttaṃ

10. The Sutta on the Growth of Wisdom

1056. …Pe… paññāvuddhiyā [M 3.0360] …pe… saṃvattantī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

1056. …lead to the growth of wisdom… The tenth.

11. Paññāvepullasuttaṃ

11. The Sutta on the Abundance of Wisdom

1057. …Pe…. Paññāvepullāya…pe… saṃvattantī”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

1057. …lead to the abundance of wisdom… The eleventh.

Sappaññavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Chapter on Wisdom, the Sixth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary is:

Sagāthakaṃ [V 3.0475] vassaṃvutthaṃ, dhammadinnañca gilānaṃ;

Caturo phalā paṭilābho, vuddhi vepullatāya cāti.

With Verses, Rains-residence, Dhammadinna, and Sickness; the four Fruits, Acquisition, Growth, and Abundance.

7. Mahāpaññavaggo

7. The Chapter on Great Wisdom

1. Mahāpaññāsuttaṃ

1. The Sutta on Great Wisdom

1058. “Cattārome, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahāpaññatāya [T 5.0518] saṃvattanti. Katame cattāro? Sappurisasaṃsevo, saddhammassavanaṃ, yonisomanasikāro, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti – ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahāpaññatā [P 5.0412] saṃvattantī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

1058. “Bhikkhus, these four things, when developed and cultivated, lead to great wisdom. What four? Association with true persons, listening to the true Dhamma, wise attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma. These four things, bhikkhus, when developed and cultivated, lead to great wisdom.” The first.

2. Puthupaññāsuttaṃ

2. The Sutta on Broad Wisdom

1059. … Puthupaññatā saṃvattantī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

1059. …lead to broad wisdom.” The second.

3. Vipulapaññāsuttaṃ

3. The Sutta on Extensive Wisdom

1060. … Vipulapaññatā saṃvattantī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

1060. …lead to extensive wisdom.” The third.

4. Gambhīrapaññāsuttaṃ

4. The Sutta on Profound Wisdom

1061. … Gambhīrapaññatā saṃvattantī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

1061. …lead to profound wisdom.” The fourth.

5. Appamattapaññāsuttaṃ

5. The Sutta on Immeasurable Wisdom

1062. … [V 3.0476] Appamattapaññatā [M 3.0361] saṃvattantī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

1062. …lead to immeasurable wisdom.” The fifth.

6. Bhūripaññāsuttaṃ

6. The Sutta on Extensive Wisdom

1063. … Bhūripaññatā saṃvattantī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

1063. …lead to extensive wisdom.” The sixth.

7. Paññābāhullasuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on Abundance of Wisdom

1064. … Paññābāhullā saṃvattantī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

1064. …lead to an abundance of wisdom.” The seventh.

8. Sīghapaññāsuttaṃ

8. The Sutta on Swift Wisdom.

1065. … Sīghapaññatā saṃvattantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

1065. …lead to swift wisdom.” The eighth.

9. Lahupaññāsuttaṃ

9. The Sutta on Quick Wisdom.

1066. … Lahupaññatā saṃvattantī”ti. Navamaṃ.

1066. …lead to quick wisdom.” The ninth.

10. Hāsapaññāsuttaṃ

10. The Sutta on Joyful Wisdom.

1067. … Hāsapaññatā saṃvattantī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

1067. …lead to joyful wisdom.” The tenth.

11. Javanapaññāsuttaṃ

11. The Sutta on Rapid Wisdom.

1068. … Javanapaññatā [P 5.0413] saṃvattantī”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

1068. …lead to rapid wisdom.” The eleventh.

12. Tikkhapaññāsuttaṃ

12. The Sutta on Keen Wisdom.

1069. … [V 3.0477] Tikkhapaññatā saṃvattantī”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

1069. …conduce to keen wisdom.” The twelfth.

13. Nibbedhikapaññāsuttaṃ

13. The Sutta on Penetrative Wisdom.

1070. … Nibbedhikapaññatā saṃvattanti. Katame cattāro? Sappurisasaṃsevo, saddhammassavanaṃ, yonisomanasikāro, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti – ime [M 3.0362] kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā nibbedhikapaññatāya saṃvattantī”ti. Terasamaṃ.

1070. …conduce to penetrative wisdom. What four? Association with good people, listening to the true Dhamma, wise attention, and practice in accordance with the Dhamma—these, monks, are the four qualities that, when developed and cultivated, conduce to penetrative wisdom.” The thirteenth.

Mahāpaññavaggo sattamo.

The Chapter on Great Wisdom, the Seventh.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of that is:

Mahā [T 5.0519] puthu vipula-gambhīraṃ, appamatta-bhūri-bāhullaṃ;

Sīgha-lahu-hāsa-javana, tikkha-nibbedhikāya cāti.

Great, broad, ample, deep; immeasurable, extensive, abundant; swift, quick, joyful, rapid; keen, and penetrative indeed.

Sotāpattisaṃyuttaṃ ekādasamaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on Stream-Entry, the Eleventh.

12. Saccasaṃyuttaṃ

12. The Connected Discourses on the Truths.

1. Samādhivaggo

1. The Chapter on Concentration.

1. Samādhisuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Concentration.

1071. Sāvatthinidānaṃ[T 5.0520][V 3.0478][M 3.0363][P 5.0414]. “Samādhiṃ, bhikkhave, bhāvetha. Samāhito, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Kiñca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Samādhiṃ, bhikkhave, bhāvetha. Samāhito, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti”.

1071. At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, develop concentration. A concentrated bhikkhu, bhikkhus, knows as it really is. And what does he know as it really is? He knows as it really is: ‘This is suffering.’ He knows as it really is: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ He knows as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ He knows as it really is: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ Bhikkhus, develop concentration. A concentrated bhikkhu, bhikkhus, knows as it really is.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, an effort should be made: ‘This is suffering’; an effort should be made: ‘This is the origin of suffering’; an effort should be made: ‘This is the cessation of suffering’; an effort should be made: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The first.

2. Paṭisallānasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Solitude.

1072. “Paṭisallāne, bhikkhave, yogamāpajjatha. Paṭisallīno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Kiñca yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Paṭisallāne[P 5.0415], bhikkhave, yogamāpajjatha. Paṭisallīno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti.

1072. “Bhikkhus, you should apply yourselves to solitude. A bhikkhu in solitude, bhikkhus, knows as it really is. And what does he know as it really is? He knows as it really is: ‘This is suffering.’ He knows as it really is: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ He knows as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ He knows as it really is: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ Bhikkhus, you should apply yourselves to solitude. A bhikkhu in solitude, bhikkhus, knows as it really is.”

“Tasmātiha[V 3.0479], bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yogo [T 5.0521] karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, an effort should be made to realize: ‘This is suffering’; an effort should be made to realize: ‘This is the origin of suffering’; an effort should be made to realize: ‘This is the cessation of suffering’; an effort should be made to realize: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The second.

3. Paṭhamakulaputtasuttaṃ

3. The First Discourse on Sons of Good Families

1073. “Ye [M 3.0364] hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ kulaputtā sammā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajiṃsu, sabbe te catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ abhisamayāya. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ kulaputtā sammā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissanti, sabbe te catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ abhisamayāya. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi kulaputtā sammā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, sabbe te catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ abhisamayāya.

1073. “Bhikkhus, whatever sons of good families in the past rightly went forth from the household life into homelessness, all of them went forth for the sake of directly realizing the Four Noble Truths as they really are. Bhikkhus, whatever sons of good families in the future will rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, all of them will go forth for the sake of directly realizing the Four Noble Truths as they really are. Bhikkhus, whatever sons of good families at present rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness, all of them go forth for the sake of directly realizing the Four Noble Truths as they really are.”

“Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Dukkhassa ariyasaccassa dukkhasamudayassa ariyasaccassa dukkhanirodhassa ariyasaccassa dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ kulaputtā sammā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajiṃsu…pe… pabbajissanti…pe… pabbajanti, sabbe te imesaṃyeva catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ abhisamayāya.

“Of which four? The noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, and the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. Bhikkhus, whatever sons of good families in the past rightly went forth from the household life into homelessness … or will go forth in the future … or are going forth in the present, all of them do so for the sake of directly realizing these very four noble truths as they really are.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, an effort should be made to realize: ‘This is suffering’; an effort should be made to realize: ‘This is the origin of suffering’; an effort should be made to realize: ‘This is the cessation of suffering’; an effort should be made to realize: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The third.

4. Dutiyakulaputtasuttaṃ

4. The Second Discourse on Sons of Good Families

1074. “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ kulaputtā sammā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā yathābhūtaṃ abhisamesuṃ, sabbe te cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisamesuṃ. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ kulaputtā sammā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā [V 3.0480] yathābhūtaṃ [T 5.0522][P 5.0416] abhisamessanti, sabbe te cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisamessanti. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi kulaputtā sammā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā yathābhūtaṃ abhisamenti, sabbe te cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisamenti.

1074. “Bhikkhus, whatever sons of good families in the past, having rightly gone forth from the household life into homelessness, directly realized the truth, all of them directly realized the four noble truths as they really are. Bhikkhus, whatever sons of good families in the future, having rightly gone forth from the household life into homelessness, will directly realize the truth, all of them will directly realize the four noble truths as they really are. Bhikkhus, whatever sons of good families at present, having rightly gone forth from the household life into homelessness, directly realize the truth, all of them directly realize the four noble truths as they really are.”

“Katamāni cattāri? Dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ kulaputtā sammā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā yathābhūtaṃ abhisamesuṃ [M 3.0365] …pe… abhisamessanti…pe… abhisamenti, sabbe te imāni cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisamenti.

“Which four? The noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, and the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. Bhikkhus, whatever sons of good families in the past, having rightly gone forth from the household life into homelessness, directly realized the truth… or will directly realize in the future… or are directly realizing in the present, all of them directly realize these four noble truths as they really are.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, an effort should be made: ‘This is suffering’… an effort should be made: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The fourth.

5. Paṭhamasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

1075. “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yathābhūtaṃ abhisambojjhiṃsu, sabbe te cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisambojjhiṃsu. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yathābhūtaṃ abhisambojjhissanti, sabbe te cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisambojjhissanti. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yathābhūtaṃ abhisambojjhanti, sabbe te cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisambojjhanti.

1075. “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past fully awakened as it really is, all of them fully awakened to the Four Noble Truths as it really is. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will fully awaken as it really is, all of them will fully awaken to the Four Noble Truths as it really is. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the present fully awaken as it really is, all of them fully awaken to the Four Noble Truths as it really is.”

“Katamāni cattāri? Dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā [T 5.0523] vā yathābhūtaṃ abhisambojjhiṃsu…pe… abhisambojjhissanti…pe… abhisambojjhanti, sabbe te imāni cattāri ariyasaccāni [P 5.0417] yathābhūtaṃ abhisambojjhanti.

“What four? The noble truth of suffering… the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past fully awakened as it really is… will fully awaken… fully awaken, all of them fully awaken to these Four Noble Truths as it really is.”

“Tasmātiha[V 3.0481], bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Therefore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, an exertion should be made to realize: ‘This is suffering’… an exertion should be made to realize: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” Fifth.

6. Dutiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Ascetics and Brahmins

1076. “Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yathābhūtaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ pakāsesuṃ, sabbe te cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ pakāsesuṃ. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yathābhūtaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ pakāsessanti, sabbe te cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ pakāsessanti. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, etarahi samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yathābhūtaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ pakāsenti, sabbe te cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ pakāsenti.

1076. “Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past declared the thorough understanding as it really is, all of them declared the thorough understanding of the Four Noble Truths as it really is. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the future will declare the thorough understanding as it really is, all of them will declare the thorough understanding of the Four Noble Truths as it really is. Whatever ascetics or brahmins in the present declare the thorough understanding as it really is, all of them declare the thorough understanding of the Four Noble Truths as it really is.”

“Katamāni [M 3.0366] cattāri? Dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ. Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā yathābhūtaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ pakāsesuṃ…pe… pakāsessanti…pe… pakāsenti, sabbe te imāni cattāri ariyasaccāni yathābhūtaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ pakāsenti.

“What four? The Noble Truth of suffering… the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. Bhikkhus, whatever ascetics or brahmins in the past declared the thorough understanding as it really is… will declare… are declaring, all of them declare the thorough understanding of these Four Noble Truths as it really is.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Therefore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, an exertion should be made to realize: ‘This is suffering’… an exertion should be made to realize: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” Sixth.

7. Vitakkasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Thoughts

1077. “Mā, bhikkhave, pāpake akusale vitakke vitakkeyyātha vitakketha (sī. syā. kaṃ.), seyyathidaṃ [T 5.0524] – kāmavitakkaṃ, byāpādavitakkaṃ, vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ. Taṃ kissa hetu? Nete, bhikkhave, vitakkā atthasaṃhitā nādibrahmacariyakā [P 5.0418] na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattanti.

1077. “Bhikkhus, do not think evil, unwholesome thoughts, that is to say: thoughts of sensual desire, thoughts of ill will, and thoughts of cruelty. For what reason? These thoughts, Bhikkhus, are not connected with benefit, are not fundamental to the holy life, and do not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, or to Nibbāna.”

“Vitakkentā ca kho tumhe, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti vitakkeyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti [V 3.0482] vitakkeyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti vitakkeyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti vitakkeyyātha. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ete, bhikkhave, vitakkā atthasaṃhitā ete ādibrahmacariyakā ete nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti.

“But when you think, Bhikkhus, you should think: ‘This is suffering,’ you should think: ‘This is the origin of suffering,’ you should think: ‘This is the cessation of suffering,’ you should think: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ For what reason? Because, Bhikkhus, these thoughts are connected with benefit, they are fundamental to the holy life, and they lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, and to Nibbāna.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Therefore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, an exertion should be made to realize: ‘This is suffering’… an exertion should be made to realize: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” Seventh.

8. Cintasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Thought

1078. “Mā, bhikkhave, pāpakaṃ akusalaṃ cittaṃ cinteyyātha cintetha (sī. syā. kaṃ.) – ‘sassato loko’ti vā ‘asassato loko’ti vā, ‘antavā loko’ti vā ‘anantavā loko’ti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti vā ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti [M 3.0367] tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Nesā, bhikkhave, cintā atthasaṃhitā nādibrahmacariyakā na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya [T 5.0525] na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati.

1078. “Bhikkhus, do not think evil, unwholesome thoughts, such as: ‘The world is eternal,’ or ‘The world is not eternal’; ‘The world is finite,’ or ‘The world is infinite’; ‘The life-principle is the same as the body,’ or ‘The life-principle is different from the body’; ‘A being exists after death,’ or ‘A being does not exist after death’; ‘A being both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘A being neither exists nor does not exist after death.’ For what reason? Because, Bhikkhus, this thought is not connected with benefit, is not fundamental to the holy life, and does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, or to Nibbāna.”

“Cintentā ca kho tumhe, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti cinteyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti cinteyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti cinteyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti cinteyyātha. Taṃ kissa hetu? Esā, bhikkhave, cintā atthasaṃhitā, esā ādibrahmacariyakā, esā nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya [P 5.0419] sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

“But when you think, Bhikkhus, you should think: ‘This is suffering,’ you should think: ‘This is the origin of suffering,’ you should think: ‘This is the cessation of suffering,’ you should think: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ For what reason? Because, Bhikkhus, this thought is connected with benefit, it is fundamental to the holy life, and it leads to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, and to Nibbāna.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Therefore, Bhikkhus, in this Dispensation, an exertion should be made to realize: ‘This is suffering’… an exertion should be made to realize: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” Eighth.

9. Viggāhikakathāsuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Contentious Talk

1079. “Mā[V 3.0483], bhikkhave, viggāhikakathaṃ katheyyātha kathetha (sī. syā. kaṃ.) – ‘na tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāsi, ahaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāmi. Kiṃ tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānissasi! Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi, ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno. Sahitaṃ me, asahitaṃ te. Purevacanīyaṃ pacchā avaca, pacchāvacanīyaṃ pure avaca. Adhiciṇṇaṃ aciṇṇaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī.) te viparāvattaṃ. Āropito te vādo, cara vādappamokkhāya. Niggahitosi, nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Nesā, bhikkhave, kathā atthasaṃhitā nādibrahmacariyakā na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati.

1079. “Monks, do not engage in contentious talk, saying: ‘You do not know this Dhamma and Vinaya; I know this Dhamma and Vinaya. How could you know this Dhamma and Vinaya? You are practicing wrongly; I am practicing rightly. My statement is coherent; yours is incoherent. You said afterwards what should have been said before, and you said before what should have been said afterwards. What you have long practiced has been overturned. Your assertion has been challenged; go and try to free yourself from it! You are refuted; if you can, disentangle yourself!’ For what reason? Such talk, monks, is not connected with the goal, is not fundamental to the holy life, and does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, or to Nibbāna.”

“Kathentā ca kho tumhe, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti katheyyātha[T 5.0526], ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti katheyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti katheyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti katheyyātha…pe… yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Navamaṃ.

“But when you do speak, monks, you should speak thus: ‘This is suffering.’ You should speak thus: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ You should speak thus: ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ You should speak thus: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ … An exertion should be made.” The ninth.

10. Tiracchānakathāsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Worldly Talk

1080. “Mā[M 3.0368], bhikkhave, anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ katheyyātha, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ mahāmattakathaṃ senākathaṃ, bhayakathaṃ yuddhakathaṃ, annakathaṃ pānakathaṃ vatthakathaṃ sayanakathaṃ mālākathaṃ gandhakathaṃ, ñātikathaṃ yānakathaṃ gāmakathaṃ nigamakathaṃ nagarakathaṃ janapadakathaṃ itthikathaṃ itthikathaṃ purisakathaṃ (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) sūrakathaṃ visikhākathaṃ [P 5.0420] kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ, pubbapetakathaṃ nānattakathaṃ, lokakkhāyikaṃ samuddakkhāyikaṃ itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Nesā, bhikkhave, kathā atthasaṃhitā nādibrahmacariyakā na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati.

1080. “Monks, do not engage in the many kinds of worldly talk. What are these? Talk about kings, talk about thieves, talk about great ministers, talk about armies, talk about dangers, talk about battles, talk about food, talk about drink, talk about clothing, talk about lodgings, talk about garlands, talk about scents, talk about relatives, talk about vehicles, talk about villages, talk about market towns, talk about cities, talk about countries, talk about women, talk about men, talk about heroes, talk about crossroads, talk about watering places, talk about relatives who have passed away, miscellaneous talk, speculation about the world, speculation about the ocean, and talk about prosperity and decline. For what reason? Monks, this talk is not connected with the goal, it is not fundamental to the holy life, and it does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, to Nibbāna.”

“Kathentā ca kho tumhe, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti katheyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti katheyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti katheyyātha, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti katheyyātha. Taṃ kissa hetu? Esā, bhikkhave, kathā atthasaṃhitā, esā ādibrahmacariyakā, esā nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

“But when you do speak, monks, you should speak thus: ‘This is suffering.’ You should speak thus: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ You should speak thus: ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ You should speak thus: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ For what reason? Monks, this talk is connected with the goal, it is fundamental to the holy life, and it leads to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, and to Nibbāna.”

“Tasmātiha[V 3.0484], bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Therefore, monks, an effort should be made concerning this: ‘This is suffering.’ … an effort should be made concerning this: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The Tenth.

Samādhivaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Concentration.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse for this chapter:

Samādhi [T 5.0527] paṭisallānā, kulaputtā apare duve;

Samaṇabrāhmaṇā vitakkaṃ, cintā viggāhikā kathāti.

Concentration, Seclusion, two further suttas on Clansmen; Two on Ascetics and Brahmins, Thought, Reflection, and Contentious and Worldly Talk.

2. Dhammacakkappavattanavaggo

2. The Chapter on the Setting in Motion of the Wheel of Dhamma

1. Dhammacakkappavattanasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Setting in Motion of the Wheel of Dhamma

1081. Ekaṃ [T 5.0528] samayaṃ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṃ viharati isipatane migadāye. Tatra [P 5.0421] kho bhagavā pañcavaggiye bhikkhū āmantesi – “dveme, bhikkhave, antā pabbajitena [M 3.0369] na sevitabbā. Katame dve? Yo cāyaṃ kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyogo hīno gammo pothujjaniko anariyo anatthasaṃhito, yo cāyaṃ attakilamathānuyogo dukkho anariyo anatthasaṃhito. Ete kho, bhikkhave, ubho ante anupagamma majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati”.

1081. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana. There the Blessed One addressed the group of five monks: 'Monks, these two extremes should not be pursued by one who has gone forth. What are the two? That which is devotion to sensual pleasures in regard to sensual objects, which is inferior, vulgar, common, ignoble, and not connected with the goal; and that which is devotion to self-mortification, which is painful, ignoble, and not connected with the goal. Monks, avoiding both these extremes, the middle path has been fully realized by the Tathāgata, which gives rise to vision, gives rise to knowledge, and leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, and to Nibbāna.'

“Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi. Ayaṃ kho sā, bhikkhave, majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā cakkhukaraṇī ñāṇakaraṇī upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati.

“And what, monks, is that middle path fully realized by the Tathāgata, which gives rise to vision, gives rise to knowledge, and leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, and to Nibbāna? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. This, monks, is that middle path fully realized by the Tathāgata, which gives rise to vision, gives rise to knowledge, and leads to peace, to direct knowledge, to awakening, and to Nibbāna.”

“Idaṃ [V 3.0485] kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ – jātipi dukkhā, jarāpi [T 5.0529] dukkhā, byādhipi dukkho, maraṇampi dukkhaṃ, appiyehi sampayogo dukkho, piyehi vippayogo dukkho, yampicchaṃ na labhati tampi dukkhaṃ – saṃkhittena pañcupādānakkhandhā pañcupādānakkhandhāpi (pī. ka.) dukkhā. Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ – yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobbhavikā ponobhavikā (sī. pī.) nandirāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ seyyathīdaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā. Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ – yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo. Idaṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā [P 5.0422] ariyasaccaṃ – ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi.

“Now this, monks, is the Noble Truth of Suffering: birth is suffering, aging is suffering, illness is suffering, death is suffering; association with the unloved is suffering, separation from the loved is suffering; not getting what one desires is also suffering. In brief, the five aggregates subject to clinging are suffering. Now this, monks, is the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering: it is this craving which leads to renewed existence, is accompanied by delight and lust, and delights in this and that—that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence. Now this, monks, is the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering: it is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving, its relinquishing, letting go, release, and non-attachment. Now this, monks, is the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering: it is this very Noble Eightfold Path—that is, Right View… Right Concentration.”

“‘Idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasacca’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pariññeyya’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe…pe… udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pariññāta’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

‘This is the Noble Truth of Suffering’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, and light arose. ‘This Noble Truth of Suffering is to be fully understood’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me… and light arose. ‘This Noble Truth of Suffering has been fully understood’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, and light arose.

“‘Idaṃ [M 3.0370] dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasacca’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pahātabba’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe…pe… [T 5.0530] udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pahīna’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

‘This is the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, and light arose. ‘That Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering is to be abandoned’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me… and light arose. ‘That Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering has been abandoned’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, and light arose.

“‘Idaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasacca’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ sacchikātabba’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe…pe… udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ sacchikata’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

‘This is the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, and light arose. ‘That Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering is to be realized’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me… and light arose. ‘That Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering has been realized’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, and light arose.

“‘Idaṃ [V 3.0486] dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasacca’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ bhāvetabba’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe…pe… udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ bhāvita’nti me, bhikkhave, pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

‘This is the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, and light arose. ‘That Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering is to be developed’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me… and light arose. ‘That Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering has been developed’—thus, bhikkhus, in regard to things unheard of before, vision arose in me, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, true knowledge arose, and light arose.

“Yāvakīvañca me, bhikkhave, imesu catūsu ariyasaccesu evaṃ tiparivaṭṭaṃ dvādasākāraṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ na suvisuddhaṃ ahosi, neva tāvāhaṃ, bhikkhave[P 5.0423], sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā [T 5.0531] pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ abhisambuddho paccaññāsiṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.).

Bhikkhus, as long as my knowledge and vision of things as they really are regarding these Four Noble Truths—with their three rounds and twelve aspects—was not thoroughly purified, I did not declare to the world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, to this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, that I had fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

“Yato ca kho me, bhikkhave, imesu catūsu ariyasaccesu evaṃ tiparivaṭṭaṃ dvādasākāraṃ yathābhūtaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ suvisuddhaṃ ahosi, athāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya ‘anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho’ti paccaññāsiṃ. Ñāṇañca pana me dassanaṃ udapādi – ‘akuppā me vimutti [M 3.0371] cetovimutti (sī. pī.), ayamantimā jāti, natthidāni punabbhavo’”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā pañcavaggiyā bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

But when, bhikkhus, my knowledge and vision of things as they really are regarding these Four Noble Truths—with their three rounds and twelve aspects—was thoroughly purified, then I declared to the world with its devas, Māra, and Brahmā, to this generation with its ascetics and brahmins, its devas and humans, that I had fully awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. And knowledge and vision arose in me: ‘Unshakable is my liberation. This is the final birth. Now there is no further becoming.’ This is what the Blessed One said. The group of five bhikkhus, delighted, rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words.

Imasmiñca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne āyasmato koṇḍaññassa virajaṃ vītamalaṃ dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi – “yaṃ kiñci samudayadhammaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ nirodhadhamma”nti.

And while this discourse was being delivered, the dust-free, stainless Dhamma-eye arose in the Venerable Koṇḍañña: ‘Whatever is subject to arising is all subject to cessation.’

Pavattite ca pana bhagavatā dhammacakke bhummā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ – “etaṃ bhagavatā bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmi”nti. Bhummānaṃ devānaṃ saddaṃ sutvā cātumahārājikā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ – “etaṃ bhagavatā bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ, appaṭivattiyaṃ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā [T 5.0532] devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmi”nti. Cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ saddaṃ sutvā tāvatiṃsā [V 3.0487] devā…pe… yāmā devā…pe… tusitā devā…pe… nimmānaratī devā…pe… paranimmitavasavattī devā…pe… brahmakāyikā devā saddamanussāvesuṃ – “etaṃ bhagavatā bārāṇasiyaṃ isipatane migadāye anuttaraṃ dhammacakkaṃ pavattitaṃ appaṭivattiyaṃ [P 5.0424] samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmi”nti.

And when the Wheel of Dhamma had been set in motion by the Blessed One, the earth-dwelling devas proclaimed aloud: ‘At Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, this unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma has been set in motion by the Blessed One, which cannot be stopped by any ascetic or brahmin, by any deva, Māra, or Brahmā, or by anyone in the world.’ Hearing the proclamation of the earth-dwelling devas, the Cātumahārājika devas proclaimed it aloud… Hearing the proclamation of the Cātumahārājika devas, the Tāvatiṃsa devas… the Yāma devas… the Tusita devas… the Nimmānaratī devas… the Paranimmitavasavattī devas… the devas of Brahmā’s retinue proclaimed aloud: ‘At Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, this unsurpassed Wheel of Dhamma has been set in motion by the Blessed One, which cannot be stopped by any ascetic or brahmin, by any deva, Māra, or Brahmā, or by anyone in the world.’

Itiha tena khaṇena (tena layena) ( ) natthi (sī. syā. kaṃ.) tena muhuttena yāva brahmalokā saddo abbhuggacchi. Ayañca dasasahassilokadhātu saṅkampi sampakampi sampavedhi, appamāṇo ca uḷāro obhāso loke pāturahosi atikkamma devānaṃ devānubhāvanti.

Thus, at that moment, at that instant, the sound ascended as far as the Brahmā world. And this ten-thousandfold world-system shook, quaked, and trembled. And an immeasurable, glorious radiance appeared in the world, surpassing the divine majesty of the devas.

Atha kho bhagavā imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi – “aññāsi vata, bho, koṇḍañño, aññāsi vata, bho, koṇḍañño”ti! Iti hidaṃ āyasmato koṇḍaññassa ‘aññāsikoṇḍañño’ tveva nāmaṃ ahosīti. Paṭhamaṃ.

Then the Blessed One uttered this inspired utterance: ‘Koṇḍañña has indeed understood! Koṇḍañña has indeed understood!’ And so it was that the Venerable Koṇḍañña came to be known as ‘Aññāsi Koṇḍañña’—Koṇḍañña Who Understood. First.

2. Tathāgatasuttaṃ

2. The Sutta on the Tathāgata

1082. “‘Idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasacca’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pariññeyya’nti [M 3.0372] bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe…pe… udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pariññāta’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ [T 5.0533] udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

1082. ‘This is the Noble Truth of suffering’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light. ‘This Noble Truth of suffering is to be fully comprehended’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light. ‘This Noble Truth of suffering has been fully comprehended’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.

“‘Idaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasacca’nti bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pahātabba’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe…pe… udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ pahīna’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

‘This is the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light. ‘This Noble Truth of the origin of suffering is to be abandoned’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light. ‘This Noble Truth of the origin of suffering has been abandoned’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.

“‘Idaṃ [V 3.0488] dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasacca’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ sacchikātabba’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe…pe. [P 5.0425]… udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ sacchikata’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi.

‘This is the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light. ‘This Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering is to be realized’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light. ‘This Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering has been realized’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.

“‘Idaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasacca’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ bhāvetabba’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe…pe… udapādi. ‘Taṃ kho panidaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ bhāvita’nti, bhikkhave, tathāgatānaṃ pubbe [T 5.0534] ananussutesu dhammesu cakkhuṃ udapādi, ñāṇaṃ udapādi, paññā udapādi, vijjā udapādi, āloko udapādī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

‘This is the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light. ‘This Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering is to be developed’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light. ‘This Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering has been developed’—O monks, in regard to dhammas unheard of before, there arose in the Tathāgatas the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light. The second.

3. Khandhasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Aggregates

1083. “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, ariyasaccāni. Katamāni cattāri? Dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ dukkhasamudayo ariyasaccaṃ dukkhanirodho ariyasaccaṃ (syā.) dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ.

1083. “O monks, there are these four Noble Truths. What four? The Noble Truth of suffering, the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering, the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering, and the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

“Katamañca[M 3.0373], bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? ‘Pañcupādānakkhandhā’ tissa vacanīyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ katame pañca (sī. syā. kaṃ.) – rūpupādānakkhandho…pe… viññāṇupādānakkhandho. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ.

“And what, O monks, is the Noble Truth of suffering? It should be said: ‘The five aggregates of clinging.’ That is to say: the form aggregate of clinging… and so on… the consciousness aggregate of clinging. This, O monks, is called the Noble Truth of suffering.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobbhavikā nandirāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā. Idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ.

“And what, O monks, is the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering? It is this craving which leads to renewed existence, is accompanied by delight and lust, and delights exceedingly in this or that state of existence; that is to say: craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence. This, O monks, is called the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering.

“Katamañca[V 3.0489], bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ.

“And what, O monks, is the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering? It is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving, the giving up of it, the relinquishment of it, the release from it, and the non-attachment to it. This, O monks, is called the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ. Imāni [T 5.0535][P 5.0426] kho, bhikkhave, cattāri ariyasaccāni.

“And what, O monks, is the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering? It is just this Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view… right concentration. This, O monks, is called the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. These, O monks, are the four Noble Truths.

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Therefore, O monks, effort should be made to realize, ‘This is suffering’… effort should be made to realize, ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ The third.

4. Ajjhattikāyatanasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Internal Sense Bases

1084. “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, ariyasaccāni. Katamāni cattāri? Dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ.

1084. “O monks, there are these four Noble Truths. What four? The Noble Truth of suffering, the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering, the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering, and the Noble Truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? ‘Cha ajjhattikāni āyatanānī’ tissa vacanīyaṃ. Katamāni cha? Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… manāyatanaṃ – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ.

“And what, O monks, is the Noble Truth of suffering? It should be said: ‘The six internal sense bases.’ What six? The eye sense base… the mind sense base. This, O monks, is called the Noble Truth of suffering.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Yāyaṃ taṇhā ponobbhavikā nandirāgasahagatā tatratatrābhinandinī, seyyathidaṃ – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ.

“And what, O monks, is the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering? It is this craving which leads to renewed existence, is accompanied by delight and lust, and delights exceedingly in this or that state of existence; that is to say: craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, and craving for non-existence. This, O monks, is called the Noble Truth of the origin of suffering.

“Katamañca[M 3.0374], bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ? Yo tassāyeva taṇhāya asesavirāganirodho [V 3.0490] cāgo paṭinissaggo mutti anālayo – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ.

“And what, O monks, is the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering? It is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very craving, the giving up of it, the relinquishment of it, the release from it, and the non-attachment to it. This, O monks, is called the Noble Truth of the cessation of suffering.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ? Ayameva ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo, seyyathidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāsamādhi – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ. Imāni [T 5.0536] kho, bhikkhave, cattāri ariyasaccāni.

And what, monks, is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering? It is this very Noble Eightfold Path, that is: right view… right concentration. This, monks, is called the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering. These, monks, are the four noble truths.

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

Therefore, monks, herein, effort should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’ … effort should be made to understand: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ The Fourth.

5. Paṭhamadhāraṇasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on Retention

1085. “Dhāretha no tumhe, bhikkhave, mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti? Evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca [P 5.0427] – “ahaṃ kho, bhante, dhāremi bhagavatā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, dhāresi mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti? “Dukkhaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi; dukkhasamudayaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā dutiyaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi; dukkhanirodhaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā tatiyaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi; dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi. Evaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, dhāremi bhagavatā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti.

1085. “Monks, do you bear in mind the four noble truths taught by me?” When this was said, a certain monk said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I bear in mind the four noble truths taught by the Blessed One.” “But in what way, monk, do you bear in mind the four noble truths taught by me?” “Venerable sir, I bear in mind suffering as the first noble truth taught by the Blessed One; I bear in mind the origin of suffering as the second noble truth taught by the Blessed One; I bear in mind the cessation of suffering as the third noble truth taught by the Blessed One; I bear in mind the path leading to the cessation of suffering as the fourth noble truth taught by the Blessed One. Thus indeed, venerable sir, do I bear in mind the four noble truths taught by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, dhāresi mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānīti. Dukkhaṃ kho, bhikkhu, mayā paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ, tathā naṃ dhārehi; dukkhasamudayaṃ dukkhasamudayo (syā. kaṃ.) kho, bhikkhu, mayā dutiyaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ, tathā naṃ dhārehi; dukkhanirodhaṃ dukkhanirodho (syā. kaṃ.) kho, bhikkhu, mayā tatiyaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ, tathā naṃ dhārehi; dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā dukkhanirodhagāminipaṭipadaṃ (pī.), dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ (ka.) kho, bhikkhu, mayā catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ, tathā naṃ dhārehi. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, dhārehi mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānīti.

“Good, good, monk! It is good indeed, monk, that you bear in mind the four noble truths taught by me. Suffering, monk, as the first noble truth was taught by me; bear it in mind as such. The origin of suffering, monk, as the second noble truth was taught by me; bear it in mind as such. The cessation of suffering, monk, as the third noble truth was taught by me; bear it in mind as such. The path leading to the cessation of suffering, monk, as the fourth noble truth was taught by me; bear it in mind as such. Thus indeed, monk, you should bear in mind the four noble truths taught by me.”

“Tasmātiha[M 3.0375][V 3.0491][T 5.0537], bhikkhu, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Therefore, monk, herein, effort should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’ … effort should be made to understand: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ The Fifth.

6. Dutiyadhāraṇasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Retention

1086. “Dhāretha no tumhe, bhikkhave, mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti? Evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ahaṃ kho, bhante, dhāremi bhagavatā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti.

1086. “Monks, do you bear in mind the four noble truths taught by me?” When this was said, a certain monk said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, I do bear in mind the four noble truths taught by the Blessed One.”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana tvaṃ, bhikkhu, dhāresi mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti? “Dukkhaṃ [P 5.0428] khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi. Yo hi koci, bhante, samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘netaṃ dukkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ yaṃ samaṇena gotamena desitaṃ. Ahametaṃ dukkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paccakkhāya aññaṃ dukkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paññapessāmī’ti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Dukkhasamudayaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ dhāremi. Yo hi koci, bhante, samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘netaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ yaṃ samaṇena gotamena desitaṃ. Ahametaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paccakkhāya aññaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paññapessāmī’ti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Evaṃ khvāhaṃ, bhante, dhāremi bhagavatā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānī”ti.

“But in what way, monk, do you bear in mind the four noble truths taught by me?” “Venerable sir, I bear in mind suffering as the first noble truth taught by the Blessed One. For, venerable sir, should any ascetic or brahmin say: ‘This is not the first noble truth of suffering that was taught by the ascetic Gotama. I, having rejected this first noble truth of suffering, will proclaim another first noble truth of suffering’—this is not possible. I bear in mind... the path leading to the cessation of suffering as the fourth noble truth taught by the Blessed One. For, venerable sir, should any ascetic or brahmin say: ‘This is not the fourth noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering that was taught by the ascetic Gotama. I, having rejected this fourth noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, will proclaim another fourth noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering’—this is not possible. It is in this way, venerable sir, that I bear in mind the four noble truths taught by the Blessed One.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhu! Sādhu kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, dhāresi mayā cattāri [T 5.0538] ariyasaccāni desitānīti. Dukkhaṃ kho, bhikkhu, mayā paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ, tathā naṃ dhārehi. Yo hi koci, bhikkhu, samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā evaṃ vadeyya – ‘netaṃ dukkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ yaṃ samaṇena gotamena desitaṃ. Ahametaṃ dukkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paccakkhāya aññaṃ dukkhaṃ paṭhamaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paññapessāmī’ti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Dukkhasamudayaṃ kho, bhikkhu…pe… dukkhanirodhaṃ kho, bhikkhu…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā kho, bhikkhu, mayā catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ desitaṃ, tathā naṃ dhārehi. Yo hi koci, bhikkhu, samaṇo vā [V 3.0492] brāhmaṇo vā evaṃ vadeyya [P 5.0429] – ‘netaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ yaṃ samaṇena gotamena desitaṃ[M 3.0376]. Ahametaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paccakkhāya aññaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ catutthaṃ ariyasaccaṃ paññapessāmī’ti – netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Evaṃ kho tvaṃ, bhikkhu, dhārehi mayā cattāri ariyasaccāni desitānīti.

“Good, good, monk! It is good, monk, that you bear in mind the four noble truths taught by me. Monk, suffering as the first noble truth was taught by me; bear it in mind as such. If any ascetic or brahmin were to say: ‘This is not the first noble truth of suffering that was taught by the ascetic Gotama. I, having rejected this first noble truth of suffering, will proclaim another first noble truth of suffering’—that is not possible. Monk, the origin of suffering... Monk, the cessation of suffering... Monk, the path leading to the cessation of suffering as the fourth noble truth was taught by me; bear it in mind as such. If any ascetic or brahmin were to say: ‘This is not the fourth noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering that was taught by the ascetic Gotama. I, having rejected this fourth noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering, will proclaim another fourth noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering’—that is not possible. Thus, monk, you should bear in mind the four noble truths taught by me.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhu, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Therefore, monk, in this teaching, effort should be made to realize: ‘This is suffering.’ … effort should be made to realize: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ The Sixth.

7. Avijjāsuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Ignorance

1087. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘avijjā, avijjā’ti bhante, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, bhante, avijjā; kittāvatā ca avijjāgato hotī”ti? “Yaṃ kho, bhikkhu, dukkhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe aññāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya aññāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu, avijjā; ettāvatā ca [T 5.0539] avijjāgato hotī”ti.

1087. That bhikkhu, having sat down to one side, said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘ignorance, ignorance.’ What, venerable sir, is ignorance? And to what extent is one overcome by ignorance?” “Bhikkhu, not knowing suffering, not knowing the origin of suffering, not knowing the cessation of suffering, not knowing the path leading to the cessation of suffering—this, bhikkhu, is called ignorance; and it is to this extent that one is overcome by ignorance.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhu, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhu, an effort should be made to know: ‘This is suffering.’ … An effort should be made to know: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The seventh.

8. Vijjāsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Knowledge

1088. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘vijjā, vijjā’ti, bhante, vuccati. Katamā nu kho, bhante, vijjā; kittāvatā ca vijjāgato hotī”ti? “Yaṃ [P 5.0430] kho, bhikkhu, dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhasamudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhu, vijjā; ettāvatā ca vijjāgato hotī”ti.

1088. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said to the Blessed One: “‘Knowledge, knowledge,’ it is said, venerable sir. What, venerable sir, is knowledge? And to what extent does one become possessed of knowledge?” “Bhikkhu, that which is knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, knowledge of the path leading to the cessation of suffering—this, bhikkhu, is called knowledge; and to this extent one is possessed of knowledge.”

“Tasmātiha[V 3.0493], bhikkhu, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhu, an effort should be made to know: ‘This is suffering.’ … An effort should be made to know: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The eighth.

9. Saṅkāsanasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Explanation

1089. “‘Idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasacca’nti bhikkhave, mayā paññattaṃ. Tattha aparimāṇā vaṇṇā aparimāṇā byañjanā aparimāṇā saṅkāsanā – ‘itipidaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasacca’nti[M 3.0377]; idaṃ dukkhasamudayaṃ…pe… idaṃ dukkhanirodhaṃ…pe… ‘idaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasacca’nti, bhikkhave, mayā paññattaṃ. Tattha aparimāṇā vaṇṇā aparimāṇā byañjanā aparimāṇā saṅkāsanā – ‘itipidaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasacca’nti.

1089. “‘This is the noble truth of suffering,’ bhikkhus, has been declared by me. Therein are immeasurable terms, immeasurable phrases, immeasurable explanations—‘Thus this is the noble truth of suffering.’ ‘This is the noble truth of the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering,’ bhikkhus, has been declared by me. Therein are immeasurable terms, immeasurable phrases, immeasurable explanations—‘Thus this is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Navamaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, an effort should be made to know: ‘This is suffering.’ … An effort should be made to know: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The ninth.

10. Tathasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the True

1090. “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, tathāni avitathāni anaññathāni. Katamāni cattāri? ‘Idaṃ dukkha’nti, bhikkhave, tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ[T 5.0540]; ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ; ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ; ‘ayaṃ [P 5.0431] dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti tathametaṃ avitathametaṃ anaññathametaṃ – imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri tathāni avitathāni anaññathāni.

1090. “Bhikkhus, these four things are true, unfailing, and not otherwise. What four? ‘This is suffering,’ bhikkhus: this is true, this is unfailing, this is not otherwise. ‘This is the origin of suffering’: this is true, this is unfailing, this is not otherwise. ‘This is the cessation of suffering’: this is true, this is unfailing, this is not otherwise. ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering’: this is true, this is unfailing, this is not otherwise. These, bhikkhus, are the four things that are true, unfailing, and not otherwise.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, an effort should be made to know: ‘This is suffering.’ … An effort should be made to know: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The tenth.

Dhammacakkappavattanavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on the Setting in Motion of the Wheel of Dhamma.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary thereof:

Dhammacakkaṃ [V 3.0494] tathāgataṃ, khandhā āyatanena ca;

Dhāraṇā ca dve avijjā, vijjā saṅkāsanā tathāti.

Dhammacakka, two concerning the Tathāgata, Khandha, and Āyatana; two concerning Dhāraṇā, Avijjā, Vijjā, Saṅkāsanā, and Tatha.

3. Koṭigāmavaggo

3. 3. The Koṭigāma Chapter

1. Paṭhamakoṭigāmasuttaṃ

1. 1. The First Discourse at Koṭigāma

1091. Ekaṃ [T 5.0541] samayaṃ bhagavā vajjīsu viharati koṭigāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “catunnaṃ, bhikkhave, ariyasaccānaṃ ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca”.

1091. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Vajjis at Koṭigāma. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, it is because of not awakening to, not penetrating the four noble truths that for this long time both I and you have run on and transmigrated.”

“Katamesaṃ [M 3.0378] catunnaṃ? Dukkhassa, bhikkhave, ariyasaccassa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Dukkhasamudayassa ariyasaccassa…pe… dukkhanirodhassa ariyasaccassa…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa ananubodhā [P 5.0432] appaṭivedhā evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca. Tayidaṃ, bhikkhave, dukkhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ, dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ anubuddhaṃ paṭividdhaṃ; ucchinnā bhavataṇhā, khīṇā bhavanetti; natthidāni punabbhavo”ti.

“Which four? Bhikkhus, it is because of not awakening to, not penetrating the Noble Truth of Suffering that both you and I have run on and transmigrated for this long course. It is because of not awakening to, not penetrating the Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering… the Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering… the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering that both you and I have run on and transmigrated for this long course. Bhikkhus, that Noble Truth of Suffering has been awakened to and penetrated. The Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering has been awakened to and penetrated. The Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering has been awakened to and penetrated. The Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering has been awakened to and penetrated. Craving for existence is cut off, the guide to existence is exhausted; now there is no further existence.”

Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, then said this further:

“Catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ, yathābhūtaṃ adassanā;

Saṃsitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ (syā. kaṃ. ka.) dī. ni. 2.155 dīghamaddhānaṃ, tāsu tāsveva jātisu.

“Because of not seeing the Four Noble Truths as they really are, we have transmigrated for a long course through these various births.

“Tāni [V 3.0495] yāni (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) etāni diṭṭhāni, bhavanetti samūhatā;

Ucchinnaṃ mūlaṃ dukkhassa, natthidāni punabbhavo”ti. paṭhamaṃ;

“These truths have been seen, the guide to existence is uprooted; the root of suffering is cut off, now there is no further existence.” The first.

2. Dutiyakoṭigāmasuttaṃ

2. 2. The Second Discourse at Koṭigāma

1092. “Ye [T 5.0542] hi keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ nappajānanti, na me te, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā samaṇesu vā samaṇasammatā brāhmaṇesu vā brāhmaṇasammatā, na ca panete āyasmanto sāmaññatthaṃ vā brahmaññatthaṃ vā diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.

1092. “Bhikkhus, any ascetics or brahmins who do not understand as it really is, ‘This is suffering’; who do not understand as it really is, ‘This is the origin of suffering’; who do not understand as it really is, ‘This is the cessation of suffering’; who do not understand as it really is, ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering’—I do not consider them ascetics among ascetics or brahmins among brahmins.
