In the same way, monks, it is by a rare coincidence that the Dhamma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata shines in the world. This human state, monks, has been obtained; a Tathāgata, an Arahant, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, has arisen in the world; and the Dhamma-Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata shines in the world.

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Therefore, monks, here exertion should be made for the realization: ‘This is suffering.’ … exertion should be made for the realization: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’”

9. Paṭhamasinerupabbatarājasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on Sineru, the King of Mountains

1119. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso sinerussa pabbatarājassa satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhipeyya. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave[T 5.0570], katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yā vā yā ca satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhittā, yo vā yo ca (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) saṃ. ni. 2.84 sinerupabbatarājā”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ, yadidaṃ – sinerupabbatarājā; appamattikā satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhittā. Saṅkhampi na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti sinerupabbatarājānaṃ upanidhāya satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhittā”ti. “Evameva [P 5.0458] kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa [M 3.0399] abhisametāvino etadeva bahutaraṃ dukkhaṃ yadidaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ; appamattakaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ. Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti, purimaṃ dukkhakkhandhaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ upanidhāya yadidaṃ sattakkhattuparamatā; yo ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti”.

1119. “Monks, suppose a man were to place seven pebbles the size of beans near Sineru, the king of mountains. What do you think of this, monks, which is greater: the seven pebbles the size of beans that were placed there, or Sineru, the king of mountains?” “Venerable Sir, this is far greater, that is, Sineru, the king of mountains. The seven pebbles the size of beans that were placed there are insignificant. Compared with Sineru, the king of mountains, the seven pebbles the size of beans that were placed there do not amount to a reckoning, do not amount to a comparison, nor do they amount to even a fraction.” “Even so, monks, for a noble disciple who is accomplished in view, a person who has penetrated the truths and who understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’… ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering,’ the suffering that has been completely destroyed and exhausted is far greater, while what remains is insignificant. Compared with the former mass of suffering that has been destroyed and exhausted, the remaining suffering for one who is at most a seven-times-returner does not amount to a reckoning, does not amount to a comparison, nor does it amount to even a fraction.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Navamaṃ.

“Therefore, monks, here exertion should be made for the realization: ‘This is suffering.’ … exertion should be made for the realization: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’”

10. Dutiyasinerupabbatarājasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on Sineru, the King of Mountains

1120. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, sinerupabbatarājāyaṃ parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya, ṭhapetvā satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yaṃ vā sinerussa pabbatarājassa parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ, yā vā satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā [V 3.0518] avasiṭṭhā”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ sinerussa pabbatarājassa yadidaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ; appamattikā satta [T 5.0571] muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā avasiṭṭhā. Saṅkhampi na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti sinerussa pabbatarājassa parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ upanidhāya satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā avasiṭṭhā”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa abhisametāvino etadeva bahutaraṃ dukkhaṃ [P 5.0459] yadidaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ; appamattakaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ. Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti, purimaṃ dukkhakkhandhaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ upanidhāya yadidaṃ sattakkhattuparamatā; yo ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti”.

1120. “Suppose, monks, Sineru, the king of mountains, were to be worn away and exhausted, leaving aside seven pebbles the size of beans. What do you think, monks? Which is greater: that which has been worn away and exhausted of Sineru, the king of mountains, or the seven pebbles the size of beans that remain?” “Venerable Sir, this is far greater, that is, what has been worn away and exhausted of Sineru, the king of mountains. The seven pebbles the size of beans that remain are insignificant. Compared to what has been worn away and exhausted of Sineru, the king of mountains, the remaining seven pebbles the size of beans do not amount to a reckoning, do not amount to a comparison, nor do they amount to a fraction.” “Even so, monks, for a noble disciple who is accomplished in view, a person who has penetrated the truths and who understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering,’ the suffering that has been completely destroyed and exhausted is far greater, while what remains is insignificant. Compared with the former mass of suffering that has been destroyed and exhausted, the remaining suffering for one who is at most a seven-times-returner does not amount to a reckoning, does not amount to a comparison, nor does it amount to a fraction.”

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Therefore, monks, here exertion should be made for the realization: ‘This is suffering.’ … exertion should be made for the realization: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’”

Papātavaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter on the Precipice

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary:

Cintā papāto pariḷāho, kūṭaṃ vālandhakāro ca;

Chiggaḷena ca dve vuttā, sineru apare duveti.

Thought, Precipice, Burning, Peak, and Darkness; two are stated with the Hole, and two others with Sineru.

6. Abhisamayavaggo

6. The Chapter on Penetration

1. Nakhasikhasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Fingernail

1121. Atha [T 5.0572][M 3.0400] kho bhagavā parittaṃ nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsuṃ āropetvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yo vāyaṃ mayā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito, ayaṃ vā mahāpathavī”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ yadidaṃ – mahāpathavī; appamattakāyaṃ bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito. Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na [V 3.0519] upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti mahāpathaviṃ upanidhāya bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito”ti. “Evameva [P 5.0460] kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa abhisametāvino etadeva bahutaraṃ dukkhaṃ yadidaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ; appamattakaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ. Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti purimaṃ dukkhakkhandhaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ upanidhāya yadidaṃ sattakkhattuparamatā; yo ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti”.

1121. Then the Blessed One, placing a little dust on the tip of his fingernail, addressed the bhikkhus: "What do you think, bhikkhus? Which is more: the little dust I have placed on the tip of my fingernail, or this great earth?" "Venerable sir, this great earth is far more. The little dust that the Blessed One has placed on the tip of his fingernail is insignificant. It does not amount to a calculation, nor to a comparison, nor to a fraction when compared with the great earth." "Just so, bhikkhus, for a noble disciple accomplished in view, a person who has penetrated the truths, the suffering that has been destroyed and utterly ended is far more. What remains is insignificant. It does not amount to a calculation, nor to a comparison, nor to a fraction when compared with the former mass of suffering that has been destroyed and utterly ended—that is, for one whose rebirths are limited to seven at most; for one who understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’… who understands as it really is: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’"

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, here an exertion should be made: ‘This is suffering’… an exertion should be made: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” First.

2. Pokkharaṇīsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Lotus Pond

1122. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pokkharaṇī paññāsayojanāni āyāmena, paññāsayojanāni vitthārena, paññāsayojanāni ubbedhena, puṇṇā udakassa samatittikā kākapeyyā. Tato puriso kusaggena [T 5.0573] udakaṃ uddhareyya. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yaṃ vā kusaggena ubbhataṃ, yaṃ vā pokkharaṇiyā udaka”nti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ, yadidaṃ – pokkharaṇiyā udakaṃ; appamattakaṃ kusaggena udakaṃ ubbhataṃ. Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti pokkharaṇiyā udakaṃ upanidhāya kusaggena udakaṃ ubbhata”nti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa…pe… yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

1122. "Suppose, bhikkhus, there were a lotus pond fifty yojanas long, fifty yojanas wide, and fifty yojanas deep, full of water, level with the brim, so a crow could drink from it. Then a man were to draw up water from it with the tip of a blade of kusa grass. What do you think, bhikkhus, which is more: the water drawn up with the tip of a blade of kusa grass or the water in the lotus pond?" "Venerable sir, the water in the lotus pond is far more; the water drawn up with the tip of a blade of kusa grass is insignificant. It does not amount to a reckoning, nor to a comparison, nor to a fraction when compared to the water in the lotus pond." "Even so, bhikkhus, for a noble disciple... an exertion should be made." Second.

3. Paṭhamasaṃbhejjasuttaṃ

3. The First Discourse on Confluence

1123. “Seyyathāpi[M 3.0401], bhikkhave, yatthimā mahānadiyo saṃsandanti samenti, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, tato puriso dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni uddhareyya. Taṃ [P 5.0461] kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni, yaṃ vā saṃbhejjaudaka”nti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ, yadidaṃ – saṃbhejjaudakaṃ; appamattakāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni. Saṅkhampi na upenti[V 3.0520], upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti saṃbhejjaudakaṃ upanidhāya dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatānī”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa…pe… yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

1123. "Suppose, bhikkhus, that where these great rivers meet and converge—namely, the Ganges, the Yamunā, the Aciravatī, the Sarabhū, and the Mahī—a person were to draw off two or three drops of water. What do you think, bhikkhus, which is more: those two or three drops drawn off, or the water in the confluence?" "Venerable sir, the water in the confluence is far more. The two or three drops drawn off are insignificant. They do not amount to a reckoning, nor to a comparison, nor to a fraction when compared to the water in the confluence." "Even so, bhikkhus, for a noble disciple... an exertion should be made." Third.

4. Dutiyasaṃbhejjasuttaṃ

4. The Second Discourse on Confluence

1124. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yatthimā mahānadiyo saṃsandanti samenti, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, taṃ udakaṃ parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya, ṭhapetvā dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni[T 5.0574]. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yaṃ vā saṃbhejjaudakaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ, yāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni avasiṭṭhānī”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ saṃbhejjaudakaṃ yadidaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ; appamattakāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni avasiṭṭhāni. Saṅkhampi na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti saṃbhejjaudakaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ upanidhāya dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni avasiṭṭhānī”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa…pe… yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

1124. "Suppose, bhikkhus, that where these great rivers meet and converge—namely, the Ganges, the Yamunā, the Aciravatī, the Sarabhū, and the Mahī—that water were to be destroyed and utterly ended, leaving only two or three drops remaining. What do you think, bhikkhus, which is more: the water in the confluence that has been destroyed and utterly ended, or the two or three drops remaining?" "Venerable sir, the water in the confluence that has been destroyed and utterly ended is far more. The two or three drops remaining are insignificant. They do not amount to a reckoning, nor to a comparison, nor to a fraction when compared to the water in the confluence that has been destroyed and utterly ended." "Even so, bhikkhus, for a noble disciple... an exertion should be made." Fourth.

5. Paṭhamamahāpathavīsuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on the Great Earth

1125. “Seyyathāpi[P 5.0462], bhikkhave, puriso mahāpathaviyā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhipeyya. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yā vā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhittā, ayaṃ vā mahāpathavī”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ, yadidaṃ – mahāpathavī; appamattikā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhittā. Saṅkhampi na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti mahāpathaviṃ upanidhāya satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhittā”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa…pe… yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

1125. "Suppose, bhikkhus, a person were to place seven pebbles the size of jujube seeds on the great earth. What do you think, bhikkhus, which is more: the seven pebbles the size of jujube seeds that have been placed, or this great earth?" "Venerable sir, this great earth is far more. The seven pebbles the size of jujube seeds that have been placed are insignificant. They do not amount to a reckoning, nor to a comparison, nor to a fraction when compared to the great earth." "Even so, bhikkhus, for a noble disciple... an exertion should be made." Fifth.

6. Dutiyamahāpathavīsuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on the Great Earth

1126. “Seyyathāpi[V 3.0521][M 3.0402], bhikkhave, mahāpathavī parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya ṭhapetvā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yaṃ vā mahāpathaviyā parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ[T 5.0575], yā vā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā avasiṭṭhā”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ mahāpathaviyā yadidaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ; appamattikā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā avasiṭṭhā. Saṅkhampi na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti mahāpathaviyā parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ upanidhāya satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā avasiṭṭhā”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa…pe… yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

1126. “Monks, suppose the great earth were to be destroyed and used up, leaving only seven pellets the size of jujube seeds. What do you think, monks, which is more: the great earth that has been destroyed and used up, or the seven pellets the size of jujube seeds that remain?” “Venerable sir, the great earth that has been destroyed and used up is far more. The seven pellets the size of jujube seeds that remain are insignificant. They do not amount to a reckoning, nor to a comparison, nor to a fraction when compared to the great earth that has been destroyed and used up.” “Just so, monks, for a noble disciple... effort should be made.” The sixth.

7. Paṭhamamahāsamuddasuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse on the Great Ocean

1127. “Seyyathāpi[P 5.0463], bhikkhave, puriso mahāsamuddato dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni uddhareyya. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni, yaṃ vā mahāsamudde udaka”nti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ, yadidaṃ – mahāsamudde udakaṃ; appamattakāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni. Saṅkhampi na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti mahāsamudde udakaṃ upanidhāya dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatānī”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa…pe… yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

1127. “Monks, suppose a person were to take up two or three drops of water from the great ocean. What do you think, monks, which is more: the two or three drops of water that were taken up, or the water in the great ocean?” “Venerable sir, the water in the great ocean is far more. The two or three drops of water that were taken up are insignificant. They do not amount to a reckoning, nor to a comparison, nor to a fraction when compared to the water in the great ocean.” “Just so, monks, for a noble disciple... effort should be made.” The seventh.

8. Dutiyamahāsamuddasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse on the Great Ocean

1128. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde udakaṃ parikkhayaṃ mahāsamuddo parikkhayaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ.) saṃ. ni. 2.81 pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya ṭhapetvā dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yaṃ vā mahāsamudde udakaṃ [T 5.0576] parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ, yāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni avasiṭṭhānī”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ mahāsamudde udakaṃ yadidaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ; appamattakāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni avasiṭṭhāni. Saṅkhampi [V 3.0522] na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti mahāsamudde udakaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ [M 3.0403] pariyādinnaṃ upanidhāya dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni avasiṭṭhānī”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa…pe… yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

1128. “Monks, suppose the water in the great ocean were to diminish and be used up, leaving only two or three drops remaining. What do you think, monks, which is more: the water that has diminished and been used up from the great ocean, or the two or three drops that remain?” “Venerable sir, the water that has diminished and been used up from the great ocean is far more. The remaining two or three drops are insignificant. They do not amount to a reckoning, a comparison, or a fraction when compared to the water that has diminished and been used up from the great ocean.” “Just so, monks, for a noble disciple… effort should be made.” The eighth.

9. Paṭhamapabbatūpamasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse with the Simile of the Mountain

1129. “Seyyathāpi[P 5.0464], bhikkhave, puriso himavato pabbatarājassa satta sāsapamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhipeyya. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yā vā satta sāsapamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhittā, ayaṃ vā himavā pabbatarājā”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ, yadidaṃ – himavā pabbatarājā; appamattikā satta sāsapamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhittā. Saṅkhampi na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti himavantaṃ pabbatarājānaṃ upanidhāya satta sāsapamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhittā”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa…pe… yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Navamaṃ.

1129. “Monks, suppose a man were to place seven mustard-seed-sized pebbles at the foot of Himavā, the king of mountains. What do you think, monks, which is more: those seven mustard-seed-sized pebbles placed there, or Himavā, the king of mountains?” “Venerable sir, Himavā, the king of mountains, is far greater. The seven mustard-seed-sized pebbles placed there are insignificant. They do not amount to a reckoning, a comparison, or a fraction when compared to Himavā, the king of mountains.” “Just so, monks, for a noble disciple… effort should be made.” The ninth.

10. Dutiyapabbatūpamasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse with the Simile of the Mountain

1130. “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, himavā pabbatarājā parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya, ṭhapetvā satta sāsapamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā. Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yaṃ vā himavato pabbatarājassa [T 5.0577] parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ, yā vā satta sāsapamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā avasiṭṭhā”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ himavato pabbatarājassa yadidaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ; appamattikā satta sāsapamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā avasiṭṭhā. Saṅkhampi na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti himavato pabbatarājassa parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ upanidhāya satta sāsapamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā avasiṭṭhā”ti. “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa abhisametāvino etadeva bahutaraṃ dukkhaṃ [P 5.0465] yadidaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ; appamattakaṃ avasiṭṭhaṃ. Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti purimaṃ dukkhakkhandhaṃ parikkhīṇaṃ pariyādinnaṃ upanidhāya [V 3.0523] yadidaṃ sattakkhattuparamatā; yo ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti”.

1130. “Monks, suppose Himavā, the king of mountains, were to diminish and be used up, until only seven mustard-seed-sized pebbles remained. What do you think, monks, which would be more: what has diminished and been used up from Himavā, the king of mountains, or the seven mustard-seed-sized pebbles that remain?” “Venerable sir, what has diminished and been used up from Himavā, the king of mountains, would be far more. The seven mustard-seed-sized pebbles that remain are insignificant. They do not amount to a reckoning, a comparison, or a fraction when compared to what has diminished and been used up from Himavā, the king of mountains.” “Just so, monks, for a noble disciple accomplished in view, a person who has attained understanding, the suffering that has diminished and been used up is far more. What remains is insignificant. It does not amount to a reckoning, a comparison, or a fraction when what remains—that is, at most seven more lives—is compared to the former mass of suffering that has diminished and been used up, for one who understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’… ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’”

“Tasmātiha[M 3.0404], bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Therefore, monks, effort should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’ … Effort should be made to understand: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The tenth.

Abhisamayavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Chapter on Comprehension is the sixth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Its summary:

Nakhasikhā pokkharaṇī, saṃbhejja apare duve;

Pathavī dve samuddā dve, dvemā ca pabbatūpamāti.

The Fingernail, the Pond, two on Mingling; Two Earths, two Oceans, and these two Mountain Similes.

7. Paṭhamaāmakadhaññapeyyālavaggo

7. The First Chapter on the Raw Grain Repetition Series

1. Aññatrasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Elsewhere

1131. Atha [T 5.0578] kho bhagavā parittaṃ nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsuṃ āropetvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yo vāyaṃ mayā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito, ayaṃ vā mahāpathavī”ti? “Etadeva[P 5.0466], bhante, bahutaraṃ, yadidaṃ – mahāpathavī; appamattakāyaṃ bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito. Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti mahāpathaviṃ upanidhāya bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito”ti.

1131. Then the Blessed One, taking up a little dust on the tip of his fingernail, addressed the monks: “What do you think, monks? Which is greater: this little dust I have taken up on the tip of my fingernail, or this great earth?” “Venerable sir, this great earth is far greater. The little dust taken up by the Blessed One on the tip of his fingernail is trifling. When compared with the great earth, it does not amount to a reckoning, it does not amount to a comparison, it does not amount to even a fraction.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, appamattakā te sattā ye manussesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye aññatra manussehi manussesu (pī. ka.) paccājāyanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Adiṭṭhattā, bhikkhave, catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Dukkhassa ariyasaccassa…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa”.

“Just so, monks, few are those beings who are reborn among humans; but far more numerous are those beings who are reborn elsewhere than among humans. For what reason? Because, monks, of not having seen the four noble truths. Which four? The noble truth of suffering… the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.”

“Tasmātiha[V 3.0524], bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Therefore, monks, exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering’… exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’”

2. Paccantasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Frontier

1132. Atha kho bhagavā parittaṃ nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsuṃ āropetvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yo vāyaṃ [M 3.0405] mayā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito, ayaṃ vā mahāpathavī”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ, yadidaṃ – mahāpathavī; appamattakāyaṃ bhagavatā [T 5.0579] paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito. Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti mahāpathaviṃ upanidhāya bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito”ti.

1132. Then the Blessed One, taking up a little dust on the tip of his fingernail, addressed the monks: “What do you think, monks? Which is greater: this little dust I have taken up on the tip of my fingernail, or this great earth?” “Venerable sir, this great earth is far greater. The little dust taken up by the Blessed One on the tip of his fingernail is trifling. When compared with the great earth, it does not amount to a reckoning, it does not amount to a comparison, it does not amount to even a fraction.”

“Evameva kho, bhikkhave, appamattakā te sattā ye majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye paccantimesu janapadesu paccājāyanti aviññātāresu milakkhesu milakkhūsu (syā. kaṃ. ka.) …pe…. Dutiyaṃ.

“Just so, monks, few are those beings who are reborn in the central lands; but far more numerous are those beings who are reborn in the frontier lands, among the ignorant barbarians… The second.

The First Series on Raw Grain, the Seventh Chapter.

Tassuddānaṃ –

Aññatra paccantaṃ paññā, surāmerayaodakā;

Matteyya petteyyā cāpi, sāmaññaṃ brahmapacāyikanti.

Elsewhere, the frontier, wisdom, intoxicants, and water; dutifulness to mother and father, and also to ascetics, brahmins, and the venerated.

1157. …Pe… “evameva [T 5.0584][P 5.0472] kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye dāsidāsapaṭiggahaṇā dāsīdāsapaṭiggahaṇā (syā. kaṃ. pī.) paṭiviratā; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye dāsidāsapaṭiggahaṇā appaṭiviratā…pe…. Sattamaṃ.

1157. …Just so, monks, few are those beings who abstain from accepting female and male slaves; but indeed, far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from accepting female and male slaves… The seventh.

8. Ajeḷakasuttaṃ

8. 8. The Discourse on Goats and Sheep

1158. …Pe… “evameva [M 3.0410] kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye ajeḷakapaṭiggahaṇā [V 3.0531] paṭiviratā; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye ajeḷakapaṭiggahaṇā appaṭiviratā…pe…. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

1158. …Just so, monks, few are those beings who abstain from accepting goats and sheep; but indeed, far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from accepting goats and sheep… The eighth.

9. Kukkuṭasūkarasuttaṃ

9. 9. The Discourse on Fowl and Swine

1159. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye kukkuṭasūkarapaṭiggahaṇā paṭiviratā; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye kukkuṭasūkarapaṭiggahaṇā appaṭiviratā…pe…. Navamaṃ.

1159. …Just so, monks, few are those beings who abstain from accepting fowl and swine; but indeed, far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from accepting fowl and swine… The ninth.

10. Hatthigavassasuttaṃ

10. 10. The Discourse on Elephants, Cattle, and Horses

1160. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye hatthigavassavaḷavapaṭiggahaṇā hatthigavassavaḷavāpaṭiggahaṇā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) paṭiviratā; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye hatthigavassavaḷavapaṭiggahaṇā appaṭiviratā…pe…. Dasamaṃ.

1160. …Just so, monks, few are those beings who abstain from accepting elephants, cattle, horses, and mares; but indeed, far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from accepting elephants, cattle, horses, and mares… The tenth.

Tatiyaāmakadhaññapeyyālavaggo navamo.

The Third Repetition Series Chapter on Raw Grain, the ninth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Naccaṃ sayanaṃ rajataṃ, dhaññaṃ maṃsaṃ kumārikā;

Dāsī ajeḷakañceva, kukkuṭasūkarahatthīti.

Dancing, beds, silver, grain, meat, maidens, female slaves, goats and sheep, fowl, swine, and elephants.

10. Catutthaāmakadhaññapeyyālavaggo

10. 10. The Fourth Repetition Series Chapter on Raw Grain

1. Khettavatthusuttaṃ

1. 1. The Discourse on Fields and Land

1161. …Pe… [V 3.0532] “evameva [P 5.0473] kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye khettavatthupaṭiggahaṇā paṭiviratā; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye khettavatthupaṭiggahaṇā appaṭiviratā…pe…. Paṭhamaṃ.

1161. …Just so, monks, few are those beings who abstain from accepting fields and land; but indeed, far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from accepting fields and land… The first.

2. Kayavikkayasuttaṃ

2. 2. The Discourse on Buying and Selling

1162. …Pe… “evameva [T 5.0585][M 3.0411] kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye kayavikkayā paṭiviratā; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye kayavikkayā appaṭiviratā…pe…. Dutiyaṃ.

1162. …Just so, monks, few are those beings who abstain from buying and selling; but indeed, far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from buying and selling… The second.

3. Dūteyyasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Acting as a Messenger

1163. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye dūteyyapahinagamanānuyogā paṭiviratā; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye dūteyyapahinagamanānuyogā appaṭiviratā…pe…. Tatiyaṃ.

1163. Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who abstain from the practice of acting as a messenger and running errands; but far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from them. Third.

4. Tulākūṭasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Deceitful Scales

1164. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye tulākūṭakaṃsakūṭamānakūṭā paṭiviratā; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye tulākūṭakaṃsakūṭamānakūṭā appaṭiviratā…pe…. Catutthaṃ.

1164. Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who abstain from deceit with scales, deceit with coins, and deceit with measures; but far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from them. Fourth.

5. Ukkoṭanasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Bribery

1165. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye ukkoṭanavañcananikatisāciyogā [V 3.0533] ukkoṭanavañcananikatisāviyogā (syā. kaṃ. pī. ka.) paṭiviratā; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye ukkoṭanavañcananikatisāciyogā appaṭiviratā…pe…. Pañcamaṃ.

1165. Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who abstain from bribery, deception, fraud, and crooked practices; but far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from them. Fifth.

6-11. Chedanādisuttaṃ

6-11. The Discourses on Cutting, etc.

1166-1171. …Pe… evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye chedanavadhabandhanaviparāmosaālopasahasākārā sāhasākārā (ka.) paṭiviratā[P 5.0474]; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye chedanavadhabandhanaviparāmosaālopasahasākārā appaṭiviratā[T 5.0586]. Taṃ kissa hetu? Adiṭṭhattā bhikkhave, catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ? Dukkhassa ariyasaccassa…pe… dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa”.

Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who abstain from cutting, killing, binding, highway robbery, plundering, and violence; but far more numerous are those beings who do not abstain from them. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, of not having seen the four noble truths. Which four? The noble truth of suffering… the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

“Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo…pe… ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

Therefore, bhikkhus, effort should be made thus: ‘This is suffering.’ … Effort should be made thus: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’ Eleventh.

Catutthaāmakadhaññapeyyālavaggo dasamo.

The Tenth Chapter: The Fourth Section of Repetitions on Raw Grain.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of it:

Khettaṃ [M 3.0412] kāyaṃ dūteyyañca, tulākūṭaṃ ukkoṭanaṃ;

Chedanaṃ vadhabandhanaṃ, viparālopaṃ sāhasanti.

The field, buying, and being a messenger, deceitful scales, bribery; cutting, killing, binding, plundering, and violence.

11. Pañcagatipeyyālavaggo

11. The Section of Repetitions on the Five Destinations

1. Manussacutinirayasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Passing Away from the Human State into Hell

1172. Atha kho bhagavā parittaṃ nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsuṃ āropetvā bhikkhū āmantesi – “taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, katamaṃ nu kho bahutaraṃ – yo vāyaṃ mayā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito, ayaṃ vā mahāpathavī”ti? “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṃ, yadidaṃ – mahāpathavī; appamattakāyaṃ [V 3.0534] bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito. Saṅkhampi na upeti, upanidhampi na upeti, kalabhāgampi na upeti mahāpathaviṃ upanidhāya bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṃ paṃsu āropito”ti. Evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye manussā cutā manussesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye manussā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe…. Paṭhamaṃ.

1172. Then the Blessed One, having placed a little dust on the tip of his fingernail, addressed the bhikkhus: “What do you think, bhikkhus? Which is more—this little dust that I have placed on the tip of my fingernail, or this great earth?” “Venerable Sir, the great earth is far more. The little dust the Blessed One has placed on the tip of his fingernail is a trifling amount. Compared to the great earth, the little dust the Blessed One has placed on the tip of his fingernail does not amount to a calculation, does not amount to a comparison, and does not amount to a fraction.” “Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from the human state, are reborn among humans; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from the human state, are reborn in hell. First.

2. Manussacutitiracchānasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Passing Away from the Human State to the Animal Realm

1173. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye manussā cutā manussesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye manussā cutā tiracchānayoniyā paccājāyanti…pe…. Dutiyaṃ.

1173. …Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from the human state, are reborn among humans; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from the human state, are reborn in the animal realm. Second.

3. Manussacutipettivisayasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Passing Away from the Human State to the Realm of Petas

1174. …Pe… “evameva [P 5.0475] kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye manussā cutā manussesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye manussā cutā pettivisaye paccājāyanti…pe…. Tatiyaṃ.

1174. …Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from the human state, are reborn among humans; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from the human state, are reborn in the realm of petas. Third.

4-5-6. Manussacutidevanirayādisuttaṃ

4-6. The Discourses on Passing Away from the Human State to the Deva Realm, Hell, and So Forth

1175-1177. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye manussā cutā devesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva [T 5.0587] bahutarā sattā ye [M 3.0413] manussā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe… tiracchānayoniyā paccājāyanti…pe… pettivisaye paccājāyanti…pe…. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

…Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from the human state, are reborn among the devas; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from the human state, are reborn in hell… are reborn in the animal realm… are reborn in the realm of petas. Sixth.

7-9. Devacutinirayādisuttaṃ

7–9. The Discourses on Devas Passing Away into Hell, etc.

1178-1180. …Pe… [V 3.0535] “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye devā cutā devesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye devā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe… tiracchānayoniyā paccājāyanti…pe… pettivisaye paccājāyanti…pe…. Navamaṃ.

…Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from the deva realm, are reborn among the devas; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from the deva realm, are reborn in hell… are reborn in the animal realm… are reborn in the realm of petas. Ninth.

10-12. Devamanussanirayādisuttaṃ

10–12. The Discourses on Passing from the Deva Realm to the Human Realm, Hell, etc.

1181-1183. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye devā cutā manussesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye devā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe… tiracchānayoniyā paccājāyanti…pe… pettivisaye paccājāyanti…pe…. Dvādasamaṃ.

…Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from the deva realm, are reborn among humans; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from the deva realm, are reborn in hell… are reborn in the animal realm… are reborn in the realm of petas. Twelfth.

13-15. Nirayamanussanirayādisuttaṃ

13–15. The Discourses on Passing from Hell to the Human Realm, Hell, etc.

1184-1186. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye nirayā cutā manussesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye nirayā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe… tiracchānayoniyā paccājāyanti…pe… pettivisaye paccājāyanti…pe…. Pannarasamaṃ.

…Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from hell, are reborn among humans; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from hell, are reborn in hell… are reborn in the animal realm… are reborn in the realm of petas. Fifteenth.

16-18. Nirayadevanirayādisuttaṃ

16–18. The Discourses on Passing from Hell to the Deva Realm, Hell, etc.

1187-1189. …Pe… “evameva [P 5.0476] kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye nirayā cutā devesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye nirayā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe… tiracchānayoniyā paccājāyanti…pe… pettivisaye paccājāyanti…pe…. Aṭṭhārasamaṃ.

…Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from hell, are reborn among the devas; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from hell, are reborn in hell… are reborn in the animal realm… are reborn in the realm of petas. Eighteenth.

19-21. Tiracchānamanussanirayādisuttaṃ

19–21. The Discourses on Passing from the Animal Realm to the Human Realm, Hell, etc.

1190-1192. …Pe… [V 3.0536] “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye tiracchānayoniyā cutā manussesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā [T 5.0588] ye tiracchānayoniyā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe… tiracchānayoniyā [M 3.0414] paccājāyanti…pe… pettivisaye paccājāyanti…pe…. Ekavīsatimaṃ.

…Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from the animal realm, are reborn among humans; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from the animal realm, are reborn in hell… are reborn in the animal realm… are reborn in the realm of petas. Twenty-first.

22-24. Tiracchānadevanirayādisuttaṃ

22–24. The Discourses on Passing from the Animal Realm to the Deva Realm, Hell, etc.

1193-1195. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye tiracchānayoniyā cutā devesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye tiracchānayoniyā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe… tiracchānayoniyā paccājāyanti…pe… pettivisaye paccājāyanti…pe…. Catuvīsatimaṃ.

1193–1195. …So too, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, on passing away from the animal realm, are reborn among the devas. But far more numerous are those beings who, on passing away from the animal realm, are reborn in hell… reborn in the animal realm… reborn in the realm of petas… The twenty-fourth.

25-27. Pettimanussanirayādisuttaṃ

25–27. The Discourse on Petas, Humans, Hell, etc.

1196-1198. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye pettivisayā cutā manussesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye pettivisayā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe… tiracchānayoniyā paccājāyanti…pe… pettivisaye paccājāyanti…pe…. Sattavīsatimaṃ.

1196–1198. …In the same way, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, on passing away from the realm of petas, are reborn among humans. But far more numerous are those beings who, on passing away from the realm of petas, are reborn in hell… reborn in the animal realm… reborn in the realm of petas… The twenty-seventh.

28-29. Pettidevanirayādisuttaṃ

28–29. The Discourse on Petas, Devas, Hell, etc.

1199-1200. …Pe… “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye pettivisayā cutā devesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye pettivisayā cutā niraye paccājāyanti…pe… evameva [P 5.0477] kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye pettivisayā cutā devesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye pettivisayā cutā tiracchānayoniyā paccājāyanti…pe…. Ekūnatiṃsatimaṃ.

1199–1200. …In the same way, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from the realm of petas, are reborn among the devas; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from the realm of petas, are reborn in hell… In the same way, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, having passed away from the realm of petas, are reborn among the devas; but far more numerous are those beings who, having passed away from the realm of petas, are reborn in the animal realm… The twenty-ninth.

30. Pettidevapettivisayasuttaṃ

30. 30. The Discourse on Petas, Devas, and the Peta Realm

1201. …Pe… [V 3.0537] “evameva kho, bhikkhave, appakā te sattā ye pettivisayā cutā devesu paccājāyanti; atha kho eteva bahutarā sattā ye pettivisayā cutā pettivisaye paccājāyanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Adiṭṭhattā bhikkhave, catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ. Katamesaṃ catunnaṃ[T 5.0589]? Dukkhassa ariyasaccassa, dukkhasamudayassa ariyasaccassa, dukkhanirodhassa ariyasaccassa, dukkhanirodhagāminiyā paṭipadāya ariyasaccassa”.

1201. …Just so, bhikkhus, few are those beings who, on passing away from the realm of petas, are reborn among the devas; far more numerous are those beings who, on passing away from the realm of petas, are reborn in the realm of petas. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, of not having seen the four noble truths. Which four? The noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the cessation of suffering, and the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering.

“Tasmātiha[M 3.0415], bhikkhave, ‘idaṃ dukkha’nti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhasamudayo’ti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodho’ti yogo karaṇīyo, ‘ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti. Tiṃsatimaṃ.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’ Exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the origin of suffering.’ Exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the cessation of suffering.’ Exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.’” The Blessed One said this. Delighted, those bhikkhus rejoiced in the Blessed One’s speech. The thirtieth.

Pañcagatipeyyālavaggo ekādasamo.

The Chapter on the Five Destinations, the eleventh.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Manussato cutā chāpi, devā cutā nirayato;

Tiracchānapettivisayā, tiṃsamatto gativaggoti.

Six on those fallen from the human realm, on those fallen from the devas and from hell, on those from the animal realm and the realm of petas—the Chapter on Destinations thus amounts to thirty.

Saccasaṃyuttaṃ dvādasamaṃ.

The Connected Discourses on the Truths, the twelfth, is concluded.

Mahāvaggo pañcamo.

The Great Division, the fifth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Maggabojjhaṅgaṃ [P 5.0478] satiyā, indriyaṃ sammappadhānaṃ;

Baliddhipādānuruddhā, jhānānāpānasaṃyutaṃ;

Sotāpatti saccañcāti, mahāvaggoti vuccatīti.

The Path, the Factors of Enlightenment, Mindfulness, the Faculties, the Right Efforts; the Powers, the Bases of Spiritual Power, Anuruddha, Absorption, Mindfulness of Breathing; with Stream-Entry and the Truths—this is called the Great Division.

Mahāvaggasaṃyuttapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Pāḷi of the Connected Discourses of the Great Division is concluded.
